If Japanese reservists or soldiers have been
concerned in such a crime it is apparent that they have
been acting on information given to them by some person
knowing that gambling was taking place in the Temple.
The only contact no with the players is the female
residing at No.107 Shanse Road, and she denies knowing
any of the persons who were playing Mah Jhong, she having
entered to worship and merely joined the game.
The Chief Priest denies knowing the players, and
states that it the custom for worshippers to linger in
the Temple and to play Mah Jhong. He denies that any
large scale gambling has taken place.
This Temple will be kept under observation in the
future, and any developments or further information
will be reported.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Complaint on Illegal Functioning of the
Japanese Military.
At 6.40 p.m. 1-6-38 Mr. R.W. Brewer, the manager
of the Ford Hire Service Fed. Inc. U.S.A. came to the
station and reported that one of their chauffeurs named
Van Ah Sung ( 樊阿生 ), permit No. 8094, had been illegally
seized and taken away by force, by three Japanese men
dressed in plain clothes, who drove him away in a private
M/car licence No. 11230 at 6.05 p.m. even date from the
Edinburgh Road Office of the Ford Hire Service.
Whilst Mr. R.W. Brewer was at the station, at about
7 p.m. even date, a telephone message was received to
the effect that the above named chauffeur had been brought
by the Japanese to the St. George's Office of the F. H.
Service, Avenue Haig and B'Well Road corner.
The undersigned accompanied by J.P.C. 232 and Mr.
R.W. Brewer immediately attended and saw M/car licence
No. 11230 parked on the East side of Avenue Haig near
B'Well Road. The above named chauffeur was found in the
office of the F. H. Service.
One of the 3 Japanese occupants of M/car Lic. No.
11230 identified himself as Corporal I. Ito of the
Western Branch of the Japanese Military Police, 94 Jess-
field Road and stated that the chauffeur had been wanted
by them for enquiries in an endeavour to trace the move-
ments of two missing Japanese soldiers, who were known

1938年6月1日下午6时40分，美国福特租车服务联合会（Fed. Inc. U.S.A.）经理 R.W. Brewer 先生来到巡捕房报告，其一名名为樊阿生（Van Ah Sung）、执照号8094的司机，于当日下午6时05分在福特租车服务行爱丁堡路办事处，被三名身着便服的日本男子非法强行抓走，并被驱赶进一辆牌照号为11230的私人机动车带走。
当 R.W. Brewer 先生在巡捕房时，约于当日下午7时，接到电话消息称，上述司机已被日本人带至海格路（Avenue Haig）与倍威尔路（B'Well Road）转角处的福特租车服务行圣乔治办事处。
署名人与警员232号及 R.W. Brewer 先生立即前往现场，发现牌照号为11230的机动车停在海格路东段靠近倍威尔路处。在上述福特租车服务行办事处内找到了上述司机。
牌照号为11230的机动车上的三名日本人之一自称是日本宪兵队西区分队下士 I. Ito，地址为极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）94号，并称他们因试图追踪两名失踪日本士兵的行踪而需要询问该司机，据悉这两名士兵曾

下午6时05分，3名身着便服的日本人乘坐牌照号为11230的机动车到达，在确认他是牌照号为12347的机动车的司机后，命令他随他们同行。他服从了命令，被带至极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）94号，在那里他就上述华人和日本人的行踪接受了讯问，随后被要求陪同几名日本宪兵队军官，并向他们展示那群人访问过的地址。他同意了，但请求允许通知其雇主。随后他被 I. Ito 下士驱车带至圣乔治办事处，警方由此获悉上述情况。

司机表示，日本宪兵队军官未对他使用暴力，他没有任何投诉。

The following is the statement of Van Ah Sing ( 范阿兴 ), age 45,
native of Yangchow, taken by me S.D.C. 279.
at B'Well Stn. on the 1-6-38. translated and interpreted by Stu Kuang Ho.

I am employed by Ford Hire Service Garage as a
chauffeur, possessing driving permit 8094 and live at No. 6
Tung Zung Li off B'well Road.

At 3.50 p.m. 1-6-38 I was told to drive a hire car
to House 153, Flat 37, Route des Soeurs. Upon arrival at the
destination, 1 male (Chinese) speaking English, wearing
foreign style clothing and 1 female speaking Japanese boarded
my car and ordered me to drive to N. Szechuen & Darroch Roads.
On arrival at the mentioned address, the female alighted but
shortly afterwards, she returned with 2 Japanese soldiers
and ordered me to take them to Great Eastern & Edinburgh Roads.
When I was passing Burkill & Tatung Roads, the man wearing
foreign clothing told me to stop and got off. When we arrived
in my car at Great Eastern & Edinburgh Roads, we waited for
about 1 minutes when the man wearing foreign clothing came
up, bringing 2 male Chinese who also entered my car and I
was then told to drive for Lau Ka Yih, Edinburgh Road opposite
Lane 152, where 2 Japanese soldiers and 2 Chinese alighted
and went inside the lane, leaving the female in the car.
About 10 minutes later, the 2 Japanese soldiers and 2 Chinese
brought another Chinese, coming out from the lane and put him
in my car. The Japanese soldiers told me to drive them to
the original place from whence they came. When at Faung Ka
Loong, 2 Chinese told me to stop and alighted and at the same
place, a man dressed in foreign clothing boarded and told me
to drive to N. Szechuen Road. Upon arrival at N. Szechuen &
Haining Roads, the man together with 2 Japanese soldiers, 1

At 12.17a.m. 25-5-38 telephone message was received
from C.I.D. 1951 on duty at 10 North Szechow Road,
reporting that he had been informed that 4 or 5 Japanese
Civilians had entered 19 North Szechow Road
in search of something.

The scene was immediately visited by ... Road,
S.I. Alexandroff, D.O.C. 67 and J. ... 243.

On arrival at this address it was learnt that the
Japanese had already left and the 1st floor front room
showed the usual disorder following a search.

Yue Oo Sz (余伍氏) was present and stated a number
of Japanese & Chinese had entered the room at about
10a.m., searched same, after which they had arrested her
husband Yue Ts Bing (余丁平) and taken him away. Yue Oo
Sz could give no reason for the arrest of her husband
but supplied the information that he was employed at the
Dah Yah Shipping Co., 458 North Szechow Road.

Enquiry in the vicinity revealed only that the party
had arrived and left by car no details of the latter
being available.

At this stage D.C. Div., D.O. "B", D.D.O. "B", Special
Branch & Inspt. i/c. were informed by Sen. Det.

At about 12noon enquiry was made at Dah Yah Shipping
Co. (Japanese owner), 458 North Szechow Road, where it

到达该地址后，得知日本人已经离开，一楼前屋呈现出搜查后常见的凌乱状态。

余伍氏（Yue Oo Sz）在场，并称上午10时许，多名日本人和中国人进入房间进行搜查，随后逮捕了她的丈夫岳丁平（Yue Ts Bing，音译）并将其带走。余伍氏无法说明其丈夫被捕的原因，但提供信息称他受雇于北四川路458号的大华轮船公司（Dah Yah Shipping Co.）。

was learnt that a number of Japanese with Yue Ts Bing
had arrived by car at about 10.45a.m. and after asking
questions re Yue Ts Lin 's employment and left stating
they were going to the Japanese Headquarters on the
bund (The old Ferry re resident ulk).

At about 12.15p.m. 25-1-46 D.S.I. Read, C.D.S. 67
/ J.P.C. 243 with Yue Oo Sz drove to this Head Quarters.
On dismounting from the car Yue Oo Sz pointed out a
Japanese who was just about to drive off in another car
and stated he was one of the Japanese who had taken her
husband away. D.S.I. Read and J.P.C. 243 approached
this Japanese and J.P.C. 243 briefly stated the object
of the enquiry, whereupon this Japanese left from the
other side of the car and went direct on to the Hulk.
After instructing Yue Oo Sz to return to the police car
and remain there D.S.I. Read, C.D.S. 67 and J.P.C. 243
proceeded to the Hulk, where they were met by Officer
i/c. (Lieut. name unknown) who, after the object of the
visit had been explained, by J.P.C. 243 escorted them
to a (his?) office and a discussion ensued.

This officer at first, did not deny or admit that
Yue Ts Bing had been arrested or was present on the Hulk
but at every evasion, it was requested that permission
be given for an interview with the Japanese who had
entered from the car. After a while, it was acknowledged
pages.zh:
1 (第2页)

获悉，多名日本人偕同岳丁平于上午10时45分左右乘车到达，在询问了关于岳林（Yue Ts Lin，音译）的工作情况后离开，并称他们要去外滩的日本总部（旧趸船居民ulk）。

1946年1月25日下午12时15分左右 [原文日期明显有误，应为1938年]，副督察长里德、67号刑事侦探社长（C.D.S. 67）/ 243号日本警务联络官（J.P.C. 243）偕同余伍氏驾车前往该总部。下车时，余伍氏指出一名正准备驾驶另一辆车离开的日本人，并称他是带走她丈夫的日本人之一。副督察长里德和243号日本警务联络官走近这名日本人，243号日本警务联络官简要说明了查询目的，随后这名日本人从车的另一侧离开，直接走上趸船（Hulk）。在指示余伍氏返回警车并留在那里后，副督察长里德、67号刑事侦探社长和243号日本警务联络官前往趸船，在那里他们遇到了主管军官（中尉，姓名不详），在243号日本警务联络官解释了来访目的后，该军官护送他们到一间（他的？）办公室，随后进行了讨论。

这位军官起初既不否认也不承认岳丁平（Yue Ts Bing，音译）已被捕或在趸船上，但在每一次回避中，警方都要求允许与从车上下来的那名日本人会面。过了一会儿，对方承认

pages.en:
that a man named Yue Ts Ring or Mac on Shing was
present on the premises and had not been
arrested but had merely been asked to wait. It was
pointed out that this man had been asked to wait prior
to any leave being granted and that he was 'under arrest'.
The officer i/c stated that no leave would be granted until
their enquiries were completed. It was then explained
that if the person concerned was not under arrest there was
no alternative but to ascertain that he was not under
arrest. Discussion centered around this for about five
minutes after which the officer i/c stated he would give
permission for 'this person' to be interviewed if
questions were confined solely to the manner in which
he had come to the Japanese Headquarters.

Yue Ts Ring was then brought into the room and
questioned.

Q. How did you come here.
A. I came at the invitation of two Japanese friends.
I was not arrested.
Q. Who searched your room.
A. I searched it myself.

After this the Officer i/c was thanked and the Police
party left at about 12.55p.m. being assured that Yue Ts
Ring would shortly be released.

At 2pm Yue Ts Ring himself came to the Station following his release at 1.45p.m. bringing with him a forged
pages.zh:
一名名为岳丁荣（Yue Ts Ring，音译）或麦成兴（Mac on Shing，音译）的男子在场，并未被捕，只是被要求等待。警方指出，此人在未获准离开之前就被要求等待，这属于“被逮捕”状态。主管军官表示，在他们的调查完成之前，不会批准离开。随后警方解释说，如果相关人员未被逮捕，则别无选择，必须确认他未被逮捕。讨论围绕这一点进行了约五分钟，之后主管军官表示，如果问题仅限于他如何来到日本总部的方式，他将允许采访“此人”。

随后岳丁荣被带进房间并接受问话。

问：你是怎么来这里的。
答：我是应两位日本朋友的邀请来的。我没有被捕。
问：谁搜查了你的房间。
答：我自己搜查的。

此后，警方对主管军官表示感谢，并在得到岳丁荣（Yue Ts Ring，音译）即将获释的保证后，于下午12时55分左右离开。

下午2时，岳丁荣（Yue Ts Ring，音译）本人在下午1时45分获释后来到巡捕房，带来了一张伪造的

photograph of a Chinese sub-inspector (antao police)
which the Japanese had taken from his home and returned
to him at his request on release.

Yue Ts Ping was questioned re this affair and his
version has been embodied in a statement attached.

The calling cards and letters mentioned in the
statement are kept by the Japanese.

In addition to the above a Confidential report has
been forwarded to D.C. 'Crime'.

Copy to Special Branch.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Yue Ts Ping ( )
native of Yangchow written by himself.
taken by me translated
at Sinza it'n on the 25-5-38. and interpreted by Clerk Lao Hai Pan.

My name is Yue Ts Ping, age 30 years and a native of
Yangchow. I am living at No. 19 Foh Di Tsung, Avenue Road,
and employed at the Dah Yah Steamship Company, 458 North
Soochow Road.

At 10a.m. 25-5-38, 2 male Chinese and 4 or 5 Japanese in
civilian dress came to my house and enquired about one named
Yue Yoong Shoong. I replied that the name they have mentioned
is my elder brother, who left Shanghai for Hankow about two
weeks ago. They then asked me what did my elder brother take
when he left Shanghai. I replied 2 leather trunks, 1 basket
and beddings. When they saw a photograph in Chapel Police
uniform on the wall, they asked me if it's me. I replied
that is my elder brother Yue Yoong Shoong. They then asked
me why the name registered in the telephone book is Yue Yoong
Shoong. I replied that my elder brother occupied this house
prior to his leaving Shanghai and I took it over after his
departure. They then searched my room but found nothing,
with the exception of a quantity of visiting cards of govern-
ment officials and 2 letters from the same source addressed to
Yue Yoong Shoong, which they found on the 2nd floor. At about
10.30a.m. they instructed me to accompany them to their
(Floating Restaurant)
headquarters/for questioning. I told them I can't go due to
business hours. They then told me that they would ask leave
from the company where I am working for me. They then caught
me on one hand and put me in a motor car, which took us to
the Dah Yah Steamship Company, and after asking leave, the
car was driven straight to the Japanese Military Police Head-
quarters. In there, they asked me the same questions mentioned

以下为岳丁平（Yue Ts Ping，音译），扬州人，由其本人书写。由本人于1938年5月25日在新闸巡捕房录取。由职员劳海潘（Lao Hai Pan，音译）传译。

我叫岳丁平，30岁，扬州人。我住在爱文义路（Avenue Road）佛地总（Foh Di Tsung，音译，可能为弄堂名）19号，受雇于北苏州路458号的大华轮船公司（Dah Yah Steamship Company）。

1938年5月25日上午10时，2名中国男子和4或5名身穿便服的日本人来到我家，询问一个叫余永盛（Yue Yoong Shoong，音译）的人。我回答说，他们提到的名字是我的哥哥，他大约两周前离开上海去了汉口。然后他们问我哥哥离开上海时带走了什么。我回答说有2个皮箱、1个篮子和被褥。当他们看到墙上有一张身穿教堂警察（Chapel Police，原文如此，可能指某种制服或误译）制服的照片时，问是不是我。我回答说那是我的哥哥余永盛。然后他们问为什么电话簿上登记的名字是余永盛。我回答说，在我哥哥离开上海之前，他住在这所房子里，他走后我搬了进来。然后他们搜查了我的房间，但除了在一些政府官员的名片和2封来自同一来源、写给余永盛的信之外，没有发现任何东西，这些是在二楼找到的。上午10时30分左右，他们命令我随他们去他们的（浮动餐厅/总部）接受问话。我告诉他们因为工作时间我不能去。然后他们说他们会替我向我就职的公司请假。然后他们抓住我的一只手，把我塞进一辆汽车，把我们带到大华轮船公司，请好假后，汽车直接开往日本宪兵队总部。在那里，他们再次问我上述

Being satisfied with my replies, they instructed me to leave at about 12.30 p.m., but when I had walked a few steps, I was told to stop again, stating that my wives had reported the matter to the police and detectives had arrived to make enquiries. After 5 or 6 minutes, they instructed me to meet the detectives, but on condition that I should tell the detectives that I went there on my own free will, that the Japanese who visited my house are my friends and that I myself disturbed the property in my room. Consequently I told the detectives as instructed when questioned. When the detectives had left, they instructed me to wait for a while. During which, they instructed me to report to them should I receive any letters from my elder brother Yue Toong Chang, or any information regarding Anti-Japanese or other political activities. At about 1.45 p.m. they sent me in their car to the Dah Wah Steamship Company. I reported to Police at 2 p.m.
The conversation between the Japanese and myself was interpreted by Chinese.

The attached further statement was taken from Wong Koh Hwa (王國華), in substantiation of his verbal statement regarding the meeting which took place during April 1938, in Room No. 201 The "Grand" Hotel, between Ma Chien Ming (馬建明), (in custody) Zung Yung Ziang (鄭永祥) and himself. This meeting is described in the previous diary forwarded in connection with this case.

Perusal of this statement, tends to strengthen the suspicion that Zung, caused the arrest of these persons in order to facilitate a taking over of the control of the "Shanghai Native Boat Owners Assn.".

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of WONG KOH HWA ( / ), 39, Married, residing
House 68, Zung An Li, Rue Porte de L'Ouest, F/Q,
native of Tuichow, Kiangsu, taken by me C.D.Sel3,
at H.C.B. on the 4/6/38 and translated interpreted by Yao Dinsin.

Before the hostilities, I was proprietor of the Koh Hwa
Weaving Factory at House 6-10 Hwa Hsing Faung, Sun Yang Road,
Chapel.

During January, 1938, through the introduction of Mr. Sung
Chuen Nyi, a friend of mine, I became acquainted with Ma Chien
Ming, alias Ma Zoong Ziang.

On the 15/4/38 I was approached by Ma Chien Ming, who
asked me to print for him one thousand flags bearing a number
as well as the characters, "Sing Zuen Loong Wei" (The Native Boats
Guild). I consented, and since that date till about the beginning
of May, I had been printing those flags at Ma's house. It was
agreed between Ma and myself that on the completion of those
flags, I would receive $340.00. I actually received from Ma the
sum of $200.00, but the balance ($140.00) is still outstanding to
this date.

As far as I know, Ma Chien Ming was formerly Chairman of
the Shanghai Native Boat Owners Friendship Association. Not long
ago, he had spent two months in making arrangements with the
Japanese Boat Administration Section for permission to allow him
alone to be the sole contractor of the Native Boats Guild. His
plans materialized on the 1st. of May, 1938, when official recog-
nition by the Japanese came into effect. Ma then established his
his offices at OO Tsung Jiao, O.O.L. There is also an enquiry
office on South Soochow Road, near the Chekiang Road Bridge, where
all native boat owners register. Those failing to register were
not allowed to pass in the Creek. All native boats loaded with
merchandise heading for Shanghai were to be berthed at Go Tsung

警方调查报告。

以下是王国华（WONG KOH HWA）（ / ），39岁，已婚，居住在法租界西敏路（Rue Porte de L'Ouest）宗安里68号，江苏泰州籍人的陈述，由我 C.D.Sel3 于1938年6月4日在中央捕房（H.C.B.）采集，并由姚丁新（Yao Dinsin，音译）翻译解释。

战事爆发前，我是位于闸北太阳庙路（Sun Yang Road，音译）华兴坊6-10号的国华织布厂的业主。

1938年1月期间，通过我的朋友宋春义（Sung Chuen Nyi，音译）的介绍，我结识了马建明，别名马仲祥（Ma Zoong Ziang，音译）。

1938年4月15日，马建明找我，要求我为他印制一千面旗帜，上面印有号码以及“辛全龙威”（Sing Zuen Loong Wei，音译，意为本帮船业公会）字样。我同意了，从那天起直到5月初，我一直在马家印制这些旗帜。马和我约定，旗帜印完后，我将收到340.00美元。我实际上从马那里收到了200.00美元，但余款（140.00美元）至今仍未支付。

据我所知，马建明曾任上海本帮船主友谊协会主席。不久前，他花了两个月时间与日本船舶管理部门安排，以获得许可，让他单独成为本帮船业公会的唯一承包商。他的计划于1938年5月1日实现，当时日本的官方认可生效。马随后在 OO Tsung Jiao（音译，可能指戈宗角或类似地名），O.O.L. 设立了办事处。在南苏州路靠近浙江路桥的地方也设有一个问询处，所有本帮船主都在那里登记。未登记者不允许通过浜（河道）。所有装载货物驶往上海的本帮船只都要停靠在 Go Tsung

Jiao, wherefrom the goods had to be unloaded and transported

They have certain regulations governing this matter, and those

Ma Chien Ling used to boast about his success. It was
known to be a very lucrative job, admired by all. Only recently
he had made arrangements to buy a car.

Prior to the official inauguration of that office, Ma
used to engage Room 201, Grand Hotel. I often visited that room
to play mahjong etc. I did so thinking that my frequent presence
there would improve the relation between Ma and myself.

On or about the 10th. April, 1938, Zung Vung Ziang came
to Room 01, and informed us of his intention to be the sole
contractor of the Native Boat Owners Guild, asking Ma Chien Ling
to do what he could to assist him. To his surprise, Ma told
him that no one else, but Ma himself, had been appointed for
that job. Zung left, after his efforts to lure Ma away from the
job, proved abortive.

马建明（Ma Chien Ling，原文拼写不一致，应指马建明）常吹嘘他的成功。众所周知，这是一份非常有利可图的工作，令人羡慕。就在最近，他还安排购买了一辆汽车。

在该办事处正式成立之前，马常租用大华饭店（Grand Hotel）201室。我经常去那个房间打麻将等。我这样做是认为，我频繁出现在那里可以改善我和马之间的关系。

1938年4月10日左右，郑永祥（Zung Vung Ziang，原文拼写不一致，应指郑永祥 Zung Yung Ziang）来到01室（应为201室之误），通知我们他打算成为本帮船主公会的唯一承包商，并请马建明尽力协助他。令他惊讶的是，马告诉他，除了马自己之外，没有其他人被任命担任该职务。郑在试图诱使马放弃该工作的努力失败后离开。

签名并画十字标记：-
王国华（WONG KOH HWA）。

Date June 7th. 19 38.
Subject Re: Illegal arrests made by the Japanese Military Police.

Made by E. J. Glover Forwarded by S.D.I. Prince.

Sir,

The attached translation of a statement, purporting to
have been made by the 101st. accused Sung Tsong Yoh, handed
over to the Japanese Gendarmerie on the 11th. Feb. 1938,
was passed to the unit signed by D.I. Uemoto.

In this statement, Sung Tsong Yoh, who is believed to
have been subsequently tried by a Military Court, and execut-
ed, admits that he was a member of a Chinese Mobile Unit,
under the command of General Yuin Chien Tung. (俞劍東).
Among the persons mentioned, as being members of this unit,
appears that of one of the recently arrested men, one Koh
Hwa (王國華). He, however, does not mention to what extent
this man is connected with the activities of this particular
corps.

Perusal of the statements made by the twelve men, who
were later handed over to the Japanese Military Authorities
has failed to reveal the name of the man, one Koh Hwa, now
in custody.

From further enquiries made it is suspected that the
arrest of the six persons now in custody was brought about
through the machinations of one named Sung Veng Ziang
(宋文祥).

The reasons for this, are as follows. One of the
arrested men, named Ma Chien Ming (馬建明) is the present
Chairman of the "Native Boat Owners Assn.". This association
which is controlled by the "Dah Dao" Govt. applies to the
Japanese authorities on behalf of all boat owners, for passes
to enable native craft to operate in Japanese controlled
areas. Wong Koh Hwa has the monopoly on the sale of flags,

事由：关于日本宪兵队实施的非法逮捕。

由 E. J. Glover 撰写，由 S.D.I. Prince 呈送。

先生：

附件中据称由第101号被告宋宗耀（Sung Tsong Yoh，音译）所作陈述的译文，该被告于1938年2月11日移交给日本宪兵队，已转交给由上本（Uemoto，音译）侦探长签署的单位。

在此陈述中，宋宗耀据信随后被军事法庭审判并处决，承认他是俞剑东（Yuin Chien Tung）将军指挥下的中国机动部队成员。在被提及为该部队成员的人员中，出现了最近被捕人员之一王国华（Koh Hwa）的名字。然而，他并未提及此人与该特定部队活动的关联程度。

查阅后来移交给日本军方的十二名男子的陈述，未能发现目前在押的王国华的名字。

经进一步查询，怀疑目前被拘留的六人的被捕是由一名叫宋文祥（Sung Veng Ziang）的人策划所致。

原因如下。被捕者之一马建明（Ma Chien Ming）是现任“本帮船主协会”主席。该协会由“大道政府”（Dah Dao Govt.，即维新政府）控制，代表所有船主向日本当局申请通行证，以便本帮船只在日本控制区运营。王国华垄断了由他印制并以利润出售给注册外籍人士的旗帜销售，

（批注：desb.）
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特科 1938年6月9日）

which are printed by him, and sold at a profit to registered

Ma Chien Ming, and Jong Koh Hwa, are therefore able to
obtain considerable financial benefits from their respective
connections with the "Native Boat Owners Assn.".

Sometime during April 1938, Jung Yung Tiang, called on
Ma Chien Ming, and Jong Koh Hwa, whilst these two men were
occupying Room No. 201, at the "Grand Hotel. He proposed
that he should be allowed to supersede Ma Chien Ming, in
obtaining passes from the Japanese Authorities. Ma Chien
Ming immediately refused to listen to this proposition, and
Jung left the room. This rebuff, coupled with the ill feeling
existing between Jung and Jong Koh Hwa, appears to have mo-
tivated the former into betraying these men to the Japanese
authorities.

He apparently was also under the impression that once
these men had been arrested it would be a comparatively easy
task for him to take over the positions held by them.

The remaining statement, has now been completed, and is
attached hereto. This statement was made by Tien Ching Dong
(田庆东) now in custody, and gives details of the events
following his arrest. He does not appear to have been very
badly treated, apart from having had his face and hands
slapped.

The Japanese authorities, according to D.S.I. Umemoto,
are desirous that the man Jong Koh Hwa be handed over to
them for trial on a charge of being a member of a "Chinese
Mobile Unit". They do not appear to be very much concerned
regarding the other five persons.

That, the arrested persons, are dubious characters,

1938年4月的某个时候，郑永祥（Jung Yung Tiang，原文拼写不一致，应指郑永祥）在大华饭店201室拜访了正在那里的马建明和王国华。他提议允许他取代马建明，从日本当局获取通行证。马建明立即拒绝听取这一提议，郑离开了房间。这次碰壁，加上郑与王国华之间存在的嫌隙，似乎促使前者向日本当局出卖了这些人。

其余的陈述现已完成，并附于此。该陈述由目前在押的田庆东（Tien Ching Dong）所作，详细叙述了他被捕后的事件。除了脸和手被打耳光外，他似乎并未受到很糟糕的对待。

"SECRET" REPORT Date May 28, 1938
Subject RE: ILLEGAL ARRESTS ETC. BY THE JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.
Made by D.I. Glover Forwarded by C.D.I. Prince

Sir,

Acting on instructions received, the undersigned
during the morning of the 28th May, 1938, escorted Wong Koh
Han (王國華) and Dung Ah Ching (唐阿金), both of whom
complained of suffering from the effects of torture to which
they were submitted by the Japanese Military Police, to the
Police Hospital, Shanhaikwan Road, where they were examined by
Doctor E. Vic.

The certificates obtained as the result of this
examination read as follows :-

MAY 28TH, 1938.

WONG KOH HAN - MALE - AGE 39 - NATIVE OF KIANGSU.

THERE ARE SEVERAL ECCHYMOTIC PATCHES IN THE
BACK, LEFT SHOULDER AREA, ON BOTH ARMS
AND THIGHS.
SOME OF THESE ARE LINEAR IN SHAPE, WHICH
INDICATES THAT THEY ARE DUE TO BEATING WITH
A STICK. ON THE OUTER ASPECT OF THE LEFT
LEG, THERE ARE TWO SMALL ROUND SKIN DEFECTS
OF THE SIZE OF A PEA, SURROUNDED BY A CRUST,
AND SURROUNDED BY A HYPERAEMIC HALO, THE ORIGIN
OF WHICH CANNOT BE DETERMINED AT EXAMINATION.
IT IS QUITE POSSIBLE THAT THEY ARE DUE TO
CIGARETTE BURNS.

CONCLUSION: THERE IS EVIDENCE THAT THE PATIENT HAS
BEEN BEATEN RATHER SEVERELY WITH A
STICK OR A SIMILAR OBJECT.

Signed : E. VIO.

"TONG AH KING - (Romanised as Daung Ah Ching in
previous reports).
AGE - 47 YEARS - NATIVE OF SOOCHOW.

THERE IS NO EVIDENCE THAT THIS MAN HAS BEEN
ILL TREATED. THERE ARE NO LESIONS IN HIS
NOSE AND THE EXAMINATION OF HIS LUNGS DOES
NOT REVEAL ANY PATHOLOGICAL INJURY.

IT IS POSSIBLE, HOWEVER, THAT WATER WAS POURED
INTO HIS NOSE, AS THIS FORM OF TORTURE DOES
NOT NECESSARILY LEAVE SIGNS BY WHICH IT COULD
BE RECOGNIZED EXTERNALLY.

Signed : E. VIO

    By arrangements made with D.S.I. Dickson, i/c of the
Finger Print Bureau, Wong Koh Hwa's injuries were photographed
as additional proof of his allegations.
    The statements taken from the six arrested persons
have now been completed. Of these, three made by Ma Chien Ming
(馬濟民), Tung Ching Tsang (陳錦昌) and Tien Ching Tong
(錢京堂) are useless, these men denying all knowledge of the
case and further stating that they were not subjected to any
form of torture.
    The other three, Wong Koh Hwa, Tsung Ah Ching and
Hyien Kwei Sung (嚴桂沈), however, appear to have suffered
more drastic treatment. Wong Koh Hwa particularly appears to
have been the person, whom the Japanese Military Police were
most anxious to arrest. They are all most emphatic in their
denials of all knowledge of the two men, Kung and Tung Kwei An
(陳冠人) whom the female Hyien Kwei Sung is alleged to have
confessed, were members of a mobile unit.
    Whether or not Wong Koh Hwa was connected with the
mobile unit to which Ma Joh Ming (馬樂鳴) was attached, is not
known, but it has been definitely established that both he and
his paramour were formerly acquainted with this man.
    The suspicion that a disreputable person named Zung
Voong Ziang (曾文祥) was responsible for their present plight
is quite feasible, as both Wong Koh Hwa and his paramour admit
that they on several occasions have been at variance with this
man, and it is possible that he took this opportunity of revenging
himself upon them.
    The suspicion that Wong Koh Hwa and the other arrested
persons was betrayed by Zung Voong Ziang is strengthened when it

    经与指纹局局长迪克森（Dickson）副督察安排，对王国华（Wong Koh Hwa）的伤情进行了拍照，作为其指控的额外证据。
    六名被捕人员的供词现已录毕。其中，马济民（Ma Chien Ming）、陈锦昌（Tung Ching Tsang）和钱京堂（Tien Ching Tong）三人的供词毫无用处，这些人否认对该案有任何了解，并进一步声称未遭受任何形式的酷刑。
    然而，另外三人，即王国华（Wong Koh Hwa）、唐阿清（Tsung Ah Ching）和严桂沈（Hyien Kwei Sung），似乎遭受了更为严厉的对待。特别是王国华，似乎是日本宪兵最急于逮捕的人。他们都极力否认认识龚某和陈冠人（Kung and Tung Kwei An）这两人，据女犯严桂沈供述，此二人是流动部队的成员。
    王国华是否与马乐鸣（Ma Joh Ming）所属的流动部队有关联，目前尚不清楚，但已确切证实，他和他的情妇以前都认识这个人。
    怀疑一个名叫曾文祥（Zung Voong Ziang）的不法分子应对他们目前的困境负责，这是完全可能的，因为王国华和他的情妇都承认曾多次与此人发生争执，他有可能借此机会向他们报复。
    当人们想起在他们被捕当晚，曾文祥曾答应去看望王国华却并未履约，尽管他就住在同一家酒店的317房间，而被捕人员则住在623房间时，对于王国华及其他被捕人员是被曾文祥出卖的怀疑便更加增强了。

although he was staying in Room 317 of the same hotel, whilst
the arrested persons occupied Room 623.

Another significant factor is that a sworn
brother of Zung Voong Ziang, one named Tseu Shi Ping (周希斌),
an employee of the Insurance Department of Messrs. Wing On & Co.
was together with Wong and the other arrested persons between
8 and 11 p.m. on the day of their arrest. On being escorted out
of the room by the Japanese, the woman prisoner, Nyien Kwei Sung,
noticed that Tseu Shi Ping was loitering in the corridor.

Tseu Shi Ping, according to Wong Koh Hwa, was
formerly attached to the Intelligence Service of the Chinese Army.

Taking advantage of his position, he started a
transportation company which removed property from the Western
District prior to the advance of the Japanese Troops.

On one occasion, whilst engaged in removing
property, he was arrested by some Chinese troops, but was later
released. On the retreat of the Chinese Forces, he together with
Zung Voong Ziang, became associated with the various pro-Japanese
societies. Zung Voorg Ziang, who is also known to Wong under the
alias of Zung Zoong (鄭重), is at present connected with the
"Shing Yah" (新亞), Koh Hwa (閩華), Wong Dao (王道) Societies
and the "Seaman's Union" (海員工會).

No further applications have been received from
the Japanese Military Police regarding their request for
assistance in order to effect the arrest of the two alleged
members of mobile units, who are now supposed to be residing in
the French Concession.

另一个重要因素是，曾文祥的一位结拜兄弟，名叫周希斌（Tseu Shi Ping），是永安公司保险部的职员，在被捕当天晚上8点至11点期间，他曾与王国华及其他被捕人员在一起。当日本人将囚犯带出房间时，女囚严桂沈（Nyien Kwei Sung）注意到周希斌正在走廊里徘徊。

据王国华称，周希斌以前隶属于中国军队的情报部门。

他利用自己的职位，开办了一家运输公司，在日军推进之前从西区搬运财产。

有一次，他在搬运财产时被一些中国军队逮捕，但后来获释。在中国军队撤退时，他与曾文祥一起，与各种亲日社团建立了联系。曾文祥（Zung Voorg Ziang），王国华也知道他的化名是郑重（Zung Zoong），目前与“新亚”（Shing Yah）、“闽华”（Koh Hwa）、“王道”（Wong Dao）会社以及“海员工会”（Seaman's Union）有联系。

日本宪兵方面没有再收到关于请求协助逮捕两名据称居住在法租界的流动部队成员的后续申请。

at H.Q.C.B. on the 27-5-38 and interpreted by D.O.I. Soong Ping Tsung

At about 12 midnight on the 24-5-38 whilst I was
playing mah-jong with Ma Shien Sing, Chen John, Dong and Lung
Ching Tsong in Room 623 of the Sun Sun Hotel, six armed
Japanese, two of whom were dressed in Chinese clothes and four
in foreign clothes, burst into the room where they conducted
a thorough search. One of the Japanese, dressed in foreign
clothes, asked me to reveal my name, to which I replied that
I was called Sung Jung. Refusing to believe the name which I
had told him, he slapped my face several times. Two of them
then left the room and returned a few minutes later in company
of another Japanese, who, directly entering the room, stared
at me for some time and commenced to chat with the other
Japanese. One of the Japanese who first came into the room
took out my silk long gown from the wardrobe and asked me
whether it was my clothing. After telling him that it was my
gown, I was ordered to put it on immediately. He then hand-
cuffed my left hand and bound my right hand with a piece of
rope. All four mah-jong players, including myself, were taken
to the Japanese Military Headquarters together with a tailor
and my paramour Hyien Kwei Sung, who were also in the room
during that time. The Japanese subjected us to various forms
of torture throughout their questioning. On the morning of
25-5-38 we were escorted to the offices of Japanese Branch
on the 2nd floor of Central Station, S.M.P., where I saw three
Japanese, one of whom I recognised as the last person who
entered Room 623, Sun Sun Hotel, and kept on staring at me
on the night of my arrest. We were later taken to H.Q.C.B.(C.1)

以下是由我，格洛弗（Glover）督察，于1938年5月27日在中央捕房总部对籍贯为___的W.J.G. 桂贤（Gwei Hsien）（____）进行的进一步陈述记录，由宋秉宗（Soong Ping Tsung）口译员翻译。

1938年5月24日午夜12点左右，当我在新新旅馆623房间与马先星（Ma Shien Sing）、陈约翰（Chen John）、董某（Dong）和龙庆宗（Lung Ching Tsong）打麻将时，六名武装日本人闯入房间，其中两人身穿中式服装，四人身穿西式服装，并对房间进行了彻底搜查。一名身穿西式服装的日本人要求我报出姓名，我回答说我叫宋荣（Sung Jung）。他不相信我告诉他的名字，扇了我几个耳光。随后其中两人离开房间，几分钟后带着另一名日本人回来，这名日本人直接进入房间，盯着我看了一会儿，并开始与其他日本人交谈。最先闯入房间的日本人之一从衣柜里拿出我的丝绸长袍，问我这是否是我的衣服。在我告诉他这是我的长袍后，我被命令立即穿上。然后他给我的左手戴上手铐，并用一根绳子绑住我的右手。包括我在内的四名麻将玩家，以及当时也在房间里的裁缝和我的情妇严桂沈（Hyien Kwei Sung），都被带到日本军事总部。日本人在审讯过程中对我们施加了各种形式的酷刑。1938年5月25日上午，我们被护送到工部局警务处中央捕房二楼的日本分部办公室，在那里我看到了三名日本人，其中一人我认出就是在我被捕当晚进入新新旅馆623房间并一直盯着我看的那个人。后来我们被带到中央捕房总部（C.1）

The following is the statement of MA TSI MING (馬子明)
native of Zaushing taken by me D.S.I. Maklaevsky
at C.I.C.B.H.Q. on the May 25th. 1938 and interpreted by D.S.I. Goong Ping Tsung.

My name is Ma Tsi Ming. I am native of Zaushing, aged 38 years, married. I am co-owner of the Chang Chi (翔記) Native Boat Company at 7 Yung San Li off Amoy Road where I also reside with my family, consisting of nine members. I have been residing in the Settlement for the last 35 years, having been brought here by my parents from Zaushing when I was 3 years of age.

On or about May 18th. 1938 I opened Room No. 623 at the Sun Sun Hotel, Kweichow Road, in order to negotiate business matters with two Municipal Mud Contractors, named Wong (翁) and Liu (廖). These contractors approached me with the object of hiring some native boats from my company for transportation of mud from Zaushing to Shanghai. They wanted to hire 30 native boats in all, but I could only provide 5 boats which they eventually hired from me.

On May 23rd. 1938, both contractors went to Zaushing in order to hire the other 25 boats and were expected to be back in Shanghai within next week. While they were away I was still retaining the room at the Hotel awaiting their return as further negotiations re. the boats should have been carried out.

On May 24th. 1938 I decided to have a Mahjong game at the room and I, therefore, invited three of my friends, namely,
Wong Kau Whe (王周華).
Zeng Ching Tsong (陳金昌).
Zeh Ching Dong (鄭慶東).

We started to play Mahjong at about 9 p.m. and continued

以下是由我，马克拉耶夫斯基（Maklaevsky）副督察，于1938年5月25日在中央情报捕房总部对籍贯为乍浦的马子明（MA TSI MING）进行的陈述记录，由宋秉宗（Goong Ping Tsung）副督察翻译。

我叫马子明。我是乍浦人，38岁，已婚。我是厦门路永山里7号翔记（Chang Chi）土驳船公司的共同所有人，我也与家人（共九口人）居住在那里。我在租界已居住35年，3岁时由父母从乍浦带到这里。

1938年5月18日左右，我在贵州路新新旅馆开了623号房间，以便与两名市政淤泥承包商，姓翁（Wong）和姓廖（Liu）的，洽谈业务事宜。这些承包商找我是为了从我公司租用一些土驳船，将淤泥从乍浦运到上海。他们想总共租用30艘土驳船，但我只能提供5艘，他们最终从我这里租用了这5艘。

1938年5月23日，两名承包商前往乍浦租用其余25艘船，预计下周内返回上海。在他们离开期间，我仍保留着旅馆房间，等待他们回来，因为关于船只的进一步谈判还需进行。

1938年5月24日，我决定在房间里打麻将，因此邀请了我的三位朋友，即：
王周华（Wong Kau Whe）。
陈金昌（Zeng Ching Tsong）。
郑庆东（Zeh Ching Dong）。

我们大约在晚上9点开始打麻将，并继续

the game until early hour of May 25th, when a number of
Japanese soldiers in plain clothes rushed into the room and
had us all arrested. Besides the above mentioned three friends
there were four females and one tailor by the name of Dong Ah
Ching (唐阿庆) in the room. We were all searched and then
Japanese soldiers conveyed us in to motor cars to the Head-
quarters of the Japanese Military Police on the corner of
North Szechuen Road and Tsunning Road. The tailor Dong Ah
Ching and one female named Yang Kau Tseng (杨桂贞) were also
taken together with us, whilst the three other females were
released at the Hotel.
When we were brought to the Headquarters, one of the
Japanese, who spoke Chinese, questioned me as to whether Wong
Kau Wha was a member of a Mobile Unit to which I replied in
the negative. The Japanese then became very angered and
slapped my face several times.
No more questions were put to me by the Japanese, who
even did not question me whether I or any of the arrested
persons were in Mobile Units or terroristic organizations.
I was then locked up in a cell and was kept there until
10 a.m. when I, together with 5 arrested persons, was brought
to Headquarters, S.M.P. During my detention at the Headquarters
of the Japanese Military Police I did not see whether any other
person of our party was tortured by the Japanese. I was also
not present during interrogation of the other arrested persons.
I can not say whether at the time of our arrest at the Sun Sun
Hotel, there was any Japanese detectives of the S.M.P. amongst

牌局直至5月25日凌晨，当时多名身着便服的日本士兵冲入房间，将我们全部逮捕。除上述三位朋友外，房间内还有四名女性以及一名名叫唐阿庆 (Dong Ah Ching) 的裁缝。我们均遭到搜身，随后日本士兵将我们押上汽车，送往位于四川北路与天潼路转角处的日本宪兵队总部。裁缝唐阿庆和一名名叫杨桂贞 (Yang Kau Tseng) 的女性也随我们一同被带走，而另外三名女性则在酒店被释放。
当我们被带到总部时，一名会说中文的日本人审问我，问黄国华 (Wong Kau Wha) 是否是某流动小组的成员，我予以否认。该日本人随即勃然大怒，多次扇我的耳光。
日本人没有再向我提问，甚至没有审问我或任何被捕人员是否属于流动小组或恐怖组织。
随后我被关进牢房，一直关押至上午10点，当时我与另外5名被捕者一起被带到工部局警务处总部。在日本宪兵队总部拘留期间，我没有看到同伙中的其他人遭受日本人酷刑。在其他被捕人员受审时，我也不在场。
我无法说明在孙孙酒店 (Sun Sun Hotel) 逮捕我们时，工部局警务处的日本侦探是否也在场

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of LUNG CHING TSONG (盧清松)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.J.I. Konovaloff
at H. M. C. B. on the 26-5-38 and interpreted by S.I. Chiu Shou Ling

My name is Lung Ching Tsong. I am a native of
Shanghai, 53 years of age, residing at 45 Rue Galle, French
Concession.

I have to state that I am a good friend of Lu Chien
Ming (盧建明) (2nd arrested) and Lien Ching Dong (連清東)
(both arrested), whom I have known for the past 10 years. In
the afternoon at about 5 p.m. on the 24-5-38 I received a
telephone message from Lu Chien Ming requesting me to attend
a mah-jong party at Room 623 of the Sun Sun Hotel, Kweichow
Road. I agreed to and promised to be there sometime later.
At the time I received this telephone message I was in my
medicine shop at 275 Honan Road. After visiting my friend I
went to the room 623, Sun Sun Hotel, where I arrived at 9 p.m.
same date. On entering the room I saw the two above mentioned
friends sitting in the room talking with one unknown to me,
who was later introduced to me by the name of Wong (王)
(1st arrested). This new acquaintance, Wong, I had never met
before. Besides these already mentioned persons, four female
Chinese, including the 6th arrested person, were present in
the room. Soon after my arrival we commenced to play a game
of mah-jong and we were playing up to midnight. When we were
about to finish this game a party of 7 or 8 Japanese in
plain-clothes (some of them wearing Chinese dress) entered
the room. On entering, one of the party immediately started
to question the 1st arrested Wong Kwoh Hwa (王國華), enquiring
if his name was Wong. The 1st arrested in reply said that
his name was Wong Yung. The man who questioned Wong Kwoh Hwa

以下为本人 D.J.I. Konovaloff 于1938年5月26日在 H. M. C. B. 对籍贯为上海的卢清松 (LUNG CHING TSONG) 所作的笔录，由 S.I. Chiu Shou Ling 翻译

我叫卢清松。我是上海人，现年53岁，居住在法租界加利街 (Rue Galle) 45号。

我必须声明，我是卢建明 (Lu Chien Ming)（第二名被捕者）和连清东 (Lien Ching Dong)（两人均被捕）的好友，我认识他们已有10年。1938年5月24日下午约5点，我接到卢建明的电话留言，请我去贵州路孙孙酒店623房间参加麻将聚会。我同意了，并答应稍后到达。
收到此电话留言时，我正在河南路275号的药店里。拜访朋友后，我前往孙孙酒店623房间，于同日晚上9点到达。进入房间后，我看到上述两位朋友坐在房间里，与一名我不认识的人交谈，此人后来被介绍给我，姓王 (Wong)（第一名被捕者）。这位新结识的王先生，我以前从未见过。除了上述提到的人之外，房间内还有四名中国女性，包括第六名被捕者。我不久到达后，我们开始打麻将，一直打到午夜。当我们快要结束这局牌时，一群七八名身着便服（其中一些人穿着中式服装）的日本人进入房间。进入后，其中一人立即开始审问第一名被捕者王国华 (Wong Kwoh Hwa)，询问他的名字是否是王。第一名被捕者回答说他的名字叫王勇 (Wong Yung)。那名审问王国华的人

after looking through his pocket book, he left the room and

在翻阅了他的钱包后，离开了房间，大约5分钟后返回。在此期间，该团伙的其他成员搜查了房间。搜查房间后，另外三名女性被允许离开，而包括我在内的其余6人被带上两辆摩托车，送往位于四川路桥附近的一栋新高层建筑。随后，两名身着便服的日本人单独将我带到一个独立的房间，审问我是否知道第一名被捕者的名字。我回答说我知道他姓王，并且我是在被捕前不久才与他相识的。审问结束后，他们将我与第二名被捕者马建明 (Ma Chien Ming) 和第五名被捕者田清东 (Tien Ching Dong) 一起护送到一个有木栅栏将走廊隔开的房间。1938年5月25日上午10点左右，我与另外五名被捕者一起从这个房间被移出，并被护送到中央捕房刑事调查处 (H.Q. Translation of statement taken from **〔此处转录不清〕** (唐万金)
by Japanese Military Police on May 28, 19**.
----------------------------------------

My name is Tung Ah Kuan, age 47, native of Soochow,
tailor by occupation, residing on 1st floor, No. 57
Rue Porte de l'Ouest. Wong Kwoh Hwa lives on the 2nd
floor in the same house. Wong moved into this house
about 10 days ago. I became acquainted with Wong after
the outbreak of the hostilities in Shanghai in August
last year. Ma Loh Hin and Wong told me that they were
members of a mobile unit. Ma disappeared after the arrest
of a gang of terrorists by the Municipal Police and I
have never met him since. Wong Kwoh Hwa lived in Room
31 Cha Loh Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, for about 20 days
prior to moving into the present address.

19**年5月28日由日本宪兵队从 **〔此处转录不清〕** (唐万金) 处获取的陈述译文。
---

我叫唐阿宽 (Tung Ah Kuan)，47岁，苏州人，职业为裁缝，居住在西门路 (Rue Porte de l'Ouest) 57号一楼。王国华 (Wong Kwoh Hwa) 住在同一栋房子的二楼。王大约10天前搬进这所房子。在去年8月上海战事爆发后，我认识了王。马洛兴 (Ma Loh Hin) 和王告诉我，他们是流动小组的成员。在马洛兴因工部局警务处逮捕一伙恐怖分子后失踪，此后我再未见过他。王国华在搬到目前的地址之前，曾在虞洽卿路 (Yu Ya Ching Road) 的查洛酒店 (Cha Loh Hotel) 31号房间住了约20天。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Dong Ah Ching (唐阿慶).
native of Soochow taken by me D.S.I. Maklaevsky
at C.I.H.Q.C.B. on the May 25th.1938 and interpreted by D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsang

My name is Dong Ah Ching. I am native of Soochow, aged
47 years, married, tailor, residing at 67 Tseng An Lee off
Rue Port de L'Ouest.

At about 3 p.m. on May 23rd 1938 I met Ma Tsi Ming
(馬濟民) on Nanking Road. I asked him whether he wished
a new summer suit to be made and he said "yes" and asked
me to come and see him at Room No. 623 the Sun Sun Hotel.

At about 6 p.m. on the same date I went to the Sun Sun
Hotel where I saw Ma Tsi Ming. Besides Ma Tsi Ming there
were his wife, Wong Kau Cha (王周華) and his paramour Yang
Kau Tseng (楊桂貞) at the room. No order for any clothing
was given to me and I walked away.

At about 5 p.m. on May 24th. I went again to Ma Tsi
Ming's room at the Sun Sun Hotel with the object of receiving
an order from him. When I entered room Ma Tsi Ming, his
wife, Wong Kau Cha and his paramour Yang Kau Tseng were
having dinner. Shortly afterwards two men, namely:-
Tseng Ching Tsang (曾金昌) and Cheng Ching Dang (鄭京唐)
(both arrested) and two unknown females also entered the
room. When Ma Tsi Ming and his party partook of dinner, four
male members of the company started to play "Mahjong", while
I was standing by the side of the table watching the game.

At about midnight, 7 or 8 Japanese in civilian clothes
rushed into the room with drawn pistols. Ordering us to
stand up, they searched each of us, as well as the room.
Upon completion of the search, the Japanese took us (5 male
and one female) down and put us in two motor cars.

以下为本人 D.S.I. Maklaevsky 于1938年5月25日在中央捕房刑事调查处总部 (C.I.H.Q.C.B.) 对籍贯为苏州的唐阿庆 (Dong Ah Ching) 所作的笔录，由 D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsang 翻译

我叫唐阿庆。我是苏州人，现年47岁，已婚，裁缝，居住在西门路 (Rue Port de L'Ouest) 旁的增安里 (Tseng An Lee) 67号。

1938年5月23日下午3点左右，我在南京路上遇到了马济民 (Ma Tsi Ming)。我问他是否想做一套新的夏装，他说“是”，并让我去孙孙酒店623房间见他。

同日傍晚6点左右，我去了孙孙酒店，在那里见到了马济民。除了马济民外，房间里还有他的妻子、王周华 (Wong Kau Cha) 和他的情妇杨桂贞 (Yang Kau Tseng)。我没有接到任何服装订单，便离开了。

5月24日下午5点左右，我再次前往孙孙酒店马济民的房间，目的是从他那里接收订单。当我进入房间时，马济民、他的妻子王周华和他的情妇杨桂贞正在吃晚饭。不久之后，又有两名男子，即：
曾金昌 (Tseng Ching Tsang) 和郑京唐 (Cheng Ching Dang)
（两人均被捕）以及两名不明身份的女性也进入了房间。当马济民及其同伴用餐时，同行的四名男性成员开始打“麻将”，而我则站在桌边观看牌局。

午夜左右，七八名身着便服的日本人持枪冲入房间。他们命令我们站起来，搜查了我们每个人以及房间。搜查完毕后，日本人将我们（5名男性和1名女性）带下楼，并让我们坐上两辆汽车。

The following is the statement of ____ taken by me ____
native of ____ at ____ on the ____ and interpreted by ____

I arrived at the Headquarters of the Japanese Military
Police, on North Szechuen Road. When I entered the Head-
quarters, Mr Yau he and his paramour Yang Kau Tseng were
separated from us and taken to a small room for questioning.
After about half an hour, they were brought back and I was
taken into the same room. Two Japanese started to inter-
rogate me asking firstly whether I knew a person by the
name of a Loh Ying (羅英) to which I answered in the
negative. Both Japanese then started to slap my face calling
me a liar. Then two other Japanese entered bringing with them
a kettle. I was then placed on a bench, one Japanese holding
me by my legs and the other one by my arms. Water was then
poured from the kettle into my nostrils. I was tortured by
this method for about half an hour during which period the
Japanese persistently questioned me re. Mr Loh Ming and
eventually extorted my confession. I admitted that I knew
Mr Loh Ming whom I first met in May of the last year at
Room No. 307 at the Astor House Hotel. I was introduced to Mr
Loh Ming by my client a lawyer, Mr. Sing Yung Soo (盛榮蘇) who
recommended me to him. During this visit I saw first time
Ong Kau Ah (now in custody) at Mr Loh Ming's room. I received
orders for clothes from Mr Loh Ming and his wife and in all
I visited him 4 times during month of May. I have never
seen him or his wife since. The Japanese then asked me whether
I knew Mr Loh Ming's present domicile to which I replied in
the negative. They then asked me whether I knew of Jong Kau
Ah being a member of Mobile Unit to which I also replied in

我到达了位于四川北路的日本宪兵队总部。当我进入总部时，姚先生 (Mr Yau he) 和他的情妇杨桂贞与我们分开，被带到一个小的房间进行审问。大约半小时后，他们被带回来，我也被带入同一个房间。两名日本人开始审问我，首先问我是否认识一个叫罗英 (Loh Ying) 的人，我予以否认。这两名日本人随即开始扇我的耳光，骂我是骗子。随后又有两名日本人进来，带来一个水壶。接着我被按在长凳上，一名日本人抓住我的腿，另一名抓住我的手臂。然后他们将水壶里的水灌入我的鼻孔。我用这种方法遭受了约半小时的酷刑，在此期间，日本人不断就罗明 (Loh Ming) 先生一事审问我，并最终逼取了我的供词。我承认我认识罗明先生，我是去年5月在礼查饭店 (Astor House Hotel) 307号房间第一次见到他的。我是通过我的客户、律师盛荣苏 (Sing Yung Soo) 先生介绍认识罗明先生的，是他把我推荐给了罗明。在这次拜访中，我在罗明先生的房间里第一次见到了翁嘉阿 (Ong Kau Ah)（目前在押）。我从罗明先生及其妻子那里接到了服装订单，在5月份期间我总共拜访了他4次。此后我再未见过他或他的妻子。日本人随后问我是否知道罗明先生目前的住所，我予以否认。他们接着问我是否知道翁嘉阿是流动小组的成员，我也予以否认

the negative. After that they finished questioning me and
having released me, took me out. After that the other four
Japanese started to beat up ong kau he by using a bamboo
stick in an attempt to extort from him confession of being
a member of a Mobile Unit. I saw when Japanese threw ong
Kau ha on the floor and one of them stood on his legs while
the other beat him about the body with bamboo stick and they
also tortured him by burning his hands with their cigarettes.
The Japanese could not, however, extort the confession from

At day break, when interrogation was over, the Japanese
put ong Kau ha, his paramour Yang Kau Tseng and my-self
into a small room where we were kept until about 9 a.m. May
25th. 1938, and then transferred to the Headquarters, S.M.P.
I did not see whether any other member of our party was sub-
jected to any form of torture, except ong Kau ha. I do not
know any person named ong Kah ing (翁克明) or Tseng Chi
Feng (郑志峰) at all and I am not a member of any Political
Party or any Anti-Japanese organisations. I do not take
any part in terroristic acts against Japanese troops here.
This is my true statement.

否认。之后他们结束了对我的审问，将我释放并带了出去。随后，另外四名日本人开始用竹棍殴打翁嘉何 (ong kau he)，试图逼取他承认是流动小组成员的供词。我看到日本人将翁嘉哈 (ong Kau ha) 摔在地上，其中一人踩住他的腿，另一人用竹棍击打他的身体，他们还用香烟烫他的手来折磨他。然而，日本人未能从翁嘉哈那里逼取到供词。

这是我的真实陈述。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of HYIEN KWEI SUNG (洪桂生)
native of Kompo taken by Mr Japanese Military Police
at on the 25-5-38 and interpreted by

My name is Hyien Kwei Sung, age 22, native of
Kompo, residing at No. 17 Yu Yung Li,
My alias is Hyien Ts Mei. I did not attend any
school and am illiterate. From the age of 17 until the time
of the outbreak of hostilities, I worked at a Chinese owned
cotton mill in the Yangtzepoo District. Since July last year
I have been cohabiting with Wong Kwok Hwa. Before the
hostilities Wong was operating a towel factory in Chapel. Since
January this year Wong has been working in the Shipping
Department of the T. T. o Government.
I know Wong Fun, Ma Loh Ming and Mr. Kung, who are
connected with a mobile unit. I met Wong Fun on a few
occasions last year at Ma Loh Ming's home at No. 9 Chengtu
Faung, Chengtu Road. I became acquainted with Ma Loh Ming in
November last year. Ma appears to have a high position in
the mobile unit and Wong has been receiving $20.00 from Ma
every month. Mr. Kung is a member of the mobile unit and he
used to meet Ma Loh Ming practically every night. I know where
he lives and I can take you there. If Mr. Kung be arrested Ma
Loh Ming's address will be known. I also know the rendezvous
of Ma, Wong and Kung. Zung Kwei Rn is also a member. I do
not know his address.

本人名为洪桂生，年龄 22 岁，
籍贯 Kompo（音译），寓居余庆里 17 号。
别名为 Hyien Ts Mei（音译）。本人未上过学，是文盲。从 17 岁起直至战事爆发，本人在杨树浦区一家华商棉纱厂工作。自去年七月起，本人与王国华（Wong Kwok Hwa）同居。战事前，王在 Chapel（音译，疑为闸北或某地名误植）经营一家毛巾厂。自今年一月起，王在 T. T. o 政府（原文如此，疑指国民政府某部门）航运科工作。
本人认识王奋、马乐鸣及孔先生，他们与一个流动小组有关联。去年，本人在成都路成都坊 9 号马乐鸣家中数次遇见王奋。本人于去年十一月结识马乐鸣。马似乎在流动小组中身居高位，王每月从马处收取 20.00 元。孔先生是流动小组成员，他几乎每晚都与马乐鸣见面。本人知道他的住址，可以带你们去那里。如果孔先生被捕，马乐鸣的地址就会知晓。本人也知道马、王和孔的碰头地点。陈贵林（Zung Kwei Rn，音译）也是成员之一。本人不知道他的地址。

The following is the statement of NYIEN KWEI SUNG (嚴桂生)
native of Zaushing taken by me D.S.I. Konovaloff
at H. J. C. B. on the 25-5-38 and interpreted by D.S.I. Chu Shou Ling

My name is Nyien Kwei Sung. I am 22 years of age,
Native of Zaushing, residing at a house No. 67, Sung Ah Li
(宋安里), off Rue Porte de la Ouest, French Concession.
At about 4 p.m. the 24-5-38, I, together with my
husband Wong Kwoh Hwa (王國華) (1st arrested) went to Room 623
of the Sun Sun Hotel, Kweichow Road, for the purpose of taking
a bath. This room was occupied by Ma Chien Ming (馬建民)
(2nd arrested) for the past 15 days and I know that Ma Chien
Ming is a friend of my husband. On arrival at the Hotel my
husband (1st arrested) telephoned to one named Zung Vung Ziang
(張永祥) who was occupying Room 317 at the same Hotel. During
the conversation I heard my husband telling Zung Vung Ziang
the number of the room (623) and inviting him to play a game
of Mahjong. However, this man has not come to the room.
Shortly after midnight (the 25-5-38) about 7 or 8 Japanese in
plain-clothes with pistols in their hands, came into the room
and one of them pointing at my husband, asked his name. As my
husband replied that his name was Wong Yung, three members of
the party left the room and after about 5 minutes when they
returned, questioned him again regarding his name and asked me
if I was a wife of Wong Kwoh Hwa. After searching the room,
the Japanese Military Police had taken me and the other five
male Chinese, including my husband, in a M/Car and conveyed to
some house situated near the bridge but I don't know the place.
When in the house I was taken alone in the room and questioned
by two Japanese in plain-clothes in the following manner :-
Question : "Has your husband any other name?"

以下为嚴桂生（NYIEN KWEI SUNG）之供词，
籍贯 Zaushing（音译），由副督察科诺瓦洛夫（D.S.I. Konovaloff）于 1938 年 5 月 25 日在 H. J. C. B.（原文缩写，具体地点不明）录取，并由副督察朱守灵（Chu Shou Ling）翻译

本人名为嚴桂生。年龄 22 岁，
籍贯 Zaushing（音译），寓居法租界西敏路（Rue Porte de la Ouest，即今西门路/自忠路一带）宋安里 67 号。
1938 年 5 月 24 日下午 4 时许，本人与丈夫王国华（Wong Kwoh Hwa）（第一被捕者）前往贵州路新新旅馆 623 房间洗澡。该房间已由马建民（Ma Chien Ming）（第二被捕者）占用 15 天，本人知道马建民是丈夫的朋友。抵达旅馆后，丈夫（第一被捕者）打电话给住在同一家旅馆 317 房间的张永祥（Zung Vung Ziang）。谈话中，本人听到丈夫告诉张永祥房间号码（623）并邀请他来打麻将。然而，此人并未来到房间。
午夜过后不久（1938 年 5 月 25 日），约七八名手持手枪的便衣日本人进入房间，其中一人指着丈夫询问其姓名。当丈夫回答名叫王勇（Wong Yung）时，这群人中的三人离开房间，大约五分钟后返回，再次盘问他的姓名，并问本人是否是王国华的妻子。搜查房间后，日本宪兵将本人及其他五名中国男子（包括丈夫）押上一辆摩托车（M/Car），送往桥附近的一处房屋，但本人不知具体地点。
在该房屋内，本人被单独带入一间房间，由两名便衣日本人按以下方式进行审问：
问：“你丈夫还有其他名字吗？”

I knew my paramour Wong Kwoh Hwa for the past

Wong Kwoh Hwa, the latter introduced me to Zung Vung Ziang, who

除上述供词外，本人还需陈述：
大约三年前，本人曾因离婚案件聘请律师马乐鸣，并前往其位于成都路成都坊 9 号的住所拜访，但自那以后，本人再未见过或遇到过马乐鸣。自从与前夫离婚后，本人在索恩伯恩路（Thorburn Road，即今泰兴路）振业织造厂担任织布工。因上海战事爆发，本人离开了这份工作。

本人与情夫王国华相识已有五年，自上海战事爆发以来一直与其同居。在成为王国华的事实婚姻妻子之前，王将本人介绍给张永祥，当时张住在伯基里路（Burkili Road，即今保基里路/普安路一带）永年里的一处住宅内。

1936 年 7 月某时，本人拜访张永祥，当时他因经济困难与妻子发生金钱争执。本人与其妻子关系甚好，出于同情，便让张永祥拿本人的戒指去典当，他典当了 17.00 元。几天后，本人再次拜访张永祥，这次他试图劝说本人辞去织造厂的工作，去当舞女。本人予以拒绝。后来，当本人遇到王国华（即现在的丈夫）时，

H. Q. C. D. Station, 8220
REPORT
Date May 27th. 19 38.
Subject Re:- Illegal arrests made by the Japanese Military Police.
Made by D.I. Glover Forwarded by C.D.I. Prince.

Sir,

During the morning of the 27th. May 1938, further investi-
gations were made regarding the paragraph contained in the state-
ment made by Wong Koh Hwa, relating to his suspicions regard-
ing a Detective attached to the S.P...

After this man had been questioned, D.S. Urum of the
S.P..., called by request at this office. During the ensuing
conversation D.S. Urum volunteered the information that he
actually went to Room No. 623, The Sun Sun Hotel, but not
until after the Japanese Military had made the arrests, with-
out informing him.

Following these arrests the Japanese Military Police
telephoned to his home, notifying him of what had occurred.
On receipt of this information he immediately proceeded to
the scene, and found that the six persons were already in
the custody of the Japanese Military Police.

At the conclusion of this interview D.S. Urum left
the office. Immediately after his departure Wong Koh Hwa
who was present during this interview, identified this
Detective whom he stated he had seen on the night of his
arrest. A short statement was taken from him, in which
he states that the Detective whom he identified was present
at the time of his arrest.

Further questioned regarding statements alleged to have
been made by them to the Japanese Military Police, Doung
Ah Ching (唐阿全), and the female Hyien Kwei Sung (展桂生),
denied that the contents of same were true. The female prisoner
also stated that she did not know of any persons named Kung
and Sung, and that the reason for her stating that she knew
them was to save herself from further ill treatment.

（左侧手写批注：）
S.
Doung
Ah Ching
D.S.
Urum's.

报告
日期：1938 年 5 月 27 日。
事由：关于日本宪兵非法逮捕之事。
呈报人：督察格洛弗（D.I. Glover） 转呈人：首席侦探督察普林斯（C.D.I. Prince）。

先生，

1938 年 5 月 27 日上午，针对王国华供词中涉及其对一名隶属于上海公共租界警务处（S.P...）的侦探的怀疑一段，进行了进一步调查。

经讯问该人后，应要求，上海公共租界警务处的副督察乌伦（D.S. Urum）来到本办公室。在随后的谈话中，乌伦副督察主动提供信息称，他确实去了新新旅馆 623 房间，但那是在日本军方实施逮捕之后，且事先并未通知他。

逮捕发生后，日本宪兵打电话到他家中，告知所发生之事。接到此消息后，他立即赶赴现场，发现六人已被日本宪兵拘留。

谈话结束时，乌伦副督察离开办公室。在他离开后，在场旁听此次谈话的王国华立即指认了这名侦探，称其在被捕当晚曾见过此人。随后录取了一份简短供词，他在其中陈述，他所指认的侦探在其被捕时在场。

就据称向日本宪兵所作的供词内容进一步讯问时，唐阿全（Doung Ah Ching）和女犯展桂生（Hyien Kwei Sung，音译，前文作洪桂生/嚴桂生）否认供词内容属实。该女犯还陈述，她并不认识名叫孔和宋（Sung，音译）的人，她之所以声称认识他们，是为了使自己免受进一步的虐待。

（左侧手写批注：）
S.
Doung
Ah Ching
D.S.
Urum's.

Further Report re Arrest of four male chinese by Japanese.

.. .. T.C.Smith
Chief .. ..

Sir,

Further to my report No.43 /30 rendered on the
25-5-38, further enquiries have been made by the undersigned
and .. .. from the roomboys, fifteen of whom stated
that at about 10.30 a.m. on the 25th inst., several Japanese entered
the hotel and arrested four male chinese in Room No.623.
The teaboy, Wong Shun (黄顺) who was interrogated stated
that since 10.00 a.m. he had been engaged in cleaning the rooms
(卢什翔) and had seen visitors daily, several male and
female chinese who occupied Room No.623.
On the above question, so far as I can ascertain several
visitors, together with Ho Zoong Liang, were taken away
by the Japanese authorities.

The teaboy could not however definitely state that
several of the male chinese when taken away by the Japanese,
had had their hands tied together with string inasmuch as, as
previously stated he was attending to the needs of guests
occupying Room No.603, this room being situated at the extreme
end of the corridor, and however, he states that whilst en route
to Room No.603, he passed several male Japanese and Chinese
dressed in civilian clothes, who at this time entered Room 623.

Further enquiries show that the Japanese remained in
the room for about 10 minutes, but during their sojourn there
in no scuffle or any heat/argument was heard, consequently the
teaboy was not aware that the occupants of this room had been
taken away until informed by guests occupying adjoining rooms.

After making a few enquiries the teaboy then informed
the night duty accountant Tung Eren Tan (陈仲山) who owing to

关于四名中国男子被日本 ____ 逮捕的补充报告 ____  T.C. Smith

先生，

继本人于 1938 年 5 月 25 日提交的第 43/30 号报告之后，具名人进行了进一步查询，并从茶房处获悉，其中十五人陈述称，当月 25 日上午 10 时 30 分左右，几名日本人进入旅馆，并在 623 房间逮捕了四名中国男子。
接受讯问的茶房黄顺（Wong Shun）陈述称，自上午 10 时起，他一直忙于打扫房间（卢什翔，音译，此处原文可能有误或为另一人名/地名夹杂），并每天看到访客，包括几名占据 623 房间的中国男女。
关于上述问题，据本人查明，几名访客连同何宗良（Ho Zoong Liang，音译）一起被日本当局带走。

然而，茶房无法确切说明几名中国男子被日本人带走时双手是否被绳子捆绑在一起，因为如前所述，他当时正在照料占据走廊尽头的 603 房间的客人；不过，他陈述称，在前往 603 房间的途中，他经过了几名身着便服的日本人和中国人，这些人当时进入了 623 房间。

进一步调查显示，日本人在房间内停留了约 10 分钟，但在其停留期间，未听到任何打斗或激烈争吵声，因此，直到相邻房间的客人告知，茶房才得知该房间的住客已被带走。

经过一番询问后，茶房随即通知了夜班会计陈仲山（Tung Eren Tan），后者由于

At 1 a.m. on 25-5-38, I observed ten or more persons came
out from the lift and proceeded to the entrance gate. Amongst
them, there was a female Chinese. Later, I heard the sounding
of a motor-car horn.
    At 2 a.m. even date, a teaboy named Tung Lon Sung came to the
accountants' office and informed me that several inmates of
Room 623 had been arrested by several Japanese in civilian clothes.
    Owing to the fact, that it was in Curfew hours and the
manager was absent from the hotel, so I reported the occurrence
to the manager at 9.30 a.m. on 25-5-38.
    The above is true.

Sir,

At about 9 a.m. May 25th. 1938, D.S.I. Umemoto,

their own initiative, and without obtaining the assistance of

Sun Sun Hotel, Szechow Road, where they arrested the six
undermentioned persons : -

7 Yoong Leu Rd, Moy Road.
3) ZUNG CHE TONG (陈锦昌), 53, Shanghai, M/Broker, 46
Rue Gilic, F.C.
（印：SPECIAL 26 MAY 1938）
4) D UNG II CHING (唐阿金), 47, Soochow, M/Tailor, 67
Zung An Rd, Rue Porto de
l'Ouest, F.C.

日期：1938年5月25日。
主题：日本宪兵队搜查四川路新新旅馆。
由副刑侦督察 G.A.V.R 呈报，经刑事侦缉处督察 FRIEDL 转发。

先生，

1938年5月25日上午9点左右，隶属于特别科的副刑侦督察
梅本（Umemoto）通知具名者，约在1938年5月25日
下午12:40，日本宪兵队擅自行动，在未获得租界警方
协助的情况下，对四川路新新旅馆623房间进行了搜查，
并逮捕了以下六人：
1) 黄国华（WONG KOH HWA），39岁，金波（Konpo，音译），男/搬运代理
行主，住法租界西蒲石路（Rue Porto de l'Ouest）67号，
众安路67号，
2) 陈济民（H. CHEN MING），38岁，乍兴（Zaushing，音译），男/航运职员，
住慕尔路（Moy Road）永禄路7号，
3) 陈锦昌（ZUNG CHE TONG），53岁，上海，男/经纪人，住法租界
吉利路（Rue Gilic）46号，
（印：1938年5月26日 特急）
4) 唐阿金（D UNG II CHING），47岁，苏州，男/裁缝，住法租界西蒲石路（Rue Porto de
l'Ouest）67号，
众安路67号，
5) 钱京康（LIEN CHING KANG），47岁，佛山（Froshan，音译），男/经纪人，住法租界奥尔西尼路（Rue Orsini）莫勒路5号，
6) 倪桂珍（NYLN KWAI JING），22岁，乍兴（Zaushing，音译），女，住法租界西蒲石路（Rue Porto de
l'Ouest）67号，
众安路67号。

据副刑侦督察梅本查明，
这些人正被拘押在虹口区。

日本宪兵队的这种专断行为令人费解，尤其是鉴于
过去三天，隶属本科的侦探已接到警告，随时听候
其差遣。

副刑侦督察 Pryde、Makinevsky 和 Konovaleff 已提交
证实此情况的报告。

在收到关于此次搜查的第一份情报后不久，副刑侦督察
梅本通知具名者，

督察

Just prior to his arrest, Ong had given six photo-

were arrested by the Japanese Military Police.

They were conveyed in two cars to the "Bridge House",
North Szechuen Road, where they were placed in separate rooms.
Ong was questioned regarding Mr. Loh Ming, but he denied knowing
this man. This is not true as Mr. Loh Ming was the lawyer who
negotiated for the divorce of his paramour from her husband.

Not satisfied with this denial, four men submitted him
to torture which continued intermittently throughout the night
until 9 a.m. the following morning. He was severely beaten, had
water forced through his nostrils and finally had his fingers
squeezed by the insertion of pencils between the joints. In
spite of this torture, he still persisted that he knew nothing
concerning Mr. Loh Ming or members of mobile units.

就在被捕前不久，翁曾将其本人的六张照片交给雍，目的是获取将其财产从浙江撤离的许可证。雍并未办理通行证，而是利用这些照片将翁登记为“安义协会”（Ang Yih Association）的成员，该协会总部设在北四川路的新亚饭店。在被捕的前一天晚上，翁曾打电话给雍，要求他到新新饭店（Sun Sun Hotel）623室拜访他。尽管雍答应前往，但他并未出现，不久之后，他们便被日本宪兵逮捕。

他们被两辆汽车押送至北四川路的“大桥公寓”（Bridge House），并被分别关押在不同的房间。翁就罗明（Loh Ming）先生一事受到讯问，但他否认认识此人。这并非事实，因为罗明先生是为其情妇与其丈夫办理离婚事宜的律师。

审讯人员对他的否认并不满意，四名男子对他施以酷刑，这种折磨断断续续持续了一整夜，直到次日上午9点。他遭到毒打，鼻孔被强行灌水，最后手指关节间被插入铅笔并用力挤压。尽管遭受了这些酷刑，他仍坚持声称对罗明先生或流动小组成员一无所知。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of ONG KOW HING (王廣興)
native of SOOCHOW taken by I. Glover
at Hq. on the 25-5-38 and interpreted by Clark Yao.

My name is Ong Kow Hing, aged 39 years, native of Soochow, N. Chever, 67 Rue de la Porte de la Ouest, French Concession.

I was formerly the proprietor of the Koh Hua (國華) Lace Factory situated at houses 6 to 10, The Sing Fung (新豐), San Yang Road (三陽路), Chapei, where I had been in business for five years, previous to which I was employed for a period of seven years at the San Sing (三星) Cotton Mill, Sing Chiang Kiang (新江灣).

On the 11th August 1937, just two days prior to the commencement of the local hostilities, I evacuated from Chapei, and went to reside at House No. 200, Yoong Shing Tsung (永興坊), Rue Galle, French Concession. I resided there for five months, during which time I and my family subsisted on the proceeds of the sale of my stock which I had brought from Chapei. As the chief tenant, name forgotten, an employee of the Sincere Coy., required the room occupied by myself and family, for some relatives of his who had evacuated from Pootung, I removed to No. unknown, Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession, just opposite to the French Municipal Abattoir. Sometime during February 1938, I again removed to No. unknown, Rue Lagrene, French Concession, which is adjacent to the Far Eastern Hospital. After residing there for some two months, I removed on the 5th May 1938 to my present address, where I cohabit with the woman in custody named Nyien Kwei Sung (倪桂珍). My lawful wife returned to her native town, Kiangying, Kiangsu, on the 13th August 1937, leaving me to care for our son aged

以下是王廣興（ONG KOW HING）的供词，苏州人，由 I. Glover 于1938年5月25日在总部录取，由 Clark Yao 翻译。

我叫王廣興，39岁，苏州人，住址：法租界西台门路（Rue de la Porte de la Ouest，即今西藏南路附近）67号，北舍弗（N. Chever，音译）。

我曾是位于闸北三阳路新豐里6至10号的國華（Koh Hua）花边厂的业主，在此经营五年，此前我在新江灣的三星（San Sing）棉纺厂工作了七年。

1937年8月11日，就在本地战事爆发前两天，我从闸北撤离，迁居至法租界加利路（Rue Galle，即今吉安路）永興坊200号。我在那里居住了五个月，期间我和家人靠出售我从闸北带来的存货所得维持生计。由于主要租户（姓名已忘，系先施公司职员）需要我和家人居住的房间给他的某些从浦东撤离的亲戚居住，我搬到了法租界蒙梯尼路（Boulevard de Montigny，即今崇德路/顺昌路一带）某号，正对面是法公董局屠宰场。1938年2月的某个时候，我又搬到了法租界拉格纳路（Rue Lagrene，即今复兴中路）某号，邻近远东医院。在那里居住约两个月后，我于1938年5月5日搬至现址，与被羁押的女子倪桂珍（Nyien Kwei Sung）同居。我的合法妻子于1937年8月13日返回其家乡江苏江阴，留下我照顾我们那年幼的儿子

into liquidation I established my own business at Chapei, where
I remained until the outbreak of the present hostilities.
About three years ago a friend of mine named Zung
Tuh Shing (陳德新) invited me to Room 329, "Sun Sun" Hotel,
Kweichow Road, for recreation. Here I was introduced to a man
named Zung Wing Ziang (鄭文祥), who was alleged to be a
Theatrical Agent. We became friends, and I often visited this
man's house situated at House No. 45, Yung Nyien Li (永年里),
Furkill Road, where I played Mah-jong with him. This is this
man's concubine's home, his lawful wife residing at House No.1,
Zung Ling Li (仁慶里), Rue Lafrene, French Concession. Toward
the end of the last lunar year, this man was taken into custody
by the Settlement Police on suspicion of being a member of a
Chinese Mobile Unit. He, however, was subsequently released.
Since this affair I have studiously avoided this man as I did
not want to become entangled in political affairs. However,
on or about the 16th March 1938, Zung Vung Ziang called me to
his concubine's home, where he informed me that he was now
working with the Japanese Military, and was employed as the
Departmental Chief of the 4th Section of the "Sing Yah" (新亞)
Association. He asked me to enroll as a member, but I evaded
answering directly, and only gave a non-committal answer.
A few days after, whilst I was in Room No. 201, Far Eastern
Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, which had been engaged by my friend
Ma Chien Ming (in custody), Zung Vung Ziang entered and during
the course of the conversation, he boasted that he could obtain
permits for the removal of property from Chapei. He stated that

大约三年前，一位名叫陈德新（Zung Tuh Shing）的朋友邀请我到贵州路新新饭店329室娱乐。在那里，我被介绍给一个叫郑文祥（Zung Wing Ziang）的人，据说他是一名戏剧代理人。我们成了朋友，我经常去他在福开森路（Furkill Road，即今武夷路）永年里45号的住所，在那里和他打麻将。这是他的妾的住处，他的正妻住在法租界拉费雷路（Rue Lafrene，即今复兴中路）仁慶里1号。去年农历年底，此人因涉嫌是中国流动小组成员而被租界警察逮捕。但他随后获释。自那件事以后，我一直刻意回避此人，因为我不想卷入政治事务。然而，在1938年3月16日左右，郑文祥把我叫到他妾的家中，告诉我他现在为日军工作，受雇为“新亞”（Sing Yah）协会第四科的科长。他要求我登记入会，但我避而不答，只给了一个模棱两可的答复。
几天后，当我在我朋友马建明（Ma Chien Ming，在押）包下的亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Road，即今嵩山路）远东饭店201室时，郑文祥走了进来，在谈话过程中，他吹嘘自己能弄到从闸北迁移财产的许可证。他说

obtain the permit before very long. On concluding this
conversation I invited Zung to my room to play mah-jong. He
accepted the invitation but stated that he would not call until
after dinner. As Zung had not arrived by 9.30 p.m., Daung Ah
Ching (唐阿金) (in custody) rang him up, and asked him if he
intended to call or not. Zung replied that he would come very
soon, but as he did not come after about half an hour, we
decided to play mah-jong without him, and invited Ting Ching
Deung (錢京堂) (in custody) to take his place. We continued
playing until arrested by the Japanese Military Police. This
took place at about 12.40 a.m. May 25th 1938, when about eight
Japanese men burst into the room with drawn pistols. Among
these men was one wearing glasses, whom I believe to be a
member of the Shanghai Municipal Police, as when brought to the
Headquarters of the S.M.P. I saw him in the Japanese Detectives
Office. One of these men questioned me as to my name, and I
replied "Wong Yoong". He then repeatedly slapped my face, and
said that I was Wong Koh Hwa. The same Detective then asked
me if I was the man wearing a "Faung" (訪) silk long gown, to
which question I replied in the affirmative. We were then
handcuffed, placed in two cars and driven to the "Bridge House",
North Szechuen Road, where we were taken to the 1st floor.
Here I was separated from the others and taken to a room, in
which there were four desks. Four Japanese who were standing
in the room began to question me. They asked me if my name
was Wong Koh Hwa, and on my replying "Yes", he asked me why I
had stated in the first place that my name was Wong Yoong.

很快就能拿到许可证。谈话结束时，我邀请Zung到我房间打麻将。他接受了邀请，但表示晚饭后才会过来。由于晚上9点30分Zung仍未到达，唐阿金（Daung Ah Ching）（在押）给他打电话，问他是否打算过来。Zung回答说很快就会来，但过了约半小时他仍未到，我们决定不等他，继续打麻将，并邀请錢京堂（Ting Ching Deung）（在押）代替他的位置。我们一直打牌，直到被日本宪兵逮捕。此事发生在1938年5月25日凌晨约12点40分，当时约有八名日本男子持枪闯入房间。这些人中有一人戴着眼镜，我认为他是上海公共租界工部局警务处的一名成员，因为当我被带到工部局警务处总部时，我在日本侦探办公室看到了他。其中一人询问我的姓名，我回答叫“Wong Yoong”。随后他反复扇我耳光，说我是Wong Koh Hwa。同一名侦探接着问我是否就是那个穿着“訪”字丝绸长衫的人，我对这个问题给予了肯定回答。随后我们被戴上手铐，分两辆车押往北四川路的“Bridge House”（大桥公寓），并被带上二楼。在这里，我与其他人分开，被带进一个房间，房内有四张书桌。四名站在房间里的日本人开始审问我。他们问我的名字是不是Wong Koh Hwa，当我回答“是”时，他问我为什么起初声称自己叫Wong Yoong。

I explained to him that it was customary for a Chinese to have
an alias. He then asked me if I knew Ma Loh Ming (馬樂鳴),
and where he is residing. I replied that I did not know this
man, whereupon I was seized and beaten by these men with a whip,
which had a thick stock and a lash. One of the men also
seized a split bamboo cane, bound with iron rings, and joined
in the assault. They suddenly ceased and promised me that if
I admitted knowing Ma, they would not trouble me again. As I
continue to deny knowing this man, I was again seized and my
legs bound together with a leather belt. They then threw me on
one of the desks, and thrashed me again. As they still could
not get an admission from me, I was dragged off the desk, and
placed on the floor. One of the men sat on my chest, one on my
abdomen, and one sat on my legs, whilst the fourth man caught
hold of my ears and forced my head into a spittoon. The man who
sat on my chest, having previously provided himself with two
kettles of water, proceeded to force water into my nostrils.
During this operation they continued to question me regarding
Ma Loh Ming. As I could not answer this question I struggled,
and succeeded in breaking loose I then attempted to end my life
by dashing my head against the floor. They then pulled me to
my feet, at the same time striking me with a stick. Becoming
desperate I shouted "Strike me on my head and kill me", at which
they desisted striking me with the stick, and only slapped my
face with their hands. They rested for a while and then
resumed their questioning regarding Ma Loh Ming. At the same time
they attempted to force a confession from me by squeezing pencils

between my fingers. After this they then applied lighted
cigarettes to my right shin. Torture in the various forms
described above continued intermittently until about 9 a.m.,
after which I was given a bowl of rice. I omitted to mention
that whilst I was being tortured I heard Daung Ah Ching (in
custody), who was being detained in another room, crying and
shouting "I will talk". After eating I was taken to another
room, and placed with Daung Ah Ching. I noticed that my
paramour, Nyien Kwei Sung, was detained in an adjoining room.
At about 10 a.m. the other three men, arrested with us the
previous night, were brought into our room. With the
exception of myself, the bindings were removed, then we were
placed in two cars and escorted to S. M. Police Headquarters.
        I have further omitted to mention that enmity had
arisen between Zung Vung Ziang and myself over my paramour.
About two years ago he desired this woman to cohabitate with
him, but she refused. His idea was that my paramour should in
common with three other girls whom he had bought, work either in
a Cabaret or some Guide Service, so that he could live on their
earnings. On many occasions he attempted to lure this woman
away from me, by making her tempting offers, but each time
failed. On one occasion he borrowed a ring from her, because
he required money to purchase a wedding present for a friend.
Having obtained this ring he pawned it for $15.00. On becoming
aware of this I forced my paramour to endeavour to persuade
Zung to return the ring, but owing to the fact that these
demands were mostly made in the presence of his friends, Zung

在我的手指之间来逼供。之后，他们将点燃的香烟烫在我的右小腿上。上述各种形式的酷刑断断续续持续到上午9点左右，之后给了我一碗米饭。我此前未提及，在受刑期间，我听到被关在另一间房间的唐阿金（在押）哭喊大叫“我说”。吃完饭后，我被带到另一个房间，与唐阿金关在一起。我注意到我的情妇Nyien Kwei Sung被关在隔壁房间。上午10点左右，前一晚与我们一同被捕的另外三名男子被带进我们的房间。除了我之外，其他人的束缚都被解除，然后我们被分两辆车押送至上海公共租界工部局警务处总部。
        我还遗漏提到一点，即Zung Vung Ziang因我的情妇与我结怨。大约两年前，他希望这名女子与他同居，但她拒绝了。他的想法是让我的情妇与其他三名他买来的女孩一起，在歌舞厅或某种导游服务处工作，以便他能靠她们的收入生活。他多次试图通过诱人的条件引诱这名女子离开我，但每次都失败了。有一次，他向她借了一枚戒指，因为他需要钱给朋友买结婚礼物。拿到戒指后，他以15美元的价格将其典当。得知此事后，我强迫我的情妇去劝说Zung归还戒指，但由于这些要求大多是在他的朋友面前提出的，Zung

declined to do so on the grounds that he had been made to lose
face. Lung eventually gave her the pawn ticket, and the ring
was redeemed by the woman for $15.00. She continued to pester
Lung for the refund of the $15.00, but only succeeded in up
to date in obtaining by instalments a total of about $12.00.
Another possible cause for enmity might be for
the following reason :-

On or about the 20th March 1938, whilst I was with
Lung and several other persons in Room No. 201, The Far
Eastern Hotel, I forcibly restrained him from assaulting a
youth over a dispute arising out of a lawsuit. This youth
who was seeking an annulment of a deed of adoption had been
introduced by Lung to Lawyer Mr. Ku Tsung (顧宗?), but as
this man did not give satisfaction the youth through the
introduction of someone else, obtained the services of Mr.
Kiang Yih Bing (江一平), by whom the case was settled. The
reason for this attempted assault was that Lung resented the
youth transferring the case to Mr. Kiang Yih Bing, after he
had introduced him to Lawyer Koo.

I have no proof that Zung Vung Ziang was the person
who gave the information which led to our arrest, but in view
of the trouble between us at various times, and the fact that
he refrained from calling on me on the date in question I
suspect that this man or one named Tseu (周) were responsible.
The man Tseu Shi Bing (周希平) visited our room for several
minutes prior to our arrest, but whether he was responsible
or not I cannot say, as none of us had any enmity with this man.

This is my true statement.

以让他丢面子为由拒绝这样做。Lung最终给了她当票，该女子以15美元赎回了戒指。她继续纠缠Lung要求退还这15美元，但到目前为止只分期追回了约12美元。
另一个可能导致仇恨的原因如下：

1938年3月20日左右，当我和Lung及其他几人在远东饭店201号房间时，我曾强行阻止他因一起诉讼纠纷而殴打一名青年。这名青年寻求废除一份收养契约，最初是由Lung介绍给顾宗律师（Mr. Ku Tsung (顧宗?)）的，但由于此人未能令人满意，该青年通过他人介绍，聘请了江一平先生（Mr. Kiang Yih Bing），案件由此解决。Lung企图实施殴打的原因是，他在将青年介绍给顾律师后，对该青年将案件转交给江一平先生感到不满。

我没有证据证明Zung Vung Ziang就是提供导致我们被捕线索的人，但鉴于我们之间多次发生纠纷，且他在事发当天并未如约来访，我怀疑此人或一名姓周（Tseu）的人对此负责。周希平（Tseu Shi Bing）在我们被捕前几分钟曾到过我们的房间，但他是否负有责任，我无法断定，因为我们与此人并无怨仇。

以上是我的真实供词。

Alleged robbery at No.74 Tsingtao Road.

At 11pm. on 11/5/38 C.P.C. 3079 brought to the
station a male Chinese named Ts Foo Daung( 朱 富 堂 ),
Cook, residing No. 37 Poh Ling Li, off Rue du Consulate,
and reported as follows:-

When patrolling Tsingtao Road at about 10-50pm. on
11/5/38 he saw a group of people outside the Yuen Fung
Z( 雲 峰 寺 ) Temple, No.74 Tsingtao Road, and overheard
the word "pistol" used. On questioning the persons they
denied knowing of any matter concerning pistols, but the
above named informed him that there had been trouble in
the Temple and that Japanese soldiers had stolen some
money. The C.P.C. entered the temple and questioned the
occupants, but could not obtain any information, and
then brought the informant to this station.

When questioned by the undersigned and C.D.C.321
the informant stated that he and several relations had
entered the Temple to worship their deceased aunt, and
later had played Mah Jheng in the Temple. He states that
he did not play the game, being merely an onlooker.

At about 10-30pm. 11/5/38 he alleges that five or
six men, one being a Chinese in foreign clothing and the
others being Japanese wearing Japanese Army uniforms, and
believed to have been armed with pistols, entered via the
open rear door and searched the players and himself, steali

1.

青岛路74号涉嫌抢劫案。

1938年5月11日晚上11点，华捕3079号将一名名叫朱富堂（Ts Foo Daung）的中国男性厨师带到警局，此人居住在领事馆路波宁里37号，并报告如下：

1938年5月11日晚上约10点50分，他在青岛路巡逻时，看到青岛路74号云峰寺（Yuen Fung Z( 雲 峰 寺 ) Temple）外有一群人，并听到有人使用“手枪”一词。在询问这些人时，他们否认知道任何关于手枪的事情，但上述报案人告诉他，寺内发生了麻烦，日本士兵偷走了一些钱。该华捕进入寺庙询问在场人员，但未获得任何信息，随后将报案人带到本警局。

经本人及刑探321号讯问，报案人称他和几名亲属进入寺庙祭拜已故的姑母，后来在寺内打麻将。他声称自己没有参与游戏，只是旁观者。

据称，1938年5月11日晚上约10点30分，五六名男子，其中一人是身穿西式服装的中国人，其余几人身穿日本军服，被认为持有手枪，通过后门进入，搜查了玩家和他本人，偷走

报案人称，其叔父朱文瑞（Ts Vung Zen）当时正在打麻将，住在纽伯格路（Nyburgh Road）附近的昌悦隆（Chang Yue Loong），但当侦探带他去那里时，他表示天黑找不到房子，也不知道门牌号。
当被问及其它玩家时，他说有一名女子住在山西路107号，并带领侦探前往，但该女子尚未回来。
报案人不愿提供更多信息，也不希望警方继续调查，但承诺在1938年5月12日找到其他玩家，并于当天下午2点将他们带到本警局。随后允许其离开。
报告当晚，侦探在青岛路进行了广泛调查，但未发现任何见过日本士兵的人，如果真有士兵出现在那条路上，这种情况不太可能发生，尽管他们有可能乘汽车到达并离开。

that he had been present when the men entered the Temple
and also describes several as being in Japanese Army
uniforms, but he hid himself and does not know what
actually took place.
    No.107 Shanse Road was again visited by detectives
and a female named Yu Yung Sz(〔此处转录不清〕) was interviewed.
She stated that she had been an onlooker at the Mah Jhong
game, and that when the men entered the Temple several
were armed with pistols with which they intimidated the
players and onlookers. She alleges that $50.00 in notes
were stolen from her person and about $10.00 from the
Mah Jhong table.
    She also states that another female player, unknown
to her, lost about $300.00.
    Further enquiries were made at the scene and vicinity
on 12/5/38, but no definite information could be obtained.
    The informant failed to attend Sinza Station at 2pm.
on 12/5/38 as he had promised, and C.D.C. 321 proceeded to
the address given by him in the French Concession and found
it to be fictitious.
    It is not improbable that loafers have been concerned
in the theft of the money, if the report is true, and
the uniforms may have been used to intimidate the players,
and may not have been Japanese Army uniforms as described
by the informant and the female player.

称那些人进入寺庙时他在场，并描述其中几人身穿日本军服，但他躲了起来，不知道实际发生了什么。
    侦探再次走访山西路107号，并询问了一名名叫Yu Yung Sz（〔此处转录不清〕）的女子。她声称自己是麻将游戏的旁观者，当那些人进入寺庙时，其中几人持有手枪，以此恐吓玩家和旁观者。她声称自己身上被偷走了50美元纸币，麻将桌上被偷走了约10美元。
    她还表示，另一名她不认识的女性玩家损失了约300美元。
    1938年5月12日，在现场及周边进行了进一步调查，但未获得确切信息。
    报案人未按承诺于1938年5月12日下午2点前往新闸警局，刑探321号前往他在法租界提供的地址，发现该地址是虚构的。
    如果报告属实，游手好闲之徒很可能参与了盗窃钱财，制服可能被用来恐吓玩家，并且可能并非如报案人和女性玩家所述的那样是日本军服。

at 12.30 p.m. a telephone message was received
at Central Station from the Manager Bank(Exchange
Shop., 584 Zeckman Road, reporting that two plain-clothes
Japanese were attempting to extort money, at the
above premises.

In response to this message a party of Police composed
of Inspt. Brownrigg, Fournier-Desfossés, J. Seller, Cpl.
Spencer and Cop. Ma, proceeded to the address.

On arrival at the shop the employees of the Wo Chen Exchange
Shop stated that at about 12.30 p.m. 13-5-38 two
Japanese entered the shop and asked for one Hosh Zung Kyi
the Chief Assistant, regarding a certain subject
having previously visited the shop to sell gold and
silver ore. The Chief Assistant replied in the negative.
This apparently proved unsatisfactory to the Japanese, as
they suggested that the Chief Assistant accompany them to
the Japanese Military Headquarters, Hongkew District, to
make a statement regarding the affair.

Hearing this demand the employees of the shop became
afraid and telephoned to Central Station, this resulting
in the attendance of the Police party.

When the Police party arrived at the scene the two
Japanese were still present in the shop, and it was learned

抵达银号后，宝成银号的职员陈述，1938年5月13日中午12时30分左右，两名日本人进入店内，询问首席助理霍松基（Hosh Zung Kyi，音译）关于此前曾来店出售金银矿石的某事。首席助理予以否认。这显然令两名日本人不满，因为他们建议首席助理随他们前往虹口区日本军事总部，就此事作出陈述。

听到这一要求，店方职员感到恐惧，遂致电中央巡捕房，从而导致警察小队到场。

total value of approximately $6,000.00, and for which the
sum of Yen 300.00 was tendered to the soldiers in payment.
The Japanese Military Police, at Chinkiang, investigated the
affair, and placed the Korean subject Haku Lee Jun under
arrest.

Kwoh Lung Kyi
ningpo                                                                 self
Central Station      13th May . 1938      translated      clerk with Chien Shih
                                          xxxxxx

My name is Kwoh Lung Kyi, age 40, native of Ningpo, employ-
ed as an assistant by the Pao Chen Native Bank, 684 Szechuan Rd.
At about 12.11 p.m. on the 13-5-38 a Japanese together with
a Korean visited our bank, and asked me if sometime ago a Korean
had sold to our bank gold and silver bars. They added, I should
follow them to the Japanese Military Headquarters, Hongkew, to
make a statement in connection with the affair, therefore I
reported to the Central Police Station by telephone. Shortly
afterwards a party of police arrived and escorted me to the
station. Foreign and Chinese detectives accompanied by
representatives of the Japanese Military Headquarters visited
our bank premises and scrutinized all books, but failed to
trace any record of our bank having purchased gold and silver
bars, from a Korean.

The above is my true statement.
                                              Signed Kwoh Lung Kyi.

中央巡捕房      1938年5月13日      翻译      钱氏（Chien Shih）职员

我叫郭龙基，40岁，宁波人，受雇于四川路684号宝成银号，任助理。1938年5月13日中午12时11分左右，一名日本人偕同一名朝鲜人来到我行，问我不久前是否有一名朝鲜人向我行出售金银条。他们补充说，我应该随他们前往虹口日本军事总部，就此事作出陈述，因此我通过电话向中央巡捕房报告。不久后，一队警察赶到并将我护送至巡捕房。外国和华人侦探在日本军事总部代表的陪同下视察了我行场所，并仔细查阅了所有账簿，但未能找到我行从朝鲜人购买金银条的任何记录。

以上是我的真实陈述。
                                              签名 郭龙基

DETAINED CUSTOMS
OFFICER FREED

Man Whisked Away From
Bund Office Returns
After Detention

Mr. Yang Wen-lung, a Customs
officer who was carried away alleg-
edly by Japanese plain-clothes men
from his office, early in May, and
has never been heard of since, is
now back home. He was released
on Monday.

According to a reliable Chinese
source Mr. Yang will not return to
his job in the near future. Since
his abduction he has been absent
for three months from office and his
wife has paid numerous visits to
foreign authorities of the Customs
Administration requesting the lat-
ter to conduct negotiations with the
proper authorities for the release of
her husband. Negotiations were said
to have been conducted by Mr.
I. H. Lawford, foreign commis-
sioner of the Customs.

The abduction of Mr. Yang, it
will be recalled, was a sequel to
the organization of a Customs Sup-
port Committee by Chinese Customs
officers to protest against the
appointment of a Chinese Customs
superintendent by the Japanese-
supported "Reformed Government"
at Nanking. For the same purpose
a short-lived strike was called by
the Customs officers and the super-
intendent never officially assumed
his new duties.

Prior to Mr. Yang's abduction
another Chinese Customs officer met
the same fate, but he was released
after negotiations. In order to
avoid further complication of the
situation the Customs authorities
later sent many Chinese Customs
officers to work in outport offices.
The support committee was dis-
solved.

被拘留的海关官员获释

男子从外滩办公室被带走
拘留后返回

杨文龙（Yang Wen-lung）先生是一名海关官员，五月初据称被日本便衣人员从其办公室带走，此后一直杳无音信，现已回到家中。他于周一获释。

据一位可靠的中国消息来源称，杨先生在近期不会重返工作岗位。自被绑架以来，他已缺勤三个月，其妻子多次拜访海关管理局的外国当局，请求后者与有关当局进行谈判以释放其丈夫。据说谈判是由海关外籍税务司 I. H. 劳福德（Lawford）先生进行的。

回顾起来，杨先生被绑架是中国海关官员组织“海关支援委员会”以抗议日本支持的南京“维新政府”任命一名中国海关监督的后续事件。出于同样的目的，海关官员发动了一次短暂的罢工，该监督从未正式就任新职。

在杨先生被绑架之前，另一名中国海关官员也遭遇了同样的命运，但经过谈判后获释。为了避免局势进一步复杂化，海关当局后来派遣许多中国海关官员到外地口岸工作。支援委员会随之解散。

海关中国地界
在租界土地章程下
警务问题构成棘手议题

昨日，继周一和周三发生两起海关官员绑架案后，本地官方人士对上海江海关总务处助理张鸿奎（Chang Hong-kwei）先生所表达的关于海关物业警务问题的不确定感表示并非夸大。这两位官员宣称。据这些消息来源称，水上警察完全束手无策。名义上，他们有权防止此类行为，正如他们有权制止并逮捕在海关场所内实施任何性质非法行为的罪犯一样。然而，水上警察仅“出于日本军方的好意”在行动。《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）获悉，在日本军队完全占领上海后的一段时间里，据说水上警察被彻底剥夺了他们的“权利”，将其职责仅限于监督外滩一侧的交通，并在码头上与上海公共租界工部局警务处（S. M. Police）合作。

根据1899年《土地章程》的规定，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）在海关大楼范围内没有管辖权。中央政府过去也曾声称，工部局（S.M.C.）对海关验货棚或海关码头均无管辖权。这一管辖权问题从未得到明确确认或争议。

既然维持这些场所内的法律和秩序不是上海公共租界警务处的职责，那么这无疑是属于水上警察管辖范围内的责任，因此责任落在水上警察肩上。

有报告称，一队水上警察袖手旁观，看着四名日本便衣人员抓获刘（Liu）……（原文不清）

鉴于他们目前的地位，这四位水上警察完全依赖日本当局，作为一个个体的存在本身都感到不确定，因此觉得无权在此类案件中采取行动。

此处有人指出，上海公共租界工部局警务处完全有权抗议随后将被捕者经租界领土运送至虹口。名义上，上海公共租界工部局警务处有权阻止此类运输。

面对现实
然而，如果面对现实，这些当局得出结论，在这些案件中，无论是水上警察还是上海公共租界工部局警务处，对其行动——或不作为——都不应受到指责。首先，他们指出，张先生已于昨晨获释；其次，强硬的行动可能会发展成更为严重的局势。目前认为，除了接受日本武装部队实际上占领虹口和杨树浦地区这一事实外，对此已无能为力。

pages.zh:
日本人释放
海关雇员

在上海江海关总务处助理张鸿奎（Chang Horng-kwei）先生被日本当局拘留约24小时后，于昨日上午11时获释。

四名身穿便服的日本人陪同张先生前往海关大楼。几名海关高级职员在场迎接他。在与同事简短交谈后，张先生休假一天并返回家中。

关于他在日本人手中遭受待遇的细节，昨日无法获得。然而，据了解，他并未见到仍被日本人拘留的海关缉私卫兵杨文龙（Yang Wen-lung）先生。

张先生是于周三上午在海关大楼三楼办公室被四名日本人绑架的。在他被抓后，海关当局立即向日方提出交涉。

pages.en:
CUSTOMS MAN IS
RELEASED
Preventive Officer Is
Still Being Held
North Of Creek

Mr. Chang Hung-kwei, junior
assistant of the Chinese Maritime
Customs, who was allegedly carried
away to Hongkew by a group of
Japanese on Wednesday morning,
was released yesterday after re-
peated negotiations between Mr.
L. H. Lawford Commissioner of
Customs and the Japanese Consular
authorities.

Mr Yang Wen lung, a Customs
preventive officer who was alleged-
ly similarly "kidnapped" last
Saturday was still being detained,
it being reported that he was lying
at the Foo Min Hospital, being
treated for injuries to his arm. It
was stated that the Japanese had
promised to release him.

It was stated last night by Chin-
ese circles attached to the Customs
that the Japanese had promised that
no repetition of similar incidents
would occur.
pages.zh:
海关人员获释
稽查员仍被拘押
在苏州河北岸

上海江海关助理员张鸿奎（Chang Hung-kwei）先生，据称于周三上午被一群日本人带往虹口，经过海关税务司劳福德（L. H. Lawford）先生与日本领事当局之间的反复谈判，于昨日获释。

据称上周六同样被“绑架”的海关稽查员杨文龙（Yang Wen lung）先生仍被拘留，据报道他正躺在福民医院（Foo Min Hospital），接受手臂受伤的治疗。据悉，日方已承诺释放他。

昨晚，隶属于海关的中方人士称，日方已承诺不再发生类似事件。
