参考中央杂项档案第489/38号，涉及日本宪兵于1938年5月9日逮捕海关缉私卫兵第98号杨文龙（楊文龍），以及摘录自1938年5月12日的《字林西报》，涉及办公助理张鸿奎（張鴻奎）于1938年5月11日被捕。海关税务司劳福德（L. H. Lawford）先生在1938年5月12日接受询问时，就这些事件是否会在海关职员中引发动乱的可能性表示，截至目前，尚未出现任何麻烦的迹象。劳福德先生进一步表示，由于日本总领事馆的高级秘书向日本宪兵进行了交涉，日本宪兵承诺在1938年5月12日中午之前将助理张鸿奎交还至劳福德先生的办公室，并且正在就归还缉私卫兵第98号杨文龙进行谈判。

关于新闻界出现的报道，称在逮捕张鸿奎时，一名日本人将手伸进口袋并以威胁的方式指向劳福德先生，劳福德先生表示他没有观察到此类手势，也不相信此事发生过。

Customs Employee Is
Still In Hands Of
Japanese Officials

Despite representations made by
Mr. L. H. Lawford, Commissioner of
the Shanghai Customs, the Japan-
ese authorities last night continued
to hold Mr. Yang Wen-lung, re-
venue guard, pending further inves-
tigation. THE CHINA PRESS learned
last night.

Mr. Yang, who was on duty in the
Customs examining shed, was seized
by five armed Japanese Monday
night and was taken to Hongkew.
Except for reports stating that he
was nabbed for inquiry, no definite
information concerning the motive
for his seizure could be obtained
yesterday.

In the meantime, the Customs is
continuing to function on a normal
basis. All hands were at work on
a full-time status yesterday.

海关雇员仍
在日本官员
手中

尽管上海海关税务司劳福德（L. H. Lawford）先生进行了交涉，《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）昨晚获悉，日本当局昨晚继续拘留缉私卫兵杨文龙（Yang Wen-lung）先生，以待进一步调查。

杨先生当时正在海关验货棚值班，于周一晚被五名武装日本人抓获并被带往虹口。除了有关他因受讯问而被捕的报告外，昨日未能获得关于其被捕动机的确切信息。

与此同时，海关继续正常运作。昨日所有人员均全职上班。

上海海关中国职员的领导人今早正在商讨采取行动以促使第98号缉私卫兵杨文龙（Yang Wen-lung）先生获释的事宜。杨先生昨天被五名武装日本便衣人员抓获并带往虹口，这与海关当局要求迅速解散他们上周六成立的“海关保护协会”的命令有关。

尽管有报道称税务司劳福德（I. H. Lawford）已与日本总领事日高（S. Hidaka）进行沟通，但杨先生今早仍被拘押在虹口。

the following:-

At about 9.30a.m. on the 9th inst, four Japanese
dressed in plain clothes arrived at the Customs
Examination Shed and proceeded to the Revenue Guards
Waiting Room on the north side of the building. They
glanced at the numbers on the collars of several Revenue

seeking some person who was absent at that particular

by them to motor car licence No. 10564 which had been

pages.en:
00396

New Employee
Of Customs Is
Seized Here

4 Japanese “Arrest”
Chang Hong-kwei
In Office

Mr. Chang Hong-kwei, assistant
of the general office of the Shang-
hai Maritime Customs, was last
night still being held by Japanese
authorities following his seizure by
four Nipponese plainclothesmen in
his office at the Custom House at
11.30 o'clock yesterday morning.
The "arrest" of Mr. Chang was
the second made by Japanese auth-
orities among Chinese members of
the Customs staff in three days.
Mr. Yang Wen-lung, revenue guard,
who was seized in front of the Cus-
toms examination shed on the Bund
Monday morning, was still in the
custody of the Nipponese last night.

Second Arrest
Although no reason was given
yesterday for Mr. Chang's seizure,
it is believed that the "arrest" was
prompted by the "go-slow" strike
declared by Chinese Customs last
week-end as a protest against at-
tempts of the "Reformed Govern-
ment" to assume control over the
Customs here.
Mr. Chang was working at his
desk in the third floor office of the
Custom House yesterday when four
Japanese in plainclothes came be-
hind the counter and asked to see
him. He was told to follow the
party of Japanese. His question as
to the reason of his "arrest" met
with silence.
Believing his captors to be
armed, Mr. Chang did not put up
any struggle. He followed the
Japanese party into the corridor
where they met Mr. L. H. Lawford,
Customs Commissioner and Mr.
W. C. Woodfield, Chief of the
River Police.

Witness Departure
Neither of the two high foreign
Customs officials were able to pre-
vent the Japanese party from tak-
ing away the "arrested" man. Both,
however, accompanied the Nippon-
ese group down the stairs and wit-
nessed the departure of Mr. Chang
and his captors in an automobile.

It is understood that Mr. Lawford
has communicated with the Japan-
ese authorities in an effort to ob-
tain the release of his two arrested
workers.

Mr. Chang, who is 24 years of
age, is a native of Wukiang, Kiang-
su. He joined the Customs service
in 1935 and has been attached to
the appraising department as an
assistant.
pages.zh:
00396

海关新职员
在此被捕

四名日本人于办公室内
“逮捕”张宏贵（音译）

上海江海关总务处助理员张宏贵（Chang Hong-kwei，音译）先生，于昨日上午11时30分在海关大楼办公室内被四名日本便衣人员拘捕后，昨晚仍被日本当局扣押。对张先生的这次“逮捕”，是三天内日本当局第二次针对海关华籍职员采取的此类行动。本周一上午在外滩海关查验棚前被拘捕的缉私警杨文龙（Yang Wen-lung，音译），昨晚仍处于日方羁押之下。

第二次逮捕

虽然昨日并未说明拘捕张先生的理由，但据信此次“逮捕”是由上周周末中国海关职员为抗议“维新政府”企图接管本地海关而宣布的“怠工”罢工所引发。

昨日，张先生正在海关大楼三楼办公室的办公桌前工作，四名日本便衣人员走到柜台后面，要求见他。他们命令张先生跟随这群日本人。当张先生询问其被“逮捕”的原因时，对方沉默不语。

张先生认为抓捕者持有武器，因此未作任何反抗。他跟随这群日本人进入走廊，在那里他们遇到了海关税务司劳福德（L. H. Lawford）先生和水警总监伍德菲尔德（W. C. Woodfield）先生。

目击离去

这两位外籍海关高级官员均未能阻止日本人带走这名“被捕”男子。然而，两人都陪同这群日本人走下楼梯，并目睹了张先生及其抓捕者乘坐汽车离开。

据悉，劳福德先生已与日本当局取得联系，努力争取释放这两名被捕职员。

张先生现年24岁，江苏吴江人。他于1935年加入海关服务，一直隶属于估价科担任助理员。

Chinese Abducted
From Customs

Revenue Guard Carried Off
By Plainclothes Japanese
In Military Car

Following the arrest of a revenue
guard in the Customs examination
shed on the Bund, the Customs
Commissioner is understood to be
taking the matter up with the
Japanese consular authorities.

According to eye-witnesses, the
revenue guard, No. 98, Yang Wen-
lung, was dragged into a military
car by plainclothes Japanese and
taken to Hongkew at about 11 a.m.
yesterday. No news of his where-
abouts was known up to last
evening.

The Chinese was reported to be in
uniform and working in the Customs
shed when a Japanese plainclothes
man ordered him, at the point of a
pistol, to follow him to a car. Seeing
the Chinese undaunted, two other
Japanese came up and started to
push him to the Bund. The efforts
of the trio were not successful until
two additional Japanese came to
their help. He was finally placed
in a Japanese military car and taken
to Hongkew.

The abduction of the Chinese was
generally believed to be connected
with the strong opposition raised by
the Chinese members of the Customs
staff to the reported transfer of the
administration to the "Reformed
Government." A meeting, attended
by the majority of revenue guards
and other Chinese members of the
indoor and outdoor staff, was called
on Saturday morning, causing the
Customs routine to be at a standstill
for several hours.

On the advice of several high
Customs officials, the men returned
to their posts. Many members of
the indoor staff had to work as late
as 6 p.m. in order to catch up
with the delay. Another meeting
was held on Sunday morning, when
the members decided to await in-
structions from the Chinese authori-
ties at Hankow.

It could not be ascertained yester-
day whether the man held by the
Japanese had in any way been
responsible for the convening of the
"protest" meeting last Saturday.

The Customs building was guarded
by the River Police yesterday.

海关华员遭绑架

缉私警被便衣日本人
用军车掳走

继一名缉私警在外滩海关查验棚被捕后，据悉海关税务司正就此事项与日本领事当局进行交涉。

据目击者称，昨天上午11时许，第98号缉私警杨文龙（Yang Wen-lung，音译）被几名日本便衣人员拖入一辆军用汽车，并被带往虹口。直至昨晚，仍无其下落的消息。

据报道，这名中国人当时身穿制服，正在海关棚内工作，一名日本便衣人员用手枪指着他，命令他跟随自己前往一辆汽车。见该中国人并未畏惧，另外两名日本人上前，开始将他推向外滩。这三人的行动起初并未成功，直到又有两名日本人前来协助。他最终被塞进一辆日本军用汽车，并被带往虹口。

普遍认为，这起中国人被绑架事件与中国海关职员强烈反对据报道将行政管理权移交给“维新政府”有关。周六上午召开了一次会议，大多数缉私警以及其他内外勤华籍职员均出席，导致海关日常工作停滞数小时。

在几位海关高级官员的建议下，职员们返回了工作岗位。许多内勤职员不得不工作至下午6点，以弥补延误。周日上午又举行了一次会议，会上职员们决定等待汉口中国当局的指示。

昨日尚无法确定，被日方扣押的男子是否对上周六召开的“抗议”会议负有责任。

昨日，海关大楼由水警负责守卫。

During the questioning his idea regarding the time seemed to be somewhat at variance with the actual facts but he adhered to his original statement regarding the taking of two male Chinese by Japanese Military detectives, and no amount of cross-questioning could shake him in any way.
On C.D.S. 47 making further enquiries at the hotel as to the possibility of anyone else having observed the incident he encountered in the Grand Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, a male Chinese one Wong Teh Wei (汪德偉) residing 219 Avenue Edward VII, who is a friend of Ngan Tsung Woo, the occupant of Room 336, the man Wong stated that his friend one Zee Ts Dau (徐大涛), 43, Ningpo, shop-master, residing House 24, Yoong On Fong, Rue Laguerre, F.C. had been taken, together with another male Chinese whom he did not know on p.m. 4-5-38 by the Japanese Military Detectives, from the Grand Hotel, to Hongkew.
C.D.S. 47 and the undersigned immediately enquired and with the assistance of the French Police succeeded, in locating the man Zee, who attended this station at 2 p.m. 6-5-38 and made a statement regarding the occurrence subject of this file (Translation attached herewith).

先生，

自提交初步报告以来，已就本报告所述案件进行了进一步调查。茶房邓永英（Deung Yoong Ying，音译）被带至本捕房，由外勤侦探小组第47号警员及本人就其于1938年5月4日关于此事所作的陈述进行了进一步讯问。

在讯问过程中，他对时间的记忆似乎与事实略有出入，但他坚持其关于两名中国男性被日本宪兵侦探带走的原始陈述，无论怎样反复盘问，都无法动摇他的说法。

当中国侦探小组第47号警员就酒店内是否有其他人目睹此事向酒店方面进一步查询时，在亚尔培路（Avenue Edward VII，今淮海中路）的大华饭店遇到一名中国男性汪德伟（Wong Teh Wei），住址为亚尔培路219号，他是336房间住客颜宗武（Ngan Tsung Woo，音译）的朋友。汪姓男子称，他的朋友徐大涛（Zee Ts Dau，音译），43岁，宁波人，店主，住址为法租界拉格路（Rue Laguerre，今永嘉路）永安坊24号，于1938年5月4日下午，与另一名他不认识的中国男性一起，被日本宪兵侦探从大华饭店带往虹口。

中国侦探小组第47号警员及本人立即展开调查，并在法国警察的协助下，成功找到了徐姓男子。他于1938年5月6日下午2时来到本捕房，并就本案所述事件作了陈述（译文附后）。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Zee Ts Ching, 43, paper-merchant, residing at
24 Wing On Faung, Rue Laguerre, F.C.
native of Ningpo..................................................taken by me Self..................................................
at Louza Station on the 6-5-38................................and interpreted by Clerk Tsung..............................

At about 7 p.m. on 4-5-38, I proceeded to Room 336 Grand
Hotel with intent to see my friend Zah Chien Chu, but was
arrested by Japanese plain clothes men as I was about to enter
in the aforementioned room and they took me to Room 345 of
the same hotel.
In the room, the Japanese plain clothes men used a rope
and bound up our hands and feet. About 10 minutes later, another
male Chinese was arrested and herded in the same room with myself.
A few minutes later, they untied our hands and feet, took us
downstairs and placed us in a M/car which carried us to a Japanese
Military Police Headquarters in Hongkew.
In the Japanese Military Police Headquarters, the Japanese
officers cross-questioned us and struck us with a wooden bar. We
told them that we were proper merchants but they still detained
us.
At about 4 p.m. on 5-5-38, one of the Japanese officers
told us that they had found that we were not guilty and that we
would be released.
At the same time, a Japanese accompanied us to the Garden
Bridge and from there I took a ricksha home.
The above is true.

Signed.

以下为徐志清（Zee Ts Ching，音译）的陈述，43岁，纸商，住址为法租界拉格路（Rue Laguerre，今永嘉路）永安坊24号。
宁波籍 ____ 由本人亲自 ____ 
于1938年5月6日在老闸捕房 ____ 并由书记员宗（Tsung，音译）翻译 ____ 

1938年5月4日晚上7点左右，我前往大华饭店336房间，意在拜访我的朋友查建初（Zah Chien Chu，音译），但在即将进入上述房间时，被几名日本便衣人员逮捕，他们将我带到同一家酒店的345房间。
在房间里，日本便衣人员用绳子绑住了我们的手脚。大约10分钟后，另一名中国男性也被逮捕，并与我一起被关在同一房间内。几分钟后，他们解开了我们的手脚，将我们带下楼，放入一辆摩托车，将我们载至虹口的一处日本宪兵司令部。
在日本宪兵司令部，日本军官对我们进行了反复盘问，并用木棍殴打我们。我们告诉他们我们是正当商人，但他们仍然拘留了我们。
1938年5月5日下午4点左右，一名日本军官告诉我们，他们发现我们无罪，我们将被释放。
同时，一名日本人陪同我们至外白渡桥，从那里我乘人力车回家。
以上属实。

签名。

1938年5月4日晚上10时30分，卑职会同警员第274号前往南京路大华饭店（Grand Hotel），就情报科报告第36/38号所涉事项进行调查。从345号房间带出三名中国女性和一名男性，他们当时正被工部局警务处侦探和日本军方侦探拘禁在该房间内，因为据信他们与336号房间的住客有关联，而在该房间内发现了一本 purportedly 具有反日性质的小册子。在此期间，一名茶房王（No. 43, 唐仲英），苏州人，住在大华饭店，报告称两名日本军方侦探逮捕了两名身份不明的中国男性，这两人曾敲过336号房间的门，并于1938年5月4日晚上9点左右将他们带走，既未通知当时在346号房间、本可提供必要协助的经理，也未通知同样在346号房间的 J. Central Police Station,
REPORT
Date ____ April, 19 38

Subject Japanese Military entering St. Luke's Hospital for the purpose of
removing an injured person.

Made by F.S. 350 "A" right Forwarded by __〔此处转录不清〕__

Sir,

At 11.45 a.m. 28-4-38 I was detailed by Sub. Inspt.
Warters to accompany J.P.C. 141 to St. Luke's Hospital, Bubbling
Road, where it was reported that the Japanese Military were
attempting to remove an injured person.

On arrival at the hospital four Japanese Military
and an Interpreter were found negotiating with Doctor Morris,
i/c of the Hospital, for the removal of a male Chinese named
Loh Yung Kev, (陸雲狗) age 30, employed at the Japanese
Club, Soone Road, who was knocked down at 8.10 p.m. 26-4-38,
on the Main Bund Road near Peking Road, by an unlicensed
Japanese Military truck (forming the subject of T.A.R. 574/38)

Doctor Morris refused to allow the injured person
to be removed on account of his condition.

Chief Inspector Iwashita later attended and explained
to the Japanese Military the condition of the patient and the
inadvisability of removing him, as a result of which they left
the Hospital at 12.15 p.m., stating that they would return in a
few days time.

● Doctor Morris informed the undersigned that he had
communicated with the American Consular authorities and had
made a complaint to them over the incident.

An unlicensed Military truck and Motor cycle were
parked outside the Hospital during the time the Military were
inside the building.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently.

D. O. "A"
D. C. (Special Branch)

F.S. 350.

由 F.S. 350 “A”区制作 转发人 __〔此处转录不清〕__

先生：

1938年4月28日上午11时45分，我受副巡长 Warters 指派，陪同 J.P.C. 141 前往蒲石路（Bubbling Road）的圣路加医院，据报日本军方正试图移除一名伤者。

到达医院时，发现四名日本军人和一名翻译正在与医院主管 Morris 医生协商，要求移除一名名为 Loh Yung Kev (陸雲狗) 的中国男性，30岁，就职于顺昌路（Soone Road）的日本俱乐部，他于1938年4月26日晚上8时10分在外滩主干道靠近北京路的地方，被一辆无牌照的日本军用卡车撞倒（此事为交通事故报告 T.A.R. 574/38 的主题）。

Morris 医生因其状况拒绝允许移除伤者。

岩下（Iwashita）总巡长随后赶到，向日本军方解释了病人的状况以及移除他的不妥之处，结果他们于中午12时15分离开医院，并表示几天后会再来。

● Morris 医生告知卑职，他已与美方领事当局取得联系，并就该事件向他们提出了投诉。

在日本军方人员在建筑物内期间，一辆无牌照的军用卡车和一辆摩托车停在医院外面。

此致，
敬礼。

“A”区总监

Subject Detention of 3 male Chinese after their escape from Japanese
        custody at the Bridge House, North Szechuen Road.

Sir,
    At 2.30 a.m. on the 14-5-38, C.C. 3080 and Private Russian
Watchman named Kleinsen employed by the Shanghai Land Investment
Coy, Jinkee Road and guarding property in the vicinity of North
Kiangse and Wouchang Road, brought to the station a male Chinese
named:-
    Yang Vung Loong (楊文龍), 23, M/Customs Guard No. 95,
    native of Shantung, residing No. 11/158 Rue Alfred Magy,
    French Concession,
whom they had arrested whilst climbing over the barbed wire
barricade on Wouchang Road near North Kiangse Road at 2.20 a.m.
    On being questioned by Inspt. Chamberlain, S.I. Sharrock,
S.I. Tao, C.D.S. 69 and the undersigned Yang Vung Loong stated
that at approximately 11.10 a.m. on the 9-5-38, he was arrested
in the Waiting Room of the Customs House, The Bund, by 4 Japanese
plain clothes military police who accused him of being the leader
of a go slow strike of the Customs Guards who were opposing the
taking over of the Customs by the New Government. After arrest
he was placed in a M/Car and blindfolded, then taken to the
Bridge House, North Szechuen Road where the cloth was taken
from his eyes, since then he has been detained in a 1st floor
room of the building. At 2 a.m. this inst. he, together with
two other male Chinese, succeeded in escaping from their room,
and as he was not handcuffed was the first to gain North Kiangse
Road.
    At 2.45 a.m. S.I.C. 464 and Private Russian Watchman
Waravin also employed by the Shanghai Land Investment Coy,
brought to the station the other 2 male Chinese named
    Zee Yoong Tuh (徐榮德), 25, S/Unemployed mechanic,

Yang Vung Loong (楊文龍 )
Shantung . . ossington
. Hongkew 14/5/38 . . Tao Keng Yong

My name is Yang Vung Loong, age 3, native of Shantung.
I was born in Shanghai and am at present residing at No.11
Lane 158 Rue Magi, French Concession. On 1/10/34 I joined
the Chinese Maritime Customs as Revenue Guard No.98.
On the 7/5/38 all the employees in the Customs went on
strike to oppose the taking over of the Customs by the New
Chinese Government, and, after a meeting, the employees went
on a "go slow" strike. but consequently resumed duty on the
9/5/38.
At about 11.10 a.m. on the 9/5/38 whilst I was staying
in the Waiting Room of the Customs Jetty, the guard, four
Japanese plain-clothes military police came and checked the
numbers of all the guards in the room, and on seeing my
number, pulled me out of the room and forced me into a
private motor car. In the car I was blind-folded and had
the idea that the vehicle proceeded towards Hongkew District.
Later the car stopped outside a high building which I later
learned was the Bridge House. They then took off the blind-
fold and took me to a room on the 1st floor where the four
same Japanese questioned me as to whether I was the leader of
the guards in promoting the strike. I denied the allegation
and as a result of my denial, they assaulted me by striking
me about the body with their clenched fists and sticks.
Finally they tied me up to a table and poured water into my
nose through a rubber tube. I consequently told them that the
leaders of the Out-door staff were two named Liang Hwo Jih
and Chao Han Shing together with others, names unknown.
pages.zh:
杨文龙 (楊文龍)
山东 . . 霍辛顿 (Hossington)
. 虹口 1938年5月14日 . . 陶庚永 (Tao Keng Yong)

我叫杨文龙，3岁（原文如此），山东人。
我出生于上海，现居住在法租界麦琪路158弄11号。1934年10月1日，我加入中国海关，担任第98号缉私卫兵。
1938年5月7日，海关所有员工为反对新中国政府接管海关而举行罢工，经过会议后，员工们进行了“怠工”罢工，但随后于1938年5月9日恢复工作。
1938年5月9日上午11点10分左右，当我在海关码头的候客室时，四名日本便衣宪兵进来核对了室内所有卫兵的编号，看到我的编号后，将我拉出房间并强行塞进一辆私人汽车。在车里我被蒙住双眼，感觉车辆正驶向虹口区。后来车停在一栋高楼外，我后来得知那是百老汇大厦（Bridge House）。他们随后摘下我的眼罩，将我带到一楼的一个房间，那四名日本人再次审问我是否是鼓动罢工的卫兵领袖。我否认了这一指控，由于我的否认，他们用紧握的拳头和棍棒殴打我的身体。最后他们把我绑在桌子上，通过一根橡胶管往我鼻子里灌水。于是我告诉他们，外勤人员的领袖是两名分别叫梁火日 (Liang Hwo Jih) 和赵汉生 (Chao Han Shing) 的人，以及其他姓名不详的人。

pages.en:
- 2 -

They then took a statement from me re my birth, education,
residence and occupation, etc. Following which they gave
me cigarettes and told me to tell the truth so that I could
escape from being shot.

At about 5.30 p.m. same date I was hand-cuffed and locked
in a room on the ground floor where I met another male Chinese
named Zee Yoong Tuh and a Russian named Nicolas. At about
6.30 p.m. after a supper of rice and fish, I was removed
to another room on the 1st floor and was further questioned
by a Japanese in uniform, believed to be a corporal of the
Military Police, but nothing further could be learned from
me. After a lapse of 45 minutes, I was taken back to the
detention room.

At about 12.30 p.m. on the 10/5/38, I was again taken
to the room where I was tortured on 9/5/38 by the same four
Japanese. There I was further questioned. They then repeated
the torture when I denied being the leader. I was asked to
write another statement which they claimed they would
verify later. I was then locked up in the same detention
room.

At about 1.30 p.m. on the 11/5/38 I was taken to another
room on the 1st floor where I was again interrogated by the
Japanese corporal in uniform and finally I admitted being the
leader of the guards. I was then taken back to the detention
room and released of the handcuffs. At about 5.30 p.m. on
the 11/5/38 one named Chang, a member of the Indoor Staff,
pages.zh:
- 2 -

随后他们就我的出生、教育、居住地和职业等情况记录了一份供词。之后他们给了我香烟，并告诉我要说实话，以免被枪决。

当天下午约5点30分，我被戴上手铐并关在一楼的一个房间里，在那里我遇到了另一名中国男子徐荣德 (Zee Yoong Tuh) 和一名名叫尼古拉斯 (Nicolas) 的俄国人。下午约6点30分，在吃过米饭和鱼的晚餐后，我被转移到一楼的另一个房间，由一名身穿制服的日本人（据信是宪兵下士）进一步审问，但我没有透露更多情况。45分钟后，我被带回拘留室。

1938年5月10日中午12点30分左右，我再次被带到1938年5月9日遭受酷刑的房间，由同样的四名日本人进行审问。在那里我受到了进一步的讯问。当我否认是领袖时，他们再次施以酷刑。他们让我写另一份供词，声称稍后会进行核实。随后我被关在同一个拘留室里。

1938年5月11日下午1点30分左右，我被带到一楼的另一个房间，再次由那名身穿制服的日本下士审问，最终我承认自己是卫兵领袖。随后我被带回拘留室，解除了手铐。1938年5月11日下午5点30分左右，一名姓张的内勤人员，

pages.en:
- 3 -

was seen being locked in the next room to mine. On the
same date another captive named Lee Kwei Sung was locked
in my room.

At about 2 a.m. 14/5/38 I together with the other two
Chinese namely: Zee Yoong Tuh and Lee Kwei Sung succeeded
in removing two planks of wood from the wall in the latrine.
I came out first and succeeded in gaining a small alleyway
off North Kiangse Road after climbing over a low wall. The
other 2 Chinese came out about 15 minutes later via the
same route. When I was about to get over the barbed wire,
I was accosted by a C.P.C. and a Russian watchman who took
me to West Hongkew Station.

I do not know the exact number of persons confined in
the Bridge House, but I think there are about 30 persons,
including a few Japanese subjects.

The above is my true and voluntary statement.

Signed
Yeng Vung Loong.

被看到关在我隔壁的房间里。同一天，另一名被捕者李桂森 (Lee Kwei Sung) 被关进我的房间。

1938年5月14日凌晨2点左右，我与另外两名中国人，即徐荣德 (Zee Yoong Tuh) 和李桂森 (Lee Kwei Sung)，成功拆下了厕所墙上的两块木板。我先出来，翻过一堵矮墙后，成功进入了江西北路的一条小巷。另外两名中国人大约15分钟后通过同一条路线出来。当我正要翻越铁丝网时，一名公共租界巡捕 (C.P.C.) 和一名俄国看守拦住了我，并将我带到虹口西区捕房。

我不知道百老汇大厦内关押的确切人数，但我认为大约有30人，其中包括几名日本籍人士。

以上是我的真实且自愿的陈述。

签名
杨文龙 (Yeng Vung Loong)。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Lee Kwei Sung
native of Chingkiang taken by me J. S. Bousfield
at W. H'kew on the 14-5-38 and interpreted by

My name is Lee Kwei Sung (李桂森) aged 31, a native of
Chingkiang. I am the proprietor of the Chien Tai Chong Wine
Shop situated in Yung An Doo Road, Pootung and at the time of
my arrest was residing at No. 3 Yuan Ching Li, Pootung.

At about 9 a.m. on the 1-5-38, I was arrested by detectives
of the Ta Tao Government Pootung, who accused me of being
concerned in the bombing of one Soo Sih Yung (蘇錫文) a few
days previously. On being taken to the government office I was
questioned regarding the bombing and as I refused to admit the
offence, was tortured by having water poured up my nose and was
struck about the body with sticks.

As a result of the torture I implicated 4 other male Chinese
as the perpetrators of the attempted assassination named:-
Tsang King Yoong (張金榮)
Wong Ta Siau (王志標)
Tsang and Lee, I also admitted having guilty knowledge of
the offence but denied having participated.

On the 6-5-38, I was removed to the Pootung Military Police
Headquarters and on the 11-5-38 was escorted to the Japanese
Military Police Headquarters at the Bridge House off North Sze-
chuen Road, I was then placed in a No. 5 detention room together
with two other male Chinese named:-
Yang Wing Loong and Zee Tsong Tuh and one Russian name
unknown.

Whilst being detained in the Bridge House I learned from
the Chinese coolie who brought our food, that we were to be shot
on the 12-5-38, we three Chinese then decided to escape.

镇江人，由我 J. S. Bousfield
于1938年5月14日在虹口西区捕房录取，并由

我叫李桂森 (李桂森)，31岁，镇江人。我是浦东永安渡路“建泰昌”酒行的老板，被捕时居住在浦东元庆里3号。

1938年5月1日上午9点左右，我被大道政府浦东分局的侦探逮捕，他们指控我参与了几天前对苏锡文 (蘇錫文) 的爆炸案。被带到政府办公室后，我就爆炸案受到审问，由于我拒绝承认罪行，遭受了往鼻子里灌水和用棍棒殴打身体的酷刑。

由于酷刑，我牵连了另外4名中国男子作为未遂暗杀的实施者，他们是：
张金荣 (Tsang King Yoong)
王志标 (Wong Ta Siau)
曾某和李某，我还承认知晓该罪行，但否认参与。

1938年5月6日，我被移送到浦东宪兵队总部，并于1938年5月11日被押送至四川北路百老汇大厦的日本宪兵队总部。随后我与另外两名中国男子一起被关在第5号拘留室，他们是：
杨文龙 (Yang Wing Loong) 和徐宗土 (Zee Tsong Tuh) 以及一名姓名不详的俄国人。

在百老汇大厦被拘留期间，我从送饭的中国苦力那里得知，我们将于1938年5月12日被枪决，于是我们三名中国人决定逃跑。

The following is the statement of ____ (徐榮德) ____________________
native of __Cootung________________ taken by me __D.C. Hossington________
at __W. H'kan____________ on the __14/__/38_______ and translated by __Mok Ku________

My name is Zee Yoong Tuh, age 26, native of Cootung S/
Unemployed, residing at No. 305 Peking Road. I was born in
Shanghai and was previously employed as a mechanic.
At about 7 a.m. on the 27- -38 I met a friend named Woo
on Nippon Road near Chekiang Road, he informed me that I could
find work as a coolie at the Tse An Zhong Edinburgh Road. I
went to the place mentioned and on arriving there at 11 a.m.
a male Chinese caught hold of me from behind.
Four male Chinese two in front and two at the rear each holding
a pistol then warned me not to shout, a Japanese, then
arrived and took out handcuffs with which he handcuffed me. The
5 then pulled me to the near side of a M/car and forced me
inside. On starting to drive the car one of the Chinese took
out a piece of paper and stuck same in front of the M/car, on
the paper was written two Chinese characters "Hao Ping" (憲兵)
and initials "T.P."
The M/car was driven to the New Asia Hotel on North
Szechuen Road, I was then detained in a room (No. Unknown) on
the 6th floor of the building. I saw about 10 Chinese there
and one of them searched me and took away from my pocket one
leather wallet containing $1.70 in notes and 30 cents in nickel
pieces, one handkerchief and paper. A Japanese wearing foreign
clothes then asked me my name and age, etc. After being ques-
tioned I was locked in a lavatory. At about 3 p.m. same date
I was escorted to the Japanese Headquarters Sing Ku Wei, Woosung
Road where I was detained with 7 Japanese and 8 Chinese in the
same room.

我叫徐荣德 (Zee Yoong Tuh)，26岁，广东顺德人/
无业，居住在北京路305号。我出生于上海，此前受雇为机械师。
1938年__月27日（原文日期残缺）上午7点左右，我在浙江路附近的日本路上遇到一位姓吴的朋友，他告诉我可以在爱丁堡路（今延安东路）的“治安中”找到苦力工作。我去了提到的地方，上午11点到达那里时，一名中国男子从背后抓住了我。
四名中国男子，前面两个后面两个，每人手持一把手枪，警告我不许喊叫，随后一名日本人到来，拿出手铐将我铐住。这五人随后将我拉到一辆摩托车旁，强行将我塞进车内。车子启动时，其中一名中国人拿出一张纸贴在摩托车前方，纸上写着两个汉字“宪兵”和缩写“T.P.”。
摩托车被开到四川北路的新亚酒店，随后我被关在该建筑6楼的一个房间里（房间号不详）。我看到那里大约有10名中国人，其中一人搜了我的身，从我口袋里拿走一个皮夹，里面有1.70元纸币和30分镍币，一块手帕和一些纸张。随后一名穿着西装的日本人询问了我的姓名、年龄等。受审后，我被锁在一间厕所里。当天下午3点左右，我被护送到吴淞路星家卫（Sing Ku Wei，音译，可能指某日本机构或地点）的日本总部，在那里我与7名日本人和8名中国人被关在同一间房里。

On the 2-5-38 I was taken out by a Japanese and questioned,
he then accused me of being a plain clothes soldier, on denying
same, I was slapped about ten times in the face and later
returned to the same room, as the Japanese could not get any
results from the questioning he told me that he would continue
to interrogate me on the following day.

On the 3-5-38 all those who were detained in the Japanese
Headquarters Peking Road were removed to the Bridge House and
I was locked in No. 2 Room together with a Russian and 18 other
Chinese.

On the 5-5-38 I was changed to Room No. 5 of the same
building where one Russian and 5 Chinese were detained. On the
8-5-38 a Japanese came in and took one of the Chinese out
for questioning. I asked him if I was convicted or not, he
replied that I would be put to death the next Monday (16-5-38).

At 10 a.m. on the 9-5-38 the three Chinese with whom I
was detained were taken out by a Japanese and at 5 p.m. same
date one named Yang Vung Loong escorted by a Japanese was
detained in the same room with me. On asking Yang why he was
arrested he stated that the Japanese accused him of being the
leader of a custom staff strike.

At 9 a.m. on the 11-5-38 one named Lee Kwai Sung was
brought in and detained in the room and when asked the reason,
stated that the Japanese accused him of throwing hand grenades.
Yang, Lee and myself then had a meeting and planned to escape.

At 2 a.m. on the 14-5-38 we took away the nails from 2
planks of wood and the two planks of wood from the room wall

1938年5月2日，我被一名日本人带出去审问，他随即指控我是一名便衣士兵，在我否认后，我被打耳光约十次，随后被带回同一房间，由于日本人从审问中未能得到结果，他告诉我第二天将继续审问我。

1938年5月3日，所有被关押在北京路日本总部的人都被转移到百老汇大厦，我与一名俄国人和另外18名中国人一起被关在2号房间。

1938年5月5日，我被换到同一栋楼的5号房间，那里关押着一名俄国人和5名中国人。1938年5月8日，一名日本人进来带走了一名中国人进行审问。我问他我是否已被定罪，他回答说下周一（1938年5月16日）我将被处决。

1938年5月9日上午10点，与我关在一起的那三名中国人被一名日本人带出，当天下午5点，一名叫杨文龙的人在一名日本人的护送下被关进与我相同的房间。我问杨为何被捕，他说日本人指控他是海关职员罢工的领袖。

1938年5月11日上午9点，一名叫李桂森的人被带进来关在房间里，当问及原因时，他说日本人指控他投掷手榴弹。杨、李和我随后开会并计划逃跑。

1938年5月14日凌晨2点，我们从房间墙壁靠近厕所的地方取下了两块木板上的钉子以及这两块木板

（印：SHANGHAI MUNI... / m3 / 20 APR. 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

REFERENCE TWO MALE CHINESE ARRESTED BY JAPANESE MILITARY AT THE FLOATING RESTAURANT, THE BUND.

At 3.45 p.m. 19-4-38, a telephone message was received reporting to the effect that two male Chinese had been arrested by Japanese soldiers and taken onto the Floating Restaurant, Peking Road Jetty, The Bund.

The undersigned and J.D.S. Y.Uruma, Special Branch, proceeded to the Floating Restaurant, The Bund, where it was explained by Cpl. Nakawa that these two male Chinese, (1) Zung Ching Wah (沈金華), 35, Shanghai, M/chauffeur, residing 8 Ching Ying Feng, Edinburgh Road, and (2) his brother named Sung Shing Ching (沈兴全), 27, Shanghai, M/chauffeur, above address, drivers of motor cars Nos. 8117 and 11777, had been loitering upon the jetty and when told to remove themselves by the Japanese sentry had apparently argued consequently they were taken aboard the Floating Restaurant to be questioned and warned.

The 1st named was handed over to the undersigned, as the questioning of this man had been completed.

The undersigned promised to caution this man to keep away from the jetty in future.

Subject Japanese Collecting Wharf Tax on Soochow Creek - press report.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford. I. S.

With reference to the attached press translation
from the Ta Lei Pao dated June 6th, enquiries show that the
levying of wharf taxes on merchandise discharged from boats
moored at jetties in the Jessfield Area, C.C.L. is being
undertaken by the Shanghai Western District Wharf Administra-
tive Section and commenced in the latter part of March, 1938.
(vide Special Branch report dated March 29th). *D80397/35

Tsu Lai-ching, mentioned in the attached press
translation, was appointed Chief of the above organization
but was murdered on April 16th outside the above office,
Jessfield Road, C.C.L., his post was taken by one Tsang Ah
Loh (vide Special Branch report dated June 3rd).

With reference to the name of Kao Yen-ping also
mentioned in the attached press report, enquiries show that
this individual is none other than Kao Yen-zah whose activi-
ties were outlined in a Special Branch report under the
heading of "Inauguration of Shanghai Wharf Coolie Association"
dated April 1st. He has interests also in the Shanghai
Western District Wharf Administrative Section, Jessfield Road,
C.C.L.

To Mei Pao and other local newspapers :- -6 JUNE 1938 A.M.

JAPANESE COLLECTING WHARF TAX ON SOOCHOW CREEK

The Japanese Pacification Section in the Western
District has appointed two Chinese named Tsu Lai-tsing
(朱来青) and Kao Yen-ping (高雁萍) to undertake the
collection of a wharf tax from boats in the Soochow Creek.
The taxes are as under :-
1) A tax of 4 cents on 100 catties of rice.
2) A tax of $5 for a boat carrying cotton.
3) A tax of 5 cents for 100 catties of vegetables.
4) $3 for a large boat carrying firewood, $2 for a medium
boat and $1 for a small boat.
5) A tax of $5 per boat carrying miscellaneous goods.
6) $3 for a large boat carrying coal and charcoal and $2
for a small boat.
7) A tax of 10 cents per ton of sand-stone.
8) $5 per boat carrying bricks.

Japanese members of the Shanghai Municipal Shipping
Control Office functioning in the International Settlement.

With reference to the remarks of the Commissioner
of Police appended to the attached report dated May 26
and submitted by Pootoo Road Station, further enquiries
by detectives attached to Pootoo Road Station and the
Special Branch have resulted in the following information
being forthcoming.

It appears that the Zung Tuh (润德) Wheat Hong,
Lane 30, No.8 Rue Montauban, recently sold to the Foo
Foong (丰丰) Flour Mill, No.126 Mokenahan Road, 1,198
bags of wheat which were stored in godowns in Wusih.
Subsequently, the Zung Tuh Wheat Hong made arrangements
with the Kuo Tai (国泰) Transportation Company, 638
North Soochow Road, whereby the latter company agreed to
transport the wheat to Shanghai at a fee of $2.30 per
bag, all taxes being paid by the transportation company.

On May 24, the Kuo Tai Transportation Company -
the manager of which is a Japanese named Mr. Matano
Tsutomu (堤勉) - transported the wheat by boat direct
to the rear entrance of the Foo Foong Flour Mill, on the
south bank of the Soochow Creek. Prior however to
arriving at the mill, a tax of $0.35 per bag was collected
when the boats were passing the Toyoda Cotton Mill.
It appears that after paying the above mentioned tax,
the boats usually proceed direct to the Wochan Road Bridge
where the cargo and tax receipts are checked by officials
of the Shanghai Municipality Shipping Control Office.

在上海公共租界内运作的上海市政航运管制办公室的日本成员。

关于警务处处长附在普陀路巡捕房提交的5月26日报告后的评语，经普陀路巡捕房和特别处所属侦探进一步查询，获得以下信息。

据悉，位于蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）30弄8号的润德（Zung Tuh）麦行，最近向莫干山路126号的丰丰（Foo Foong）面粉厂出售了1,198袋储存在无锡仓库的小麦。随后，润德麦行与北苏州路638号的国泰（Kuo Tai）运输公司达成协议，由后者以每袋2.30元的费用将小麦运往上海，所有税费由运输公司支付。

5月24日，由日本人堤勉（Matano Tsutomu）先生担任经理的国泰运输公司，用船直接将小麦运至苏州河南岸丰丰面粉厂的后门。然而，在到达面粉厂之前，当船只经过丰田棉纺厂时，每袋被征收0.35元的税款。据悉，在缴纳上述税款后，船只通常直接前往武昌路桥，由上海市政航运管制办公室的官员检查货物和税收收据。

If the receipts and cargo are found to be in order,
the boats are then allowed to proceed to their destination
for unloading after a further payment of an inspection
fee of $0.10 per bag to the Shipping Control Office.

As the cargo of wheat destined for the Foo
Foong Flour Mill had not been inspected and checked by
the aforementioned control office, the three boats in
which the wheat was loaded were towed to the Woochen
Road Bridge, Chapei, by Japanese on May 29.

Following negotiations by the Kuo Tai Transportation
Company with the Shipping Control Office, it was arranged
that following the payment of an inspection fee of
$119.80, the wheat would be delivered to the Foo Foong
Mill by trucks belonging to the above mentioned control
office at a charge of $5.00 per truckload of 50 bags.
This was accordingly done, the wheat being delivered to
the Foo Foong Flour Mill on May 30, all fees and taxes
having been paid by the Kuo Tai Transportation Company.

From the information submitted above it appears
that the loadahs of the boats were at fault in failing
to proceed to Woochen Road. In view of the fact that
the transportation company is a Japanese operated concern,
it would appear probable that the loadah's error has
already been explained to the company by Japanese officials
of the Shanghai Municipality Shipping Control Office.

K. J. Harding

1938年5月26日上午9时45分，莫干山路126号阜豐（Foo Foong）面粉厂的总监督田潼甫（Dien Tung Poo）来到巡捕房报告称，1938年5月25日下午，当小麦从停靠在面粉厂私人码头的苏州河船只上卸载时，日本人进行干涉，两艘部分卸货的船只被他们带走，截至报告时尚未归还。

经赵炳坤（Chao Ping Kun，音译）特别处督察和署名人查询，查明情况如下：-

1938年5月25日上午9时许，3艘载有共计1,100袋小麦的船只从无锡抵达阜豐面粉厂，与其他运麦船只一起停靠在面粉厂的私人码头。

因此，1938年5月25日下午1时，两名麦行代表，即洪佐庭（Hung Tsao Ding）和刘诸標（Lien Shu Piau，音译），抵达面粉厂，开始卸船。

Lieu Shu Piau (廖修標).

Ningpo.                                          Himself.
10.45 am            26.5.38.          translated
                                    xxxxxxxx      Clerk Chin Hung Keng.

My name is Lieu Shu Piau. I am 38 years old and native
of Ningpo. I am employed as a cargo deliverer at Zung Tuh
Wheat Hong, No. 8, Ziang Yue Lee, Rue Montauban, French Town.
At about 1 p.m. on the 25.5.38., I and Hung Tsao Wing,
also a cargo deliverer, were detailed to unload 1,100 bags of
wheat from 3 boats at Foo Foong wharf and deliver same to the
Foo Foong Flour Mill. Between 2 and 3 p.m. when we were
unloading same, I noticed that a Japanese together with a
Chinese alighted from a motor car which they parked outside
Fen Sing No.2 Flour Mill. They came to the wharf where they
prevented the carrying coolies for working and asked me for a
pass. I replied to them that the management of the Zung Tuh
Wheat Hong had negotiated with Koh Tah (高泰) Transportation
Company to convey the wheat from Tientsin, thus all the transport-
ing fees, taxes etc had already been paid to Koh Tah Co by our
hong. I further stated that if anything was wrong, he should
approach the Koh Tah Co. After saying this, I went to the
Wheat Department of the Foo Foong Flour Mill, but the Japanese
followed. He tried to communicate with some place through
telephone but failed to make a connection. Then he and the
Chinese left us and drove away in the car.

About 15 minutes later, this Japanese accompanied by
one other Japanese who wore uniform, one plain clothes Japanese
and two Chinese sailed for this wharf again on a launch. On
seeing them to land, I immediately proceeded to the Wheat
Department of the Foo Foong Flour Mill. However, the Japanese
with whom I conversed before, followed and dragged me to the
pages.zh:
廖修標（Lieu Shu Piau）。

宁波。                                          本人陈述。
上午10:45            1938年5月26日。          翻译
                                    xxxxxxxx      职员陈洪庚（Chin Hung Keng）。

我叫廖修標。今年38岁，籍贯宁波。我在法租界蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）祥悦里8号宗德（Zung Tuh）麦行受雇为送货员。
1938年5月25日下午1点左右，我和同为送货员的洪祖荣（Hung Tsao Wing，音译）被派往福丰码头，从3艘船上卸下1,100袋小麦，并运送至福丰面粉厂。下午2点至3点间，当我们正在卸货时，我注意到一名日本人和一名中国人从一辆停在芬星第二面粉厂（Fen Sing No.2 Flour Mill，音译）外的汽车上下来。他们来到码头，阻止搬运苦力工作，并向我要通行证。我回复他们说，宗德麦行管理层已与高泰（Koh Tah）运输公司协商，由该公司将小麦从天津运来，因此所有运费、税款等已由我行支付给高泰公司。我进一步表示，如果有任何问题，他应去找高泰公司。说完这些，我去了福丰面粉厂的小麦部，但那名日本人跟了过来。他试图通过电话与某地联系，但未能接通。随后他和那名中国人离开我们，驾车离去。

大约15分钟后，这名日本人陪同另一名身穿制服的日本人、一名便衣日本人和两名中国人，再次乘坐汽艇来到本码头。看到他们登陆，我立即前往福丰面粉厂的小麦部。然而，之前与我交谈的那名日本人跟了上来，并将我拖到

pages.en:
Sheet 2.

wharf, where he asked me the whereabouts of the responsible
man of the Koh Tah Transportation Co. At the same time, he
smacked me on my face twice and ordered me to re-load the wheat
onto the boats again. Having agreed to this, I promised to
negotiate with the Foo Foong Flour Mill authorities, but
instead, left the mill via the front gate returned to my hang.
I don't know what happened afterwards. The occurrence was
reported by the Foo Foong Flour Mill.
This is my true statement.

signed. Lieu Shu Piau.

码头，在那里他问我合德（Koh Tak，音译，前文作Koh Tah/Koh Teh）运输公司负责人的下落。同时，他扇了我两记耳光，并命令我将小麦重新装回船上。我对此表示同意，承诺与福丰面粉厂当局协商，但我反而从前门离开工厂，回到了我的行号。之后发生了什么我不知道。此事件由福丰面粉厂报告。

Hung Tsoo Ding (洪祖定)。
Ningpo.                                          Himself.
10.45 am            26.5.38.          translated    Clerk Chin Hung Kong.
                                      XXXXX

My name is Hung Tsoo Ding. I am 32 years of age
and native of Ningpo. I am employed as a cargo deliverer
at Zung ruh (崇裕) wheat Hong, No. 8 Ziang Yue Lee, Rue
Montauban, French Concession.

At about 1 p.m. 25.5.38., I and Lieu Shu Piau
were detailed to unload 1,100 bags of wheat from 3 boats at
Foo Foong Wharf. Between 2 and 3 p.m. when we were unloading
same, I observed a Japanese and a Chinese alighted from a moto
car which they parked at the entrance of Foh Sing No. 2 Flour
Mill and came to the wharf. They conversed with Lieu Shu Piau
but I could not hear what was being said other than the Japan-
ese asking Lieu for a pass. Later, I saw a launch coming
towards us in which there was a Japanese who wore uniform, 2
plain clothes Japanese and 2 Chinese. After they had landed,
the Plain clothes Japanese dragged Lieu Shu Piau out of the
wheat department of the Foo Foong Flour Mill and asked him
for the responsible man of the Koh Tak (合德) Transportation
Co. As Lieu was unable to locate the wanted man, the Japanese
smacked Lieu's face twice. I being afraid of the occurrence
immediately went to the Accounting Office of the Foo Foong
Mill so I don't know what happened afterwards. However, when
I came out of the mill, I found 2 boats partly loaded with
wheat were out of sight. Later the Foo Foong Flour Mill
reported the occurrence to the Police.

This is my true statement.

Signed, Hung Tsoo Ding.

宁波。                                          本人陈述。
上午10:45            1938年5月26日。          翻译    职员陈洪康（Chin Hung Kong，音译）。

我叫洪祖定。今年32岁，籍贯宁波。我在法租界蒙托邦路祥悦里8号崇裕（Zung ruh）麦行受雇为送货员。

1938年5月25日下午1点左右，我和廖修標被派往福丰码头，从3艘船上卸下1,100袋小麦。下午2点至3点间，当我们正在卸货时，我看到一名日本人和一名中国人从一辆停在佛星第二面粉厂（Foh Sing No. 2 Flour Mill，音译）入口处的汽车上下来，来到码头。他们与廖修標交谈，但我听不清他们在说什么，只听到日本人向廖氏索要通行证。后来，我看到一艘汽艇向我们驶来，船上有一名身穿制服的日本人、2名便衣日本人和2名中国人。他们登陆后，那名便衣日本人将廖修標从福丰面粉厂小麦部拖出来，向他索要合德（Koh Tak）运输公司的负责人。由于廖氏无法找到所需之人，该日本人扇了廖氏两记耳光。我因害怕此事，立即去了福丰面粉厂的会计室，所以我不知道之后发生了什么。然而，当我走出工厂时，我发现两艘部分装载小麦的船只已不见踪影。后来福丰面粉厂向警方报告了此事。

这是我的真实陈述。

签名：洪祖定。

Sung Yee Shiang (宋義祥)。
An'wei.                                         Himself.
10.45 am            26.5.38.       Translated by   Chin Hung Keng.
                                     XXX

My name is Sung Yee Shiang. I am 33 years of age,
native of An'wei and residing at 29, Foo Foong Li, Yokanahan
Road. I am employed as Manager of the Wheat Department of the
Foo Foong Flour Mill.
    Between 3 and 4 p.m. on the 25.5.38., when I was
working in my office, a Japanese wearing foreign style suit
approached me ordering that the 416 bags of wheat bought
from Zung Tuh (宗德) Wheat Hong be returned to the original
boats in Soochow Creek. He stated that the reason for them
doing so is due to the fact that Zung Tuh Wheat Hong had not
paid the necessary taxes. I admitted that the wheat was bought
from the said hong by us, but we were not aware that taxes
had not been paid. He then again ordered me to return the
wheat. I told him that we had mixed the other wheat and stored
same in the godown. I then requested him to receive some other
wheat of same quality and weight as we could not return the
original wheat. He agreed to this suggestion and went away.
Then I instructed the coolies of this mill to place 416 bags
of wheat outside the Wheat Department of this mill (near the
Bamboo fence) and await his return. However, he failed to
come back from that time. I don't know what happened after-
wards. The occurrence was reported to the Police by Bien
Tung Poo, the General Supervisor of our mill.
    This is my true statement.

                                        signed: Sung Yee Shiang.
pages.zh:
宋义祥（Sung Yee Shiang）。
安徽。                                         本人陈述。
上午10:45            1938年5月26日。       翻译者   陈洪庚（Chin Hung Keng）。
                                     XXX

我叫宋义祥。今年33岁，籍贯安徽，居住在姚家弄路（Yokanahan Road，音译）福丰里29号。我在福丰面粉厂受雇为小麦部经理。
    1938年5月25日下午3点至4点间，当我在办公室工作时，一名身穿西式西装的日本人走近我，命令将从宗德（Zung Tuh）麦行购买的416袋小麦退回苏州河上的原船。他声称这样做的原因是宗德麦行未缴纳必要税款。我承认我们确实从该商号购买了小麦，但我们并不知道税款未缴。他再次命令我退回小麦。我告诉他，我们将小麦与其他小麦混合并存放在仓库中。随后我请求他接收一些其他同等质量和重量的小麦，因为我们无法退回原始小麦。他同意了这一建议并离开。然后我指示本厂苦力将416袋小麦放置在本厂小麦部外（靠近竹篱笆处），等待他回来。然而，从那以后他再也没有回来。之后发生了什么我不知道。此事件由本厂总主管边东浦（Bien Tung Poo，音译）报告给警方。
    这是我的真实陈述。

                                        签名：宋义祥。

BUREAU OF PREVENTION OF EVASION OF PAYMENT OF DUTIES

Being practically devoid of revenue, the
"Reformed Government of the Chinese Republic," since its
establishment in Nanking, has been constantly in conflict
with the Dah Dae City Government over the question of
jurisdiction over the various revenue collecting organs
in Shanghai.

It is learned that an agreement has now
been reached between these two administrations over this
question, whereby another revenue collecting bureau known
as "The Bureau of Prevention Against Evasion of Payment
of Duties," in addition to the one established at the
Toyoda Cotton Mill, was established last week in Chapel
near the Wucheng Road Bridge (**〔此处转录不清〕**). All revenues
collected by this new bureau are to be handled by the
"Reformed Government of the Chinese Republic". All goods
coming to Shanghai from inland ports by boats must be
discharged at the Wucheng Road Bridge pending transportation
to their respective destinations by the motor trucks of
this new revenue collecting bureau. The charges for
this service are remitted to the new government in Nanking.

27
f220
/3 8-38

标准日期：1938年4月28日（上午）

防止逃漏税捐局

由于几乎没有任何财政收入，“中华民国维新政府”自南京成立以来，一直就上海各征税机构的管辖权问题与大都市政府（Dah Dae City Government，音译，疑指上海市政府或相关机构）发生冲突。

据悉，双方行政当局现已就此问题达成协议，除此前在丰田棉纱厂设立的机构外，上周又在武昌路桥附近的教堂（Chapel，音译，或指具体地名）**〔此处转录不清〕**设立了另一个名为“防止逃漏税捐局”的征税机构。该新局征收的所有税款均由南京的“中华民国维新政府”处理。所有从内地港口经水路运抵上海的商品，必须在武昌路桥卸货，待由该新征税机构的汽车卡车转运至各自目的地。此项服务的费用汇交至南京的新政府。

West Hongkew Station, S-38
REPORT
Date May 10th, 19 38
Subject Attempt by Japanese to Prevent Unloading of Boats Moored to S.M.C. Jetty.
Made by D.S. Gibson. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 4.50 p.m. 10-5-38 telephone message was received from the Two Press Packing Co., 546 North Soochow Rd., reporting that Japanese were preventing unloading of cotton from boats tied up to the S.M.C. Jetty outside their Godown.

Inspector Trodd, D.S. Gibson, F.B.I. King Woo, and C.D.C. 222 immediately proceeded to the scene where enquiries were made.

It was ascertained that about 3.15 p.m. three motor trucks loaded with bales of cotton arrived outside the Two Godown, the trucks having brought the cotton from a steamer moored at the Bund. The cotton is owned by a cotton dealer, Chu Ying Sung (周慶生), Room No. 467, 500 Avenue Edward VII.

At the same time a river junk also loaded with cotton which had been brought from Foochow, tied up to the S.M.C. Jetty outside the Two Godown. The cotton in the boat is owned by a dealer, Tsang Yoong Yin (張永), 77/83 Avenue Edward VII.

（印：RECD 11 MAY '38 S.M.P.）

On coolies commencing to unload the cotton from the trucks and the junk about 3.30 p.m. and take it into the Two Godown, a Japanese, dressed in civilian clothing, arrived at the S.M.C. Jetty having come on a boat on the Soochow Creek from the West.

The Japanese approached Chu Ying Sung, the owner of the cotton on the motor trucks, and, stating that he was an official of the Tao Tao Government, demanded to know if any tax had been paid. Chu Ying Sung replied that the Customs tax had been paid but that the receipts were in the possession of one, Woo Tsang Chi (何昌期).

The Japanese then instructed the coolies that the cotton could not be unloaded from either the trucks or the boat.

dcsb

事由 日本人试图阻止停靠在工部局码头的船只卸货。
报告人 D.S. Gibson。转呈人 [签名]

先生：

1938年5月10日下午4时50分，接北苏州路546号 Two Press Packing Co.（两丰打包公司）电话报告称，日本人正在阻止在其仓库外停靠在工部局码头的船只卸载棉花。

特罗德巡官（Inspector Trodd）、D.S. Gibson、F.B.I. King Woo 以及 C.D.C. 222 立即赶赴现场进行调查。

经查实，下午3时15分左右，三辆装载棉包的卡车抵达 Two Godown（两丰仓库）外，这些棉花是从停泊在外滩的一艘轮船上运来的。该批棉花属于棉商周慶生（Chu Ying Sung），地址为爱德华七世路500号467室。

与此同时，一艘同样装载着从福州运来棉花的内河驳船也停靠在 Two Godown 外的工部局码头。船上的棉花属于商人張永（Tsang Yoong Yin），地址为爱德华七世路77/83号。

（印：1938年5月11日收悉 上海公共租界工部局警务处）

下午3时30分左右，当苦力开始从卡车和驳船上卸下棉花并搬入 Two Godown 时，一名身穿便服的日本人乘船从西边沿苏州河而来，抵达工部局码头。

该日本人走近卡车上棉花的所有者周慶生，声称自己是“道道政府”（Tao Tao Government）的官员，要求知晓是否已缴纳税款。周慶生回答说海关税已缴纳，但收据在何昌期（Woo Tsang Chi）手中。

随后，该日本人指示苦力不得从卡车或船上卸载棉花。

Sir,

    With reference to the above I beg to report that at
1.45 p.m. 12-4-38, a telephone message was received from
Lieutenant Kenglar, U.S.M.C. stationed at the Ichang Road
S.F.B. Station to the effect that a very large number of
boats were being stopped and/or turned back by the Japanese
soldiers on the north side of the creek.

    A J.P.C. and a C.D.C. along with F.S. Sims were sent
to enquire as to the sudden influx of boats into this area.
    The D.O. "B" had also been informed by the U.S.M. Corps
and attended the scene as did the undersigned but despite
diligent and prolonged enquiries the exact reason for the
influx of boats and stoppage by the Japanese Military could
not be learned.

    The following rumours were obtained but without
confirmation:

    1. That hostilities had re-commenced in the vicinity
       of Soochow.

       as to levies to be paid by the boatmen.

    3. That the Dah Tao Government (per Japanese Authorities)
       had arrived at an understanding re levies with the
       boatmen who were being held up on the Creek above
       "Pok Shing Ching" area and that as the fees were
       paid the boats were being released.

Louza Station,
REPORT
Date April 19th, 19 38.

Subject re Japanese soldiers instructing boatmen on the Soochow Creek.

Made by D.C. 10 MacLennan Forwarded by Chief Inspector.

Sir,

At 6.10.p.m. 19-4-38, a telephone message was received from C. .C.1179, through street telephone box No.1, to the effect that Japanese soldiers were preventing Chinese boatmen from unloading rice on the Soochow Creek.

C.D.C.336 and the undersigned immediately attended but the soldiers had already departed.

Enquiries revealed that at about 6.p.m. 19-4-38, a private motor car, Lic. No. unknown, stopped on North Soochow Road, about 60 yards East of Yu Ya Ching Road Bridge (West Hongkew District) and from it two Japanese soldiers and one Chinese Interpreter alighted and crossed over the boats to the centre of the Creek. The Chinese Interpreter then instructed numerous boatmen that in future they were to cease unloading rice from boats in that section of the creek and were to unload the rice at the Wucheng Road Bridge, Chapei. This latter bridge is located about 100 yards West of Yu Ya Ching Road Bridge. The two soldiers and Interpreter then returned to the M/Car and proceeded East on North Soochow Road.

Referring to Louza Misc. Report No.298/38, dated 17-4-38, two shots are said to have been fired from a Japanese Military launch on the Soochow Creek near Chekiang Road Bridge at about 8.30.a.m. 17-4-38 apparently due to boat congestion in that area preventing the Japanese launch from making progress.

It is therefore possible that to-day's instructions to the boatmen were given as a means of lessening the mass of boats in the vicinity of Chekiang and Yu Ya Ching Road Bridges in order that Japanese launches might have more freedom.

事由 关于日本士兵在苏州河指示船民一事。

报告人 D.C. 10 MacLennan 转呈人 总巡官。

先生：

1938年4月19日下午6时10分，通过1号街头电话亭接到 C. .C.1179 的电话报告，称日本士兵正在阻止中国船民在苏州河卸载大米。

C.D.C.336 和签署人立即赶赴现场，但士兵已经离开。

调查显示，1938年4月19日下午6时许，一辆车牌号不详的私人汽车停在北苏州路，位于虞洽卿路桥（西虹口区）以东约60码处，两名日本士兵和一名中国翻译从车上下来，跨过船只来到河道中央。随后，这名中国翻译指示众多船民，今后不得在该河段从船上卸载大米，而应将大米卸在闸北的武进路桥。后者位于虞洽卿路桥以西约100码处。这两名士兵和翻译随后返回汽车，沿北苏州路向东驶去。

参照1938年4月17日的老闸杂项报告第298/38号，据说1938年4月17日上午8时30分左右，一艘日本军用汽艇在浙江路桥附近的苏州河上开了两枪，显然是因为该区域船只拥堵阻碍了日本汽艇的前进。

因此，今天对船民的指令可能是为了减少浙江路和虞洽卿路桥附近的大量船只，以便日本汽艇能有更多的行动自由。

（左侧批注及印章）：
SI
有任何评论吗？

"130. 156/38          """
                        Ginza
                        April 21st,      '38.

At 4.23 p.m. 21/4/'38, telephone message was re-
ceived from C.I.C. 3078 that Japanese had arrived in a
Motor Car on West Soochow Road near Markham Road Bridge,
had boarded one of the boats and arrested a male Chinese
taking him away with them.

Immediate enquiries by D.S.I. Head and C.D.3. 19
ascertained the following.

The Japanese is the same person according to boatmen
as referred to in Diary 1. (Mr. H. Inouye) and at the time
was wearing the yellow coloured uniformed of the Tao Tao
Government.

At about 4.15 p.m. the above Japanese arrived in
motor car S.D.P. (number unknown) together with two other
Japanese in plain clothes and 1 Chinese in plain clothes,
besides the chauffeur. The car was stopped about 75 yards
East of Markham Road Bridge where all but the chauffeur
left the car and went on to three 'wood' boats tied along-
side. They arrested the Loadah, Ying Kyi Vang (杨其旺) and
escorted him to the car and drove away. C.P.C. 3078
witnessed this from Markham Road Bridge but was too far
away to obtain the number of the car, though he knows same
bore an S.D.P. plate.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH / 22 APR. 1938 / MB）

（批：D.C.S.B. / ... / 2214. / ...）

"130. 156/38          """
                        银座（Ginza）
                        1938年4月21日。

1938年4月21日下午4时23分，接到中央情报科（C.I.C.）3078号电话报告称，日本人乘坐一辆汽车抵达靠近马克汉路（Markham Road，今海宁路）桥的西苏州路，登上其中一艘船，逮捕了一名中国男子并将其带走。

经警司处长（D.S.I.）Head和刑事侦缉处第三科（C.D.3.）19号立即调查，查明情况如下。

据船夫指认，该日本人与日记1中提及者为同一人（H. Inouye先生），当时身穿“大道政府”的黄色制服。

下午4时15分左右，上述日本人乘坐一辆特别市警察局（S.D.P.）牌照的汽车（号码不详）抵达，车上除司机外，还有两名便衣日本人和一名便衣中国人。汽车在马克汉路桥以东约75码处停下，除司机外所有人下车，走向停靠在旁边的三艘“木”船。他们逮捕了船老大杨其旺（Ying Kyi Vang），将其押送至汽车并驾车离去。中央巡逻警员（C.P.C.）3078从马克汉路桥目击了这一过程，但因距离过远未能记下汽车号码，不过他确知该车悬挂特别市警察局（S.D.P.）牌照。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 特务处 / 1938年4月22日 / MB）

Misc. 1 /70                                                                 Sino

2 (Sheet 2)

Tsang Ching Teu (曾正斗) also attached to the boat
arrived during enquiry and stated he had already been to
the office of the Japanese in Ch'pei (North of Wuchen Road
Bridge) and had paid $30.00 fine for the release of Ying
Kyi Vung, so effecting his release though Ying Kyi Vung had
not returned to the boat at the time of enquiry.

Tsang Ching Teu stated that the $30.00 fine had been
imposed because a tax of $35.00 per truck load of wood
(unloaded and transported in the International Settlement)
had not been paid.

In explanation of this tax it was learnt that these
boats had been first ordered to tie up on the Tao Tao
Government side of the creek but as $10.00 tax per boat
was paid, the removal was not insisted upon. The expense
of unloading cargo on Tao Tao Government side of the creek
is fixed at $10.00 per truck load hire plus $15.00 per
truck load tax. ($35.00 in all). Should the boatmen elect
to unship their goods on the Settlement side and even
though they use transport which they pay for, The Tao Tao
Government still insist on the $35.00 per truck load being
handed to them. In the event of non payment the action
taken of arrest and demand for release as shown above, is
resorted to.
pages.zh:
杂项 1 /70                                                                 中文

2（第2页）

曾正斗（Tsang Ching Teu）也随船抵达，在调查期间到达并陈述，他已前往闸北（吴淞江桥以北）的日本人办事处，支付了30.00美元罚款以释放杨其旺（Ying Kyi Vung），从而使其获释，尽管在调查时杨其旺尚未返回船上。

曾正斗称，处以30.00美元罚款的原因是未支付每卡车木材35.00美元的税款（在公共租界内卸货并运输）。

关于此项税款的解释获悉，这些船只最初被命令停靠在河道的大道政府一侧，但由于每艘船支付了10.00美元税款，当局未坚持要求移泊。在河道的大道政府一侧卸货的费用定为每卡车租金10.00美元加上每卡车税款15.00美元（共计35.00美元）。如果船主选择在租界一侧卸货，即使使用自行付费的运输工具，大道政府仍坚持要求向其缴纳每卡车35.00美元。如不支付，则采取上述逮捕并要求赎人的行动。

With reference to the notation by D.C.(Special Branch)
in connection with the report from Louza Station(308/38)
dated April 19, to the effect that on April 19, two Japanese
soldiers, accompanied by a Chinese interpreter had instructed
the boatmen berthed at Yu Ya Ching Road Bridge(West Hongkew
district) to proceed to Wuchen Road Bridge, Chapei, and unload,
instead of at the jetties in Louza district; the following
information has been obtained:-

Commencing from April 19 all boats arriving at Shanghai
via Soochow Creek loaded with commodities including rice, will
be required to unload at the Wuchen Road Bridge, Chapei, and
the owners of such cargoes will be obliged to pay the unloading
and delivery charges which will be assessed at $40.00 per
truckload. The charges which will be strictly enforced, are
paid to an office situated in a shed near the Wuchen Road
Bridge, which is staffed by several Chinese and Japanese
subjects in plain clothes and outdoor parties from this office
patrol the Creek in small boats compelling all boatmen to
remove to Wuchen Road Bridge to unload(Vide Louza reports,
308/38, D. 8220; Sinsa, Misc. 156/38; Central Misc. 443/38).

Discreet enquiries have been carried out and show
that the so-called "Shanghai Municipality Shipping Control
Office(上海市船舶管理處)," situated at Meng Foong Road
Bridge, Chapei, is responsible for the collection of these
taxes. This office was established by one named Teong(董),
nicknamed "Long Feet An Wen(長脚阿文)," a notorious loafer
in Chapei, who, it is reported, has secured the backing of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters by promising to pay
the Naval Authorities $10,000 per quarter irrespective of the

由 _______ 和 _______ 制作，由警司 Crawford 转呈

（左侧手写批注：档案 308. 6）
（左侧手写批注：附两份副本）
（左侧手写批注：CPA D.C.(a)）

（左侧手写批注：E. 副本送 D.M? 3/6 P.A to D G D 8.55）

鉴于特务处主管（D.C.）就老闸捕房（Louza Station）于4月19日提交的报告（308/38）所作的批示，该报告称4月19日，两名日本士兵在一名中国翻译的陪同下，指令停泊在虹口区西段俞家泾路桥（Yu Ya Ching Road Bridge）的船夫前往闸北吴淞江桥卸货，而非在老闸区的码头卸货；现获得以下信息：

自4月19日起，所有经苏州河抵达上海并装载包括大米在内的货物的船只，均被要求在闸北吴淞江桥卸货，此类货物的所有者必须支付卸货及交付费用，标准为每卡车40.00美元。这些费用将被严格执行，支付给位于吴淞江桥附近棚屋内的一处办事处，该办事处由数名便衣中日人员任职，并从该办事处派出外勤小组乘坐小船在河道巡逻，强迫所有船夫移至吴淞江桥卸货（参见老闸报告，308/38，D. 8220；Sinza，杂项 156/38；中央杂项 443/38）。

经 discreet enquiries（审慎调查）显示，所谓的“上海市船舶管理处”，位于闸北孟福路（Meng Foong Road，音译）桥，负责征收这些税款。该办事处由一名姓董（Teong）、绰号“长脚阿文”的人建立，此人是闸北著名的游手好闲之徒，据报道，他通过承诺无论该办事处征收的税款收入如何，每季度向日本海军当局支付10,000美元，从而获得了日本海军陆战队司令部的支持。

Central Station,
REPORT
Date April 25th, 1938.

Subject Japanese functioning on Soochow Road.

Made by/ ____ and ____ Forwarded by Inspector Browning.

Sir,
At 9.05 a.m. 24-4-38, C.P.C. 2621 informed the Station,
Japanese in plain clothes but wearing military caps, had
arrested a Chinese male on Soochow Road near Honan Road Bridge.
D.J.I. Ross, J.D.C. Kobayashi and C.I.C. 260 investigated,
ascertaining that a number of Japanese in an unlicensed M/Car
had at about 9 a.m. arrested at the S.M.C. Loading Jetty, on
Soochow Road a few yards west of Honan Road Bridge, proceeded
to the Jetty and arrested one Koo Sen Wen, 43, Paoshan,
M/Merchant, residing at Paoshan for alleged non-payment of
taxes to the "Ta Tao Government. The investigating officers
found in the above M/Car another Chinese one Chuen Tsoong Fah,
63, Pootung, M/Boatman, residing Tsingpoo, who had been arrest-
ed earlier by the same Japanese party on Soochow Road west
of Chekiang Road Bridge, for alleged non-payment of taxes. The
Japanese responsible for the detention of the two named Chinese
was learned to be K. Tagawa attached to the Nishimwa Section
of the Japanese Military Special Service Mission as an
instructor in the Chapel District of the Ta Tao Government
(Revenue Section) with an office at 719 Dixwell Road. The two
named Chinese were late released to the custody of the S.M.P.
on the instruction of Mr. Yoshizaki also of the named Special
Service Section and after enquiries at Central Station were
released on instructions of D.O. "A" Division.

〔此处转录不清〕 Inspt.
Officer-in-charge.

D.O. "A" Division.
Special Branch.
25/4.

先生，
1938年4月24日上午9时05分，中央巡逻警员（C.P.C.）2621通知捕房，在靠近河南路桥的苏州路上，有身穿便衣但戴军帽的日本人逮捕了一名中国男子。副督察 Ross、日籍侦探 Kobayashi 和中央情报科（C.I.C.）260进行了调查，查明上午9时许，一群日本人乘坐一辆无牌机动车，在河南路桥以西几码处的苏州路工部局装卸码头，逮捕了一名顾森文（Koo Sen Wen），43岁，宝山籍，商人，居住于宝山，涉嫌未向“大道政府”缴纳税款。调查人员在上述机动车内发现另一名中国人全宗法（Chuen Tsoong Fah，音译），63岁，浦东籍，船夫，居住于青浦（Tsingpoo，音译），他此前因同样涉嫌未缴纳税款，在浙江路桥以西的苏州路上被同一伙日本人逮捕。据悉，负责拘留这两名中国人的日本人是川田（K. Tagawa，音译），隶属于日本军事特务团西村组（Nishimwa Section，音译），担任大道政府闸北区（税务科）指导员，办公地点位于狄思威路（Dixwell Road，今溧阳路）719号。这两名中国人后来根据同属该特务团的吉崎（Yoshizaki，音译）先生的指示，移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）监管，并在中央捕房查询后，根据“A”分区警务总监（D.O.）的指示予以释放。

〔此处转录不清〕 巡官。
主管警官。

“A”分区警务总监。
特务处。
4月25日。

This call for assistance was responded to by F.S.237
Yablonsky and S.I.C.141C, and immediately the facts were
known ... Yablonsky ordered that the station be informed.

The male Chinese detained at the S.M.C. Landing Jetty
proved to be one named Foo Sen Wen (傅守文), 43, Paehhan,
m/merchant, residing at Baoshan. When questioned Foo Sen
Wen stated that, at about 8.40 a.m. 24-4-38 he brought 12
piculs of rice in sacks to the above jetty in a cargo
junk from Baoshan. The laodah of this cargo junk is one
named Lee Mao An (徐敖). Prior to leaving Baoshan Foo
Sen Wen paid the sum of $4.80 tax to the Baoshan Hsien
Autonomy Committee Branch Office, at Yoh Pu (杨浦), Paehhan
and received a receipt authorizing him to transport the
rice to Shanghai. The rice was transported to Shanghai
via the Whangpoo River and entered the Soochow Creek at
the Garden Bridge. When the junk was alongside the S.M.C.
Jetty arrangements were made to unload the rice, and
after 15 sacks were unloaded a motorcar arrived on the
scene. Foo Sen Wen states that two male Chinese alighted
from the motorcar and asked for the owner of the rice, and
upon his claiming ownership the two men attempted to push
him into the motorcar.

A typewritten copy of a statement made by Foo Sen Wen
pages.zh:
杂项443/38(C)

1（第2页）

哨子以求援助。

FS.237 Yablonsky（音译）和 SIC.141C 响应了这次求助呼叫，并在立即了解事实后……Yablonsky 下令通知捕房。

在工部局登陆码头被扣留的中国男子经查名为傅守文（Foo Sen Wen），43岁，宝山（Paehhan，音译）籍，商人，居住于宝山。经讯问，傅守文陈述，1938年4月24日上午8时40分左右，他用一艘来自宝山的货驳船将12担袋装大米运至上述码头。该货驳船的船老大名为徐敖（Lee Mao An，注：原文拼音Lee对应李，但中文名给的是徐，此处依原文括号内中文译出，或为OCR/记录错误，暂按原文括号处理）。在离开宝山之前，傅守文向位于杨浦（Yoh Pu）的宝山县自治委员会办事处支付了4.80美元税款，并收到一张授权他将大米运往上海的收据。大米经黄浦江运至上海，在外白渡桥进入苏州河。当驳船靠岸工部局码头时，安排了卸米事宜，在卸下15袋后，一辆汽车抵达现场。傅守文称，两名中国男子从汽车上下来，询问大米的主人，在他声称所有权后，这两人试图将他推入汽车。

一份由傅守文所作陈述的打字副本

pages.en:
Misc 443/38 (C,
1 (Sheet 3)

In connection with the affair, and another by the laodah
of the junk, see who on. is attached. Also attached are
copies of the statements made by the police officers
participating in the incident.
On the motorcar was found another male Chinese Chuer
Tsoong 蔡中宗, cox, boatman, residing at
Tsingloo, who when questioned this man also claimed that
he had been detained by the police. It appears that he
brought in his boat from Singpoo 800 bundles of Chinese
toilet paper for sale in Shanghai. At Suchong Road
bridge he paid the sum of $12.00 tax on this paper to the
representatives of the Lah Lao Government and obtained
for the amount a receipt which was handed to the laodah,
of the junk. At about 8 a.m. 24-4-38 the junk tied along
side a jetty at North Soochow Road, west of Chekiang
Road or edge (West Hongkew District) and unloading
operations were started. Sometime afterwards two male
Chinese approached and requested to meet the owner of the
cargo. When Chuen Tseong Ah came forward they asked to
be shown the tax receipt, but in the meantime the laodah
had left the junk and the receipt could not be produced.
This resulted in the men pushing him into a motorcar and
he was then driven to Naman Road Bridge, along Settlement
roads.
pages.zh:
Misc 443/38 (C,
1 (第3页)

关于此事，以及该舢板船老大（laodah）的另一份陈述，见附件。此外，还附上了参与此事件的警官所作的陈述副本。
在汽车上发现另一名中国男子蔡中宗（Chuer Tsoong），职业为船夫，居住在青浦（Tsingloo）。在接受询问时，该男子也声称曾被警方拘留。据悉，他用船从新浦（Singpoo）运来800捆中国卫生纸到上海出售。在苏州路桥，他向“拉老政府”（Lah Lao Government，原文如此，疑为大刀会或伪政权之误译）的代表支付了该批纸张的税款12.00元，并获得了一张收据，该收据已交给舢板船的老大。1938年4月24日上午8点左右，该舢板停靠在浙江路以西的北苏州路码头旁（虹口西区边缘），并开始卸货。过了一会儿，两名中国男子上前要求见货主。当钱宗发（Chuen Tseong Ah，音译）上前时，他们要求查看纳税收据，但此时船老大已离开舢板，无法出示收据。结果，这些人将他推入一辆汽车，随后沿着租界道路将其驱至纳曼路桥（Naman Road Bridge）。

pages.en:
Misc.443/38(C)
1 Sheet 4.

At Central Station Chuen Soong Fah produced a
receipt to show that he had also paid the sum of $7.50
to the Chinese Maritime Customs Branch Office, 496 North
Soochow Road, in connection with the paper, and had been
issued with a Clearance Certificate by that authority.
A translated copy of the statement made by Chuen
Soong Fah in connection with the incident is attached.
It was learned that the Japanese responsible for
detaining the two Chinese was one named K. Tagawa,
attached to the Nishimura section of the Japanese
Military Special Service Mission, the headquarters of
which is situated at 719 Dixwell Road, as an instructor
in the Chapei District of the Ta Tao Government (Revenue
Section).
When questioned K. Tagawa stated a number of cargo
junks had failed to obtain the necessary passes from the
Ta Tao Government to permit them sail on the Soochow
Creek and had also failed to pay tax to the authority
for the cargo transported in the boats. They had located
the two Chinese described above and had requested them to
attend the Revenue Branch Station, at Suchang Road,
Chapei, to instruct them regarding the procedure, and to
obtain passes and pay taxes. Unfortunately, When Kee Ser
Yen was visited on board the junk at Honan Road Bridge
pages.zh:
Misc.443/38(C)
1 第4页。

在中央巡捕房，钱松法（Chuen Soong Fah，音译）出示了一张收据，表明他就该批纸张已向位于北苏州路496号的中国海关分支办事处支付了7.50元，并由该机构签发了结关证书。
附上钱松法就此事所作陈述的翻译副本。
经查，负责拘留这两名中国人的日本人名为K. Tagawa，隶属于日本军方特务机关西村组（Nishimura section），该机关总部设在狄思威路719号，其身份是大道政府（Ta Tao Government）闸北区（担任教官）（税务科）。
在接受询问时，K. Tagawa称，有多艘货船未能从大道政府获得必要的通行证以允许其在苏州河航行，也未就船上运输的货物向当局缴纳税款。他们找到了上述两名中国人，并要求他们前往闸北苏州路的大道政府税务分所，以便向他们指导相关程序，并办理通行证及缴纳税款。不幸的是，当他们在河南路桥登上舢板拜访季森炎（Kee Ser Yen，音译）时，

pages.en:
Misc.443/38(C)

1 (Sheet 5,

he decamped onto the jetty, and at this juncture the
Chinese constable attended.

While the investigation was in progress Mr. Yoshizaki
attached to the Japanese Military Special Service Mission
719 Dixwell Road, arrived on the scene in motorcar Lic.
No.B.L.F.299. This gentleman, who was wearing Special
Service Mission uniform at the time, stated that he had
instructed his subordinates that the Chinese who infring-
ed the regulations must not be detained but requested to
attend the Revenue Sub Station. Mr. Yoshizaki instructed
that the two Chinese could be released from custody.

It was pointed out to Mr. Yoshizaki that his
subordinates were infringing the rights of the Internat-
ional Settlement by arresting persons suspected of evading
payments of taxes, without first applying for the
necessary assistance, and that these actions must cease.

Messrs Yoshizaki and Tagawa refused to attend
Central Station, and were permitted to go.

The two Chinese who had been detained, Kee San Wen
and Chuen Taeong Ph, were taken to Central Station. The
laodah of the cargo junk, Zee Mao An, was also called to
the Station for enquiries.

The Officer-in-charge, Inspector Browning,
communicated the facts of the case to Mr. H.B.M. Roberts
D.O. "A" Division, who instructed that when enquiries
pages.zh:
Misc.443/38(C)

1 (第5页,

他逃窜至码头上，就在此时，中国巡捕赶到。

在调查进行期间，隶属于狄思威路719号日本军方特务机关的吉崎先生（Mr. Yoshizaki，音译）乘坐牌照号为B.L.F.299的汽车抵达现场。这位当时身穿特务机关制服的绅士表示，他曾指示下属，不得拘留违反规定的中国人，而应要求其前往税务分所。吉崎先生指示释放这两名被拘留的中国人。

有人向吉崎先生指出，他的下属在未首先申请必要协助的情况下，逮捕涉嫌逃税的人员，侵犯了国际租界的权利，必须停止此类行为。

吉崎先生和Tagawa先生拒绝前往中央巡捕房，获准离开。

两名被拘留的中国人，季三文（Kee San Wen，音译）和钱东发（Chuen Taeong Ph，音译），被带往中央巡捕房。货船的老大郑毛安（Zee Mao An，音译）也被召至巡捕房接受问询。

值班督察官Browning将案情通报给“A”分区助理总监H.B.M. Roberts先生，后者指示，在完成问询后，

pages.en:
MISC.440/36
1 (Sheet 6)

were any later, the two Chinese should be granted their
freedom.

J.D.S. Kobayashi communicated with Sgt. Major Kanno,
who had previously been informed regarding a number of
similar incidents reported to Louza Station, and informed
him regarding the action of the members of the Special
Service Mission. Sgt. Major Kanno informed J.D.S.
Kobayashi that Major Keyashi would be consulted regarding
the case and the persons responsible would be warned that
such action on Settlement roads must cease forthwith.

Sgt. Major Kanno was also informed regarding the
intention to release the two Chinese and that Mr.
Yoshizaki did not desire to take action against the men.
Sgt. Major Kanno stated that he understood the position.

At the conclusion of the enquiries the two Chinese
were permitted to go.

〔此处转录不清〕
D.S.36 Kobayashi.
C.D.C.260.

〔此处转录不清〕
Cop. Det. 1/c.

D.D.O."A" Div.
pages.zh:
MISC.440/36
1 (第6页)

应给予这两名中国人自由。

小林J.D.S.（J.D.S. Kobayashi）与菅野警佐（Sgt. Major Kanno）取得联系，此前菅野警佐已获悉向卢家嘴巡捕房（Louza Station）报告的多起类似事件，小林向其通报了特务机关成员的行动。菅野警佐告知小林J.D.S.，将就本案咨询Keyashi少校（Major Keyashi，音译），并将警告责任人，必须立即停止在租界道路上的此类行动。

菅野警佐还获悉了释放这两名中国人的意图，以及吉崎先生不希望对这些人员采取行动。菅野警佐表示他理解这一情况。

问询结束时，这两名中国人获准离开。

〔此处转录不清〕
D.S.36 小林。
C.D.C.260。

〔此处转录不清〕
Cop. Det. 1/c.

“A”分区副助理总监。

pages.en:
FM. 2
G. 55M-1-38

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Central Police Station,
REPORT
Date April, 24th, 1938.

Subject Argument between Japanese and C.P.Cs. 2621 and 1410
at Honan Road and Soochow Road corner.

Made by F.S. 237 Yablonsky Forwarded by ............................................................

Sir,

Re the above, I beg to report that at ..10 a.m. 24-4-38,
whilst on duty on Honan Road Bridge, I was approached by C.P.C.
1410 who informed me that C.P.C. 2621 was in trouble with
several Japanese.

On my arrival at the spot, I saw a big crowd of Chinese
and three Japanese in an unlicenced m/car. The Japanese were
dressed in civilian clothes, but wore military type hats, there
were also two Chinese in the car i/e. one claiming to be a Da
Tao Government Official and the other stated that he was a
Lodah of a boat lying in Soochow Creek and had been arrested
on Soochow Road by the other occupants of the car for none
payment of the taxes.

I told the Japanese that they must wait until I informed
the Central Police Station.

D.S.I. Ross and J.D.S. Kobayashi came in answer to my
report and questioned the parties concerned.

J.D.S. Kobayashi later informed the Japanese military
Authorities who also attended.

The Officer i/c stated that he did not wish to detain
the Chinese lodah and would not permit the Japanese or Chinese
Government Official to go to Central Police Station for further
enquiries. Then they all left and the lodah was taken to the
station by D.S.I. Ross for questioning.

I am, Sir,

Your Obedient Servant,

E Yablonsky
F.S. 237

D.O. "A".
D.C. (Special Branch)
pages.zh:
FM. 2
G. 55M-1-38

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 ____ 
中央巡捕房，
报告
日期：1938年4月24日。

主题：日本人与中央巡捕房警员2621号和1410号在河南路与苏州路拐角处的争执。

由 F.S. 237 Yablonsky 呈报 转发人 ____ 

先生，

关于上述事项，谨报告如下：1938年4月24日上午..10点，当我在河南路桥执勤时，中央巡捕房警员1410号走近我，告知我中央巡捕房警员2621号正与几名日本人发生纠纷。

当我到达现场时，我看到一大群中国人和三名日本人坐在一辆无牌汽车里。这些日本人穿着便服，但戴着军式帽子；车里还有两名中国人，即一名自称是大道政府官员，另一名声称自己是停在苏州河上的一艘船的船老大（Lodah），因未缴纳税款而被车上的其他人于苏州路逮捕。

我告诉日本人，他们必须等待，直到我通知中央巡捕房。

副督察长Ross和小林J.D.S.接到我的报告后赶来，并对有关各方进行了询问。

后来，小林J.D.S.通知了日本军方当局，他们也到达了现场。

负责警官表示，他不希望拘留这名中国船老大，也不允许日本人或中国政府官员前往中央巡捕房接受进一步问询。随后他们都离开了，船老大则由副督察长Ross带到巡捕房接受讯问。

此致，

您顺从的仆人，

E Yablonsky
F.S. 237

“A”分区助理总监。
特别课侦探主任。

pages.en:
C.P.C. 1410

Central 24/4/38 translated
///// Clerk Sung.

At about 9.06a.m. 24/4/38 whilst being on duty on Soochow Rd.
near Honan Rd. I suddenly heard someone blow a police whistle. I
rushed to the scene and saw that two Japanese accompanied by a male
Chinese were engaged in pushing another male Chinese into an
unlicensed m/car. At this juncture C.P.C. 2621 tried to intervene,
and was refused by the Japanese. Then P.C. 237 also came to the
scene and eventually instructed C.P.C. 2621 to telephone to the
station. After a while, a Japanese policeman arrived. As I do not
understand either Japanese or English, I do not know anything
further.

Signed.
pages.zh:
中央巡捕房警员 1410

中央 1938年4月24日 翻译
///// 书记员 Sung。

1938年4月24日上午9点06分左右，当我在靠近河南路的苏州路执勤时，突然听到有人吹警哨。我赶到现场，看到两名日本人伴同一名中国男子，正将另一名中国男子推入一辆无牌汽车。此时，中央巡捕房警员2621号试图干预，但遭到日本人拒绝。随后，警员237号也来到现场，并最终指示中央巡捕房警员2621号打电话回巡捕房。过了一会儿，一名日本警察到达。由于我不懂日语或英语，因此不知道后续情况。

签名。

pages.en:
Zee Mao An,age 24,native of Faoshan,M/Boatman
// C.D.S.118
translated
///// Clerk Sung.
Central 24/4/38

Lee Mao An,age 24,native of Foshan,M/boatman.
At about 8a.m. on the 23/4/38 I rowed my boat from Faoshan to
Shanghai together with my customer named Koo Seu Vung who brought
with him 12 piculs of rice, and the boat arrived at Shanghai at
about 5p.m. same date. Upon arrival I tied up at Soochow Rd. near
Henan Rd.
At about 8a.m. 24/4/38,Koo Seu Vung hired a handcart to unload
his rice to the jetty,whereupon some Japanese came and arrested Koo
Seu Vung. This I observed whilst aboard the boat.
Cross signed.
pages.zh:
郑毛安（Zee Mao An），24岁，佛山籍，男/船夫
// C.D.S.118
翻译
///// 书记员 Sung。
中央 1938年4月24日

李毛安（Lee Mao An，音译，原文与前文Zee Mao An不一致，照实译出），24岁，佛山籍，男/船夫。
1938年4月23日上午8点左右，我与我的顾客顾修荣（Koo Seu Vung，音译）一起划船从佛山（Faoshan，原文如此，通常指佛山，但也可能是宝山等地名的误拼，此处依原文译）前往上海，他带了12担大米，船只于当天下午5点左右抵达上海。抵达后，我将船系泊在靠近河南路的苏州路。
1938年4月24日上午8点左右，顾修荣雇了一辆手推车将大米卸到码头上，这时一些日本人前来逮捕了顾修荣。这一切是我在船上观察到的。
交叉签名。

pages.en:
Chuen Tsoong Fah,63,rootung,boatman
// ..i... 118
Central 24/4/38 ///// Clerk Sung.
translated

I brought by boat from Tsingpoo 800 bundles of toilet paper
to Shanghai,tax to the amount of J.C.C() being duly paid to the
"Dah Dao" Government. receipt for this amount was received.
At about 8a.m. 24/4/38 whilst unloading the toilet paper fro
the boat which was tied up alongside N.Soochow Road,I was approac
ed by two unknown male Chinese who pushed me into a m/car. I told
them that I had paid the required tax and that the receipt for sa
was in possession of the laodah who had just left the boat.
These men ignored my explanation. After the m/car had been driven
near Honan Rd. bridge,another male Chinese was pulled into the
m/car. At this juncture the male Chinese raised a cry of alarm,to
which a C.F.C. responded. We were then brought to the station.
Cross signed.
pages.zh:
钱宗发（Chuen Tsoong Fah），63岁，如东（rootung，音译）籍，船夫
// ..i... 118
中央 1938年4月24日 ///// 书记员 Sung。
翻译

我用船从青浦（Tsingpoo）运了800捆卫生纸到上海，已向“大刀”政府（"Dah Dao" Government） duly 缴纳了金额为J.C.C()的税款。收到了该金额的收据。
1938年4月24日上午8点左右，当我在停靠于北苏州路旁的船上卸载卫生纸时，两名陌生的中国男子上前将我推入一辆汽车。我告诉他们我已经缴纳了所需的税款，且收据在刚刚离开船只的船老大手中。
这些人无视我的解释。当汽车行驶到靠近河南路桥的地方时，另一名中国男子被拉进汽车。此时，该中国男子发出呼救声，一名中央巡捕房警员（C.F.C.，原文如此，应为C.P.C.）响应。随后我们将被带到巡捕房。
交叉签名。

pages.en:
Koo Seu Vung, age 43, native of Paoshan
// ..D.S.118
Central 24/4/38 ///// Clerk Sung.
translated

At about 8.45a.m. on the 24/4/38 I brought 12 piculs of
rice by boat from Paoshan to Shanghai. I paid $4.80 as tax on the
rice at Paoshan. Upon arrival at Soochow Rd. Jetty near Honan Rd.
bridge, I hired a m/truck with a view to unloading the rice(at
that time I was standing on the jetty) when a m/car arrived from
which alighted two male Chinese who asked for the owner of the
rice. I replied that I was the owner. On learning this, the two
male Chinese without explanation pushed me into their m/car, in
which I discovered were seated a male Japanese and a Chinese
chauffeur. I raised a cry of alarm and a C.P.C. came to the scene
who insisted on bringing us to the station.

Cross signed.
pages.zh:
顾修荣（Koo Seu Vung），43岁，宝山（Paoshan）籍
// ..D.S.118
中央 1938年4月24日 ///// 书记员 Sung。
翻译

1938年4月24日上午8点45分左右，我用船从宝山运了12担大米到上海。我在宝山支付了4.80元的大米税款。抵达靠近河南路桥的苏州路码头时，我雇了一辆卡车准备卸大米（当时我正站在码头上），这时一辆汽车驶来，车上下来两名中国男子，询问大米的主人是谁。我回答我是主人。得知这一点后，这两名中国男子不加解释地将我推入他们的汽车，我发现车里坐着一名日本男子和一名中国司机。我发出呼救声，一名中央巡捕房警员赶到现场，坚持要将我们带到巡捕房。

交叉签名。

pages.en:
wong Hai Ising,C.r.C. 2621(Central)

Central          24/4/38          translated
                                  /////      Clerk Sung.

At 9.05a.m. on the 24th inst.,whilst on duty at the Honan
road bridge,I saw an unlicensed stationary m/car at the west of
the bridge. Upon seeing that a male Chinese under the escort of
four Japanese were about to enter the car,I approached them in
order to ascertain what was the matter. The Japanese informed
me not to interfere with their affair. However,as the affair
was also my responsibility I stopped the party from boarding the
car. At this juncture,one of the Japanese inserted his hand into
his trousers' pocket in the manner as if to fetch something
therefrom,and I immediately took my service pistol in hand,as a
precaution against the Japanese drawing a pistol,or any other
untoward incident. I then blew my whistle. This attracted F.S.
237 and C.P.C. 1410 who arrived at the scene shortly afterwards.
Upon observing the arrival of the police officers,the Japanese
then released the man whom they had apprehended. I afterwards
communicated with the station by telephone. I later saw another
male Chinese sitting in the said m/car. He was then instructed
to leave the car and accompany me to the station. The above is
my true statement.

                                  Signed.

黄海兴（wong Hai Ising，音译），中央巡捕房警员 2621号（中央）

中央          1938年4月24日          翻译
                                  /////      书记员 Sung。

本月24日上午9点05分，当我在河南路桥执勤时，我看到桥西侧停着一辆无牌汽车。看到一名中国男子在四名日本人的押送下正要进入汽车，我走近他们以查明发生了什么事。日本人告诉我不要干涉他们的事务。然而，由于此事也是我的职责范围，我阻止了这群人上车。此时，其中一名日本人将手伸进裤袋，动作仿佛要从中取出什么东西，我立即手持佩枪，以防日本人拔枪或发生其他意外事件。随后我吹响了哨子。这吸引了F.S. 237和中央巡捕房警员1410号，他们不久后到达现场。看到警察到达，日本人随即释放了他们扣押的人。随后我通过电话与巡捕房联系。后来我看到另一名中国男子坐在上述汽车里。随后他被指令下车并随我前往巡捕房。以上是我的真实陈述。

                                  签名。

Date April 23, 1938.

Subject File Miscellaneous No. 308.

Made by Insp. Williamson Forwarded by C.I. Officer i/c

Sir,

I beg to report that at 9.40 a.m. 23-4-38, a telephone message was received from C.P.C. 106 from Street Telephone No.3 (Fokien - Soochow Roads) to the effect that Japanese Military were stopping rice from being landed on Soochow Road.

J.P.C. 126 and the undersigned proceeded to the Creek and made enquiries. On the arrival, the Japanese soldiers had left by boat. It would appear that about 9.20 a.m. a Japanese soldier armed with a sword walked along Soochow Road from West to East and took up a position about twenty yards East of Shansi Road Bridge where a convoy of rice boats are moored. He warned the boatmen not to unload the rice there and then left on a small boat west on the Soochow Creek.

It would appear that the soldier wished these boats to proceed to the Rice Jetties at Yu Ya Ching Road where a tax is imposed. It would appear these boats were trying to evade the tax.

No other incident occurred.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 25 APR 1938）

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Inspector

S.I.

日本捕房126号警员及本人随即前往该浜进行调查。抵达时，日本士兵已乘船离开。据查，约上午9时20分，一名佩刀的日本士兵沿苏州河路由西向东行走，在山西路桥以东约二十码处停泊着一队运米船的位置站定。他警告船夫不得在此处卸载大米，随后乘坐一艘小船沿苏州河向西离去。

Sir,

The second described person Soong Pao Dien (宋宝田) was
interviewed on the morning of the 22-4-38, when the following
was learned:- He had been taken to a dwelling situated on
Tatung Road near Wuchen Road, formerly occupied by the S.M.C.P.
Bureau, where he was questioned by a number of Japanese, some
of whom were in uniform and others in civilian clothes, with
regard to the source of the rice. On being told that it had
come from a godown situated on Szechuen Road he was allowed to
go, having been detained there about three hours.

With reference to the 1st described person Yang Ah Tung
(杨阿统), as far as can be ascertained, he is still being held
by the Japanese at the aforementioned premises. The reason for
which, it is said that the Japanese are demanding $51.00, alleged
taxation dues.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 23 APR. '38 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

Dr. Kobayashi has been informed and he will continue
with further enquiries. He is of the opinion that in this
instance it is not the Japanese Military that is concerned, but
members of the Consolidated Tax Bureau.

Statement of Soeng Pao Dien attached.
Enquiries proceeding.

//////// Clerk Sih Yun Pai.

I, an assistant employed at the Yah Chong Tuh Rice
Shop, 208 Avenue Road, beg to state the following:
Between 11.30 a.m. and 12.30 p.m. on 21-4-38, I took
delivery of 177 bags of rice from the Lee Yih Co.'s godown,
30 Szechuen Road, transporting same to outside the Land Bank
of China's Godown. At about 1.50 p.m. same date, two
Japanese and one Chinese came to the place in a cream coloured
K/car and they alighted. Then they asked me who was the
owner of the rice, and in reply I stated that the owner was
in his shop. Following this the Japanese caught hold of me
to enter his car, same being then driven to the Tu Tao Police
Bureau, Ta-tung Road, via Yu Ya Ching Road, Jinza Road and
Wu-chen Road Bridge. I was detained in the Detention House
of the said Police Bureau for about three hours. On explain-
ing the reason of my being brought to the bureau, one Chinese
told me that the case would be dealt with by the Financial
Bureau, and that I should wait for the arrival of Tsing Zaung,
a Japanese. At about 4.45 p.m. the said Japanese arrived,
and on ascertaining the facts of the case he allowed me to
leave.
The two Japanese who brought me to the Police Bureau,
are described as follows: One dressed in yellow uniform with
a sword on his person, the other wearing foreign style clothing.
The Chinese was an interpreter.

Signed a cross-marked: Soon Pao Dien.

我，爱多亚路208号协昌德米行雇员，谨陈述如下：
1938年4月21日上午11时30分至下午12时30分之间，我从四川路30号李益公司仓库提取了177袋大米，并将其运送至中国通商银行仓库外。同日下午约1时50分，两名日本人和一名中国人乘坐一辆奶油色小轿车来到该地并下车。随后他们问我谁是米主，我回答说米主在他的店里。随后，日本人抓住我强行让我进入他的汽车，该车随即经虞洽卿路、静安寺路和吴淞路桥开往大同路道台警察局。我在该警察局的拘留所被扣留了约三个小时。在解释我被带到警局的原因后，一名中国人告诉我，此案将由财政局处理，让我等待一名叫 Tsing Zaung 的日本人到来。下午约4时45分，该日本人到达，在查明案情事实后，他允许我离开。
带我到警察局的两名日本人描述如下：一人身穿黄色制服，随身佩刀；另一人身穿西式服装。那名中国人是一名翻译。

Reference, functioning of Japanese on Soochow Creek Jetty,
East of Yu Ya Ching Road Bridge.
D.S. 20 Brotherton
Chief Inspector.

Sir,

At 1.45p.m. on the 21-4-38, a telephone message was
received from S/I Ching to the effect that Japanese were inter-
fering with the unloading of rice at a jetty, East of Yu Ya Ching
Road Bridge and Soochow Road.

C.D.C.98, J.P.S. 168, S/I Curtis and D.C. Brotherton
attended, where, on arrival, the Japanese had already left,
having driven away South along Yu Ya Ching Road in M/Car, S.D.F.
Lic. No.388, taking with them two Chinese, named:-
(1) Yung Ah Kung (楊阿光) 27, Footung,
M/Boatman, Boat No.57013.
(2) Soong Foo Man (宋宏田) 38, Footung,
Wheelwright, employee, Yan Cheong Yah (協昌德)
Rice Shop, 308 Avenue Road.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / 22 APR. 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

Enquiries revealed that two boats were tied to the afore-
mentioned Jetty unloading rice, best part of which had already
been landed. When at about 1.45p.m. 21-4-38, M/Car Lic. No.
S.D.F. 388 drew up on Yu Ya Ching Road, alighting from which
was two Japanese accompanied by a male Chinese, presumably
Interpreter. The Japanese were dressed in dark green drill
uniform and unarmed, they, all three then proceeded to the Jetty
and accosted the aforementioned two male Chinese, the gist of
what had actually transpired during their short conversation was
not heard by S/I Ching or the C.P.C.s on duty at the Bridge.

However, from enquiries among persons in the vicinity, it
would seem that the Japanese through the aid of their interpe-
ter wanted to know where the owner of the rice was, on being
informed that he was not present, they then took away the two
persons described above (Owner of the rice is Sung Voo Young
), 308 Avenue Road).

D.C.S.B.
