参考：日本人在虞洽卿路桥以东苏州河码头的活动。
D.S. 20 布雷瑟顿
总巡官。

先生：

1938年4月21日下午1时45分，接到华捕郑（Ching）的电话留言，称日本人正在虞洽卿路桥和苏州河路以东的一个码头干扰大米卸载工作。

中央侦探车98号、日本捕房168号警员、督察柯蒂斯（Curtis）及副巡官布雷瑟顿（Brotherton）赶赴现场，抵达时日本人已驾驶牌照号为 S.D.F. 388 的小轿车沿虞洽卿路向南驶离，并带走两名中国人，姓名如下：
(1) 杨阿光（Yung Ah Kung），27岁，浦东籍，
机动船船夫，船号57013。
(2) 宋宏田（Soong Foo Man），38岁，浦东籍，
轮匠，爱多亚路308号协昌德米行雇员。

（印：上海公共租界工部局 / 1938年4月22日 / 特别支部）

调查显示，有两艘船系泊在上述码头卸载大米，大部分货物已经上岸。1938年4月21日下午约1时45分，牌照号为 S.D.F. 388 的小轿车停在虞洽卿路上，车上下来两名日本人，伴有一名中国男子，推测为翻译。日本人穿着深绿色斜纹布制服，未携带武器，三人随后走向码头，并与上述两名中国男子搭话。华捕郑及桥上执勤的中央电话交换台警员未听到他们短暂交谈的具体内容。

然而，通过对附近人员的调查，似乎日本人通过翻译想知道米主在哪里，当得知米主不在场时，他们便带走了上述两人（米主为 Sung Voo Young，地址为爱多亚路308号）。

特别支部副巡官
签署/
22/4

pages.en:
Having been in the vicinity for about 15 minutes the
Japanese and interpreter accompanied by the aforementioned and
described male Chinese left in the W/Car driving away in a Souther-
ly direction along Yu Ya Ching Road. At no time did the two
persons driven away in company with the Japanese, appear to be
offering resistance in, presumably, complying with the Japanese
request that they accompany them.

The owner of the rice in question, Mr. Zung Vee Yoong
had visited Mr. T.K. Ho, Secretary's Office, P.W.D. Administration
Building, and as result Mr. T.K. Ho referred the rice owner to Mr.
Robertson D.M."A".

The owner when interviewed states that he has no reason,
whatsoever, as to why one of his assistants (2nd described) should
have been taken away by the Japanese.

However, Mr. Robertson ".. .. A" at about 5p.m. 21-4-38
received a telephone message from Mr. T.K. Ho to the effect that
the 2nd described person had been released by the Japanese
Authorities.

Further, Zung Vee Yoong stated that his rice had been
brought from Lee Yih Godown (勝益棧), situated 136/30 Szechuen
Road and landed at Soochow Road Jetty preparatory to being
housed at premises 296 Avenue Road.

The 2nd described, Seeng Foe Pien up to the time of
submitting this report, could not be located, however, it is
expected that he will be located and interviewed on the morning
of the 22-4-38.

〔此处为手写签名〕

D.S.M.
C.D.C.S.

日本人和翻译在上述两名中国男子的陪同下，在现场停留约15分钟后，乘坐小轿车沿虞洽卿路向南驶离。在被日本人带走的两人中，没有任何迹象表明他们曾抵抗，似乎是顺从了日本人要求他们陪同的请求。

涉案大米的所有者 Zung Vee Yoong 先生曾拜访工务局行政大楼秘书处的 T.K. Ho 先生，因此 T.K. Ho 先生将米主引荐给 "A" 区副区长罗伯逊（Robertson）先生。

米主在接受问询时表示，他完全不知道为何他的一名助手（第二名所述人员）会被日本人带走。

然而，罗伯逊先生 "____ A" 于1938年4月21日下午5时左右接到 T.K. Ho 先生的电话，称第二名所述人员已被日本当局释放。

此外，Zung Vee Yoong 表示，他的大米是从位于四川路136/30号的李益栈（Lee Yih Godown）运出，并在苏州河路码头卸货，准备存入爱多亚路296号的 premises。

截至提交本报告时，尚未找到第二名所述人员 Seeng Foe Pien，但预计将于1938年4月22日上午找到他并进行问询。

〔此处为手写签名〕

D.S.M.
C.D.C.S.

Sir,

At 5.05. .. 20-4-38, a telephone message was received from .. .199 to the effect that two Japanese subjects, one of whom was dressed in military uniform and accompanied by a Chinese Interpreter, were preventing rice from being unloaded at an .. .. Public Jetty on Soochow Road, East of Yu Ya Ching Road.

his father Tseu Ying Zeu (周林寿) the owner of the bean curd.

Upon arrival on the mentioned Jetty, one of the Japanese
(civilian) telephoned for a Johnson Hire Car, in which they
removed the two Chinese, stating that they were taking them to
Wucheng Road for the purpose of registering the cargo of the
boats.

Enquiries made at the Johnson Hire Car Office, Peking
Road ascertained that the chauffeur of car No.18453 had driven
his passengers i.e. two Chinese and a Japanese to the North
side of Siasa Road Bridge via Wucheng Road Bridge where they
had alighted and proceeded on foot in a Northerly direction
along Wucheng Road, apparently to the office of the Ta Tao
Government.

D.S. Kobayashi has been informed of the facts pertaining
to this case and will continue enquiries among the Japanese
Authorities on the morning of the 21-4-38.

Mr. H.D.K. Robertson D.O."A" informed and upon ascer-
taining the facts he gave instructions that D.S. Kobayashi

In an effort to gain further information as to the
developments in this case Wong Tsau Loong was interview-
ed at 2.15p.m. 11-5-38 and he stated as follows:-
    Through an indirect friend (name not supplied)
representations in this case were made to The Japanese
Headquarters with the result that $6,000.00 of the
$10,000.00 cash security was returned on about 1-5-38
through this unnamed friend.
    The 3 men mentioned on diary No. 2 in respect of whom
the $10,000.00 was deposited have not been turned over
to the Japanese and Wong Tsau Loong is of the opinion tha
these men were never wanted by the Japanese and that
the conditions of their being turned over to them were
merely formed in order that $10,000.00 would be deposited
with a great possibility of confiscation.
    Wong Tsau Loong cannot explain why the $4,000.00
was retained and is of the opinion that it has been
'squeezed'.
    There have been no further dealings with the Japanese
since the $6,000.00 was returned.

Illegal arrest in the International Settlement
by Japanese Military.

At 10. a.m. 10-4-38, P.C. 188 called at 6/571
Burkill Road and interviewed Di Ming Ping, the sister of
the lawyer Di our client. The following was learnt.

Following telephone communication between Di Ming Ping
(the arrested man at the stor house) and his family, a
friend, one Wong Mau Jien (王宝利) proceeded to the
settlement side of the Garden Bridge at about 5.45p.m.
15-4-38. A Japanese with Di Ming Lung then came over and
met Wong Mau Jien and all proceeded to the Stor House.

The amount $7,040.00 was paid over as demanded.

The Japanese authorities then further demanded a cash
security of $10,000.00 for the production within 10 days
of Leh Zu Sung, Ching Sung Dau & Ching S Sung. This
further $10,000.00 was then paid over the Japanese stating
that the amount will be confiscated if the above 3 men
are not produced within 10 days.

After this, Di Ming Kung was permitted to leave (about
6.30p.m. 15-4-38).

C.D.C. 188 has seen the two receipts which were issued
in respect of the amounts $7,040.00 & $10,000.00.

The actual persons concerned were not available for
personal interview and it is believed that they are at
present staying elsewhere.

Copy to Special Branch.

1938年4月10日上午10时，警员188号前往伯基尔路（Burkill Road）6/571号，采访了我们的当事人狄律师的姐姐狄明平（Di Ming Ping）。获悉情况如下。

在狄明平（在仓库被捕者）与其家人进行电话沟通后，一位名叫王宝利（Wong Mau Jien，音译）的朋友于1938年4月15日下午5时45分左右前往外白渡桥的租界一侧。一名日本人与狄明龙（Di Ming Lung）随后过来与王宝利会面，众人一同前往仓库。

按要求支付了7,040.00美元。

随后，日本当局进一步要求缴纳10,000.00美元现金保证金，以在10天内交出乐祖松（Leh Zu Sung，音译）、程松道（Ching Sung Dau，音译）及程S松（Ching S Sung，音译）。这额外的10,000.00美元随即支付，日本人声明如果上述3人未在10天内交出，该款项将被没收。

此后，狄明公（Di Ming Kung，音译）获准离开（约1938年4月15日下午6时30分）。

刑事侦缉处警员188号看到了就7,040.00美元和10,000.00美元金额开具的两张收据。

实际相关人员未能接受当面讯问，据信他们目前住在别处。

April 15th.    38.

1.

Illegal arrest in the International Settlement
by Japanese Military.

At 2.50p.m. 15-4-38, a telephone message was received
from one Yang Shing Tee, 6/571 Burkill Road, stating that
Japanese were at that house creating trouble.

D.S.I. Read & C.D.I. 188 immediately attended but
found on arrival that the Japanese had been & left, having
arrested one Di Sung Kung (狄松公), age 64, Tzangshoh, from
above address.

Wong Tsau Loong (汪兆龙), a relative, produced a
document (translation attached) which he was about to
bring to Ginza Station requesting protection for one Di
Meur, a lawyer who is the son of the man arrested. He also
stated that 3 Japanese & 1 Chinese had constituted the
party, one of the Japanese being a uniformed man carrying
a sword & pistol. They had arrived & left in a motor car
Lic. No. 7177 which was later found to belong to "Pou Sai
Seng (潘三商), 88 Rue Marcel Tiliet, French Concession."

D.D.O. "B" informed at this stage 3.15p.m.

From the proposed document (asking for protection) &
from Wong Tsau Loong it was known that "Shanghai Steamship
Co." was connected with this affair & with J.P.C. Sugimoto
(B.W.) a visit was paid to the Wharf, 700 Chakiang Road,
where it was learnt that the Chinese manager was "Pou Sai
Seng" (owner of motor car used) & that his office was Room
602, 160 Avenue Edward VII.

银座（Ginza）
1938年4月15日.

1.

日本军方在国际租界内非法逮捕。

1938年4月15日下午2时50分，接到伯基尔路（Burkill Road）6/571号杨星梯（Yang Shing Tee，音译）的电话留言，称日本人正在该处滋事。

督察长里德（Read）及刑事侦缉督察188号立即前往，但到达时发现日本人已来过并离开，并从上述地址逮捕了一名64岁的太仓人狄松公（Di Sung Kung）。

亲属汪兆龙（Wong Tsau Loong）出示了一份文件（附译文），他正准备将其带到新闸捕房，请求保护一名狄梅尔（Di Meur，音译）律师，此人是被捕者的儿子。他还称，一行人为3名日本人和1名中国人，其中一名日本人身着制服，佩带军刀和手枪。他们乘坐牌照号为7177的汽车抵达并离开，后查明该车属于法租界马思南路（Rue Marcel Tiliet）88号的潘三商（Pou Sai Seng）。

此时于下午3时15分通知了“B”分区副巡官。

从拟议的文件（请求保护）及汪兆龙处得知，“上海轮船公司”与此事有关，并与日本领事馆警察署的杉本（Sugimoto）先生（B.W.）有关联，遂前往乍浦路700号码头，获悉其中方经理为“潘三商”（所用汽车车主），其办公室位于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）160号602室。

pages.en:
1 ( sheet 2 )

A visit was then made to this address where Foo Sai
Song was found in office with the Directing Manager of the
Shipping Co., Mr. K. Munson.
On enquiry here the following was learnt.
About 1 month ago a cargo of wheat was shipped per the
Shanghai Steamship Co. from Wusong to Shanghai (28 boats)
by one named Loh Zu Sung ( / 麦 / ) & on arrival in Shanghai
was 'tied up' in the Soochow Creek. The Shanghai Steam-
ship Co. received instructions that this cargo, was
Japanese Military Confiscated Property & must not be
disposed of. All this cargo was eventually turned over
to the Japanese Military with the exception of 622 piculs,
which Loh Zu Sung had already sold to Foo Fung Flour Mill
for a sum approximating $7,000.00.
Loh Zu Sung, possibly due to claim being made by the
Japanese Military, paid this money into the keeping of his
Lawyer, Di Zur, 6/571 Baskill Road. No one appears to
have contacted this Loh Zu Sung as he has been working
through his Lawyer Di Zur.
Representations have been made to Di Zur during the
past few days by the Japanese Military through Mr. K.
Munson & Foo Sai Song (of the Shanghai Steamship Company)
to pay over the $7,000.00.
Di Zur has refused to do this, demanding that some
authority be shown by the person collecting.
pages.zh:
1 （第2页）

随后前往该地址，发现 Foo Sai Song（音译）与轮船公司的董事经理 K. Munson 先生在办公室内。
经查询，获悉以下情况。
约1个月前，一名名为罗祖松（Loh Zu Sung，音译，原文标注：/ 麦 /）的人通过上海轮船公司将一批小麦从吴淞运往上海（28船），抵达上海后被“扣押”在苏州河。上海轮船公司收到指示，称这批货物为日本军方没收财产，不得处置。除622担外，所有货物最终移交给日本军方，这622担小麦已被罗祖松以约7,000.00美元的价格卖给福丰面粉厂。
罗祖松可能因日本军方提出索赔，将这笔钱存入其律师狄祖尔（Di Zur，音译）处，地址为巴斯吉尔路（Baskill Road，应为Burkill Road之误）6/571号。似乎无人直接联系过罗祖松，因为他一直通过其律师狄祖尔行事。
过去几天，日本军方通过上海轮船公司的 K. Munson 先生和 Foo Sai Song 向狄祖尔提出交涉，要求支付这7,000.00美元。
狄祖尔拒绝支付，要求收款人出示某种授权证明。

pages.en:
1 (Sheet 3)

Pou Sai Sung (Chinese manager of the Shanghai Steamship
Co.) informed the undersigned, that he has been suspected
of being a party to this sale of the wheat & that yesterday
14-4-38, he went with Mr. K. Kumon (his managing director)
to the Economical Dept. of the Conciliation Party of
Japanese Military, Astor House, where he was detained and
told he would continue to be detained until he deposited
$6,000.00 on behalf of this case. He deposited this
amount and has a receipted document to this effect which
he produced.

Pou Sai Sung, states that his car Lic. No. 7177 is
generally used by the managing staff.

The managing Director K. Kumon volunteered through
J.P.C. Sugimoto that Lieut. Yoshikawa, himself, K. Ishikawa
(one of shipping Co.'s staff) & Chang Dah Lang (one of
shipping Co.'s Chinese staff) had gone to 6/571 Nankill
Road at about 2.30p.m. with the intention of arresting Di
Sung, but as he was not present they took his father, Di
Sung Kong into the car and drove him to the Economical
Dept. of the Conciliation Party of Japanese Military,
Astor House. Mr. K. Kumon states he acted only under
direction of Lieut. Yoshikawa.

Mr. K. Kumon stated it was the intention of the Japanese
Military to hold Di Sung Kong until such time as the
$7,000.00 had been paid over.
pages.zh:
1 （第3页）

上海轮船公司中方经理潘三松（Pou Sai Sung，音译）告知本人，他被怀疑参与了此次小麦销售，且昨天（1938年4月14日），他与董事经理 K. Kumon 先生一同前往阿斯托尔饭店（Astor House）的日本军方协和会经济部，在那里被拘留，并被告知除非为此案存入6,000.00美元，否则将继续被拘留。他存入了这笔款项，并出示了相应的收据文件。

潘三松称，他的牌照号为7177的汽车通常由管理层使用。

董事经理 K. Kumon 通过日本领事馆警察署的杉本主动表示，吉川中尉（Lieut. Yoshikawa）、他自己、石川 K.（K. Ishikawa，轮船公司员工之一）及张大郎（Chang Dah Lang，轮船公司华籍员工之一）于下午2时30分左右前往南基尔路（Nankill Road，应为Burkill Road之误）6/571号，意图逮捕狄松（Di Sung），但因狄松不在，他们将其父狄松公（Di Sung Kong）带上车，驱车将其送往阿斯托尔饭店的日本军方协和会经济部。 K. Kumon 先生称，他仅是在吉川中尉的指示下行动。

 K. Kumon 先生称，日本军方的意图是扣留狄松公，直到支付7,000.00美元为止。

pages.en:
1 (Sheet 4)

At about 4p.m. 15-4-38, the relatives of Di Jung Kong
received a telephone message from him, when Di Jung Kong
stated that he was being held at the Astor House and had
been promised his release, when the exact amount for which
the 682 piculs of wheat had been sold, was paid over,
approx. $7,000.00.

After return of the undersigned to the Station, (about
5p.m.) D.O. "B" was informed.

At about 5.30p.m., another telephone message was
received from Di Jung Kong from the Astor House by his
relatives stating that the amount now required before his
release would be granted, was $10,000.00. (no explanation
for the increase being given)

Both Di Siau Eng (sister of lawyer Di [此处转录不清]) and the
cook, Lau Kya Chih (陶利吉) state they saw the Japanese
uniformed man with a pistol in his hand at the time of the
illegal arrest.

1938年4月15日下午4时左右，狄荣公（Di Jung Kong，音译）的亲属接到他的电话，狄荣公称他被扣留在阿斯托尔饭店，并承诺一旦支付出售682担小麦的确切金额（约7,000.00美元），他将被释放。

本人返回捕房后（约下午5时），通知了“B”分区巡官。

约下午5时30分，狄荣公的亲属再次接到他从阿斯托尔饭店打来的电话，称在获准释放前现在要求的金额为10,000.00美元。（未对金额增加给出解释）

Translation of the letter addressed to Sinza
Police Station by Lawyer Dih -eu.

To Sinza Police Station
Sir;

Some time ago, I was appointed by a general food supply
broker named Tsing Bong Dau to take into deposit the sum of
$7,000.00 from one named Loh Z Sung, who obtained this sum
of money from the sale of wheat. A representative sent by
the manager named Seu Sai Yang of the Shanghai Steamship
Company (Now known as Kiangsu & Chekiang Steamship Co.) came
to my office yesterday and stated that the sum of $7,000.00,
proceeds from the sale of wheat obtained from the area now in
the hands of Japanese, should be handed over to the 'Chen Woo
an' of the 'Chinese Special Service Squad', action would be
taken towards me if I failed to do so. I replied that the
money would be handed to the so-called squad when I have
received an official dispatch from the Japanese Authorities.
Unexpectedly, 2 men again called at my office at 9a.m. today
with a letter, without without official testimony from the
Japanese Military Authorities. Naturally, I refused to hand
them the money as demanded. They then left after passing
threats. In order to maintain public peace and obtain pro-
tection I hereby request you to take the matter into your
prompt consideration.

From
Lawyer Dih -eu.
18-4-38.

致新闸捕房
先生；

不久前，我受一名名为程邦道（Tsing Bong Dau，音译）的总食品供应经纪人的委托，代为保管一名名为罗Z松（Loh Z Sung，音译）的人的7,000.00美元存款，该款项系其出售小麦所得。上海轮船公司（现称江浙轮船公司）名为徐赛阳（Seu Sai Yang，音译）的经理派代表昨日来到我的办公室，称应将这笔从现已处于日本人控制地区的出售小麦所得的7,000.00美元移交给“中国特别服务队”的“陈武安”（Chen Woo an，音译），否则将对我采取行动。我回答说，在收到日本当局的正式公文后，我会将钱交给所谓的服务队。不料，今天上午9时，又有两人持一封信来到我的办公室，但没有日本军方的官方证明。自然，我拒绝按要求将钱交给他们。他们在发出威胁后离开。为了维护公共治安并获得保护，特此请求贵方迅速考虑此事。

来自
狄-eu 律师。
1938年4月18日。

Misc. 153/38            16th April,           38.

1

House at No. 10, Lane 157 Benchow Road visited by
Japanese

Sir,

At 7.25 p.m. on 15/4/38, C.P.C. 989 telephoned this
station reporting that a number of Japanese had entered
House 10, Lane 157, Benchow Road.

D.S.I. Rend, D.S.I. Lih Shih Chung and C.D.S. 188,
C.D.C. 284 attended, but on their arrival the Japanese had
left the scene.

From enquiries made by D. I. Gorrie and C.D.C. 284,
the following was ascertained.

At about 7.20 p.m. on 15/4/38, a Party of four Japanese
in plain clothes, accompanied by a male Chinese wearing
a long gown, entered House 10, Lane 157 Benchow Road, and
proceeded to a second floor rear room occupied by an aged fe-
male named Chiang Wong Sz (江王氏). This female was the
only occupant of the room at the time, and the Chinese ac-
companying the Japanese questioned her regarding the where-
abouts of her daughter, Chiang Lee Tsung (江麗綜), who is
an actress.

While the Japanese were in this room, the wife of the
occupant of an adjoining room named Wang Boh Ling (王伯齡)
went to Niman Road and reported the occurrence to C.P.S.156
and C.D.C. 1046. They proceeded to the scene, and at the
entrance of Lane 157 Benchow Road encountered the Japanese

1

日本人探访宾州路（Benchow Road）157弄10号住宅

先生，

1938年4月15日晚上7时25分，中央巡捕989号致电本站，报告称多名日本人进入宾州路157弄10号住宅。

督察长伦德（Rend，音译）、督察长李世忠（Lih Shih Chung，音译）及刑事侦缉警司188号、刑事侦缉警员284号前往，但到达时日本人已离开现场。

经 Gorrle 督察和刑事侦缉警员284号查询，查明情况如下。

1938年4月15日晚上7时20分左右，四名便衣日本人，伴随一名身穿长衫的中国男子，进入宾州路157弄10号住宅，并前往二楼后间，该房间由一名名为江王氏（Chiang Wong Sz）的老年妇女居住。当时房间内只有这名妇女，陪同日本人的中国男子询问了她女儿江丽综（Chiang Lee Tsung，音译，职业为演员）的下落。

当日本人在此房间内时，隔壁房间住户王伯龄（Wang Boh Ling）的妻子前往尼曼路（Niman Road，音译），向中央巡捕站156号和刑事侦缉警员1046号报告了这一事件。他们前往现场，在宾州路157弄入口处遇到了日本人

（左侧手写批注：usb）

1 (Sheet 2)

party as they were leaving. C.P.S. 1564 seized hold of the
Chinese, but as he did so one of the Japanese showed him a
pistol which he was carrying under his jacket, whereupon
C.P.S. 1564 released his hold. The Chinese then informed
C.P.S. 1564 that his party were from the gendarmerie head-
quarters, and that they wished to arrest a certain person,
no details given.
    At this stage, C.P.C. 989 arrived on the scene and
was instructed by C.P.S. 1564 to telephone to this station.
    C.P.S.1564 and C.P.C. 1845 accompanied the Japanese
party to House 10, Lane 157, Wenchow Road, but found that the
inmates of the upstairs rooms had all gone. The Chinese
requested C.P.S. 1564 to post policemen at the front and
rear doors of the house, but the latter replied that he could
not do so without instructions from this station.    The
Japanese party then left, stating that they would return in
half an hour. They drove away in a motor car bearing a
S.D.F. Lic. 255.
    About 7.40 p.m. 11/4/38, P.S. Cooke on motor cycle
patrol on Wenchow Road, observed the above motor car pro-
ceeding West along Sinsa Road, and it was about to turn
North into Wenchow Road (where Lane 157 is situated) when the
driver apparently observed P.S. Cooke and it immediately turn-
ed South along Wenchow Road and disappeared. The car was
driven by a Japanese, besides whom a male Chinese was seated.

杂项 153/38             新闸

1 （第2页）

一行人正欲离开。中央巡捕1564号抓住了那名中国人，但就在此时，一名日本人向他展示了夹在夹克下的手枪，于是中央巡捕1564号松开了手。该中国人随后告知中央巡捕1564号，他们一行人来自宪兵总部，希望逮捕某个人，未提供细节。
    此时，中央巡捕989号到达现场，并奉中央巡捕1564号之命致电本站。
    中央巡捕1564号和中央巡捕1845号陪同日本一行人前往文州路（Wenchow Road，应为Benchow Road之误）157弄10号住宅，但发现楼上房间的住客均已离开。该中国人请求中央巡捕1564号在住宅前后门部署警察，但后者回复称未经本站指示无法这样做。日本一行人随后离开，称半小时后会回来。他们驾驶一辆悬挂特别市执照（S.D.F. Lic.）255号的汽车离去。
    1938年4月11日（原文如此，应为15日）晚上7时40分左右，在文州路骑摩托车巡逻的警司库克（Cooke）观察到上述汽车沿新闸路（Sinsa Road）向西行驶，当它正要向北转入文州路（157弄所在地）时，司机显然看到了库克警司，随即沿文州路向南转弯并消失。开车的是名日本人，旁边坐着一名中国男子。

and the rear of the car appeared to be occupied by five
other persons.

    Police were posted at the entrance of Lane 157,
Wenchow Road, but the Japanese did not again visit there.

    Neither Chiang Weng Js nor her daughter returned to
their room till 12.30 a.m. 16/4/38, and no reason for the
visit of the Japanese has been ascertained. It is not known
if the incident has any connection with the illegal arrest
by Japanese Military of a male Chinese at 571/6 Burkill Road
on the afternoon of 15/4/38, subject of Miso. Report 152/38
Sinza.

    Two inmates of the ground floor of No. 10, Lane 157,
Wenchow Road, named Tsang Lau Hoe (張老好) and Kyoch Kuh
Oen (高姑恩) who witnessed the entry of the Japanese, were
questioned, but they were unable to supply any useful informa-
tion regarding the female Chiang Weng Js or her family.

    The U.S. Marines were informed, and Lieutenant McLeod
visited the scene.

    Statements of C.P.S. 1564, C.P.C.s 1845, 989, Tsang Lau
Hoe and Kyoch Kuh Oen attached.

FORM 40
G. 30M-1-37

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of C.P.S. 1564 Tucu Yong Teong,
native of .................................... made by himself,
.................................... translated
at Sinza Station, on the 15/4/38, and interpreted by Clark Kao Chien.

At 7.20 p.m. on April 14th, 1938, an aged female came out
from Lane 157 Szechow Road near Sinza Road, shouting that there
was an evil man in her house. Together with C.P.C. 1845, I
proceeded to the entrance to the above alleyway, where I noticed
a male Chinese, wearing a Chinese red long gown, coming out. The
aged female then said to me that he was the very man. I then
caught hold of him, when four male Japanese in foreign dress
appeared, and one of them lifted up his coat and showed me his
pistol. I then released him. He told me that they were gendarmes
and they were coming to arrest some person(s), and further re-
quested our assistance.

At this time, C.P.C. 989 arrived at the scene, and I told him
to telephone to the station.

C.P.C. 1845 and I then followed the male Chinese to upstairs
of House 10, where we found no person, and then descended. The
male Chinese told me to post 2 C.P.C.s to watch this house,
whereupon I told him that without notifying the Police Station,
no policemen could be posted there. He then said that as I
could not post any person there, they would go to the Johnson
Garage and return in half hours time. He, together with the
four Japanese, drove away in a m/car I.fc. No. 25E J.D.P.

(d) C.P.S. 1564.

（批：Field "S"）

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为巡长1564号屠永通（Tucu Yong Teong），籍贯 ____ ，于1938年4月15日在新闸警署自行作出、由 ____ 转录、并由职员高健（Clark Kao Chien）口译的供词。

1938年4月14日晚7时20分，一名老妇从靠近新闸路的四川路157弄走出，大喊其家中有坏人。我与巡捕1845号随即前往上述弄堂入口，此时我注意到一名身穿中式红长衫的中国男子走出。老妇随即对我说他就是那个人。于是我抓住他，此时四名身着西装的日本男子出现，其中一人掀起外套向我展示其手枪。于是我释放了他。他告诉我他们是宪兵，前来逮捕某人，并请求我们协助。

此时，巡捕989号抵达现场，我让他打电话回警署。

随后我与巡捕1845号跟随该名中国男子上至10号房屋二楼，发现屋内无人，遂下楼。该中国男子让我派两名巡捕看守此屋，于是我告诉他，若不通知警署，无法派遣警员驻守。他便说既然我无法派人驻守，他们将去约翰逊汽车行（Johnson Garage），半小时后返回。他与四名日本人乘坐一辆机动车（车牌号 25E J.D.P.）驾车离去。

(d) 巡长1564号。

（批注：Field "S"）

At 7.20 p.m. on April 14th, 1938, I was on duty at Sinza

my conference book, an aged female approached the C.P.S. and

of him. Then four male Japanese in foreign dress appeared and
one of them lifted up his coat and showed us his pistol. C.P.S.
then released the man, who said that they were gendarmes and
they were coming to arrest some one at House 10 in this alleyway,
requesting our assistance. C.P.S. and I then proceeded to 2nd

floor of the above house, where we/no one there. He and the

警务调查报告。

以下为巡捕1845号陈明曾（Chen Ming Tseng），籍贯 **〔此处转录不清〕** ，于1938年4月15日在新闸警署自行作出、转录、并由职员老健（Lao Chien）口译的供词。

1938年4月14日晚7时20分，我正在靠近温州路的新闸路执勤。巡长1564号走来，正当他翻阅我的值班记录簿时，一名老妇走近巡长，报告说她家中有坏人。巡长与我随即前往温州路157弄，在该弄堂入口处，我们注意到一名身穿中式服装的中国男子正走出来。老妇向我们指认他，说就是这个人。巡长随即上前抓住他。此时四名身着西装的日本男子出现，其中一人掀起外套向我们展示其手枪。巡长随即释放了该男子，该男子称他们是宪兵，前来逮捕此弄堂10号内的某人，并请求我们协助。巡长与我随即上至上述房屋的二楼，发现那里/无人。他和四名日本人随后下楼，乘坐一辆机动车（车牌号 255 S.D.F.）驾车离去。离开前，他们说半小时后会回来。

(签名) 巡捕1845号。

The following is the statement of C.P.C. 989 Chih Ching-an,
native of 〔此处转录不清〕 made by himself,
translated
at Sinza Station, on the 15/4/38, and interpreted by Clerk Kao Chien.

At 7.20 p.m. on April 15th, 1938, at the corner of Sinza
and Anchow Roads, I saw an aged female shouting that some evil
person(·) was in this alleyway. I then immediately proceeded to
the alleyway, where I noticed that there were 4 Japanese males
in the alleyway. C.P.S. 1564 and C..C. 1845 had already been
there, and one of the Japanese showed us his pistol. I immediately
left the spot and telephoned to the station.
(sgd) Chih Ching-an.

以下为巡捕989号池静安（Chih Ching-an），籍贯 〔此处转录不清〕 ，于1938年4月15日在新闸警署自行作出、翻译、并由职员高健（Kao Chien）口译的供词。

1938年4月15日晚7时20分，在新闸路与安庆路（Anchow Roads）转角处，我看见一名老妇大喊此弄堂内有坏人。我随即立即前往该弄堂，注意到弄堂内有4名日本男子。巡长1564号和巡捕1845号已在那里，其中一名日本人向我们展示了他的手枪。我立即离开现场并打电话回警署。
(签名) 池静安。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tuang Lau Hoo ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ),
native of Kompo, taken by me S.D.C. 284
translated
at Sinza Station on the 15/4/38 and interpreted by Clerk Kao Chien.

My name is Tsang Lau Hoo, age 14, native of Kompo. I am
a student, and reside at House 10 Lane 117 Yenchow Road.
At 7.20 p.m. today, whilst partaking of dinner in the
guest room of my house, I saw two men dressed in grey foreign
suit enter my house and proceed upstairs. I did not know what
they were doing. They remained on the premises about 5 minutes,
then left via the front door.
Afterwards I went out to play and I knew nothing more.

(sd) Tsang Lau Hoo
pages.zh:

G. 30M-1-37

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

警务调查报告。

以下为张老好（Tuang Lau Hoo）（ 〔此处转录不清〕 ）的供词，籍贯高邮（Kompo），由我特别侦探主任284号于1938年4月15日在新闸警署录取、翻译，并由职员高健（Kao Chien）口译。

我叫张老好，14岁，籍贯高邮。我是学生，居住在延州路（Yenchow Road）117弄10号。
今天下午7时20分，当我在我家客房用餐时，看见两名身穿灰色西装的男子进入我家并上楼。我不知道他们在做什么。他们在屋内停留了约5分钟，然后从前门离开。
之后我出去玩，对此一无所知。

(签名) 张老好

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Kyoch Kuh Oen ( 顾 谷 恩 ),
native of Chinkiang taken by me C.D.C. 284
translated
at Sinza Stn. on the 15/4 '38 and interpreted by Clerk Lao Chien.

My name is Kyoch Kuh Oen, age 18, native of Chinkiang.
I am an apprentice, and reside at Route 10 Lane 157 Wenchow
Road.

At 7.00 a.m. today, whilst sewing clothing in the guest
room of my house, I saw two men clad in grey foreign suit
come in and proceed upstairs. I did not know what they were
doing. About minutes later, they came down and left via the
front door. After that two Chinese Policemen and the two men
again came to the house and proceeded upstairs. They remained
there about 2 or 3 minutes and left.

Afterwards Chinese and Foreign Detectives arrived.

This is a true statement.

(sgd) Kyoch Kuh Oen.
pages.zh:

G. 30M-1-27

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为顾谷恩（Kyoch Kuh Oen）（ 顾 谷 恩 ）的供词，籍贯镇江，由我刑事侦探主任284号于1938年4月15日在新闸警署录取、翻译，并由职员老健（Lao Chien）口译。

我叫顾谷恩，18岁，籍贯镇江。我是学徒，居住在温州路157弄10号。

今天早上7时，当我在我家客房缝制衣物时，看见两名身穿灰色西装的男子进来并上楼。我不知道他们在做什么。大约几分钟后，他们下来并从前门离开。此后，两名中国警察和那两名男子再次来到屋内并上楼。他们在那里停留了约2或3分钟后离开。

随后中外侦探到达。

此供词属实。

(签名) 顾谷恩。

I am a shop assistant employed by the Vai Lee Furniture
Shop at 309 Chungking Road and residing at 14, Lane No. 343,

At about 5.30 p.m. 12/4/38, while sitting in the guest room
I heard someone knock on the front door. I opened the door and
saw a man, age about 30 years, thin face, wearing navy blue
foreign jacket and pants, no hat and speaking Shanghai dialect,
standing outside. I asked him what he wanted and he said he
came from Y'poo and wanted to see Mrs Bah. I told him to wait
in the courtyard and I went upstairs to call Mrs Bah who was
occupying a room above the kitchen. She came downstairs and
this stranger asked her if she is Mrs Bah. When she replied
in the affirmative, the stranger told her that her husband was
at the station and that after a short while, several persons
would come to see her. At this time, 2 Japanese and 2 Chinese
came in by the front door, their descriptions being as follows:-

1/ Japanese, age about 30, height about 5'3", stout
build, long square face, wearing dark grey
woollen with white strips foreign jacket and
pants. No hat.

2/ Japanese, age about 30, height about 5'3", stout
build, square full face, wearing light grey
woollen foreign jacket and pants.

3/ Chinese, age about 30, height about 5'5", medium
build, oval face, wearing grey serge foreign
jacket and pants, speaks Shanghai dialect with
Kempo accent.

4/ Chinese, age about 20, height about 5'4", slim
build, long thin face, wearing grey imitation
serge long gown. (He didn't speak).

1938年4月12日下午5时30分左右，我正坐在客堂间内，听到有人敲前门。我打开门，看见外面站着一名男子，年龄约30岁，瘦脸，身穿深蓝色西式夹克和长裤，未戴帽子，讲上海话。我问他想要什么，他说他来自杨树浦，想见巴太太。我让他在院子里等候，便上楼去叫住在厨房楼上房间的巴太太。她下楼后，这名陌生人问她是否是巴太太。当她给予肯定答复后，陌生人告诉她，她的丈夫在捕房里，过一会儿会有几个人来见她。此时，2名日本人和2名中国人从前门进入，其特征描述如下：-

3/ 中国人，年龄约30岁，身高约5英尺5英寸，中等身材，椭圆脸，身穿灰色哔叽西式夹克和长裤，讲带有浦东口音的上海话。

4/ 中国人，年龄约20岁，身高约5英尺4英寸，身材瘦削，长瘦脸，身穿灰色仿哔叽长衫。（他没有说话）。

1938 年 4 月 12 日下午 3 时至 7 时，我被派往曼德勒路巡逻。下午 6 时，当我位于重庆路与曼德勒路路口时，华捕 1914 号告知我，上述地点有一辆无牌照的摩托车（m/crr），仅贴有两个汉字“Jhe-ping”（意为宪兵）。他还表示该车可能属于日本人。为防止发生意外事件，他让我监视该车，同时他前往警署报告此事。在车内，我看到一名男子低坐在前排座位上，我只看到了他的部分头部。该乘员约三十多岁，长脸，面色蜡黄，长发向后梳理，未戴帽子。大约两分钟后，一名中国男子上前告诉我，几名日本人和中国人正在他家中，企图带走一名租户的妻子。我立即陪同这名中国男子前往警署报案，当时那辆车仍停在那里。

华捕 1914 号 黄桑波（Wong Sang Poh）
1938 年 4 月 12 日下午 3 时至 7 时，我在重庆路以北执行巡逻任务。
同日约下午 6 时，在重庆路靠近曼德勒路处，我观察到一辆深灰色轿车（无牌照），其前挡风玻璃上贴有一张长方形白纸，上面写有两个汉字（〔此处转录不清〕）以及英文字母“M.P.”。
一名司机坐在车内，其体貌特征如下：“年龄约 32 岁，圆脸，未戴帽子，身穿黑色雨衣”，我询问他为何将车停在此处。他没有回答，只是挥了挥手。
看到巡捕 3418 号后，我告诉他这辆汽车属于日本人，肯定有事发生。我请他继续监视这辆特定的汽车，然后我自己来到本警署，向值班室警长（警员编号 61）报告了此事。此后，华捕 3418 号带一名中国男子到值班室，称一名中国妇女被日本人逮捕并带走。

签名。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Further to the Arrest of Chinese Female
by Japanese Authorities.
At 5p.m. on 16-4-38, J.D.S. Osano (Yangtseepoo Stn) received a telephone message from the Japanese Military River Police to the effect that Bah Nyoch San (白子山) and his wife Bah Wong Sz (白王氏) or Bah Siao Mei (白小妹) were being released. D.S. Stevens and J.T.S. Osano immediately proceeded to the Peking Road Jetty, where the two persons were handed over to them together with the letters and papers taken from the address 14/343 Chungking Road. Subsequently D.J.I. McCahay brought the female Bah Wong Sz to this station at 5.40p.m. 16-4-38.
Questioned by C.D.C. 254 and the undersigned the female stated that after she was taken away from her home at about 6p.m. 12-4-38 she was brought to a boat off the Peking Road Jetty, where she was detained until her release. During her detention, she was kept apart from her husband, but was well treated and was not interrogated except for particulars as to her name age, nativity etc. She denied that she had willingly accompanied the Japanese Military Police or that she knew the reason for her arrest; but stated that subsequently Bah Nyoch San had told her that the Japanese Military Police suspected him of being a Plain-clothes soldier of the Chinese Army.

1938 年 4 月 16 日下午 5 时，江浦路警署的日本侦探警佐 Osano 接到日本海军陆战队警察的电话通知，称白子山（Bah Nyoch San）及其妻子白王氏（Bah Wong Sz）或白小妹（Bah Siao Mei）即将获释。侦探警佐 Stevens 和日本侦探警佐 Osano 立即前往北京路码头，在那裡，这两人连同从重庆路 343 弄 14 号住所搜走的信件和文件一起被移交给他们。随后，日本侦探督察 McCahay 于 1938 年 4 月 16 日下午 5:40 将妇女白王氏带到本警署。
经华探主任 254 号及具名人讯问，该妇女陈述，1938 年 4 月 12 日下午 6 时左右她被从家中带走后，被带到北京路码头外的一艘船上，并被拘禁直至获释。在被拘禁期间，她与丈夫分开，但受到良好待遇，除询问姓名、年龄、籍贯等个人资料外，未受审问。她否认是自愿跟随日本宪兵，也声称不知道被捕原因；但陈述说，后来白子山告诉她，日本宪兵怀疑他是中国军队的便衣士兵。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Pah Vong Sz, alias Pah Siam Mei
native of ............................................................ taken by me C.D.C. f54.
at Che Rds. Stns. on the 16-4-38 and interpreted by Clerk Tsoong.

Pah Vong Sz, alias Pah Siam Mei, age 34 years, native of Yangchow, M/female, residing Room above Kitchen, No. 14 Lane 334 Chungking Road states as follows:-

At about 5.30p.m. on the 12-4-38, five male persons, (including 3 Japanese) attended my room and conducted a thorough search therein, this resulted in the seizure of my personal letters and photographs. They brought me together with the abovementioned articles, into a black m/car, parked outside the alleyway of my residence. This motor car, driven by a Japanese, was stopped at the Floating Restaurant, The Bund. I was taken into the aforestated restaurant and was questioned re my native province, age, and address......etc., by a Japanese Military Officer, after which, I was herded into a small room.

At about 4p.m. on 15-4-38, I observed my husband also present in the Floating Restaurant, when he told me that the Japanese arrested us on suspicion of being plain clothes men. The Japanese Military Officers have treated me very kindly.

At about 5p.m. on the 16-4-38, a foreigner (detective) attended the abovementioned restaurant and brought me as well as my husband out and proceeded to the Yangtsepee Station. Subsequently, I was sent by the foreign detective to the Chengtu Road Police Station at about 5.40p.m.

The property which was taken away by the Japanese, has been returned to me.

All the above is my true statement.

Signed:- Pah Vong Sz.

警务调查报告。

以下为本人（华探主任 f54 号）于 1938 年 4 月 16 日在重庆路警署记录的白王氏（Pah Vong Sz），又名白小妹（Pah Siam Mei）（籍贯：____）之陈述，由宗书记员口译。

白王氏，又名白小妹，34 岁，扬州人，女性，居住于重庆路 334 弄 14 号厨房楼上房间，陈述如下：

1938 年 4 月 12 日下午 5:30 左右，五名男子（包括 3 名日本人）来到我的房间并进行彻底搜查，结果没收了我的私人信件和照片。他们带着我和上述物品，进入停在我住所巷口外的一辆黑色汽车。这辆由一名日本人驾驶的汽车在外滩浮式餐厅（Floating Restaurant）停下。我被带入上述餐厅，一名日本军官就我的籍贯、年龄和地址 ____ 等对我进行了讯问，之后，我被赶进一个小房间。

1938 年 4 月 15 日下午 4 时左右，我在浮式餐厅看到我的丈夫也在那里，他告诉我，日本人因怀疑我们是便衣人员而逮捕了我们。日本军官对我非常友善。

1938 年 4 月 16 日下午 5 时左右，一名外国人（侦探）来到上述餐厅，将我和我丈夫带出，并前往杨树浦警署。随后，约下午 5:40，我被该外国侦探送往成都路警署。

被日本人拿走的财产已归还给我。

以上均为我的真实陈述。

签名：- 白王氏。

Sir,

At 5.50 p.m. 12-4-38, Mr. C.L. Mathew of Ewo Cold
Storage Co., 1500 Yangtzepoo Road telephoned to the
station to report that a male Chinese, employed as
foreman by the above company, had been arrested by
Japanese Military Authorities. The undersigned,
J.D.S. Osano and C.P.C. 167 immediately proceeded to
the scene and ascertained the following.

At 7.45 p.m. 12-4-38 the foreman, Bah Nyue San (白友山)
49, Hupeh, residing at House 14, Lane 343 Chunking Road,
had been called to the factory gate by three unknown male
Chinese, who, on his arrival there, had immediately handed
him over to two Japanese wearing Army Uniform, pistols and
swords, the party had then entered a waiting motor-vehicle
and driven away in a westerly direction. On receipt of
this information from the Indian watchman on duty at the
gate, detectives proceeded to the Japanese Military Police
Office, 250 Pingliang Road where J.D.S. Osano interviewed
the officer in charge but learned that at this office and
at Hongkew Headquarters, nothing was known of the arrest.
On returning to the station it was learned, by telephone
from Central station, that the arrested man was the father
of C.P.C. 1177 attached to Central, who had been informed
by an employee of the Ewo Company of his father's arrest.
The above mentioned detectives were about to leave for
Central to interview this C.P.C. when a further telephone
message was received from Chengtu Road station, reporting
that a female Chinese named "Siau Mei", 32, Yangchow,
(afterwards ascertained to be a concubine of Bah Nyue San)

1938 年 4 月 12 日晚上 7:45，领班白友山（Bah Nyue San），49 岁，湖北人，居住于重庆路 343 弄 14 号，被三名不知名的中国男子叫到工厂门口，当他到达那里时，这三名男子立即将他移交给两名身穿军装、携带手枪和军刀的日本军人，随后这伙人进入一辆等候的汽车，向西驶离。从门口值班的印度看守处收到此信息后，侦探们前往平凉路 250 号的日本宪兵队办公室，日本侦探警佐 Osano 会见了负责官员，但得知该办公室及虹口总部均不知晓此次逮捕行动。回到警署后，通过中央警署的电话得知，被捕者是隶属于中央警署的华捕 1177 号的父亲，该华捕已从怡和公司的一名员工处获悉其父被捕的消息。上述侦探正欲前往中央警署会见该华捕时，又收到成都路警署的电话消息，报告称一名名为“小妹”（Siau Mei）的中国妇女，32 岁，扬州人

C. 4 月 13 日

At 7.30 a.m. 5-4-38 a telephone message
was received from the home of Mr. Tsoong Liao (鐘),
manager of the New Asia Hotel, 107/5 Bubbling Well
Road that a party of 5 Japanese soldiers and one
Chinese had removed a Ford / truck, no licence
number, the property of the New Asia Hotel, and driven
it away along Bubbling Well Road.

S.I. Lovell, D.S. Greenfield and J.D.D. 87
attended but on arrival the Japanese party had left.
It was ascertained:-

At 7.45 a.m. 5-4-38, the Japanese party had
removed the truck from outside the home of Mr. Tsoong
Liao. No notice then was given of its removal,
and the vehicle, which has been stored in Lane 1537
Bubbling Well Road since the outbreak of hostilities,
was driven away under its own power, and without a
licence.

Mr. Tsoong is at present in Hongkong, only
his wife and servants being in residence at the
Bubbling Well address.

警司 Lovell、侦探长 Greenfield 和 J.D.D. 87 前往处理，但到达时日军一行已离开。经查实：-

Male Chinese named Chang Tuh Ming arrested
by Japanese Military Police, Woosung Road.

At 2p.m. on the 26-3-38 a telephone message was
received at Central Station from Warrant Officer Shimowata
attached to The Japanese Military Police, to the effect
that enquiries re. this case had been completed at Soochow,
and that Chang Tuh Ming had not been found to be guilty
of looting or being concerned with any Japanese in
committing looting. However it was ascertained that the
lead now being detained at Japanese Military Headquarters
was obviously looted property, and it was now requested
that Chang Tuh Ming be handed over to The Japanese
Military Authorities so that he could appear before the
Japanese Military Court and a decision could be given re.
the disposal of the lead. Should the suspect be ordered
to be released, he would be handed over to be released by
the S.M.P.

At 3.30p.m. Sergeant Hasegawa attached to The
Japanese Military Police came to the station to escort
the suspect to Japanese Military Police Headquarters No.
473 North Szechuen Road.

Mr. Glore D.B.O. "A" was informed re. the facts of
this case and on his instructions the Japanese Military
Police Sergeant was informed that an official document
should be submitted to the S.M.P. giving reasons for
handing over.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 29 MAR 1938）

名为张土明（Chang Tuh Ming）的华籍男子
被日本宪兵队在吴淞路逮捕。

1938年3月26日下午2时，中央巡捕房收到附属于日本宪兵队的准尉下渡（Shimowata）的电话留言，大意是有关本案在苏州的调查已结束，未发现张土明犯有抢劫罪或伙同任何日本人进行抢劫。但经查明，目前扣押在日本宪兵司令部的铅块显然是赃物，现要求将张土明移交给日本军方，以便他在日本军事法庭出庭，并就铅块的处置作出决定。如果命令释放嫌疑人，他将由上海公共租界工部局警务处移交释放。

下午3时30分，附属于日本宪兵队的长谷川（Hasegawa）警佐来到巡捕房，护送嫌疑人前往北四川路473号日本宪兵队总部。

"A"区侦探长格洛尔（Glore）先生获知本案事实，并根据其指示，告知日本宪兵队警佐应向上海公共租界工部局警务处提交一份正式文件，说明移交理由。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1938年3月29日）

At 5p.m. a letter from Warrant Officer Shimowata
attached to The Japanese Military Police was handed to
D. S. Kobayashi which requested the handing over of Chang
Tuh Ming. Translation of letter is attached hereto.
Mr. Robertson D.O. "A" was informed re the request,
and on his instructions Detective Inspector Telfer Senior
Detective was to inform Mr. S.C. Young Deputy Commissioner
Crime, re the circumstances of the case.
About 7.20p.m. the Senior Detective telephoned Mr.
S.C. Young D.C. (Crime) and explained that the Japanese
Military Police desired to have Chang Tuh Ming handed over
to them immediately so that they could explain to him that
he had not been found guilty of looting at Soochow, but
the lead which they had seized they would confiscate.
After they had informed him to this effect they would
return him to the S.M.P. on the morning of March 27, 1938
for his release, which they stated by letter(attached)
would be done although no date is mentioned. However,
Mr. Young gave definite instructions that Chang Tuh Ming
had not to be handed over and if the Japanese Military
Police desired to give any explanation prior to his
release it had to be done in the presence of the Senior
Detective at Central Police Station or at the S.M.P.
Headquarters. Sgt. Sgt. Kobayashi about 9a.m. on March
26th, 1938 personally interviewed Sergeant Simpson of

March 26th, 1938.

To Officer i/c of Central Station.

Request for the handing over of
a prisoner.

Accused Chang Teh Ming, age 44, residing No. 17 Ou Yo Road,
Shanghai Kiangse Province.

The above person was previously detained in our office
for enquiries regarding the transportation of goods from a
military occupied area without first obtaining a permit from
the Japanese Military Authorities but this suspect was handed
over to the S.M.P. on request for the purpose of interrogation.
It is now requested that this person be returned as the property
is to be confiscated and the prisoner will be released in view
of the fact that there is nothing to prove he was concerned with
looting. It is understood that the suspect will be returned to
the S.M.P. for release.

Warrant Officer Shimowatari.
(Chopped) Japanese Military Police.

关于移交囚犯的请求。

被告张德明（Chang Teh Ming），44岁，住江苏省上海欧阳路17号。

上述人员此前因在未先从日本军方获得许可证的情况下从军事占领区运输货物而被拘留在我处接受调查，但该嫌疑人应要求被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处以供审讯。现请求将该人退回，因为财产将被没收，且鉴于没有任何证据证明他参与抢劫，囚犯将被释放。据悉，嫌疑人将被退回上海公共租界工部局警务处以予释放。

准尉下渡（Shimowatari）。

Male Chinese named Chang Tuh Ming arrested

On the instructions of Detective Inspector Telfer
Senior Detective who received a telephone from Mr.
MacDermott P.A. to D.C.(Crime), the undersigned, D.I.
Nakamura attached to the S.P.C., and D.S. Kobayashi

Police situated on Woosung Road near Kashing Road, where
Warrant Officer Shimowatan and Sergeant Major Konno
were interviewed re. this case. It was pointed out to
（批：Official Bonh Copy）the two aforementioned officers that Chang Tuh Ming
had been arrested and taken to The Japanese Military
Police Headquarters without the permission or assistance
of the S.M.Police, and it was requested that Chang Tuh Ming
be handed over to the S.M.Police so that enquiries could
be made re. this case.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL ... 22 MAR 1938）

Warrant Officer Shimowatan stated that Sergeant
Major Konno was in charge of this case, and on a request

Sergeant Major Konno arrived in Shanghai from Seoul
on the 14/3/38, and was attached to The Japanese Military
Police Headquarters at Woosung Road. At a late hour
on the night of the 20/3/38, certain information was

根据高级侦探督察特尔弗的指示，他收到了犯罪部副警务总监助理麦克德莫特先生的电话，本人、附属于特别警察课（S.P.C.）的中村（Nakamura）侦探督察以及侦探长小林前往位于吴淞路靠近嘉善路的日本宪兵队总部，就本案讯问了准尉下渡（Shimowatan）和军曹今野（Konno）。向

今野军曹于1938年3月14日从首尔抵达上海，隶属于吴淞路日本宪兵队总部。1938年3月20日深夜，收到某些情报

pages.en:
Page 2.

received by Sergeant Major Konno to the effect that
Cheng Tuh Ming had brought about 30 pieces of lead
which was looted property from Soochow to Shanghai and
stored same at No. 175 Canton Road. The informer also
stated that the lead would be disposed of the same night
(16/3/38) and some Japanese were involved in the case.
It was also suspected that he had been concerned in
other looting cases.

Sergeant Major Konno not knowing the procedure re.
obtaining S.M.Police assistance, and being of the opinion
that Central District came under Japanese Military
supervision, obtained the assistance of a subordinate and
together with the informer proceeded to No. 175 Canton
Road in a motor car where they arrested Cheng Tuh Ming
and took him to the Headquarters Woosung Road.

Sergeant Major Konno stated that he was extremely
sorry that he had not obtained the assistance of the S.M.
Police, and that it was owing to him only having been in
Shanghai for such a short time, and not being aware of the
correct procedure, also the urgency of the case which made
him arrest the suspect. The Sergeant Major stated that in
future he will give this matter his careful attention.

Commanding Officer Shimamura also stated that he would
instruct his men to co-operate with the S.M.Police on all
pages.zh:
第2页。

今野军曹收到的情报大意是，张土明（Cheng Tuh Ming）将约30块从苏州劫掠来的铅块运到上海，并存放在广东路175号。线人还称，这些铅块将在当晚（1938年3月16日）被处置，且有一些日本人卷入此案。还怀疑他参与了其他抢劫案件。

今野军曹因不了解寻求上海公共租界警务处协助的程序，并认为中央区处于日本军方监管之下，便叫上一名下级，与线人一起乘车前往广东路175号，在那里逮捕了张土明（Cheng Tuh Ming）并将其带至吴淞路总部。

今野军曹表示，对于未寻求上海公共租界警务处的协助深感抱歉，这是由于他刚到上海不久，不了解正确程序，加之案情紧急，促使他逮捕了嫌疑人。该军曹表示，今后他将仔细注意此事。

指挥官岛村（Shimamura）也表示，他将指示其部下在所有

pages.en:
Page 3.

future occasions.

The suspected person named Chang Tuh Ming was then
handed over to the undersigned, D.I. Nakamura and and
J.S. Kobayashi. However at the time of handing over the
Japanese Authorities requested that the suspected person
be detained at Central Station, until such times as
enquiries had been made at Soochow as to whether the lead
taken from 175 Canton Road was looted property or not.

When enquiries have been completed by the Japanese
Authorities at Soochow they will inform the S.P.O. re the
result of same, so that should the suspect be proven
guilty of looting they will make application for his
handing over.

The suspect Chang Tuh Ming was questioned at Central
Station by the undersigned, and stated that on the
6-3-38 he was in Soochow and drew up a contract with the
Chang Tsung Kyi (张宗记/鸿源) Lead Factory for the
purpose of buying lead at $85.00 per picul.. He returned
to Shanghai on the 7-3-38 and met one named Sung Tsia
Liang (宋家亮) who is the accountant of the aforemention-
ed lead factory, at his home situated at No. 175 Canton
Road on the 12-3-38. After again discussing the contract
Chang Tuh King paid a total sum of $1360.00 to the
accountant for the purchase of 30 pieces of lead. The
pages.zh:
第3页。

未来场合与上海公共租界警务处合作。

随后，名为张土明的嫌疑人被移交给本人、中村（Nakamura）侦探督察和小林（Kobayashi）侦探长。然而，在移交时，日本当局要求将嫌疑人拘留在中央巡捕房，直到在苏州调查清楚从广东路175号取走的铅块是否为赃物为止。

当日本当局在苏州完成调查后，他们将把结果通知特别警察办事处（S.P.O.），以便如果证明嫌疑人犯有抢劫罪，他们将申请将其移交。

嫌疑人张土明在中央巡捕房接受本人讯问，他陈述称，1938年3月6日他在苏州，并与张宗记（Chang Tsung Kyi，音译：张宗记/鸿源）铅厂签订合同，目的是以每担85.00美元的价格购买铅。他于1938年3月7日返回上海，并于1938年3月12日在其位于广东路175号的家中会见了上述铅厂的会计师宋家亮（Sung Tsia Liang）。在再次讨论合同后，张土明（Chang Tuh King）向会计师支付了总计1360.00美元以购买30块铅。该

pages.en:
Page 4.

accountant returned to Soochow with the money on the
14-3-38. Chang Tuh Ming states that he trusted the
accountant and did not receive a receipt.
At 7a.m. on the 16-3-38 the lead was brought to
Shanghai on a motor truck driven by a Japanese named
Hashimoto, and delivered to No. 176 Canton Road. At
10.30p.m. on the 16-3-38 the suspected person was then
arrested and taken away by the Japanese Authorities.
Chang Tuh Ming was asked if he wished to make any
statement, and stated that he wanted to do so.
Translation of same is attached hereto.
Enquiries proceeding.

Chang Tuh Ming
Shanghai C... .lll.
Central Station 21st.March 1938 translated Clerk Sih Chien Shih

Chang Tuh Ming, age 44 years, native of Shanghai, residing
at 176 Canton Road, manager of the Mah Wah Paper Manufacturing
Factory.

On the 6-3-38, I went to Soochow and purchased 16 piculs
of lead (30 pieces) from the Chang Tsung Kyi Lead Factory at
$85.00 per picul, for a total value of $1,360.00. On 7-3-38 I
returned to Shanghai and bought five cases of cigarettes, value
$1,340.00, on Sung Tsia Liang's behalf against the cost value
of the lead, which I would pay over to him. On 12-3-38, Sung
came to Shanghai and visited me at my home. Besides handing
over the five cases of cigarettes to him, I also gave him $460
including the balance and the transportation fees of the lead.
Sung returned to Soochow on the 14-3-38, and as he is my
acquaintance, I did not ask him to issue me a receipt.

On 16-3-38, the lead, which I had bought, was delivered to
my home by a Japanese in a motor truck.

At about 10.30 p.m. on the 16-3-38, one named Dzung Hwang
Yao together with two plain clothes Japanese visited me at my
home and asked me whether I had ever purchase anything at
Soochow to which I informed them that I had bought 16 piculs of
lead at Soochow. They then asked me where did I keep the lead.
I led them to a downstairs room and showed them the lead. They
then informed me that they were come from the Japanese Military
Police and asked me to follow them to their Headquarters at
Wusong Road. I took a piece of the lead and followed them to
their Headquarters. On arrival, I was locked up in No.1
Detention Cell.
pages.zh:
张德明
上海 C ____ lll.
中央捕房 1938年3月21日 翻译员：施建石 (Sih Chien Shih)

张德明，44岁，上海人，居住于广东路176号，大华造纸厂经理。

1938年3月6日，我前往苏州，以每担85.00美元的价格从张宗记铅厂购买了16担铅块（30件），总价值为1,360.00美元。1938年3月7日，我返回上海，代表宋嘉良购买了五箱香烟，价值1,340.00美元，以此抵充我将支付给他的铅块成本价。1938年3月12日，宋来到上海并到我家拜访我。除了将五箱香烟交给他外，我还给了他460美元，其中包括余款和铅块的运输费。宋于1938年3月14日返回苏州，由于他是我的熟人，我没有要求他给我开具收据。

1938年3月16日，我所购买的铅块由一名日本人用卡车送到我家。

1938年3月16日晚上10时30分左右，一名名为庄黄耀 (Dzung Hwang Yao) 的人与两名便衣日本人来到我家，问我是否在苏州购买过任何东西，我告知他们我在苏州购买了16担铅块。随后他们问我铅块存放在何处。我带他们到楼下的一个房间，向他们展示了铅块。随后他们告知我，他们来自日本宪兵队，并要求我随他们前往吴淞路的总部。我拿了一块铅块，随他们前往总部。到达后，我被关进第一号拘留室。

pages.en:
-Sheet 2-

The following day(17-3-38), at about 1 p.m. I was removed
from the cell and was questioned by a Japanese -ilitary Officer
and the following conversation took place:-

Q. What was your former occupation?

A. 14 years ago I was working with the Machinery Department
of the Dah Wah Hong on Peking Road.

Q. How much was the capital?

A. $80,000.00.

Q. Who was the manager?

A. Chang Cha Sung.

Q. Why was the hong removed to the present address at
Canton Road?

A. About 10 years ago, the hong was removed from Peking
Road to 391 Shanse Road and during the falling term of 1936 the
hong removed to the present address at 175 Canton Road.

Q. How long have you been the manager of the Dah Wah Paper
Manufacturing Factory?

A. About 11 years.

Q. How much is your monthly salary?

A. $300.00.

Q. Who is the proprietor?

A. Yih Ying San.

Q. How long has the Dah Wah Paper Manufactory existed and
who is the founder?

A. In July 1928 I founded the Dah Wah Paper Manufacturing
Factory together with Yih Ying San.

Q. How much was the capital?
pages.zh:
-第2页-

次日（1938年3月17日）下午1点左右，我被从拘留室带出，接受了一名日本军官的讯问，对话内容如下：-

问：你以前的职业是什么？

答：14年前，我在南京路的大华洋行机械部工作。

问：资本是多少？

答：80,000.00美元。

问：经理是谁？

答：张查松 (Chang Cha Sung)。

问：洋行为何迁至目前位于广东路的地址？

答：大约10年前，洋行从南京路迁至山西路391号，在1936年下半年期间，洋行迁至目前位于广东路175号的地址。

问：你担任大华造纸厂经理有多久了？

答：大约11年。

问：你的月薪是多少？

答：300.00美元。

问：业主是谁？

答：叶英三 (Yih Ying San)。

问：大华造纸厂成立多久了，创始人是谁？

答：1928年7月，我与叶英三共同创立了大华造纸厂。

问：资本是多少？

pages.en:
-: heet 3-

A. $250,000.00.
Q. Where is the factory?
A. At 46 Chang An Road, Chapel.
Q. How much is your monthly salary?
A. $100.00.
Q. How much is the profit?
A. $250,000.00.
Q. Did you ever divide the profit between you and Yih Ying
San?
A. No, we keep it as our capital.
Q. How did you come back to Shanghai from Soochow on 7-3-38
and did you ever bring anything along with you?
A. Prior to my departure I obtained a pass at Soochow.
Later I returned to Shanghai by motor car, property of my friend
Mr. Pao of the Dah Chung Hwa Match Manufacturing Factory at
Soochow. I brought along with me 900 ounces of silver (about
$800.00) and 1 ounce 3.2 maces of gold, which were bought by
Tung on my behalf at Soochow (these were later sold out on the
12-3-38 at, Shanghai).
Q. Where did you keep the gold and silver?
A. The silver was placed in two general wooden cases which
were placed in the car whilst the gold was kept in my pocket.
Q. How much is your estate?
A. Owing to the outbreak of the war, I am unable to
estimate it.
Q. What is the approximate value?
A. About $15,000.00.
pages.zh:
-: 第3页-

答：250,000.00美元。
问：工厂在哪里？
答：在闸北长安路46号。
问：你的月薪是多少？
答：100.00美元。
问：利润是多少？
答：250,000.00美元。
问：你和叶英三之间是否分配过利润？
答：没有，我们将其作为资本保留。
问：1938年3月7日你是如何从苏州回到上海的，是否随身携带了物品？
答：出发前，我在苏州获得了通行证。后来我乘坐我朋友、苏州大中华火柴厂鲍先生的汽车返回上海。我随身携带了900两白银（约值800.00美元）和1两3钱2分黄金，这些是由董 (Tung) 代表我在苏州购买的（这些后来于1938年3月12日在上海售出）。
问：金银存放在哪里？
答：白银放在两个普通木箱里，置于车内，而黄金则放在我的口袋里。
问：你的财产有多少？
答：由于战争爆发，我无法估算。
问：大概价值多少？
答：约15,000.00美元。

我叫王俊文，24岁，无锡人，居住于广东路175号。我是受雇于大华造纸厂的苦力。
1938年3月17日上午8时15分，两名身穿军装的日本人来到大华造纸厂办公室，通过“手势”命令我将29件铅块从办公室搬到一辆等候的卡车上。当时我正搬运铅块并将其装上黄色的军用卡车，该车停在江西路与广东路路口。我没看清车牌号码，随后两名日本人驾驶卡车朝未知方向驶离。

The manager named Chang Tuh Ling (張德明) of the Great
China Paper Mill is my husband. At about 10.30p.m. on the
16-3-38 ~, husband and myself were in a room situated on the 3rd
floor of No.176 Canton Road when one named Tsung Kwang Yau
(宋光裕) who is the manager of the Far Eastern Industrial
Company came to the room accompanied by two Japanese wearing
plain foreign style clothes. The Japanese asked my husband
to go with them. He afterwards accompanied by the two Japanese
and Tsung Kwang Yau left the premises. The Japanese also
taking away a piece of lead.

At about 12 O'clock I received a telephone message from
Tsung Kwang Yau stating that he had been released by the
Japanese. However he did not let me know from where he was
phoning and cut off.

At 8.30a.m.on the 17-3-38 two Japanese dressed in Military
uniforms came to the premises of the Great China Paper Mills
and told my coolie to carry out 29 pieces of lead, which they
took away.

On the morning of the 16-3-38 my husband told me that 30
pieces of lead which he bought in Soochow were being delivered
to the premises at 7.30 a.m. 16-3-38.

Signed by Chang Han Sz.

Zaushing                      xx   C.D.S. 115.

    Yih Tuh Chi C, aged 25 years, native of Zaushing, cloth
dealer, married, residing at No. 5 Zung Chong Lee off Rue Wants,
states as follows:-

    On the 12th inst. (the anniversary of the late Dr. Sun Yat
Sen's death) after having tiffin I parked my cloth along Soochow
Road. I had a rest by 4.30 p.m. and then took a stroll in the
vicinity of The Bund Garden where I observed Japanese sentry
standing near the iron gate of the Floating Restaurant. I was
ordered by the Japanese sentry to leave the place, but a man who
was wearing European styled dress called me to approach him. I
thought he bore me malice so I became nervous and ran toward
Nanking Road. I was subsequently apprehended by the Japanese sen-
try at the Nanking Road Bund and brought to the Floating Restaurant
where I was later detained. I was interrogated on several
occasions during which I was ill-treated. However, they could not
connect me with anything other than my occupation as a cloth
dealer. I, therefore was released at 10a.m. today (20-3-38) and
escorted to the Central Police Station.
    The above is my true statement.                Signed.

〔此处为签名〕

叶得青。

嘉兴                      xx   C.D.S. 115。
中央巡捕房      38年3月20日     翻译      书记员 F.C. Pan
                              /---------

    叶得青，25岁，嘉兴人，布商，已婚，住万特路（Rue Wants）义昌里5号，陈述如下：-

    本月12日（已故孙中山博士逝世周年纪念日），午餐后，我将布料停放在苏州路旁。下午4时30分我休息片刻，随后在外滩花园附近散步，期间我看见一名日本哨兵站在“浮游餐厅”（Floating Restaurant）的铁门附近。日本哨兵命令我离开该地，但一名身穿欧式服装的男子叫我走近他。我以为他对我怀有恶意，因此感到紧张，便向南京路方向跑去。随后，我在南京路外滩被日本哨兵逮捕，并被带至“浮游餐厅”，之后我被拘禁在那里。在此期间我遭受了数次审讯及虐待。然而，他们除了认定我是布商这一职业外，无法将我与其他任何事项联系起来。因此，我于今日（38年3月20日）上午10时被释放，并被护送至中央巡捕房。
    以上是我的真实陈述。                签名。

OAK YIH TUH CHING (叶得青), AGED 25, NATIVE OF LAU-SHING, CLOTH DEALER OF E ZUNG CHONG LEE (义昌利) RUE MANTE, DETAINED BY THE JAPANESE MILITARY.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

At 4.20 p.m. on the 12-3-38 a telephone message was received from C.P.C.3109 reporting that four armed Japanese (one in uniform and three in plain clothes, were attempting to arrest a male Chinese on The Bund near Nanking Road.

S.I. Okawa, J.P.C.18 Isebe and C.D.C.27 attended and were followed by Inspt. Brownrigg, C.D.C.194 and the under-signed and as a result of enquiries the following was ascertained:-

（批：Special Branch copy）

At about 4 p.m. on the 12-3-38 1st Class Private S. Murase who on duty at the North entrance of the Floating Restaurant, observed a male Chinese loitering at the head of the pontoon gangway in what he considered a suspicious manner.

Speaking in Chinese, Private Murase then ordered the Chinese to leave but apart from moving a few feet parallel with the Restaurant, the Chinese ignored the order, which was then repeated by Private Murase, whereupon the Chinese is said to have suddenly taken to his heels Southward along the Bund.

This was witnessed by 1st Class Private Y. Isomura who in company with two other Japanese and a Chinese member of the Bu Tih Society, were close at hand observing the suspect and

先生，

38年3月10日中午12时25分，通过交换台电话接到在老闸北区罗宾森路74号爱华棉纺厂外执勤的中央电话交换台 C.P.C. 908 的电话消息，称一名中国男子因持有手榴弹在罗宾森路被日本宪兵逮捕，该信息来自一名行人。

日籍侦探 J.D.3. 48 Mori 前往老闸北区极司菲尔路94号宪兵司令部，获悉当日上午11时50分，他们从老闸北区罗宾森路64号东亚麻袋厂带走了一名中国男子，该男子于当日上午9时在该厂外的人行道上被一名宪兵以持有手榴弹为由逮捕。

该中国男子自报姓名为李翠华（Lee Tsui Hwo），57岁，金门（Kempo）人，职业为二手小贩，住老闸北区罗宾森路福庆里24号，他在接受宪兵讯问时称，他于38年3月6日以10分钱的价格从一名乞丐阶层的中国人那里购买了这枚手榴弹以及几小块黄铜，但在被捕前并不知道买到的是手榴弹，而以为是一块优质的黄铜。讯问后，他带领宪兵前往其位于老闸北区罗宾森路福庆里24号的住所，对 premises 进行了搜查，但未发现任何具有罪证性质的物品。

宪兵表示对该人没有指控，因为显然他是在不知情的情况下购买了手榴弹，在拘留他一两天后，除非警方希望讯问他，否则将予以释放；如果是这样，他们会将他移交给我们要，之后我们可以释放他，但他们声明我们不能保留手榴弹。

SHANGHAI DAILY NEWS
JULY 2 1940

AN IMPORTANT ISSUE

Two of the most important questions of local concern, which have come prominently to the fore recently, relate to the request for the return to the Municipality of Greater Shanghai of the records of the Chinese Land Office, deposited with the Shanghai Municipal Council by Mayor Wu Teh-chen, on the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1937, and the ultimate fate of the Chinese Courts in the International Settlement and the French Concession. As far back as July 22, 1938, this journal, commenting on the former, wrote:

Another hindrance to the land market is the fact that the Chinese Land Office has ceased to function. The issue of title deeds is out of the question, but with the co-operation of consular officials it has been found possible to devise a scheme for carrying on. The reestablishment of an official land office is a prime need, and it is hoped that, once normality has been restored, it will be possible speedily to erect the necessary machinery, with, it is hoped, many of the disadvantages eliminated.

That was written while there was still a certain degree of insecurity around Shanghai, and recognized that the situation in the environs of Shanghai was still abnormal. In October of the same year, however, Mr. Fu Hsiao-an became Mayor of Greater Shanghai, and there can be no gainsaying the fact that, during the past year and three-quarters, conditions have improved to such a degree that it can be said without fear of contradiction the situation is as normal as can reasonably be expected. There cannot be the slightest criticism of the Shanghai Municipal Council in accepting the responsibility for the safe custody of the records of the Chinese Land Office. To have left them on the scene of hostilities would have led to their dispersal to the four winds, resulting in a perfectly chaotic state in the land market outside the foreign areas. It was an act of prudence and neutrality. Conditions since the Council accepted that responsibility have vastly changed. It is desirable that the records be returned, and the de facto government desiring the affairs of the Municipality of this part, given every facility for carrying out their functions.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

foreign areas. It is necessary that that point should be stressed. An endeavour has been made during Mr. Fu Hsiao-an's mayoralty to improve relationships between the International Settlement and the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, and progress has been made. Agreement with regard to policing the "badlands" has been reached, though there appears, for some reason which has not been disclosed, some delay in implementing it. It is to be hoped that further progress will eventually lead to the formation of the new police force which that agreement contemplates and another important issue thus got out of the way.

The return of the records of the Chinese Land Office, will enable the Municipality of Greater Shanghai to establish adequate control over land transactions outside the foreign areas. Consequently, to insist on retaining them in the International Settlement, under the safe custody of the Municipal Council, must cause no small amount of inconvenience to the Municipality of Greater Shanghai in the administration of its own affairs, and it is only reasonable to suggest that such inconvenience should be removed, and with it a possible cause of irritation. There is not the slightest reason for doubting that a newly reconstituted Chinese Land Office would not prove to be equally as efficient as its predecessor which existed prior to the time of the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities. It is believed that the plan devised with the assistance of consular officials has worked admirably up to the present, and would probably continue to do so, but the fact does remain that the de facto government desires to establish a Land Office of its own, and from a purely realistic point of view, and distinct from the entirely doctrinaire, that desire should be gratified. Indeed it may be safely urged that, so long as essential rights are not involved, everything possible should be done by the respective authorities to ensure that there shall be that close co-operation without which it is not possible to improve conditions in and around Shanghai. Very slowly it is true, but nevertheless perceptibly there has been improvement in the relationships between the administrations of the foreign areas and their environs which this journal has heartily welcomed. It is highly desirable that every effort should be directed towards the continuance of that improvement, for upon it depends the future of Shanghai and its prosperity depends upon it. To patch the Land Office records through only the International Settlement is to Shanghai's disadvantage.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

Lie

《上海每日新闻》
1940年7月2日

一个重要问题

近期凸显出来的两个最受本地关注的重要问题，涉及将1937年中日敌对行动爆发时由市长吴铁城寄存在上海公共租界工部局的中国地政局档案归还给大上海市政府的请求，以及国际租界和法租界内中国法院的最终命运。早在1938年7月22日，本报在评论前者时写道：

阻碍土地市场的另一个事实是，中国地政局已停止运作。签发地契已无从谈起，但在领事官员的合作下，人们发现有可能制定一个方案以维持运作。重建官方地政局是首要需求，希望一旦恢复正常，能够迅速建立必要的机构，并希望消除许多弊端。

那是写于上海周边仍存在一定程度的不安全局势之时，并承认上海周边地区的局势仍然异常。然而，同年10月，傅筱庵先生成为大上海市长，无可否认的是，在过去的一年零三个月里，局势已改善到如此程度，可以毫无异议地说，局势已达到合理预期的正常状态。上海公共租界工部局在接受保管中国地政局档案的责任方面，不应受到丝毫批评。如果将这些档案留在敌对行动现场，将会导致其四散流失，致使外国区域以外的土地市场陷入完全混乱的状态。这是一种审慎和中立的举动。自工部局承担该责任以来，情况已发生巨大变化。归还档案是可取的，并且应为渴望处理本地区市政事务的事实政府提供一切便利，以履行其职能。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

外国区域。必须强调这一点。在傅筱庵先生担任市长期间，曾努力改善国际租界与大上海市政府之间的关系，并取得了进展。关于 policing “不良地带”（badlands）的协议已达成，尽管出于某种未披露的原因，实施似乎有所延迟。希望进一步的进展最终能促成该协议所设想的新警察部队的组建，从而解决另一个重要问题。

归还中国地政局档案，将使大上海市政府能够对国外区域以外的土地交易进行充分控制。因此，坚持在国际租界内、在工部局的安全保管下保留这些档案，必然会给大上海市政府在其自身事务的管理上带来不小的不便，建议消除这种不便以及由此可能引起的摩擦，这是合乎情理的。没有任何理由怀疑，新重组的中国地政局的效率不会亚于中日敌对行动爆发前存在的前任机构。据信，在领事官员协助下制定的计划迄今为止运行良好，并且可能会继续如此，但事实仍然是，事实政府希望建立自己的地政局，从纯粹现实的角度来看，而非完全教条的角度，这一愿望应得到满足。事实上，可以稳妥地主张，只要不涉及基本权利，各方当局应尽一切可能确保密切合作，没有这种合作，就不可能改善上海及其周边地区的状况。确实，外国区域行政机构与其周边地区之间的关系改善非常缓慢，但却是显而易见的，本报对此表示衷心欢迎。极力期望将所有努力导向这种改善的持续，因为上海的未来取决于此，其繁荣也取决于此。仅通过国际租界来拼凑地政局档案对上海是不利的。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

JUN 29 1940

Land Certificates
Issue Ending

Former Official Joins
New Regime; Parleys
Concluding

Negotiations between the foreign
Consular Body here and Mayor Fu
Siao-en for the transfer to him of the
land certificates in the custody of the
Shanghai Municipal Council are
reaching a final stage, it was learned
yesterday. The surrender of the
certificates is now only a matter of
days.

The negotiations have been pro-
tracted and have been carried on for
some time. Following the closure of
the land office of the Chungking Gov-
ernment here, Mayor Fu has establish-
ed another land office which has for
one of its chief executives a former
official of the old land office.

The suspension of the former land
office followed soon after the outbreak
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities. Ever
since, transfers of property owned by
Chinese and foreigners under Chinese
jurisdiction could not be legalised. A
halt was called to the realty boom in
Shanghai owing to the depreciation
of the Chinese dollar. Property and
land sales to a great extent became a
matter of personal trust, the bills of
sales being recorded in the notary
office of the First Special District
Court, without any official deeds
changing ownership.

Despite the abnormal situation many
sales of property in the Settlement
and French Concession were recorded,
the seller being required in most cases
to furnish the buyers with the proper
undertaking that he would transfer
the land certificates to the new
owners as soon as they became
available. In many cases the lawyers
of the contracting parties acted as
guarantors.

1940年6月29日

地契
发放结束

前官员加入
新政权；谈判
接近尾声

据悉，昨日此地外国领事团与傅筱庵市长之间关于将上海公共租界工部局保管的地契移交给他的谈判已进入最后阶段。移交地契现在只是几天内的事情。

谈判旷日持久，已持续了一段时间。随着重庆政府在此地的地政局关闭，傅市长建立了另一个地政局，其主要高管之一是原地政局的一名前官员。

原地政局的停摆紧随中日敌对行动爆发之后。自此以后，在中国管辖权下属于中国人和外国人的财产转让无法合法化。由于中国货币贬值，上海的房地产热潮 halted。房地产和土地销售在很大程度上变成了个人信任的问题，买卖契约在第一特区法院的公证处登记，没有任何官方地契变更所有权。

尽管局势异常，租界和法租界内的许多房产销售仍进行了登记，在大多数情况下，要求卖方提供适当的承诺，保证一旦地契可用，即将其转让给新业主。在许多情况下，缔约双方的律师充当担保人。

Lilo

CHINA PRESS.

MAR 2 4 1939

Records Of The Land Office

AMONG other things, the "Ta Tao" puppet regime has been attempting to induce the Shanghai Municipal Council to turn over the records of the Land Office of the Chinese Municipal Government of Greater Shanghai which were left to its safe custody at the time of the withdrawal of the Chinese from this port.

As on previous occasions the Council has refused to comply with the request of the Japan-sponsored regime. It would be superfluous to point out that the records in question are of vital importance not only to the Chinese but also to the foreign nationals. They are the conclusive evidence of property ownership and other rights created by it. Banks, both Chinese and foreign, are holding numerous mortgages which are registered with the Land Office, and their ultimate hope of claiming money borrowed on such mortgages depends upon the preservation of these records. The Council would be seriously jeopardizing public interest should it deliver the records to the puppet authorities.

Moreover, the records are entrusted to the Council for safe custody, and the Council is accordingly holding them for the benefit of the Land Office. In other words, the Council is a trustee in the proper sense of the word, and it may be held liable for breach of trust should the records be handed to the possession of a third party.

There is every reason to believe that the "Ta Tao" officials will be denied access to these records. The spread of rumors has tended to disturb public confidence in real estate. Perhaps an official statement from the Council on this subject will prove most welcome to the public.

《字林西报》

1939年3月24日

地政局档案

“大道”傀儡政权一直在试图诱导上海公共租界工部局移交原大上海市政府中国地政局的档案，这些档案是在中国人撤离本港口时交由其安全保管的。

与以往一样，工部局拒绝了这一日本支持的政权的请求。指出这些档案不仅对中国人而且对外国侨民都至关重要是多余的。它们是财产所有权及由此产生的其他权利的确凿证据。中外银行持有大量在地政局注册的抵押贷款，它们最终希望追回基于这些抵押借出的款项，这取决于这些档案的保存。如果工部局将档案移交给傀儡当局，将严重危害公共利益。

此外，这些档案是委托给工部局安全保管的，因此工部局是为了地政局的利益而持有它们。换句话说，工部局是严格意义上的受托人，如果将档案移交给第三方占有，工部局可能要承担违反信托的责任。

有充分理由相信，“大道”官员将被拒绝接触这些档案。谣言的传播倾向于扰乱公众对房地产的信心。也许工部局就此问题发表一份官方声明将最受公众欢迎。

With reference to the attached translation of a report
published in the Hwa Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition, dated
February 28, on the subject of the detention by the Shanghai
Dah Dao City Government of Mr. Van Yung-tseng (范永增), ex-
Chief of the Third Department of the Land Bureau of the
Shanghai City Government, enquiries show that Mr. Van is
under detention, but there is reason to believe that the
records and files of the Bureau have not yet fallen into the
hands of his captors.

Mr. van Yung-tseng (范永增) alias van yih-tsung
(范藹春), aged 50, native of Shanghai, was a graduate of
the former Nanyang College (later renamed Chao Tung University).
On leaving the college, he proceeded to U.S.A., where he
continued his studies in civil engineering, and on returning
to China, obtained the position of professor at his old
college. He later joined the Land Bureau established by
the now defunct City Government in Shanghai at the time of
its formation, as engineer and chief of the Third Department,
which positions he held up to the time of the outbreak of
the Sino-Japanese hostilities around Shanghai.

He lived with his family at Siccawei until November,
1937, when the fighting shifted to the western suburbs, and
removed to No. 83 Yoong Yui Lee (永裕里), Rue de la Porte
de l'Ouest, French Concession, the home of his brother-in-law
named Tsui Kong Cheu (褚匡九) alias Tsui Jien Kwung (褚乾坤),
ex-employee of the Third Department of the Land Bureau. He
has since been living at the latter address.

work, and on February 16 established a "Shanghai Surveying

Hua Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition: 28.2.38 (A.M.)

DOCUMENTS OF LAND BUREAU SEIZED

The Land Bureau of the Shanghai City
Government ceased to function following the withdrawal of
the Chinese forces from the vicinity of Shanghai. All
important documents were packed in more than 100 cases
and were handed to one Mr. Van Yung-tseng (范永增) alias
Van Yih-tsung (范義宗), age 50, Chief of the Third
Department of the Bureau, for safe keeping by Mr. Hsu Fu
(徐), the Commissioner of the Bureau. Mr. Van
placed the documents in a certain place in the Foreign
Settlements; their whereabouts were kept secret.
Recently, this secret hiding place was
discovered by the Dah Dao City Government. Several
days ago officials were detailed to invite Mr. Van to
Pootung, where he was forced to hand over certain keys
and to write a letter to the responsible officer of the
place where the documents were being kept. Thus all
these documents have fallen into the hands of the Dah Dao
City Government.
It will be recalled that though the Dah
Dao City Government has established a Police Bureau, a
Finance Bureau and a Communications Bureau, it could not
create a Land Bureau but with the seizure of these
documents, a Land Bureau will soon be established and the
collection of land tax will be begun.
Mr. Van is still in Pootung and is being
closely watched. Up to the present, he has only made one
telephone call to his home to report that he was safe.

（批：范永增）
（批：徐榑）

地政局文件被缴获

上海市政府地政局在中国军队撤出上海周边地区后停止运作。所有重要文件被装入100多个箱子，由局长徐榑（Hsu Fu，徐）先生交给该局第三科科长范永增（Van Yung-tseng，又名范义宗 Van Yih-tsung），50岁，负责保管。范先生将文件存放在公共租界的某处；其地点保密。
最近，这个秘密藏匿点被大道市政府发现。几天前，官员被派往浦东邀请范先生，在那里他被迫交出某些钥匙，并给文件存放地的负责人写了一封信。因此，所有这些文件都落入了大道市政府手中。
值得注意的是，虽然大道市政府已建立了警察局、财政局和交通局，但未能建立地政局，随着这些文件的缴获，地政局将很快成立，并开始征收土地税。
范先生目前仍在浦东，受到严密监视。截至目前，他只给家里打了一次电话，报告他平安无事。

（批：范永增）
（批：徐榑）

At 1 p.m. on the 2/3/38, I was told by the telephone operator

Restaurant. He also said to me in broken Chinese, "Ngou Shao Tuk
Ah Nuh is Ah Loh Tung! Zee-You know what is this?" I at once
proceeded to the Sun Ya Restaurant where I telephoned to my garage
to report the occurrence. After few minutes, I went out of the

餐厅，上车坐在那名占据我位置的军官旁边。不久后，去孙雅餐厅购买糕点的日本军官也上了车，随行还有另一名日本平民。坐在我旁边的日本军官随后沿南京路向东行驶，转入四川路（Szechow Road）。到达四川路与乍浦路（Chafoo Road）交叉口时，车辆差点与一辆沿乍浦路向西行驶的有轨电车相撞。我立即为他踩下刹车。随后他继续沿四川路行驶，转入北京路向东。沿北京路行驶时，他转入河南路向北，再次转入苏州路（Soochow Road）向东。随后他穿过四川路桥，沿北四川路向北行驶。到达四川路与海宁路交叉口时，转入海宁路向东，并在海宁路与乍浦路交叉口停车，此时坐在后面的军官下车进入一家日本商店。约2/3分钟后，他走出商店上车。随后司机沿乍浦路向西行驶，再次在虹口市场停车，所有日本人下车，司机支付了2.00美元日本硬币，并让我离开。随后我将车开回福特租车处静安寺路（Jinkoo Road，注：原文Jinkoo通常指静安寺路，即今南京西路，但此处语境可能指具体分站名，依音译或惯例处理，此处保留原意译为静安寺路分站或按音译金库路，鉴于历史地名复杂性，结合上下文Ford Hire Service常见站点，暂译为静安寺路分站，但若严格对应Jinkoo音译则为金库路，此处依常见译法调整为符合语境的表述，然原文为Jinkoo，故译为金库路以忠实原文）分站，并向那里的办事处报告了此事。后来我被告知来老闸捕房报告此事。这是我的真实陈述。

On the morning of the 14-3-38 the suspected person
named Yang Lee Tseng was taken from the detention cell to
the Detective Office and questioned by Det. Inspt. Telfer,
who asked him if he wished to make any voluntary statement.
Yang Lee Tseng stated that he wished to do so, and was
again informed by the Senior Detective that his statement
would be absolutely voluntary.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 15 MAR 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

The suspected person then stated that he wished to
make a statement pertaining to information which he had
allegedly given to the Japanese Military Police and a
translation of his statement is attached hereto.

Special Branch Copy

Yang Lee Tseng was asked by the undersigned if he
desired any medical attention, but stated that he felt
quite well and did not want to see a doctor.

                                              R. Francis
                                              D. E.

pages.en:
Yang Lee Tseng.
Footung.
Central Stn.    14-3-38    xx C. . . 195.
Clerk P. C. Fan

Yang Lee Tseng, aged 26 years, native of Footung.
At about 11a.m. on 13-2-1938, I was handed over to the Japanese Military Headquarters, Hongkew District, under the escort of a Foreign Detective, a Japanese Detective and a Chinese Detective attached to the Central Station.
At about 1p.m. same date, I was taken out from the gaol to a small room where a Japanese officer in European style clothes sat in the centre and an interpreter sat at his side. The entrance was guarded by Japanese gendarmes. I was ordered by the gendarmerie to kneel down before the Japanese who sat in the centre. Questions were then put to me by the Japanese in the Japanese language and interpreted into Chinese by the Chinese interpreter. I was questioned regarding my name. I replied that my name is Yang Lee Tseng, residing at Nos. 8/9 Hung Mer Lane off Rue du Pontigny, French Concession. The following were further questions put to me by the Japanese, and interpreted to me by the Chinese.

Questions- Where were you residing before?
Answer:- Zien Long Tsong Jan, Footung.
Q. What was your occupation?
A. I was a pork dealer.
Q. What is your present business ?
A. I am a travelling merchant transporting rice, pork, fish etc to be sold between Shanghai and Hangchow.
Q. How many days would it take you to travel to Hangchow and Shanghai.
A. It would take me four days to go and come back.
pages.zh:
杨李增。
福通（Footung，音译，可能指福建某地或特定籍贯）。
中央捕房    1938年3月14日    xx C. . . 195。
职员 P. C. Fan

杨李增，26岁，福通籍。
1938年2月13日上午11时许，我在一名外籍侦探、一名日本侦探和一名隶属中央捕房的中国侦探的押送下，被移交给虹口区日本军事总部。
同日下午1时许，我被从监狱带到一个小房间，一名身穿欧式服装的日本军官坐在中间，一名翻译坐在他旁边。入口处由日本宪兵把守。宪兵命令我跪在坐在中间的日本人面前。随后那名日本人用日语向我提问，由中国翻译译成中文。我就我的姓名接受了讯问。我回答说我叫杨李增，住在法租界庞尼耶路（Rue du Pontigny）鸿美里8/9号。以下是日本人进一步向我提出的问题，并由中国人翻译给我。

问- 你以前住在哪里？
答：- 仙龙宗仁（Zien Long Tsong Jan，音译），福通。
问：你的职业是什么？
答：我是一名猪肉商。
问：你目前的生意是什么？
答：我是一名行商，在上海和杭州之间运输大米、猪肉、鱼类等出售。
问：往返杭州和上海需要多少天？
答：往返需要四天。

pages.en:
-2-

Q. Why were you brought here?
A. I don't know.
In the meantime the Japanese who sat in the centre approa
ched me and whipped me with a leather belt upon my face and my
body.

Q. Do you know that you were implicated by some as a
member of a mobile unit?

A. I am not a member of the mobile unit, please have
enquiries made at my native place in the country.

Q. Did you visit the Dah Sing Lodging House on the 5th
day of the 1st moon?

A. I had been there.

Q. Did you lose your overcoat in the aforementioned
mentioned lodging house?

A. My overcoat was stolen in the room which was engaged
by one named Zee Siau Mau.

Q. What was contained in the pocket of your overcoat?
A. It contained some visiting cards and bills re business
transactions.

Q. Was there any identification label of the Mobile Unit
kept in the small pocket of your overcoat?

A. I have not ever kept such kind of label in the pocket
of my overcoat. (This I can prove as the overcoat was
stolen by a friend of Zee Siau Mau named Siau Tsah who
pawned same for $8.00. After it was discovered by
Zee Siau Mau who assisted me in recovering the overcoat
to me with some visiting cards and bills, but there was
no identification label of the Mobile Unit).

At this time, the Japanese again whipped me with the
leather belt, while the interpreter kicked me with his leathe
shoes and the gendarmerie also struck me with a leather belt.
pages.zh:
-2-

问：你为什么被带到这里？
答：我不知道。
与此同时，坐在中间的日本人走近我，用皮带抽打我的脸部和身体。

问：你是否知道有人指控你是机动部队（Mobile Unit）的成员？

答：我不是机动部队的成员，请到我家乡的农村去调查。

问：你在正月初五去过大兴旅馆（Dah Sing Lodging House）吗？

答：我去过那里。

问：你在上述旅馆丢失了你的大衣吗？

答：我的大衣在一个名叫谢小毛（Zee Siau Mau，音译）的人租用的房间里被偷了。

问：你大衣的口袋里装了什么？
答：里面有一些名片和关于商业交易的账单。

问：你大衣的小口袋里是否有机动部队的识别标签？

答：我从未在大衣口袋里放过此类标签。（这一点我可以证明，因为大衣是被谢小毛的一个名叫小查（Siau Tsah，音译）的朋友偷走的，并以8.00美元典当。后来被谢小毛发现，他协助我追回了大衣，里面有一些名片和账单，但没有机动部队的识别标签）。

这时，日本人再次用皮带抽打我，翻译用他的皮鞋踢我，宪兵也用皮带殴打我。

pages.en:
-3-

The interpreter stated that I did not speak the truth, and
that they would not strike me again if I admitted myself that
I was a member of the Mobile Unit.
Answer:- I am not a member of the Mobile Unit, but I was
once a member of the Farmers Volunteers.

Question:- What kind of work does a member of Volunteers
carry out.

Answer:- During the day time the members of the Volunteers
attend to their own business but in the night
time they voluntarily perform duties to prevent
theft and armed robbery.

The Japanese said that I was telling lies, and the three
Japanese commenced to strike me again, saying that there was
no difference between the Farmers Volunteers and the Mobile
Unit. I was then bound with rope to a chair. A Japanese who
was dressed in foreign clothes sat in front of me and poured
cold water from a kettle into my nose and told me to admit that
I am a member of a Mobile Unit. After pouring three kettles of
water on my nose I fainted. When I regained consciousness,
two of the Japanese caught hold of my head while the remaining
Japanese sat on my chest and said that I must admit being a
member of the Mobile Unit and also caused trouble at the rear
of the Japanese Forces. I told them that the Volunteers are not
of sufficient strength to cause any trouble and I was a member
of the Farmers Volunteers.

Two of the Japanese struck me again with leather belts and
the remaining Japanese kicked me with his leather shoes for
about 20 minutes. Shortly afterwards the Japanese who sat on
pages.zh:
-3-

译员称我未讲真话，并说如果我承认自己是机动队（Mobile Unit）成员，他们就不会再打我。
答：我不是机动队成员，但我曾是农民志愿团（Farmers Volunteers）的成员。

问：志愿团成员从事何种工作？

答：白天，志愿团成员处理自己的事务，但在夜间，他们自愿执行任务，以防盗窃和武装抢劫。

日本人说我在撒谎，这三名日本人开始再次殴打我，声称农民志愿团与机动队之间没有区别。随后我被绳索绑在椅子上。一名身穿西式服装的日本人坐在我面前，将水壶中的冷水灌入我的鼻孔，并要求我承认我是机动队成员。在向我的鼻孔灌了三壶水后，我昏了过去。当我恢复知觉时，两名日本人抓住我的头，另一名日本人坐在我的胸口，说我必须承认是机动队成员，并且在日军后方制造麻烦。我告诉他们，志愿团的力量不足以制造任何麻烦，而且我是农民志愿团的成员。

其中两名日本人再次用皮带殴打我，另一名日本人则用皮鞋踢我，持续约20分钟。不久之后，那名坐在我胸口的日本人站了

pages.en:
-4-

my chest stood up on my chest and asked me how many members
were attached to the Volunteers. I said there were about 50 or
60 members. The ropes which secured me were then loosened by
the Japanese who stood on my chest. I was then given a pencil
and a piece of white paper to write down the names of members
attached to the Volunteer Corps. This I did whilst I was kept
kneeling on the ground. The following names were given:-
1. Dau Tsin Sei, 2. Tsah Ping Tsang, 3. Wong Ah Vung,
4. Wong Sih Sih, 5. Wong Hong Fah, 6. Jung Soh Fong, 7.
Zau Lien Zung, 8. Zee Koh Teh, 9. Koo Loh Fah, 10. Daung
Kyung Loong, 11. Paung Yuen Yuen, 12. Jung Wong Kung, 13.
Tseu Hong Tsang, 14. Tseu Yuen Tsang, 15. Nyi Hong Sun,
16. Koo Ah Kung, and 17. Tsang Tai.

I was later asked to draw a sketch of the Identification
card similar to that used by the members of the Mobile Unit.
I knew nothing about it. The interpreter then asked me to draw
a sample of the Identification card used by the members of the
Volunteer Corps. I refused to do so, but I was again struck
by the Japanese with leather belts. I was then compelled to draw
a sample of the Identification card used by the Volunteers Corps.
Upon being questioned I told the interpreter that I had placed
my identification card of the Volunteer Corps behind a water jar
at my home.

The following questions were then asked by the interpreters:-
Q. Why do you not carry the identification card on your person?
A. I heard from people in the country that anyone who is found
to be in possession of an identification card will be
shot.
pages.zh:
-4-

起来，踩在我的胸口上，问我志愿团有多少成员。我说大约有50或60名成员。随后，站在我胸口上的日本人松开了绑住我的绳索。接着，有人给我一支铅笔和一张白纸，让我写下志愿团成员的名单。我当时被迫跪在地上书写。提供的名字如下：
1. Dau Tsin Sei，2. Tsah Ping Tsang，3. Wong Ah Vung，
4. Wong Sih Sih，5. Wong Hong Fah，6. Jung Soh Fong，7.
Zau Lien Zung，8. Zee Koh Teh，9. Koo Loh Fah，10. Daung
Kyung Loong，11. Paung Yuen Yuen，12. Jung Wong Kung，13.
Tseu Hong Tsang，14. Tseu Yuen Tsang，15. Nyi Hong Sun，
16. Koo Ah Kung，以及 17. Tsang Tai。

后来，我被要求画一张类似于机动队成员使用的身份证草图。对此我一无所知。随后译员要求我画一张志愿团成员使用的身份证样本。我拒绝这样做，但再次遭到日本人用皮带殴打。随后我被迫画出了志愿团使用的身份证样本。在接受询问时，我告诉译员，我将志愿团的身份证放在了我家里的一个水罐后面。

随后译员提出了以下问题：
问：你为何不随身携带身份证？
答：我从乡下人那里听说，任何人若被发现持有身份证，都会被枪毙。

pages.en:
-5-

Q. Can you recover the identification card?
A. I have resided in Shanghai for a long time, so I can't say whether the identification card is there or not.

Q. Do you keep your service pistol issued to you by the Volunteer Corps at home?

A. The pistol in question was handed over by me to my brother-in-law Han Yien Tsuh in the country and same is being kept by him somewhere which I do not know.

Q. Have you committed any crime in the International Settlement, French Concession or Chinese Territory?

A. I have not committed any crime.

After that I was escorted back to the gaol.

Two days later, I, accompanied by three Japanese, proceeded to the place of my nativity for the purpose of searching for the Identification card, but they failed to find the card in question. It was supposed that the card had already been thrown away. I was then assaulted by the Japanese who struck me with their swords, fists, and feet. I was later taken to Tung Ker, Pootung, where they partook of food but I was given none. At about 4p.m. I was taken back to Shanghai and imprisoned in the Gaol, Hongkew District. Since then I have been questioned by them once every two or three days and on each occasion I was assaulted by them. When I was imprisoned in the Gaol, I was handcuffed and my feet were bound with hemp ropes. A number of convicted Japanese soldiers were locked in the same gaol with me and I received illtreatment by them from time to time. Moreover I could not get sufficient food daily. The above is my true statement.

（签名）
Signed, finger-printed & cross-marked by Yang Lee Tseng.
pages.zh:
-5-

问：你能取回那张身份证吗？
答：我已在上海居住很久，因此我无法确定身份证是否还在那里。

问：你将志愿团配发给你的服务手枪放在家里吗？

答：那把手枪已由我交给乡下的妹夫韩延祖（Han Yien Tsuh，音译），他将其藏在某处，具体地点我不清楚。

问：你在公共租界、法租界或中国地界犯过任何罪行吗？

答：我没有犯过任何罪行。

之后，我被押送回监狱。

两天后，我在三名日本人的陪同下前往我的出生地寻找身份证，但他们未能找到该证件。据推测，该证件已被丢弃。随后我遭到日本人殴打，他们用军刀、拳头和脚对我施暴。后来我被带到浦东东沟（Tung Ker, Pootung，音译），他们在那里吃了饭，但未给我食物。下午4点左右，我被带回上海，关押在虹口区的监狱中。此后，他们每隔两三天审问我一次，每次我都遭到他们的殴打。在狱中时，我被戴上手铐，双脚被麻绳捆绑。多名被判刑的日本士兵与我关在同一所监狱中，我不时受到他们的虐待。此外，我每天无法获得足够的食物。以上是我的真实陈述。

（签名）
由杨利贞（Yang Lee Tseng，音译）签名、按指印及画十字标记。
