Japanese Military Head-
quarters.
Detective Office.

SUSPECTED ANTI-JAPANESE TERRORIST
ARRESTED BY JAPANESE MILITARY FORCE.

At 11a.m. on the 13/3/38 the undersigned and U.S.
Kobayashi again interviewed Sergeant Tokutani attached
to The Japanese Military Police re. the suspected person
named Yang Lee Tseng.

Sergeant Tokutani stated that Yang Lee Tseng would
again be handed over to the S.M.Police, but he requested
that the suspected person be detained at Central Station,
until a letter was received at Japanese Military Police
Headquarters from The Commissioner of The S.M.Police
giving reasons as to why Yang Lee Tseng had not been hand-
ed over to be dealt with according to Japanese Military
Law, on evidence submitted. If Midori Igarashi, Commandant
of Gendarmerie, was satisfied re. the reason for not handing
over to the Japanese Military, a representative would be sent
to The Commissioner of S.M.Police to request that Yang
Lee Tseng be released.

Yang Lee Tseng was handed over to the undersigned and
his property was also handed over and brought to Central
Station.

Detective Inspector Telfer was informed, and he
acquainted Mr. Aiers D.D.S. "A". with the facts. Mr. Aiers
instructed that Yang Lee Tseng be detained.

Enquiries proceeding.

AB.

中央巡捕房
1938年3月13日

8.

上午11:00 - 下午12:30
1938年3月13日。
日本军方总部。
侦探办公室。

涉嫌反日恐怖分子
由日本军队逮捕。

1938年3月13日上午11时，本人与美国籍警探小林（U.S. Kobayashi，音译）再次会见了隶属于日本宪兵队的德谷警长（Sergeant Tokutani，音译），谈及名为杨利贞（Yang Lee Tseng）的嫌疑人。

德谷警长表示，杨利贞将再次移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.Police），但他要求将该嫌疑人拘留在中央巡捕房，直到日本宪兵队总部收到上海公共租界工部局警务处总监的信函，说明为何未根据提交的证据将杨利贞移交以依照日本军法处理的原因。如果宪兵队司令五十岚绿（Midori Igarashi，音译）对不移交给日本军方的理由感到满意，将派代表前往上海公共租界工部局警务处总监处，要求释放杨利贞。

杨利贞已移交给本人，其财物也已移交并带至中央巡捕房。

已通知侦探督察特尔弗（Detective Inspector Telfer），他向“A”区副总监艾尔斯先生（Mr. Aiers D.D.S. "A"，音译）通报了事实。艾尔斯先生指示拘留杨利贞。

调查正在进行中。

（左侧批注及签名：）
AB.

（签名）

“A”区副总监办公室。

JCSB
（签名）

（签名）

205/38 (Misc.)        Central
                      March 1st,      38

         7

10 a.m. to 11 a.m.            Detective Office.
1-3-38.

SUSPECTED ANTI-JAPANESE TERRORIST
ARRESTED BY JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE

At 10 a.m. on the 1-3-38, Sergeant Tokutani again
brought to Central Station a statement taken from the
suspected person Yang Lee Tseng (楊利楨) at Japanese
Military Police Headquarters. The statement, which was
signed and finger-printed by Yang Lee Tseng, stated that
he had been formerly a member of the Chinese Peotung
Guerilla Corps, also having been attached to a fire
brigade corps coming under Chinese Military supervision.
The suspected person also stated that he had concealed an
identification pass in his home in Peotung.

On the 27-2-38 the suspected person was taken to
Peotung by Sergeant Tokutani, but a search of his house
failed to find the identification pass.

Sergeant Tokutani stated that although the suspected
person was not now an active member of the Chinese Peotung
Guerilla Corps, he must have knowledge of other active
members who were disturbing Japanese Military Forces.
Sergeant Tokutani again requested that Yang Lee Tseng be
handed over to the Japanese Military Authorities.

Detective Inspector Solder was informed re the facts
of this case, and on his instructions, Det. Nakaguchi
accompanied Tokutani returned to Interpreter Mr. MacDonnell,
Polo to Bds. (Shanghai).

上午10:00 至 11:00            侦探办公室。
1938年3月1日。

涉嫌反日恐怖分子
由日本宪兵队逮捕

1938年3月1日上午10时，德谷警长再次将一份在日本宪兵队总部从嫌疑人杨利贞（楊利楨）处取得的供词带到中央巡捕房。该供词由杨利贞签名并按指印，称他以前是中国浦东游击队（Chinese Peotung Guerilla Corps，音译）的成员，也曾隶属于受中国军方监督的一个消防队。该嫌疑人还称，他在浦东的家中藏有一张通行证。

1938年2月27日，德谷警长将嫌疑人带往浦东，但对其住所的搜查未能找到该通行证。

德谷警长表示，虽然该嫌疑人目前不再是中国浦东游击队的活跃成员，但他肯定知道其他正在扰乱日军部队的活跃成员的情况。德谷警长再次要求将杨利贞移交给日本军方当局。

已就本案事实通知索尔德侦探督察（Detective Inspector Solder，音译），根据他的指示，中口侦探（Det. Nakaguchi，音译）陪同德谷返回翻译麦克唐纳先生（Mr. MacDonnell，音译）处，地址为跑马厅路（Polo to Bds. (Shanghai)）。

麦克德莫特先生（Mr. MacDermott，音译）指示将该供词移交给特别警官（S.P.O.）进行翻译，并将翻译副本提交给负责犯罪的副总监杨先生（Mr. Young, Deputy Commissioner Crime）。

参见负责犯罪的副总监杨先生关于囚犯财物的备注。

本人认为财物随囚犯一起移交，且是出于诚意移交的，因为德谷警长也表示，日本当局希望检查在他身上发现的任何文件。日本军方随时会归还囚犯的财物。

1938年3月1日，也向麦克德莫特先生解释了有关财物的事实，他表示嫌疑人的财物可由日本当局保管，等待对此案的最终决定。

弗朗西斯
B. S.

副警长 1/8

SUSPECTED ANTI-JAPANESE TERRORIST
ARRESTED BY JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE

At 11.50 a.m. on the 24-2-38, a telephone message
was received from Sergeant Takutani, Japanese Military
Police, stating a letter was being sent to the Commission-
er of Police from Hideri Sagurashi, Commander of Gendar-
merie, requesting that the suspected person named Yang
Lee Tseng be handed over to the Japanese Military, as he
had admitted having been connected with the Chinese
Peotung Guerilla Corps.

A copy of the letter sent to the S.P.O. by Hideri
Sagurashi was obtained by D.S. Kobayashi on the morning
of the 26-2-38 and is attached hereto.

The suspected person Yang Lee Tseng was handed over
to the Japanese Authorities at 11 a.m. on the 23-2-38
for questioning, on the instructions of Mr. Young, Deputy
Commissioner Crime. He should have been returned to
the S.M. Police on the 25-2-38 but is still in the custody
of the Japanese Military Police, Woosung Road, pending a
decision.

由日本宪兵队逮捕

1938年2月24日上午11:50，接到日本宪兵队高谷警长（Sergeant Takutani，音译）的电话留言，称宪兵队指挥官相乐英照（Hideri Sagurashi，音译）正致信警察总监，要求将名为杨利贞的嫌疑人移交给日本军方，因为他已承认与中国浦东游击队有关联。

1938年2月26日上午，警探小林（D.S. Kobayashi，音译）获得了相乐英照发给特别警官（S.P.O.）的信件副本，附于此。

根据负责犯罪的副总监杨先生的指示，嫌疑人杨利贞已于1938年2月23日上午11时移交给日本当局接受讯问。他本应于1938年2月25日归还给上海公共租界工部局警务处，但目前仍由吴淞路日本宪兵队羁押，等待决定。

Shankenko No. 101.
Shanghai Gendarmerie Headquarters,
February 25, 1938.

Major F. W. Gerrard,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Re Request for Extradition of Member of Anti-Japanese Guerrilla Corps.

Sir,

During the time your prisoner Yang Lee Tsung
(楊利忠), aged 29 years, native of Pootung, residing
at Lung Tseu Lou, ing House (神州旅館 ), 159 Chekiang
Road, International Settlement, had been loaned to us
for the purpose of investigating his connection with the
Anti-Japanese Guerrilla Corps, he has made the following
statement thus definitely establishing his association
with the Corps.

"Following the retreat of Chinese troops from Pootung,
one Yao Tsing Wei (陶俊偉) organized a guerrilla corps
there towards the beginning of November last year. I joined
this corps on the recommendation of Tsai Ping Tsong
(蔡炳章 ) who was then a member. I was issued with
a membership card by Tsai at the same time as two other
new members, namely, Tsao Lien Zung (趙連城 ) and Sung
Siao Mao ( 沈小毛 ). The object of the Corps was to
disturb the rear of the Japanese forces. With this object
in view we waited for an opportunity, but in vain. On or
about December 10 last year I moved into the French Con-
cession and at that time I travelled between Shanghai and
Tungchow frequently, bringing pigs and vegetables which I
disposed of in Shanghai. At that time I was advised by
Tsai on three occasions to return to Pootung to work with
the Corps, but I refused and continued to live in the
Concession.

The membership card I left when I went to Shanghai for
pages.zh:
参宪第101号。
上海宪兵队总部，
1938年2月25日。

F. W. 杰拉德少校（Major F. W. Gerrard），
警察总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

关于引渡反日游击队成员的请求。

先生：

在贵方囚犯杨利忠（Yang Lee Tsung，楊利忠），29岁，浦东人，居住在公共租界浙江路159号神州旅館（Lung Tseu Lou, ing House，音译）期间，借予我方以调查其与反日游击队的关联时，他作出了如下陈述，从而确凿地确立了他与该团体的联系。

“去年11月初，在中国军队从浦东撤退后，陶俊伟（Yao Tsing Wei，音译）在那里组织了一支游击队。经当时已是成员的蔡炳章（Tsai Ping Tsong，音译）推荐，我加入了该队。蔡同时向我及另外两名新成员，即赵连城（Tsao Lien Zung，音译）和沈小毛（Sung Siao Mao，音译）发放了会员证。该团体的目的是扰乱日军后方。为此我们等待机会，但徒劳无功。去年12月10日左右，我搬入法租界，当时我经常往返于上海和通州（Tungchow，音译）之间，运送猪和蔬菜在上海出售。当时蔡曾三次劝我回浦东为该团体工作，但我拒绝了，并继续住在租界内。

我去上海时将会员证留下，因为

pages.en:
- 2 -

fear of detection lest I should fall into the hands of
the Police in the Settlement or Concession."

In view of the foregoing statement made by the
prisoner at this office, you are kindly requested to
hand him over to us as his activities have had connection
with the safety of the Japanese troops.

Yours faithfully,

Sealed : Midori Igarashi,

Commandant.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

害怕被发现，以免落入租界或公董局警察手中。”

鉴于囚犯在本处作出的上述陈述，恳请阁下将其移交给我们要，因为他的活动关系到日军的安全。

此致，

盖章：五十岚绿（Midori Igarashi），

司令。

Page 2.

being detained by the Japanese Authorities be questioned
by detectives attached to Central Station.

At 11.30a.m. on the 22/2/38 Yeng Lee Tseng was
taken by D.S. Hide and D.S. Kobayashi to Japanese
Police Headquarters Woosung Road. When he was confronted
by the Japanese witness named Han Yen Tseh,he denied
all knowledge of this person, but later admitted
that Han Yen Tseh was his brother-in-law. He further
admitted having been attached to the Headquarters of
The Peace Preservation Corps in Pootung about 4 years
ago,but he denied having had possession of a pistol,
and stated that same was the property of his brother-
in-law. Han Yen Tseh who had always kept the weapon.
The suspected person was left at Japanese Police
Headquarters for questioning.

At 2p.m. on the 22/2/38 D.S. Francis,D.S. Kobayashi
and Clark Lee Yang Kee proceeded to the Japanese
Headquarters and with their permission Han Yen Tseh was
questioned and a statement taken,translation of which
is attached hereto.

The Japanese Authorities handed the suspected
person named Yeng Lee Tseng over to the undersigned and
D.S. Kingswood and stated that owing to the absence of
their interpreter,they had not been able to question
him re. any anti-Japanese activities,and that he be
pages.zh:
第2页。

被日本当局拘留的证人进行讯问。

1938年2月22日上午11时30分，警佐海德（Hide）和警佐小林（Kobayashi）将杨利增（Yeng Lee Tseng）带至吴淞路日本警察总部。当其与名为韩彦哲的日本证人当面对质时，他否认认识此人，但后来承认韩彦哲是其姐夫。他还承认大约4年前曾在浦东保卫团总部任职，但他否认拥有手枪，并称该手枪为其姐夫韩彦哲所有，一直由韩保管。嫌疑人被留在日本警察总部接受讯问。

1938年2月22日下午2时，警佐弗朗西斯（Francis）、警佐小林（Kobayashi）和李杨基（Clark Lee Yang Kee）前往日本总部，经许可对韩彦哲进行了讯问并记录了供词，译文附后。

日本当局将名为杨利增（Yeng Lee Tseng）的嫌疑人移交给下述签名人及警佐金斯伍德（Kingswood），并表示由于翻译不在，他们未能就任何反日活动对其进行讯问，并要求将其

pages.en:
Page 3.

still detained at Central Station, until they had
another opportunity for interrogation.

On being again brought to Central Station the
suspect was questioned re. persons visiting him at his
home in Footung, and stated that on one occasion his
friend named Zung Zai Loong (朱才龍) who is a wine
broker, and another named "Zung" ( 張 ) visited his
home on or about Feb. 9th 1938 and they drank wine
and talked about business, at no time did any conversa-
tion take place regarding snipers.

It is worthy of mention that whilst detectives
were questioning Han Yen Tseh at Japanese Police
Headquarters, he was asked if he knew as to whether
Yang Lee Tseng was connected with any Anti-Japanese
organisation, and he stated that he did not know.

Detective Inspector Telfer informed Mr. Aiers
D.D.O."A". re. the request of the Japanese Authorities
to have the suspected person again detained, and on
Mr. Aiers instructions he is still detained at Central
Station.

Translation of letter received by S.P.O. from
Commander of Japanese Gendarmerie obtained by D.S.
Kobayashi and is also attached to this file.

〔签名〕
Sergt Det. 1/c.

〔签名〕
D. S. 162.
pages.zh:
第3页。

继续拘留在中央巡捕房，直到他们有机会再次进行审讯。

嫌疑人被再次带回中央巡捕房后，就探访其浦东住所的人员接受了讯问，他称1938年2月9日左右，他的朋友朱才龙（Zung Zai Loong，朱才龍，酒商）和另一名姓“张”（Zung，張）的人曾到访其家，他们饮酒并谈论生意，期间从未进行过有关狙击手的谈话。

值得一提的是，当侦探在日本警察总部讯问韩彦哲时，曾问他是否知道杨利增是否与任何反日组织有关联，他回答说他不知道。

侦探督察特尔弗（Telfer）就日本当局要求再次拘留嫌疑人的请求告知了“A”区副侦探长艾尔斯（Aiers）先生，根据艾尔斯先生的指示，该嫌疑人仍被拘留在中央巡捕房。

由警佐小林从日本宪兵队指挥官处获得的、由特别警务官收到的信件译文也已附入本档案。

Han Yeu Tseh
Anhwei                                S.S. Francis.
        22-1-38                       Clerk I.I.

My name is Han Yeu Tseh, aged 33 years, native of Suchow,
Anhwei. I am keeping a work shop at Toong Keu, Lootung, and
my home is at No. 46 Sien Loong Trung Jao.
    At about 1 p.m. on the 10-2-38, a party of Police under
Inspector Yoong came to my shop at Toong Keu and requested me
to take them to Yang Lee Tseng's home at Yang Ke Zah, as the
latter is a relative of mine. Before taking them to the
above place I told Inspector Yoong that Yang Lee Tseng was at
Shanghai and not in his home. Arriving at Yang's home, it was
found that he was indeed not there. A search of the house was
made but nothing of an incriminating nature was found. I was
later brought to the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters, Woosung
Road, Shanghai, as a witness and questioned by the Japanese
Authorities.
    Yang Lee Tseng's sister is my wife and therefore Yang is
my brother-in-law. I have known Yang for about 6 or 7 years.
Four years or so before, Yang was keeping a pork shop but as
he had some money, he gave the shop to me. Yang Lee Tseng
is in the habit of drinking wine and gambling, so his mother
does not like him. As I am her son-in-law, she allowed me to
have the shop and told me to be careful with the shop business.
    About 5 or 6 years ago, Yang Lee Tseng was a member of the
Peace Preservation Corps and I saw him on many occasions wearing
khaki uniform. When he handed over the shop to me, he also
left the corps. What he has been doing since that time, I do
not know. I simply know that he comes from and goes to Shanghai
very constantly. Whilst Yang Lee Tseng was engaged as a member
pages.zh:
韩彦哲（Han Yeu Tseh）
安徽                                S.S. 弗朗西斯。
        1938年1月22日                       情报股书记员。

我叫韩彦哲，现年33岁，籍贯安徽苏州。我在浦东同古（Toong Keu, Lootung）经营一家作坊，家住仙龙中街（Sien Loong Trung Jao）46号。
    1938年2月10日下午1时许，一队由杨（Yoong）督察带领的警察来到我在同古的店铺，要求我带他们去杨克扎（Yang Ke Zah）的杨利增家，因为杨利增是我的亲戚。在带他们去上述地点之前，我告诉杨督察，杨利增在上海，不在家里。到达杨家后，发现他确实不在那里。对房屋进行了搜查，但未发现任何罪证。随后我被作为证人带至上海吴淞路日本宪兵队总部，并接受日本当局的讯问。
    杨利增的妹妹是我的妻子，因此杨是我的姐夫。我认识杨大约六七年了。大约四年前，杨经营一家猪肉铺，但因为有些积蓄，他把店铺转让给了我。杨利增有饮酒和赌博的习惯，所以他母亲不喜欢他。因为我是她的女婿，她允许我接手店铺，并嘱咐我要小心经营店铺业务。
    大约五六年前，杨利增是保卫团成员，我曾多次见他身穿卡其色制服。当他把店铺转让给我时，他也退出了保卫团。从那以后他在做什么，我不知道。我只知道他经常往返于上海。当杨利增受雇为保卫团

pages.en:
Han Yeh Tsuh (page 2)

of the Preservation Corps, he had a short pistol. He is still
keeping it now. One day during the 11th moon last year, whilst
he was in Footung, I saw him carry the pistol in his pocket.
He told me that he kept same for self protection. When Yang
came to Shanghai he used to either hand the pistol to his
mother or his wife to conceal. One day during the 11th moon
last year, when I returned to my shop from Toong Keu, I
observed Yang and two other men (names unknown to me) in the
shop. I did not hear what they were talking about. On the
8th day of the first moon this year and at tiffin time, when
I returned to my shop, I again saw Yang Lee Tseng and two
other men in the shop (One was one of the two men seen on the
1st occasion during the 11th moon, later known to be as one
named Zung, and the other one was not known to me, as it was
the first time I saw him). The two friends of Yang said there
were members of the Special Corps in the South and Yang Lee
Tseng replied that if there were members of the Special Corps
there, You go to Shanghai.

I did not hear anybody mention anything about Yang Lee
Tseng joining any anti-Japanese Or other terrorist movements.
He had had no connections with any of such movements.

On returning to my shop on the 8th day of the 1st moon
and when seen by Yang Lee Tseng, he told me to go and have my
chow. It appears that he did not wish me to listen to their
conversation, but he did not seem to be very angry.

I do not know whether Yang is concerned in any anti-
Japanese activities and I did not hear anybody say about Yang
being concerned in same.

Cross marked. Han Yeh Tsuh.
pages.zh:
韩彦哲（第2页）

成员期间，他有一支短枪。他现在仍然保留着它。去年农历十一月的一天，当他在浦东时，我看见他把枪放在口袋里。他告诉我，他保留枪支是为了自卫。当杨来上海时，他通常会把枪交给他的母亲或妻子藏匿。去年农历十一月的一天，当我从同古回到我的店铺时，我看见杨和另外两名男子（姓名不详）在店里。我没有听到他们在谈论什么。今年正月初八午饭时间，当我回到店铺时，我又看见杨利增和另外两名男子在店里（其中一人是去年农历十一月第一次见到的两人之一，后来得知此人名叫张，另一人我不认识，因为那是我第一次见到他）。杨的两名朋友说南方有特种部队成员，杨利增回答说，如果那里有特种部队成员，你就去上海。

我没有听到任何人提及杨利增加入任何反日或其他恐怖运动。他与任何此类运动都没有关联。

今年正月初八回到我的店铺时，杨利增看见我，叫我去吃饭。看来他不想让我听他们的谈话，但他似乎并没有很生气。

我不知道杨是否参与任何反日活动，我也没有听到任何人说杨参与其中。

画叉标记。韩彦哲。

Translation.

To Major F.W. Gerrard, Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Sir,

Re handing over of a member of the anti-Japanese
Special Corps to the Japanese Military Police.

A Chinese named Yang Li Tseng (楊利楨), residing at
Room 443, Zung Chow Hotel (神州), No. 159 Chekiang Road, as a
result of the investigation by the Japanese Gendarmerie, was
revealed to be a member of a Chinese Special Corps which was
organised in Pootung. A witness named Han Yeh Tseh (韓賢哲)
aged 33, proprietor of a pork shop, native of Suchow (四州),
Anhwei, residing at No. 45 Zien Loong Tsoong Jau (錢隆中街), Toong
Kew, Pootung, when he was questioned on February 20, 1938, stated
that Yang Li Tseng returned to his mother's home in company with
his two comrades, one of them known as a certain Chen (陳), about
November, last year, and conferred with them regarding the Special
Corps. He further stated that Yang secretly conferred with the
aforementioned comrades on February 7, this year at the mother's
home. According to the information, it was revealed that Yang,
after requesting the members of his family to conceal his pistol
of small calibre, left for the Settlement with the intention of
creating disturbances in the Japanese controlled area. Should his
intention be carried out, it would greatly affect the welfare of
the Japanese army, therefore it is requested that Yang be handed
over to the Japanese Gendarmerie for enquiries.

Yours respectfully,

Midori Igarashi,
Commander of Gendarmerie.

致上海公共租界工部局警务处处长
F.W. 杰拉德少校。

先生：

关于向日本宪兵队移交一名反日特种部队成员事宜。

经日本宪兵队调查，居住在浙江路159号神州大旅社（Zung Chow Hotel，神州）443室的一名中国人杨利楨（Yang Li Tseng，楊利楨），被揭露为在浦东组织的一支中国特种部队成员。一名名为韩贤哲（Han Yeh Tseh，韓賢哲）的证人，33岁，猪肉铺店主，籍贯安徽四州（Suchow，四州），居住在浦东同古（Toong Kew）钱隆中街（Zien Loong Tsoong Jau，錢隆中街）45号，在1938年2月20日接受讯问时陈述，杨利楨于去年11月左右与两名同志（其中一人已知为陈某）一同回到其母亲家中，并与他们商讨有关特种部队的事宜。他还陈述，杨于今年2月7日在其母亲家中与上述同志秘密会晤。据情报显示，杨在要求家人藏匿其小口径手枪后，怀着在日控区制造骚乱的意图前往租界。如果其意图得逞，将严重影响日军的安全福利，因此请求将杨移交给日本宪兵队进行讯问。

此致
敬礼，

宪兵队指挥官
五十岚绿（Midori Igarashi）

走廊对面紧邻437号房间的443号房间的住客熟络起来。由于一无所获，侦探们随后前往法租界罗家威捕房（Loh Ka Wei Station，音译），在他们的协助下，对蒙梯尼大道89号底层的一间小房间进行了搜查，但同样毫无结果。

值得注意的是，当侦探们带着被告到达其住所时，一位名叫瞿孙氏（Jeu Jung Ss，音译）的中国老妇人惊呼道：“你昨晚（1938年2月18日）去拜访朋友后，回来得太晚了。”这位老妇人是居住在同一栋房屋内的律师瞿成（Jeu Sung，音译）的妻子。经讯问，该老妇人称嫌疑人从事蔬菜、猪肉和鱼类的经纪业务，但由于中日战事导致巨大亏损，他的生意几乎全部破产。

Central Stn.      19-:-38      --------/   Clerk F.C. Fan

My name is Foo Nyue Vung, aged 33 years. I am a native of
Shantung, residing in Room No. 5, (2nd floor), 451 Foochow Road.
I am married and a flour bag maker by profession.

About one month ago I made the acquaintance of Siau Yang at
the Kung Yuen Story Teller House, situated at No. 5 Ynung Sing Ka,
where he is the proprietor, and is very intimate with me. His
cousin Yang Lee Tseng, the proprietor of a pork shop situated at
Tung Ker, Pootung was known to me during my frequent visits at the
Room No. 437 of the Tung Chow Hotel, Chekiang Road. On learning
Yang Lee Tseng was being detained at the Police Station, I,
therefore, came to the station and tried to ascertain the reason
of Yang's detention. So far he has no connection with the
Pootung Police Bureau.

The above statement is true.

                               Signed:- Foo Nyue Vung.

〔此处转录不清：左侧签名〕
pages.zh:
Foo Nyue Vung（吴译文，音译）。

山东                      XX 华籍侦探副巡长 185
                               翻译
中央捕房      19-:-38      --------/   书记员 F.C. Fan

我叫 Foo Nyue Vung，现年33岁。我是山东人，居住在福州路451号5室（二楼）。我已婚，职业是面粉袋制作工。

大约一个月前，我在位于永星街5号的公缘书场结识了小杨（Siau Yang，音译），他是该书场的老板，与我关系非常密切。他的表弟杨立正是浦东东沟一家猪肉店的老板，我在浙江路中州旅馆437号房间多次拜访期间认识了他。得知杨立正被拘留在警察局后，我因此来到警局，试图查明杨被拘留的原因。据我所知，他与浦东警察局没有任何关联。

以上陈述属实。

                               签名:- Foo Nyue Vung.

Van Ah Pao.

Ningpo
Central Stn.    19-?-38    XX C.D.I. Wei Kyung Yoh
                             / translated    Clerk F.C. Pan

My name is Van Ah Pao, aged 39 years. I am a native of Ningpo,
residing at No. 6 Yueh Jing Tsung, off Pakhoi Road. Formerly I
was a foreman employed by the Whangpoo Conservancy Bureau. Since
the August 13th hostilities, I was compelled to cease my work, but
I still receive my monthly salary.

In December, 1937 I became acquainted with Yang Lee Tseng on
board the S.S. Moller en route to Tungchow. I then knew him to be
a travelling merchant for transporting cigarettes, pork oil etc
from Shanghai to Tungchow for sale, and chickens, fish, and pork
from Tungchow to Shanghai. When he arrived at Shanghai he used to
stay in the Zung Chow Hotel. On the 10th inst. he booked room
437 in the above hotel, because his family is at Tong Ker, Pootung.
On hearing of the arrest of Yang Lee Tseng, I visited the station
and tried to ascertain the reason for his detention. As far as I
know, he has no connection with the Pootung Police Bureau.

The above statement is true.        Signed:- Van Ah Pao.

〔此处转录不清〕
pages.zh:
Van Ah Pao（范阿宝）。

宁波
中央捕房    19-?-38    XX 华籍侦探督察 Wei Kyung Yoh（魏景耀，音译）
                             / 翻译    书记员 F.C. Pan

我叫 Van Ah Pao，现年39岁。我是宁波人，居住在北海路月泾总弄6号。我以前是黄浦浚浦局的工头。自八一三战事以来，我被迫停止工作，但我仍领取月薪。

1937年12月，我在前往通州（Tungchow）的“莫勒”号轮船上结识了杨立正。当时我知道他是一名行商，负责将香烟、猪油等从上海运往通州销售，并将鸡、鱼和猪肉从通州运往上海。他抵达上海时通常住在中州旅馆。本月10日，他在上述旅馆预订了437号房间，因为他的家在浦东东沟。听到杨立正被捕的消息后，我访问了警局，试图查明他被拘留的原因。据我所知，他与浦东警察局没有任何关联。

以上陈述属实。        签名:- Van Ah Pao.

At 9.30 p.m. on the 18-2-38 F.C.2 Taylor, S..C.624,
and C.I.C.2041 brought to the station a member of the
Japanese Military Police named Sergeant S. Tokutani and
a male Chinese named Tang Lee Tseng (杨利曾), 29, Pootung,
M/broker, residing at No.89 Boulevard des Montigny, F.C.,
whom he arrested at Nanking Road and Szechuen Road corner
at 9.25 p.m. Other three members of the Japanese Mili-
tary Police named (1) Corporal S. Okutani, (2) 1st class
private M. Sakamoto, and (3) 1st class private Y. Yadoni-
sa, all attached to the Intelligence Department of the
Military Police followed the police party to the Charge
Room.

Enquiries by the undersigned, J.D.S. Kobayashi and
C.D.S.185 ascertained the following:-

At 9.25 p.m. on the 18-2-38 whilst S.P.C.624 was on
traffic duty at Nanking & Szechuen Roads corner the male
Chinese named Tang Lee Tseng came up to him with his
hands handcuffed, and said "robbers", "robbers". The
S.P.C. arrested the Chinese, and at this time Sergeant
S. Tokutani of the Military Police also approached the
S.P.C. who also arrested him. C.P.C.2041 who was on
duty in close proximity to the scene on hearing the above

涉嫌反日恐怖分子
被日本宪兵逮捕。
---

1938年2月18日晚上9时30分，法籍巡长2号泰勒（Taylor）、印籍巡长624号以及华籍巡长2041号将一名名为德富见（S. Tokutani，音译）的日本宪兵军曹和一名名为杨利曾（Tang Lee Tseng，音译，原文如此，前文为杨立正）的29岁中国男子带到警局。该男子系浦东人，职业为经纪人，居住在法租界蒙梯尼大道89号。他于当晚9时25分在南京路与四川路路口被捕。另外三名隶属于宪兵情报部的日本宪兵成员，即(1) 奥谷（S. Okutani，音译）伍长，(2) 坂本（M. Sakamoto）一等兵，和(3) 矢殿佐（Y. Yadonisa，音译）一等兵，跟随警察队伍进入收押室。

经下述人员，即日籍侦探副巡长小林（Kobayashi）和华籍侦探副巡长185号讯问，查明如下情况：

1938年2月18日晚上9时25分，当印籍巡长624号正在南京路与四川路路口执行交通勤务时，一名双手被铐的中国男子杨利曾走到他面前，喊道“强盗”、“强盗”。该印籍巡长逮捕了这名中国人，此时宪兵队的德富见军曹也走近该印籍巡长，并将其逮捕。当时在附近执勤的华籍巡长2041号听到上述“强盗”的喊声后，拔出手枪跑过去协助

Misc.205/38(C)

1 (Sheet 3)

Police were going to keep observation, whilst another
member would proceed to Central Station to obtain
assistance to arrest the suspected person. In the mean-
time they had a waiting motor car, licence No.S.D.F.210,
parked close to the vicinity.

At 9.10 p.m. Yang Lee Tseng arrived at Nanking and
Szechuen Roads corner accompanied by two informers. On
approaching the food shop situated at No.88 Nanking Rd.,
the two informers went into the shop but Yang Lee Tseng
got suspicious, refused to enter and attempted to hurry
away. However, the four members of the Japanese Military
Police who were keeping watch, thinking he was going to
escape, surrounded him, handcuffed him, and were taking
him towards their motor car to bring him to Central
Station, when he escaped and ran shouting "Jang Neu"
towards S.P.C.624, who was on traffic duty at Nanking
and Szechuen Roads corner.

As Yang Lee Tseng was running towards the S.P.C. the
Military Police did not give immediate chase, but Sgt.
S. Takatani followed him and came to the Station with
the S.P.C.

The suspected person on being questioned stated that
he is a broker dealing in fish, pork and vegetables. He
has been residing in Shanghai for the past 3 months, as
he had to leave his residence in Peetung owing to the

警察负责监视，而另一名成员则前往中央捕房寻求协助以逮捕嫌疑人。同时，他们有一辆牌照号为 S.D.F.210 的等候汽车停在附近。

晚上9时10分，杨立正在两名线人的陪同下来到南京路与四川路路口。当接近位于南京路88号的食品店时，两名线人进入店内，但杨立正产生怀疑，拒绝进入并试图匆忙离开。然而，负责监视的四名日本宪兵成员认为他要逃跑，便包围了他，给他戴上手铐，并准备将他带上他们的汽车送往中央捕房，此时他逃脱并向正在南京路与四川路路口执行交通勤务的印籍巡长624号跑去，边跑边喊“强盗”（Jang Neu，音译）。

当杨立正跑向印籍巡长时，宪兵没有立即追赶，但高谷（S. Takatani，音译）军曹跟随他，并与印籍巡长一起来到警局。

pages.en:
Misc.205/38 (C)

1 (Sheet 5)

The suspected person strongly denies being connected
with the "anti-Japanese" terrorists, or Chinese Military
and also states that he has never been charged before.

Sgt. Tokutani received instructions over the
telephone from Captain Tsukamoto who is in charge of the
Japanese Military Police requesting the Police to detain
the suspected person, until he makes application to the
Commissioner of Police, on the morning of the 19-8-1938
for him to be handed over to the Japanese Authorities.

Detective Inspector Telfer, Senior Detective 1/c,
informed Mr. Robertson, D.O."A" re the facts of this case
and on his instructions Yang Lee Tseng is detained at
Central Station pending proof being furnished by the
Japanese Authorities to substantiate their allegation.

The Japanese informers did not come to the Station
and the Japanese Authorities also requested that
detectives do not visit the suspect's address, as this
would have a tendency to warn other associates residing
at other addresses.

Statements of suspected person, F.S. Taylor, S.P.C.
634 and C.P.C.8041 are attached hereto.

Sen. Det. 1/c.

嫌疑人强烈否认与“反日”恐怖分子或中国军队有任何关联，并声称此前从未被指控过。

德谷（Tokutani）警士接到负责日本宪兵队的塚本（Tsukamoto）队长的电话指示，要求警方拘留该嫌疑人，直至1938年8月19日上午他向警务处长提出申请，将其移交给日本当局。

泰尔弗（Telfer）侦探督察、高级侦探一等长就本案事实告知“A”区警官罗伯逊（Robertson）先生，并根据其指示，在日本当局提供证据证实其指控之前，将杨李增（Yang Lee Tseng，音译）拘押在中央巡捕房。

日本线人未前往巡捕房，日本当局还要求侦探不要前往嫌疑人的住址，因为这可能会警告居住在其他地址的其他同伙。

随函附上嫌疑人陈述、F.S. Taylor、S.P.C. 634 及 C.P.C.8041 的报告。

Yang Lee Tseng
Pootung                                C.0).C. .185
Central Station    18th Feb. 1938    translated    Clerk Sih Chien Shih
                                     xxxxxxxx

Yang Lee Tseng, age 29 years, native of Pootung, married,
broker, residing at No.89 Heng Meu Lee, Boulevard des Montigny,
F.C.

At about 11 a.m. this inst. I went to see a friend named
Chu Ah Sai at room No.437 Zung Chow Hotel, Chekiang Road, but
I failed to meet him. His wife told me that Chu Ah Sai had
gone to Tunchow. Whilst on the lift, I met another friend
named Loh Ioong Liang, who asked me to go and have tiffin at
his home, to which I agreed. We then walked to Loh's home at
Carter Road. After waiting for a few minutes, another two
male Chinese entered the house. Loh then introduced them to
me as "Lung" and "Chu", who are Loh's friends. We had tiffin
together at Loh's home. After we had partaken of our midday
meal, Chu became drunk. Loh then called three ricshas and
asked me to take them to the Zung Chow Hotel. On arrival at
the hotel, the watchman refused to allow "Chu" to enter the
building because he was drunk. I then called another two
ricshas and conveyed "Chu" back to Loh's home, where Chu slept
on the floor of the guest room. I then again went to Room 433
of the Zung Chow Hotel and informed Loh that Chu had slept in
his home, after that I went to Room 437 and met one named Fan
Ah Pao to talk over business transactions. As the vegetable
price going low, I felt very unhappy and went to sleep in Room
443.

At about 6 p.m. a pock-marked boy came and called me to
answer a telephone call. After I had told the caller that my
name is "Yang", he informed me that his name is "Sang" and
pages.zh:

浦东                                C.O.C. .185
中央巡捕房    1938年2月18日    翻译    书记员施健时（Sih Chien Shih，音译）

杨李增（Yang Lee Tseng，音译），29岁，浦东人，已婚，经纪人，住法租界蒙梯尼大道（Boulevard des Montigny）恒美里89号。

本月上午11时许，我前往浙江路中州旅馆437室拜访一位名叫朱阿四（Chu Ah Sai，音译）的朋友，但未见到他。他的妻子告诉我，朱阿四已去通州。当我在电梯里时，遇到了另一位名叫罗永良（Loh Ioong Liang，音译）的朋友，他邀请我去他家吃午饭，我答应了。随后我们步行至卡特路（Carter Road）罗的家中。等待几分钟后，又有两名中国男子进入屋内。罗随后向我介绍他们为“龙”（Lung）和“朱”（Chu），称他们是罗的朋友。我们在罗家一起吃了午饭。午饭后，朱喝醉了。罗叫了三辆黄包车，让我送他们回中州旅馆。到达旅馆后，看守因朱醉酒拒绝让他进入大楼。于是我又叫了两辆黄包车，将朱送回罗家，朱睡在客房的地板上。随后我再次前往中州旅馆433室，告知罗朱睡在他家，之后我去了437室，遇见一位名叫范阿宝（Fan Ah Pao，音译）的人洽谈生意。由于菜价下跌，我感到很不高兴，便去443室睡觉。

下午6点左右，一个脸上有麻子的男孩来叫我接电话。我告诉打电话的人我叫“杨”后，他说他叫“桑”（Sang，音译），并且

pages.en:
-Sheet 2-

and asked me to have supper with him, but I refused. About 20
minutes later Loh came back to the room and I informed him that
"Sung" had phoned me and asked me to have supper with him. Loh
suggested that we go together, but I again refused, telling Loh
that I do not feel very well. A few minutes later, "Sung" came
to the house, holding a bottle of wine in his hand, and again
asked Loh and myself to have supper with him. We then proceed-
ed to the Wu Foong Tsai Foodshop on Nanking Road, where we had
our supper. After we had partaking our food, I intended to go
to the Zung Chew hotel to sleep, but Sung asked me to accompany
him to visit a friend at Nanking Road. On arrival at a food
shop on Nanking Road, Sung asked me to wait for him outside
whilst he himself entered the premises. About 5 minutes later
4 foreign dressed Japanese approached me, each pointed at me
with a pistol. One of them took out a pair of handcuffs and
placed them on my wrist. Two of them then entered a waiting
motor car whilst the remaining two forced me to enter the car.
I then raised an alarm by shouting "Jang Dau" and at the same
time ran towards S.F.C. in the vicinity. a C.F.C. also came
to my assistance and asked me the matter. After I had informed
them the above, they took me together with the Japanese to the
Central Police Station.

This is my true statement.

Signed and cross marked
pages.zh:
-第2页-

邀请我和他一起吃晚饭，但我拒绝了。大约20分钟后，罗回到房间，我告诉他“宋”（Sung，音译）给我打过电话，邀我吃晚饭。罗建议我们一起去，但我再次拒绝，告诉罗我感觉不太舒服。几分钟后，“宋”来到住处，手里拿着一瓶酒，再次邀请罗和我一起吃晚饭。随后我们前往南京路的五丰斋食品店（Wu Foong Tsai Foodshop，音译）吃晚饭。吃完饭后，我打算去中州旅馆睡觉，但宋要求我陪他去南京路拜访一位朋友。到达南京路的一家食品店后，宋让我在外面等他，他自己进了店内。大约5分钟后，4名穿着西式服装的日本人走近我，每人都用手枪指着我。其中一人拿出一副手铐戴在我的手腕上。随后两人进入一辆等候的汽车，另外两人强迫我进入车内。我随即高喊“强盗”（Jang Dau）报警，同时向附近的S.F.C.（注：可能指锡克警察或特定警员代号）方向跑去。一名C.F.C.（注：可能指中国警察或特定警员代号）也前来协助，并询问情况。在我告知上述情况后，他们我与日本人一同带到了中央巡捕房。

这是我的真实陈述。

Japanese
Police In
Settlement

Chinese Is Seized By
Plain Clothes Men
On Nanking Road

An untoward incident occurred
on Nanking Road and Szechuen
Road corner at about 9.40 p.m. last
night when a Chinese ran up to a
Sikh constable on traffic duty,
showed him his handcuffed hands
and asked for help. The Chinese
was immediately followed by a
Japanese in civilian garb.
The Sikh being unable to leave
his traffic post, handed the com-
plainant over to a Chinese con-
stable of the S.M.P., who brought
the man to the Central Police
Station, the Japanese accompany-
ing them, but demanding that the
handcuffed Chinese be handed over
to him, as he stated that he was
a member of the Japanese Military
Police.
The group was followed to the
Central Police Station by three
other Japanese dressed in civilian
clothes, who later identified them-
selves as members of the Japan-
ese Military Police and requested
that the Chinese be handed over
to them as he was suspected of
anti-Japanese terroristic activities.
The Settlement Police refused to
grant the request prior to investigat-
ing the case and after lengthy dis-
cussion the Chinese was detained in
the cells at the Central Station
pending inquiries being made.
It is believed that the man was
seized by the Japanese on the
street and managed to slip out of
their hands and ran up to the
policemen asking for help.

租界内的
日本
警察

便衣人员在
南京路抓获
一名中国人

昨晚约9点40分，在南京路与四川路拐角发生了一起意外事件，一名中国人跑到一名正在执行交通勤务的锡克巡捕面前，展示他被手铐铐住的双手并求助。该中国人身后紧跟着一名身穿便服的日本人。
由于锡克巡捕不能离开交通岗位，他将报案人移交给一名公共租界工部局警务处的中国巡捕，后者将该男子带往中央巡捕房，日本人随行，但要求将被铐的中国人交给他，因为他声称自己是日本宪兵队成员。
另有三名身穿便服的日本人跟随该群体来到中央巡捕房，他们后来表明身份为日本宪兵队成员，并要求将该中国人移交给他们，理由是他涉嫌从事反日恐怖活动。
租界警方拒绝在未调查案件的情况下批准这一请求，经过长时间讨论，该中国人被拘押在中央巡捕房的牢房内，以待进一步查询。
据信，该男子是在街上被日本人抓获的，他设法挣脱并跑向警察求助。

At 7.20a.m. 29-1-38 Jong Yue Ngo, (王百鵝),
shopassistant employed by the "Universal" Butchery, 945 Yu
Yuen Road came to the station and reported that at about
11.30p.m. 28-1-38, another shopassistant named Jen Tseng
Kyi, (詹根仔), 23, Pootung, employed at above shop had
been arrested by the Japanese Military Police Search Party
outside the said shop.

show that the arrested man together with two other shop-
assistants namely Jong Li Ming, (王立民), and Wong Ngeoh
Su, (王瑞), at about 11.30p.m. 28-1-38 were returning
from godown at No.399 Edinburgh Road to their shop, when
outside of the above address they were stopped and searched

and work of the General Mao Zeh Tung, (毛澤東), leader of
the 8th Army (title of the book unknown), following which
he was led away by the said officers, whilst the other two
shopassistants were allowed to return to their shop.

August 23, 1938.

Bank of China Apartments - Present Situation

Lane 92 Houses 1 to 9, House 94 and No.96
Jessfield Road form one large piece of ground, the
property of the Bank of China. Before the outbreak
of hostilities, the houses in Lane 92 and House 94
were occupied by senior officials of the Bank of China
while No.96 consisting of blocks of apartments were
occupied by staff members of the Bank.

On January 13th, 1938 No.94 Jessfield Road was
taken over by the Japanese Military Police and occupied
by them with effect from January 18th. About half a
month later the same organ occupied the houses in Lane
No.92. Shortly after this the Japanese Military
attempted to occupy the Staff Quarters forming No.96
Jessfield Road but as a result of negotiations carried
out by the Bank officials direct with the Japanese
Military, the latter contented themselves with placing
a board at the entrance to the premises stating that
the property was under the jurisdiction of the
Japanese Forces and allowed the Bank employees to
remain in occupation.

With reference to the exact location of the
premises with regard to the Municipal Road on which
it is situated the following facts have been ascertained:

The premises in question (No.96 Jessfield Road)
have a main gate as well as a side gate, both opening on
to Jessfield Road, but no other side or rear doors exist.
This place, notwithstanding the fact that it does not
bear a Settlement Number plate has for a long time been
known to the public, as well as the General Post Office,
as No.96 Jessfield Road. The Revenue Department of
pages.zh:
1938年8月23日。

中国银行公寓 - 现状

极司菲尔路92弄1至9号、94号及96号构成一大片土地，为中国银行所有。在战事爆发前，92弄内的房屋及94号由中国银行高级职员居住，而由公寓楼组成的96号则由该行普通职员居住。

1938年1月13日，极司菲尔路94号被日本宪兵接管，并于1月18日起由其占用。约半个月后，同一机构占用了92弄内的房屋。此后不久，日本军方试图占用构成极司菲尔路96号的职员宿舍，但经中国银行官员直接与日本军方谈判，后者仅在入口处放置一块告示牌，声明该物业处于日军管辖之下，并允许银行员工继续居住。

关于该物业与其所在市政道路的确切位置关系，已查明以下事实：

涉案物业（极司菲尔路96号）有一个大门和一个侧门，均开向极司菲尔路，但无其他侧门或后门。此地虽未悬挂租界门牌号，但长期以来公众及邮政总局均将其称为极司菲尔路96号。上海工部局捐务处

the Shanghai Municipal Council records this place
as the Centro Terrace, Jessfield Road. Situated
therein are 113 houses, the landlord of which, the
Bank of China, pays the Municipal Tax regularly.
This house as will be seen by the attached
sketch, is situated on the East side of Jessfield

In the past, the Municipal Police have
never functioned in the compound which has always
been guarded by armed watchmen posted by the Bank.
However by the terms of the Secretary
General's memorandum to the Commissioner of Police
and Municipal Advocate, dated April 12th, 1935,
wherein he states that the Shanghai Municipal
Police should continue to function on Extra-
Settlement roads and property abutting thereon,
it appears that the latter have every right to
police the premises in question.

如附图所示，该房屋位于极司菲尔路东侧，金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）以北约15码处。
过去，警务处从未在该大院内执行职务，该院一直由中国银行派遣的武装看守守卫。
然而，根据1935年4月12日总办致警务处长及市政律师的备忘录条款，其中指出上海公共租界警务处应继续在越界筑路区域及毗邻物业行使职权，看来警务处完全有权对涉案物业进行警务管理。

REPORT
Date August 17 1938.

Subject Raid at 96 Jessfield Road, staff quarters of the Bank
of China.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

With reference to the Commissioner's remarks
on attached report, Mr. Nee Shiao Pun (倪孝本), a staff
officer of the Bank of China, was interviewed on August 17,
1938, and the following details ascertained:-

Early on the morning of August 13 a Japanese
search party which was accompanied by a Chapei policeman
visited Room 150 Apt. 7, 96 Jessfield Road. It is occupied
by Mr. Yang Wei Chuen (楊匯川), an employee of the Bank.
(Mr. Yang is now in Hongkong). A search was made of the
room and a few copies of the Ta Mei Wan Pao and booklets
alleged to be anti-Japanese were found. The Japanese then
arrested two sons of Mr. Yang age 18 and 15 respectively,
and a friend named Chu who happened to be on the premises.
These three men were taken away.

Chu and the younger son were released on the
afternoon of August 13 whilst the elder son Yang Yee Lien
(楊以廉) is still being held. Mr. Nee states that
through information received as a result of enquiries,
the prisoner has been removed to No.94 Jessfield Road,
headquarters of the Japanese Gendarmerie. He is allowed to
communicate with other members of his family and there
is probably no danger to his life.

由 谭绍良（Tan Shao Liang）警司 制作并转呈

参照警务处长在所附报告上的批注，于1938年8月17日约谈了中国银行职员倪孝本（Nee Shiao Pun）先生，并查明以下细节：-

8月13日清晨，一支由一名闸北警察陪同的日本搜查队访问了极司菲尔路96号7座150室。该房间由中国银行雇员杨汇川（Yang Wei Chuen）先生居住。（杨先生现居香港）。对该房间进行了搜查，发现了几份《大美晚报》及据称具有反日性质的小册子。随后，日本人逮捕了杨先生的两个儿子，年龄分别为18岁和15岁，以及当时恰好在场的一位姓朱的朋友。这三人被带走。

朱某和小儿子于8月13日下午获释，而长子杨以廉（Yang Yee Lien）仍被拘押。倪先生称，通过问询获得的消息得知，囚犯已被转移至极司菲尔路94号，即日本宪兵队总部。他被允许与其他家庭成员通信，其生命安全可能没有危险。

in plain clothes raided 96 Jessfield Road, quarters of Chinese

men, accompanied by an interpreter visited the Bank's
Staff Quarters at 94, Jessfield Road near Kinnear Road,

another examination, and after placing seals on 2 motor
cars and 3 inside doors of the premises, left, taking
with them the Bank's private motor bus, license No.18616.

bus, and had made arrangements for its removal with the

Subject Japanese military motor car containing hand-grenades ranked outside
the Yangtsze Hotel on 6-1-38.
Made by Det. MacAdie Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 10.05 a.m. 6-1-38 a Japanese military motor car,
unlicensed bearing a plate with a star, a small number 14 and
a larger number 1403 drove up to the Yangtsze Hotel along
Nankow Road from Yu Ya Ching Road and ranked outside the
entrance to the Yangtsze Hotel. One Japanese in plain clothes
was standing on the running board while three Japanese in
military uniform were in the car. All four men alighted and
entered the Yangtsze Hotel. It was then observed that one of
the military men was armed with a pistol of the Mauser type
with box holster. The driver of the car before leaving secured
the offside front and rear doors of the vehicle with a chain
and padlock. However, C.P.C. 2079 on point duty on looking
into the car observed an uncovered wooden box containing a
number of hand-grenades on the floor of the car in front of
the rear seats. The box was clearly visible to passersby. The
C.P.C. informed his sergeant C.P.S. 1019 and also S.I. Casely
in charge of traffic who visited him and the station was in
turn informed. Mr. R.D.M. Robertson D.O. "A", C.I. Shellswell
and Det. MacAdie attended the scene but the motor car drove
away with the four occupants northwards along Yunnan Road
into Nanking Road at 10.45 a.m. During the time the vehicle
was ranked outside the Yangtsze Hotel it was unoccupied and
none of the Japanese kept watch on it.

Enquiries by D.S. MacAdie at the Hotel in question
ascertained from the manager that the four Japanese proceeded
to Room 214 of the Hotel which had been engaged on 5-1-38
by the Japanese in plain clothes. According to the register

1938年1月6日上午10时05分，一辆无牌照、挂有星形标志、小号14和大号1403号牌的日本军用汽车，从虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）沿南京路（Nankow Road）驶至扬子饭店，并停在扬子饭店入口外。一名便衣日本人站在踏板上，车内有三名身穿军服的日本人。四人全部下车进入扬子饭店。随后观察到其中一名军人携带一支带盒式枪套的毛瑟型手枪。司机在离开前用链条和挂锁锁住了车辆右侧的前后车门。然而，正在执勤的华捕2079号向车内查看时，发现后座前的车地板上有一个未遮盖的木箱，里面装有若干手榴弹。路人可以清楚地看到该箱子。该华捕通知了其上司华捕1019号，以及负责交通的巡佐 Casely 先生，后者前来查看，捕房也随即接到通知。A区督察长 Robertson 先生、探员 Shellswell 先生和 MacAdie 侦探赶赴现场，但该车载着四名乘客于上午10时45分向北沿云南路驶入南京路离开。在车辆停在扬子饭店外期间，车内无人，且没有日本人看守车辆。

MacAdie 高级侦探在上述酒店进行的问询中，从经理处获悉，这四名日本人前往酒店的214房间，该房间已于1938年1月5日由那名便衣日本人预订。根据登记簿

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Louss Station,
REPORT
Date January 6th, 19 38.

Subject (in full) Japanese military motor car containing hand-grenades ranked
outside the Yangtze Hotel on 6-1-38.

Made by C.I. Gascoyne Forwarded by

Sir,

At approximately 10.30 a.m. 6-1-38 I reached Hankow-Yunnan
Road intersection during the course of my district patrol. C.P.C.
No. 3079 on post duty at that point informed me that four or five
fully armed Japanese soldiers had entered the Yangtze Hotel a
few minutes previously and that he had already informed the
Station. Further, he stated in the unattended military m/car
(unlicensed) which was parked on the north side of Hankow Road
west of Yunnan Road near the entrance door to the Hotel, he
had observed several bombs therein. I accompanied him to the
vehicle and observed an uncovered wooden box on the floor at the
rear of the driver's seat, containing four or five grenades of the
"potato masher" type. These missiles were clearly visible to
any person desiring to glance in whilst passing the vehicle and
no chauffeur or military guards were in evidence.

I instructed the C.P.C. to watch for any further develop-
ments and then returned to the Station and conveyed the informa-
tion to S.I. Shellswell i/c Louss Station.

Yours obediently.

Sub-Insp.

老闸捕房，
报告
日期 1938年1月6日。

事由（全称） 1938年1月6日，一辆载有手榴弹的日军军用汽车停在扬子饭店外。

呈报人 C.I. Gascoyne 转呈人

敬启者，

1938年1月6日上午约10时30分，我在辖区巡逻途中抵达汉口路与云南路路口。当时在该处执勤的华籍巡长（C.P.C.）第3079号告知我，几分钟前有四至五名全副武装的日本士兵进入了扬子饭店，且他已通知捕房。此外，他表示，在停于饭店入口附近、云南路以西汉口路北侧的一辆无人看管的军用汽车（无牌照）内，他观察到数枚炸弹。我随他前往该车辆，并在驾驶座后方的地板上看到一个未加盖的木箱，里面装有四至五枚“马铃薯捣碎器”式手榴弹。任何路过并有意瞥视车内的人都能清楚地看到这些弹药，现场未见司机或军事警卫。

我指示该华籍巡长留意后续事态发展，随后返回捕房，并将此情况通报给老闸捕房主管副督察（S.I.）Shellswell。

谨此呈报。

副督察

C.P.C.079  Teling Sung,
attached to Louza Station.
/ D.S. Mc Allie.
Louza Stn.    5-1-38    translated.    Marks with Sun Pal.
///////

At 7.40 a.m. on 5-1-38, I came on duty and was
posted to Traffic Post No.36 at the corner of Hankow and
Yunnan Roads. At 10.04 a.m., I saw a Japanese military
m/car come from west to east on Hankow Road and stopped
outside the Yangtsze Hotel. Three Japanese in military
uniform alighted from the car while a Japanese in plain clothes
who had been standing on the running board of the car also
alighted and all entered the Yangtsze Hotel. One of the
soldiers was armed with a long pistol of the Mauser pattern
with box holster. I then left my point and proceeded to the
Police Telephone at the corner of Hankow and Yu Ya Ching
Roads with the object of informing the Station. However,
on arrival I found that P.C. C.P.C.1666 on duty there had
already telephoned to the Station. I then walked back along
Hankow Road to my point and passing on the near side of the
m/car I observed a wooden box on the floor of the car without
a cover and packed inside were as far as I could see four
cylindrical objects which appeared to be hand-grenades. The
grenades were about 12 inches long including the handle and
the metal part was about 3" in diameter. The handle was about
1" to 1½" in diameter. The box was on the near side of the
car in front of the rear seats. I reported the occurrence to
S.I. Oaseley and C.P.S.1019 as they visited me on point duty.
At 10.45 a.m. the m/car left turning north into Yunnan Road
and thence to Nanking Road. Before leaving the car, the
driver of the car secured the front and rear offside door
handles with a chain and padlock. None of the Japanese watched

华籍巡长（C.P.C.）079 Teling Sung，
隶属老闸捕房。
/ D.S. Mc Allie.
老闸捕房    1938年1月5日    翻译。    与孙帕尔（Sun Pal）标记相符。

1938年1月5日上午7时40分，我上岗执勤，被派往汉口路与云南路路口的第36号交通岗。上午10时04分，我看见一辆日军军用汽车沿汉口路由西向东行驶，并停在扬子饭店外。三名身穿军装的日本人从车上下来，同时一名此前站在车踏脚板上的便衣日本人也下了车，众人均进入扬子饭店。其中一名士兵配备有一支带盒式枪套的毛瑟式长手枪。随后我离开岗位，前往汉口路与虞洽卿路路口的警用电话处，旨在向捕房报告。然而，到达后我发现正在此处执勤的华籍巡长（C.P.C.）第1666号已经通过电话向捕房报告。于是我沿汉口路走回我的岗位，经过该军用汽车近侧时，我观察到车内地板上有一个未加盖的木箱，据我所见，里面装有四个圆柱形物体，看似手榴弹。包括手柄在内，手榴弹长约12英寸，金属部分直径约3英寸。手柄直径约1至1.5英寸。木箱位于车内后排座位前方的近侧。当副督察（S.I.）Oaseley和华籍巡佐（C.P.S.）第1019号来岗巡视时，我向他们报告了此事。上午10时45分，该军用汽车左转进入云南路，随即驶往南京路。在离开车辆前，司机用链条和挂锁锁住了车辆前部和后部的远侧车门把手。在日本人进入扬子饭店期间，无人看守

C.P.C. 1019 Yue Pei-ling attached to Louza
// D.C. Macadie
Louza Station 6-1-38 Clerk Chu Teu Yee

At 10.20 a.m. 6-1-38, I visited No. 36 point at the corner of Yunnan and Hankow roads in the course of traffic supervision and C.P.C. 2079 on that point informed me that a Japanese military motor car was outside the Yangtze Hotel and asked me to look inside the car. I accompanied him to the car which was parked on Hankow road north side west of Yunnan Road outside the entrance to the Yangtze Hotel. On looking into the car I saw an uncovered wooden case about 18" long; and about 8' wide in which were several hand-grenades. I could not count the number but I know they were hand-grenades because I saw some seized by detectives in the Oriental Hotel in November 1937. I then instructed C.P.C. 2079 to inform the station again of the occurrence. No person was in the motor car while no one was looking after the vehicle. The doors were all closed and the glass windows were shut.

(Sgd) Yue Pei Ling

老闸捕房 1938年1月6日 书记员 Chu Teu Yee

1938年1月6日上午10时20分，我在进行交通督导期间巡视了云南路与汉口路路口的第36号岗位，该岗位的华籍巡长（C.P.C.）2079号告知我，扬子饭店外有一辆日军军用汽车，并请我查看车内情况。我随他前往停在云南路以西、扬子饭店入口外汉口路北侧的汽车。向车内看去，我看见一个长约18英寸、宽约8英寸（原文如此，疑为8英寸）的未加盖木箱，里面装有数枚手榴弹。我无法清点具体数量，但我确认它们是手榴弹，因为我曾在1937年11月见过探员在东方饭店查获类似物品。随后，我指示华籍巡长（C.P.C.）2079号再次向捕房报告此事。车内无人，亦无人照看车辆。车门全部关闭，玻璃窗也已关好。

（签名）Yue Pei Ling

Subject Arrest of Chinese Y.M.C.A. employee by Japanese Military Police
- released.
Made by D.S.I. Shih Hsi-chien Forwarded by C. Gonsalves

Information has been received to the effect that
Mr. John K.H. Jen, Secretary of the Y.M.C.A. Western
District Social Centre, who was arrested by the Japanese
Military Police on January 1, was released on January 24.
The reason for his release is reported to be due to
insufficient evidence to prefer a charge against him, but
his release was accelerated through efforts by Mr. Wilbur
of the National Committee of the Chinese Y.M.C.A. and one
Mr. Inouye, General Secretary of the Japanese Y.M.C.A.
The above information was confirmed by Mr. F.W.
Soong, Secretary of the Chinese Y.M.C.A., who stated that
the services of Mr. Jen had since been dispensed with, and
that Mr. Jen had returned to his native place via Ningpo.

pages.en:
165

Chinese Describe Four
Day Captivity In Hands
Of Japanese Military

Seized At YMCA In Settlement; Four Questioned,
Released; One Alleged Red Still Held;
Hardships, Third Degree Endured

Other Chinese Detained By Military

“THE darkest moments in my life were spent during the
four days when I was being held a prisoner together
with four other Chinese by the Japanese military; the un-
certainty of my fate at the hands of the Japanese added to
my mortal fear and apprehension.”

That was what one of the five Chinese, who were seized
by a party of Japanese soldiers on New Year's Day from the
Chinese Y.M.C.A. Western District
Social Center, 2400 Robison Road
(International Settlement), said in
an exclusive interview with a re-
presentative of the Shanghai
Evening Post today. Four of the
five were released by the Japanese
on Tuesday afternoon.

Held Four Days

Held prisoners for four days at
the Kung Dah No. 3 Mill at Bre-
nan Place near Tseohadoo on
suspicion of being communists, the
men went through some of the
most trying moments of their lives.
They were kept in a small, dark
cell for three nights and four days
and during their forced detention
were not allowed even the slightest
freedom of movement, said one of
the men who regained his liberty
Tuesday.

Six Chinese had been seized by
a party of about a dozen
Japanese soldiers, two Japan-
ese constables of the S.M.P.,
and two plainclothesmen, shortly
before 3 p.m. on Saturday
from the premises of the Y.M.C.A.
Social Center. The men taken
into custody by the Japanese in-
cluding the director of the social
center, Mr. Ren Kwei-ho, who is
still being held by the Japanese,
two janitors of the center, one
coolie employed by a foreigner at
the Cathay Mansions and a labor-
er. Chinese Police Constable 890
was also arrested, but released at
once.

Broke Into Premises

The Japanese broke into the pre-
mises and without asking any ques-
tions herded together all the men
there at the time and bound them
with rope, whisking them away
to the Kung Dah Mill. The police
constable was off duty then in
plainclothes. The laborer had come
to the social center to get medical
treatment at the clinic when he was
seized by the Japanese. The coolie
in the employ of a foreigner had
been visiting the place to see one
of the janitors.

Arriving at the mill, the
captors sent for Chinese inter-
preters and the men were subject-
ed to careful questioning as to
their past and present careers in
Shanghai. One of the janitors
named Sun Tien-han was without
provocation hit in the face with a
wooden club by one of the Japan-
ese during the questioning and
several others were slapped by the
guards. The police constable was
at once released when his identity
was disclosed.

No Beds Provided

After the questioning, the five
were locked in a dark cell which
had no bed nor even a chair. Also
in the room was one school
teacher named Chen who had
been seized by the Japanese on
December 18 at the Hwa Hwa
Academy, Yu Yuen Road. The six
of them occupied a grass mat on
the cement floor which was con-
tinually wet. They were not
molested that night.

During the second day, Mr. Ren
was separately questioned several
times. He is said to have told the
janitors that he was suspected by
the Japanese of being a red.
During the grilling it is alleged
that the Japanese used the third
degree, according to one of the
four just released. Aside from
Mr. Ren, the others were strictly
let alone and given three meals of
rice and salted radish. Apparently
the Japanese had intended to
seize only Mr. Ren.

Again Questioned

On Monday, the janitors were
questioned through interpreters
without resorting to third degree.
The Japanese questioned them in
regard to their occupation and
the activities of the social center.
Apparently satisfied with the
grilling, the two janitors were
again dumped into the cell.

On the fourth day, Tuesday, the
two janitors, the laborer, and the
foreigner's coolie were set free
after noon. But before being re-
leased, all of them were warned
not to re-visit the Y.M.C.A.
on penalty of death. The school
teacher named Chen and Mr. Ren
were not released.

Other Chinese Held

According to one of those re-
leased, several other Chinese are
alleged to be detained at the mili-
tary headquarters. The prisoners
were not given the slightest free-
dom of movement. A guard even
accompanied them to the lavatory.
The guard, however, is said to
have been friendly to the prison-
ers.

The Y.M.C.A. social center on
Robison Road had been engaged
in educating factory workers in
the western district up to the time
of its closure on December 29. The
night school for workers had some
300 students.

165

中国人描述被日军
囚禁四日的经历

在租界基督教青年会被捕；四人受审后获释；一人涉嫌赤化分子仍被拘押；
遭受苦难及酷刑逼供

其他被军方拘留的中国人

“我生命中最黑暗的时刻，是与另外四名中国人一起被日军囚禁的那四天；命运掌握在日本人手中的不确定性加剧了我极度的恐惧和忧虑。”

这是元旦当天在公共租界罗勃生路2400号中国基督教青年会西区社会中心被一队日本士兵逮捕的五名中国人之一，今天在接受《上海晚邮报》记者独家采访时所说的话。五人中的四人于周二下午被日本人释放。

被囚禁四天

据周二重获自由的一名男子称，这些人因涉嫌是共产主义者，在曹家渡附近布伦南广场的公大第三纱厂被囚禁了四天，经历了他们生命中最艰难的时刻。他们在狭小黑暗的牢房里度过了三个夜晚和四个白天，在被迫拘留期间，连最轻微的行动自由都不被允许。

周六下午3点前不久，约十二名日本士兵、两名上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本巡捕以及两名便衣人员，从中国基督教青年会社会中心的场所带走了六名中国人。被日本人拘留的人包括该社会中心主任任贵和（Ren Kwei-ho，音译），他目前仍被日本人扣押；该中心的两名看门人；一名受雇于外国人的苦力，住在华懋公寓（Cathay Mansions）；以及一名劳工。华籍巡捕第890号也被逮捕，但随即获释。

闯入场所

日本人闯入场所，未加询问便将当时在场的所有男人聚集在一起，用绳子捆绑，迅速将他们带到公大纱厂。当时该巡捕下班休息，身着便衣。那名劳工是在来到社会中心诊所寻求医疗救治时被日本人抓获的。那名受雇于外国人的苦力是去那里看望其中一名看门人的。

到达纱厂后，抓捕者叫来了中文翻译，并对这些人在上海的过去和现在的职业进行了仔细盘问。在盘问期间，一名名叫孙殿汉（Sun Tien-han，音译）的看门人无缘无故被一名日本人用木棍击打面部，其他几人也被警卫扇耳光。当该巡捕的身份被揭露后，他立即获释。

未提供床铺

盘问结束后，这五人被锁在一间既无床也无椅子的黑暗牢房里。房间里还有一名姓陈的学校教师，他是日本人于12月18日在愚园路华华学院（Hwa Hwa Academy，音译）逮捕的。他们六人睡在水泥地上的一张草席上，地面持续潮湿。当晚他们未受骚扰。

第二天，任先生被单独审问了数次。据说他告诉看门人，日本人怀疑他是“赤色分子”。据刚获释的四人之一称，在审讯过程中，日本人 allegedly 使用了酷刑（third degree）。除了任先生外，其他人未被严加干涉，每日供应三餐米饭和咸萝卜。显然，日本人原本只打算逮捕任先生一人。

再次受审

周一，看门人通过翻译接受了讯问，未使用酷刑。日本人询问了他们的职业和社会中心的活动情况。似乎对审讯结果感到满意，这两名看门人再次被扔进牢房。

第四天，即周二，中午过后，两名看门人、那名劳工以及那名外国人的苦力被释放。但在获释前，所有人都受到警告，不得再次访问基督教青年会，否则处以死刑。姓陈的学校教师和任先生未获释放。

其他被拘押的中国人

据获释者之一称，据称还有其他几名中国人被拘留在军事总部。囚犯没有任何行动自由。甚至有一名警卫陪同他们去厕所。然而，据说这名警卫对囚犯态度友好。

罗勃生路上的基督教青年会社会中心一直从事西区工厂工人的教育工作，直至12月29日关闭。工人夜校约有300名学生。

REPORT
1st January 1st, 1938.
Subject Chinese Y.M.C.A., No.422 Bubbling Well Road, raided by Japanese Military Police.
Made by J.J.S. Burton. Forwarded by 〔签名潦草无法辨认〕

Sir,

At 2155 hrs. on the 1.1.38., a telephone message was received from P.S. 32, Aberdeen through street telephone No. 3, Robison and Fergyuson corner, to the effect that Japanese Military had entered the Chinese Y.M.C.A., 422, Bubbling Well Road, and a party of Chinese under the control of the Military had arrived and found the said Military searching the said premises having with them about 98 Japanese attached to Bubbling Well Station.

The following is the information obtained by the undersigned:-

At about 2100 hrs. on the 1.1.38. 10 members of the Japanese Military Police in two motor cars proceeded to Bubbling Well Station and requested assistance to raid the Chinese Y.M.C.A. on Robison Road. Sub-Inspector Yamaguchi instructed J.P.S. 98 to accompany the said Military to Footoo Road Station, where necessary assistance should be obtained. However, the Military Police after leaving Bubbling Well Station, informed J.P.S. 98 that they did not have time to visit Footoo Road for assistance and proceeded direct to the said Y.M.C.A., where upon arrival they jumped out of the cars with drawn pistols, ran into the premises and commenced to search and placed under arrest 5 male Chinese who were on the premises when they entered. These males whose particulars as far as can be ascertained are as follows:-

(Ten) 1. Sing Tsung Hao (任春浩), age 32, native of Kaushing, clerk, employed at the Y.M.C.A.
2. Tsang Tsang Nan (張壽南), age 41, native of Shantung, teaboy, employed at the Y.M.C.A.
3. Sung Dien Kwang (孫殿光), native of Hopeh, also teaboy, employed at the Y.M.C.A.

1938年1月1日。
事由 日本宪兵搜查静安寺路422号中国基督教青年会。
呈报人 J.J.S. Burton. 转呈人 〔签名潦草无法辨认〕

敬启者，

1938年1月1日21时55分，通过罗勃生路与弗格森路路口的3号街道电话，接到来自阿伯丁捕房（P.S. 32）的电话消息，称日军已进入静安寺路422号中国基督教青年会，一批受军方控制的中国人抵达现场，发现上述军方正在搜查该场所，随行约有98名隶属于静安寺捕房的日本人。

以下是本人获得的信息：

1938年1月1日约21时，10名日本宪兵成员乘坐两辆汽车前往静安寺捕房，请求协助搜查罗勃生路上的中国基督教青年会。山口（Yamaguchi）副督察指示日本巡佐（J.P.S.）第98号陪同上述军方人员前往虹口捕房（Footoo Road Station），以获取必要的协助。然而，日本宪兵离开静安寺捕房后，告知日本巡佐第98号他们没有时间前往虹口寻求协助，并直接前往上述基督教青年会。到达后，他们拔出手枪跳出汽车，冲入场所开始搜查，并将进入时在场的5名中国男子逮捕。这些男子的详细信息经查证如下：

(十) 1. Sing Tsung Hao (任春浩)，32岁，江苏嘉兴人，职员，受雇于基督教青年会。
2. Tsang Tsang Nan (張壽南)，41岁，山东人，茶役，受雇于基督教青年会。
3. Sung Dien Kwang (孫殿光)，河北人，亦为茶役，受雇于基督教青年会。

这些男子的双手被反绑在背后，与宪兵队查获的大量宣传品一起被带上两辆等候的汽车，宪兵队声称这些宣传品具有反日性质。

由于车内空间不足，无法容纳所有宪兵以及被捕的5名男子，三名宪兵被留下等待汽车返回，随同留下的还有警员编号98（J.P.S. 98）。

在他们驾车离开之前，通过警员编号98（J.P.S. 98）询问这5名男子将被带往何处，答复是带往其位于极司菲尔路138号公大第三棉纱厂的总部。另外三名宪兵在等待汽车返回期间，在青年会（Y.M.C.A.）后方发现另一名中国男子并将其拘留，然而，经讯问时该男子声称他是隶属于总队的警员编号3291（C.P.C. 3291），但他们不允许他离开青年会大院，称他们希望核实其身份，而他身着便服，无法证明其身为巡捕的说法，但他们表示将把他带往戈登路总队，在那里可以核实其身份，因此汽车到达后，他们将他带往戈登路总队，经核实身份后将其释放。

本捕房警员未获知此次搜查行动的原因，当行动结束后，他们离开时并未向警方说明在租界内逮捕5名中国男子的原因。

Settlement.

Mr.riers, D.C. Divisions, Mr. Young, D.C. Crime,
D.O. and D.D.D.U. "B" informed. Mr. Young instructed the under-
signed to inform the Japanese Military authorities that they
had conducted a raid and made arrests inside the Settlement.
Accordingly J.D.J. 48 Mori visited the Japanese Military Police
Headquarters, No.138 Jessfield Road, where he interviewed
Captain Okamora and informed him as above, who in turn replied
that he was very sorry to have caused trouble and knew that the
premises were in the Settlement, but having no time and not
being able to get hold of any Japanese police on the telephone,
had instructed Corporal Shibuya of the Military Police to
proceed to Bubbling Well Station and make necessary arrangements
for the raid. He further went on to state that the 5 male
Chinese arrested on the premises are suspected of being
concerned in bomb throwings and teaching anti-Japanese doctrines
and should they find on completion of their enquiries that they
were concerned in anti-Japanese activities, they would be dealt
with according to Japanese Military Law, and if there was
nothing against them they would be released.

J.D.S. 48 Mori will keep in touch with the
Japanese Military Police with view to ascertaining the result
of their enquiries into the 5 males as to what happens to them,
when this information is obtained, a further report will be
forwarded.

〔签名〕
D.D.I.

租界内。

已通知分区副督察长 Riers 先生、刑侦副督察长 Young 先生、值班警官及“B”区副侦探长。Young 先生指示具报人通知日本军方当局，他们已在租界内进行搜查并实施逮捕。据此，日籍警员编号48 Mori 前往位于极司菲尔路138号的日本宪兵队总部，会见了 Okamora（音译）上尉并如上告知，后者随即回复说，对于造成麻烦深感抱歉，并知道该处所位于租界内，但因时间紧迫且无法通过电话联络到任何日本警察，故指令宪兵下士 Shibuya（音译）前往静安寺捕房，为搜查行动做出必要安排。他进一步表示，在该处所逮捕的5名中国男子涉嫌参与投掷炸弹及传授反日思想，如果在调查结束后发现他们参与反日活动，将依据日本军法处置，如果未发现不利证据，则将予以释放。

日籍警员编号48 Mori 将与日本宪兵队保持联系，以查明对这5名男子调查的结果及他们的下落，一旦获得此信息，将提交进一步报告。

〔签名〕
副侦探长助理（D.D.I.）

Sir,

Four of the males arrested by the Japanese Military
at the Chinese Y.M.C.A. No. 4200 Robison Road at about 2.55 pm
on the 1.1.38 were released from the Kung Dah Cotton Mill,
No. 138 Jessfield Road by the Japanese Military Police at
5 p.m. on the 4.1.38.

The released males are:- Tsang Tsung Nan, Sung Dien
Kwung, Wong Zien Kwung and Wong Zau Shing, when questioned
at the station as to their treatment whilst being detained by
the Japanese Military they stated that they were well looked
after and had nothing to complain of, also stating that with
the exception of asking them what they were doing at the
Y.M.C.A. no other questions were put to them by the Japanese
Military. On their release these men took up residence
at No.3 Refugee Camp, Rue de Zaizoong, French Concession.

In reference to Nying Tsung Hao this man is still
detained and the military are continuing enquiries into his
past activities and they cannot say whether he will eventually
be released or not.

D.D.O. "B" Division.

自提交本案原始报告以来，警方已采取适当措施，以便在必要时立即为威海卫路203号和245号的这两家店铺提供援助，但截至目前，此前通报的所谓日本军方团体成员均未到访上述任一地址。

侦探已对本捕房所属各科警员进行了进一步调查，内容是关于1937年11月24日或11月25日日本团体据称访问威海卫路203号成都橡胶轮胎店一事，但没有警员实际目睹任何日本军方人员在上述日期进出该处，也没有警员注意到上述当局的军用汽车停放在所述处所外。然而，下列警员表示，他们观察到一辆符合本案唯一目击者学徒[周华]所描述特征的汽车，于1937年11月25日下午3时至3时40分之间经过该区。看到车上有几名日本军官，但由于未发生不幸事件，警员未记下

He explained that he had been compelled to close his shop immediately after the departure of the first visit of the Japanese Military Officers, he being very frightened and could not sleep during the night. Fearing that they might keep their word and return to the shop again, he thought that it is better personally leave the premises in order to avoid any unfortunate misunderstanding or being falsely incriminated by Japanese Military Authorities for some unknown reason. He accordingly proceeded to the house of his cousin named Kung Chiang Tu (江章土) at No. 564/145 Avenue Road, where he remained with him (cousin) during the last few days. He further led detectives to the above address, where his cousin was interviewed and verified his statement.

In response to further questioning, Kung Hsieh Tu (江協土) stated that he had no slight idea in regard to the unexpected visits of the Japanese. He further explained that a certain Japanese civilian visited his shop and purchased a second-hand "Firestone" rubber motor car tyre, size 475-19," for $5.00, which amount was accordingly paid. The said Japanese visited the shop again in the same afternoon requested him (Kung Hsieh Tu) to repair an old "Goodrich" motor car rubber

37年12月22日，是我第一天上班。约下午2点40分，

The second described person is employed as an
apprentice in his shop and is the only eye-witness, who
supplied the Police with the alleged information in regard
to the visits of Japanese Military Officers to the above
shop as explained in the following pages of this report.
The 3rd, 4th, and 5th described are sub-tenants, who
occupy various rooms inside the above shop premises, while
the 6th and 7th named persons are sub-tenants of an
adjoining coal shop at 205 Weihaiwei Road.

The Chengtu Rubber Tyre Shop is situated at the
South Eastern Corner of Chengtu Road and Weihaiwei Road,
which adjoins the coal shop at 205 Weihaiwei Road. The
above two shops use the same and only staircase at the
back leading to various rooms on the upper floors on
both premises although there are different front entrances
to their shops.

Following the alleged visits of the Japanese Military
Officers, the sub-tenants on both premises became frighten-
ed and persuaded the 1st described, co-proprietor of the
Chengtu Rubber Tyre Co, to file a complaint at this
Station in order to seek for early Police protection.

Subsequent investigations by D.I. Hill, D.T.I. Tsui
Liu and C.P.S. 192 reveal that the 1st described, who is
also the sole proprietor of the Hsia Kee Motor Car Parts

所述第二人在其店内担任学徒，是唯一的目击者，
他向警方提供了关于日本军官造访上述
店铺的信息，详情见本报告后续页面。
所述的第三、第四和第五人是分租客，
他们占用上述店铺 premises 内的不同房间，而
第六和第七名提及的人员是相邻的威海卫路 205 号煤店的分租客。

成都橡胶轮胎店位于成都路与威海卫路的东南角，
毗邻威海卫路 205 号的煤店。上述两家店铺共用
后方通往两处物业楼上各个房间的同一座楼梯，尽管
它们的店铺正面入口不同。

在日本军官涉嫌造访之后，两处物业的分租客感到
恐惧，并劝说成都橡胶轮胎公司的合营店主（即所述第一人）
向本捕房投诉，以寻求警方的尽早保护。

随后，侦探督察 Hill、侦探总巡徐刘（Tsui Liu，音译）和华籍巡捕 192 号进行的调查显示，所述第一人
同时也是祥记

pages.en:
1/Sheet 3.

Shop (祥记) at 345 Weihaiwei Road, had entered into
partnership with his friend named Kong Hsueh Ta (江学芝)
for the establishment of the Chen:tu Rubber Tyre Shop
at 203 Weihaiwei Road on 20-7-37, the total capital
amounting to $500.00, which was equally invested by them.
The 1st described though being a co-partner of the latter
shop spends most of his time in his own shop at 345
Weihaiwei Road and occasionally visits the Chengtu Rubber
Tyre Shop at 203 Weihaiwei Road during day time. His
partner Kong Hsueh Ta (江学芝), who takes full
responsibilities of the business, sleeps in the shop at
203 Weihaiwei Road with the apprentice (2nd described)
at night. In his (the partner) temporary absence during
the day, the apprentice, who is the only employee in the
shop, takes charge of all business transactions with
consent of both partners.
At about 4p.m. on 28-12-37, whilst the apprentice
was alone in the shop at 203 Weihaiwei Road, a male person
clad in Khaki military uniform appearing to be a Japanese
Officer entered the shop via the open front door. Think-
ing that he was a customer, the apprentice politely asked
him as to what he would like to purchase. The so-called
Japanese Officer (believed to be a Manchurian), who spoke
fluent Shantung dialect, replied in the negative but
pages.zh:
1/第3页。

汽车配件店（祥记）的唯一店主，该店位于威海卫路 345 号，
他于 37年7月20 日与名为江学芝（Kong Hsueh Ta）的朋友合伙，
在威海卫路 203 号成立了成都橡胶轮胎店，
总资本额为 500.00 美元，由双方等额投资。
所述第一人虽然是后一家店铺的合营伙伴，但大部分时间
都在他自己位于威海卫路 345 号的店里度过，偶尔在白天
去威海卫路 203 号的成都橡胶轮胎店看看。他的合伙人江学芝（Kong Hsueh Ta）
承担全部经营责任，夜间与学徒（所述第二人）一起
睡在威海卫路 203 号的店里。在他（合伙人）白天暂时
离开期间，作为店内唯一雇员的学徒，在征得两位合伙人
同意的情况下，负责所有业务交易。
37年12月28日下午4点左右，当学徒
独自在威海卫路 203 号的店里时，一名身穿
卡其色军装的男子（看似是一名日本军官）通过敞开的前门进入店内。学徒
以为他是顾客，礼貌地询问他想购买什么。这位所谓的
日本军官（被认为是满洲人），说着流利的山东话，予以否认，但

pages.en:
1/Sheet 4.

demanded to see the proprietor of the shop. Asked as
to which proprietor he would like to interview and his
name, the officer did not give any answer but immediate-
ly walked out of the shop, following which the apprentice
also came out from the shop and observed the officer
ascend a black "Chevrolet" sedan motor car, parked
outside the front door of the shop in a Western position.
He further noticed a Japanese flag tied to the front
mud-guard of the car, which body was covered with mud-
stains as if the vehicle had been in military use. The
apprentice further stated that with exception of the
front glass screen of the car, the blinds on the side
and back glass screens were fully lowered at that
moment. He, however, maintained that he definitely
saw five other Japanese Military Officers wearing same
Khaki uniform inside the car when the first officer,
with whom he had conversation in the shop, opened the
left door of the car and boarded same. He failed to
notice the license number of the vehicle in question
but observed a black oblong plate being affixed to the
back mud-guard bearing several white Japanese characters,
the first two of which, according to his memory, were
similar to Chinese characters "千九", meaning thousand
and nine in Chinese. The car and the occupants were
pages.zh:
1/第4页。

要求见店主。当被问及他想见哪位店主及其姓名时，
该军官没有回答，而是立即走出店铺，随后学徒
也走出店铺，观察到该军官登上了一辆停在
店门前西侧的黑色“雪佛兰”轿车。
他还注意到车头挡泥板上系着一面日本国旗，车身
覆盖着泥渍，仿佛该车辆曾被用于军事用途。学徒
进一步陈述说，除了车前挡风玻璃外，侧面和后部的
遮阳帘当时都已完全放下。然而，他坚持表示，当刚才
在店里与他交谈的那位军官打开左车门上车时，他确实
看到了车内还有另外五名身穿同样卡其色制服的日本军官。
他未能注意到涉事车辆的车牌号码，但观察到后挡泥板上
固定着一块黑色的长方形牌子，上面有几个白色的日文字符，
据他记忆，前两个字符类似于中文的“千九”，在中文里意为
一千和九。该车及车内人员

pages.en:
1/9heet 5.

being subsequently driven to an Eastern direction along
Weihaiwei Road. The period of their visit was said to
only last a few minutes.

At about 5.30p.m. same afternoon when the third above
described person, a sub-tenant in the house, returned
home, the apprentice informed him of the above occurrence.
At about 7p.m. same evening one of the co-proprietors
Kong Hsuch Ts returned to the shop, the apprentice also
reported to him regarding the intrusion of the Japanese
Officers. The former remarked that it was very strange
for the Japanese to visit his shop and ask for the
proprietor. Half hour later the apprentice proceeded
to informant's (1st described) shop at 345 Weihaiwei Road
and informed the 1st described, who subsequently consult-
ed this case with his partner Kong Hsuch Ts. The latter
denied any knowledge of the purpose of the Japanese visit
to the shop.

At about 4a.m. on 23-12-37 Kong Hsuch Ts, who was
sleeping in the lower back room of the shop at 205 Chengtu
Road, got out of bed and awakened the apprentice, who
slept on the floor in the front shop room, and informed
the latter that he would go out for a short while to
attend an important business and that if any Japanese
Military Officers arrived again and asked for the
pages.zh:
1/9heet 5.

随后沿威海卫路（Weihaiwei Road）向东驶离。据说他们停留的时间仅几分钟。

同日下午约5时30分，上述第三人（该房屋的转租人）回家时，学徒将上述事件告知了他。当晚约7时，共同经营者之一孔学慈（Kong Hsuch Ts，音译）回到店里，学徒也向他报告了日本军官闯入一事。前者表示，日本人来到他的店里寻找店主，这非常奇怪。半小时后，学徒前往位于威海卫路345号的举报人（即上述第一人）的店铺，告知了上述第一人，后者随即与其合伙人孔学慈商议此事。后者否认知晓日本人来访店里的目的。

1937年12月23日凌晨4时许，睡在成都路（Chengtu Road）205号店铺后间楼下的孔学慈起床，唤醒了睡在前店房间地板上的学徒，并告知后者他将外出片刻去处理一件重要事务，如果再有日本军官前来询问

pages.en:
1/9heet 6.

proprietor, the apprentice was to inform them that
he had left for his country place. The apprentice
obeyed his orders and locked the front shop door after
Kong Hsueh Ts left the shop. Half an hour later (prior
to daybreak), the apprentice was again awakened by a
knock at the front shop door. Enquired as to who it
was, the intruder did not give his name but told the
apprentice to immediately open the door. Thinking that
he was his employer, who had probably returned to the
shop, the apprentice subsequently turned on the light
and unlocked the door but was amazed when he saw the
same Japanese Officer, who had visited the shop on 28-
12-37, appear at the door-way. The latter walked in-
side the shop room and demanded to know the whereabouts
of the proprietor. When the apprentice informed him
that the proprietor did not return to the shop on the
previous night, the Japanese did not believe him and
walked inside the adjoining back room. Having failed to
find any occupant on the ground floor, the officer did
not proceed upstairs but returned to the shop room and
said to the apprentice in Wenchang dialect, "The proprietor
was not in the shop yesterday nor is he in the shop today.
I will come back to the shop tomorrow (30-12-37) at 3p.m.
to see and if he is not here again, you had better be
pages.zh:
1/9heet 6.

店主，学徒应告知他们店主已回乡下去了。学徒遵从其命令，在孔学慈（Kong Hsueh Ts，音译）离开店铺后锁上了前店门。半小时后（天亮前），学徒再次被前店门的敲门声惊醒。询问来者何人，闯入者未报姓名，而是命令学徒立即开门。学徒以为是其雇主可能返回店里，便随后打开电灯并解锁房门，但惊讶地发现出现在门口的竟是12月28日（原文如此，应为22日之误或笔误，依上下文逻辑推断）曾来过店里的那名日本军官。后者走进店内房间，要求知道店主下落。当学徒告知他店主前一晚未回店时，日本人不相信他的话，走进了相邻的后间房间。因在一楼未找到任何人，该军官未上楼，而是返回店内房间，用文昌方言对学徒说：“店主昨天不在店里，今天也不在店里。我明天（12月30日）下午3点会再来店里看看，如果他还不在此，你最好小心点。”

pages.en:
1/Sheet 7.

careful". The officer having finished his conversation
instructed the apprentice to follow him outside the shop,
which the latter did. On coming out from the shop, the
apprentice alleged that he again saw the same motor car
being parked in the same position as on the previous
occasion. One of the occupants in the car, also a
Japanese Military Officer, subsequently descended from
the vehicle and directed the first mentioned officer
and the apprentice to go into the shop room again. The
second officer held in his hand a folded envelope, on
which the apprentice saw three Chinese characters "司令部"
meaning "Military Headquarters". He was unable to read
all the characters on the envelope as they were partly
covered by the hand of the said officer. As soon as
the officer intended to show the envelope to the appren-
tice, a third Japanese officer stepped into the shop and
stopped him, saying a few words to him (2nd officer) in
Japanese, which (apprentice) was unable to understand.
Following their conversation, the third officer took
possession of the letter and together with the other two
Japanese Officers left the shop and ascended the waiting
car, in which the apprentice saw three other Japanese
Officers, bringing a total of six in number, seated to-
gether. The car was being driven away in an Eastern dir-
ection along Beiping Road. The second visit lasted
about five minutes.
pages.zh:
1/Sheet 7.

小心”。该军官结束谈话后，指令学徒跟随他到店外，学徒照做了。走出店铺后，学徒称他再次看到同一辆汽车停在与此前相同的位置。车内的一名乘客（也是一名日本军官）随后下车，指挥前述第一名军官和学徒再次进入店内房间。第二名军官手中拿着一个折叠的信封，学徒看到上面有三个汉字“司令部”，意为“Military Headquarters”（军事总部）。由于信封部分被该军官的手遮挡，学徒无法看清信封上的所有文字。正当该军官打算向学徒展示信封时，第三名日本军官走进店里并阻止了他，用日语对他（第二名军官）说了几句话，学徒听不懂这些话。交谈之后，第三名军官拿走了信件，并与另外两名日本军官一起离开店铺，登上等候的汽车，学徒看到车内还坐着其他三名日本军官，共计六人。汽车沿北平路（Beiping Road）向东驶离。第二次来访持续了约五分钟。

pages.en:
1/sheet 8.

No disturbance created or search conducted on the
whole premises by any member of the Japanese party who
visited the shop, nor did any of them remove any
movable property from the shop.

Thorough enquiries were made by detectives among
the inmates on the above premises and various assistants
in nearby shops but no one could corroborate the state-
ment made by the young apprentice as regards any visits
of the Japanese Military Officers to above shop, nor
did any one notice a Japanese Military car on which
a Japanese flag was flying being parked outside the
premises.

C.P.C.'s 3367, and 2763 on Traffic Post at the
junction of Chengtu Road and Weihaiwei Road on First
day (4p.m. to 8p.m.) and Second Day (12noon to 4p.m.) du<
on 22-12-37 respectively were questioned but denied any
knowledge of the alleged visits of any Japanese Military
Officers to the above shop during their tour of duty.
They further stated that they did not notice any presence
of a Japanese Military Car at the corner of Chengtu and
Weihaiwei Roads between the above mentioned times. Same
could not have escaped their notice for their post is
only a short distance from the front entrance of the shop.

A female named Wu Tsang ~s ( 吴张氏 ), who complies
pages.zh:
1/sheet 8.

来访的日本人员中，没有任何人在整个 premises（处所/房产）内制造骚乱或进行搜查，也没有任何人从店里拿走任何动产。

侦探对上述处所的住户以及附近店铺的各种助手进行了彻底询问，但无人能佐证年轻学徒关于日本军官来访上述店铺的陈述，也无人注意到有一辆悬挂日本旗帜的日本军车停在该处所外。

分别于1937年12月22日第一天（下午4时至8时）和第二天（中午12时至下午4时）在成都路与威海卫路交界处交通岗执勤的中国警务员（C.P.C.）编号3367和2763接受了问询，但均否认在值班期间知晓有任何日本军官来访上述店铺。他们进一步表示，在上述时间段内，未注意到成都路与威海卫路拐角处有任何日本军车出现。鉴于他们的岗位距离店铺正门仅很短距离，若有车辆出现不可能逃过他们的注意。

一名名为吴张氏（Wu Tsang ~s）的女性，符合

pages.en:
1/Sheet 9.

the front upstairs room on the same premises, verified
that she was awakened by knocks at the front shop door
at about 5a.m. on 23-12-37 but she failed to get up to
see who it was.

The 1st described (informant) was questioned by
detectives and stated that he used to have some business
transactions with Japanese civilian customers for the
sale of motor car parts prior to the Shanghai Hostilities
but had very little dealings with them since. He could
not give any reason as to why the Japanese Military
Officers should visit the shop. The early and sudden
departure of his partner Keng Hsieh Ts from the shop on
the morning of 23-12-37 points out to the suspicion of
his connection with the Japanese visits.

The 1st described was further questioned but stated
that he did not know the present whereabouts of his
partner, who is strongly suspected of being sought for
by the Japanese Authorities for reasons unknown. He
(1st described) has been instructed to notify the police
as soon as his partner puts in an appearance.

The reason of why he delayed this report was that
he did not think the Japanese were looking for him.

Meanwhile, two C.P.C.s are being posted outside the
Changta Rubber Tyre Shop at 365 Weihaiwei Road and two
outside the 1st described's shop at 365 Weihaiwei Road

侦探讯问了上述第一人（举报人），他陈述在上海战事之前，他曾与一些日本平民客户有过汽车零部件销售的商业往来，但此后与他们很少有交易。他无法解释日本军官为何要来访店铺。其合伙人孔学慈（Keng Hsieh Ts，音译）于1937年12月23日清晨突然离开店铺，这一情况使人怀疑他与日本人的来访有关联。

上述第一人进一步接受讯问时表示，他不知道其合伙人的当前下落，该合伙人被强烈怀疑因不明原因正被日本当局搜寻。他（上述第一人）已接到指示，一旦其合伙人露面，立即通知警方。

他延迟报告的原因是，他认为日本人不是在找他。

与此同时，两名中国警务员（C.P.C.s）被部署在威海卫路365号昌泰橡胶轮胎店（Changta Rubber Tyre Shop）外，另有两名部署在上述第一人位于威海卫路365号的店铺外

Ch.Rd.?tn.            23-12-37                 XXXXXXXX       "

Tsang Pao Hwo (張寶華), age 17 years, native of Chinkiang,
"/apprentice Chengtu Rubber Tyre Co., 203 Weihaiwei Road.
    I am employed as an apprentice in the Chengtu Rubber Tyre
shop at 203 Weihaiwei Road, residing at the same address.
    At about 4p.m. 22-12-37, a certain male wearing Japanese
Khaki uniform, speaking fluent Shantung dialect entered the shop.
I thought he wanted to purchase some motor car parts and asked
him as to what he wanted. He replied in the negative but
demanded to see the proprietor of the shop. I then asked him
which proprietor he wanted to see and the proprietor's name,
he did not answer. I further told him that the proprietor had
gone out and asked him about the purpose of his visit. He failed
to answer me and walked out of the shop. I followed him and
saw him board a black "Chevrolet" sedan, parked outside the
front door of the shop. The vehicle in question was covered
with mud-stains and with exception of the front window screen
the remaining glass screens were lowered with blinds. A
Japanese flag was tied to the front mud-guard of the motor
but I did not notice the licence number plate. When the
officer opened the side door of the car and boarded same,
was able to see 5 other Japanese Military Officers sitting
together in the car. I further saw a black oblong plate with
Japanese Characters and similar to Chinese "一千" in white
meaning "Thousand and Nine", affixed to the back mud-guard
when the car was driven away in a Eastern Direction along
Weihaiwei Road.
    At about 8.30p.m. same date a sub-tenant in the house No.
pages.zh:
张宝华（Tsang Pao Hwo）
镇江                                      xx -D.?.I. T'ai Liu
                                               已翻译
成都路.?tn.            1937年12月23日                 XXXXXXXX       "

张宝华（Tsang Pao Hwo），17岁，镇江籍，
“成都橡胶轮胎公司学徒，威海卫路203号。
    我受雇为威海卫路203号成都橡胶轮胎店的学徒，居住在同一地址。
    1937年12月22日下午4时许，一名身穿日本卡其色制服、能说流利山东话的男子进入店内。我以为他想购买一些汽车零部件，便问他想要什么。他予以否认，但要求见店主。于是我问他想见哪位店主以及店主的姓名，他没有回答。我进一步告诉他店主外出了，并询问他来访的目的。他没有回答我，便走出了店铺。我跟随他出去，看到他登上了一辆停在店门前的黑色“雪佛兰”轿车。该车车身沾满泥渍，除前挡风玻璃外，其余玻璃窗均放下了遮阳帘。车头挡泥板上系着一面日本旗，但我未注意到车牌号码。当该军官打开车门上车时，我看到车内还坐着其他五名日本军官。我还看到车尾挡泥板上贴着一块黑色的长方形牌子，上面有日文字符，类似于中文的“一千”，白色字样，意为“一千零九”（Thousand and Nine，原文如此，可能指部队番号或标识），当汽车沿威海卫路向东驶离时我看到了这一点。
    同日晚上约8时30分，房屋内的转租人苏景藏（Su Jing Tsang，音译）回家，我告诉了他。同日晚上约7时

pages.en:
-2-
Su Jing Tsang returned home and I told him. At about 7.00p.m.
same evening my employer Kong Hsueh Ta came back to the shop
and I also told him the above. He asked me the purpose of
the Japanese visit. I told him that I did not know. He said
that he had nothing to do with Japanese. At about 7.30p.m.
same date I went to the shop of my another employer Tsang Kyung
Tsung at 345 Weihaiwei Road and also told him of the occurrence.
I subsequently went to sleep on the floor of the shop room at
203 Weihaiwei Road. At about 4a.m. on 23-12-37, my employer
Kong woke me up and told me that he would go out for a short
while. He further told me that if any Japanese visited the
shop and asked for him, I could tell the Japanese that he
had gone to country. Half an hour after the departure of
my employer, I heard a knock at the front shop door and asked
him who he was. He told me to open the door. I then switched
on the light and on opening the door I saw the same Japanese
officer, who visited the shop previously, appear at the door-
way. He again asked me where the proprietor of the shop was.
When I told him that he did not return on the previous night,
he did not believe my statement and went inside the adjoining
room. After he failed to find anyone inside, he came out and
said to me, "The proprietor was not in the shop yesterday nor
to be in the shop today? I will come back to the shop tomorrow
at 3.00p.m. (24-12-37) and if he is not here again, you had
better be careful". He further asked me to follow him outside
which I did. On coming out from the shop, I saw the same
pages.zh:
-2-
我的雇主孔学达（Kong Hsueh Ta，音译）回到店里，我也将上述情况告诉了他。他问我日本人来访的目的。我告诉他我不知道。他说他与日本人没有任何关系。同日晚上约7时30分，我去了我的另一位雇主曾庆宗（Tsang Kyung Tsung，音译）位于威海卫路345号的店铺，也将此事告诉了他。随后我在威海卫路203号的店铺房间地板上睡觉。1937年12月23日凌晨4时许，我的雇主孔先生叫醒我，告诉我他要外出片刻。他还告诉我，如果有日本人来店里找他，我可以告诉日本人他回乡下去了。在我雇主离开半小时后，我听到前店门有敲门声，便问他是谁。他让我开门。于是我打开电灯，打开门后，我看到此前曾来过店里的那名日本军官出现在门口。他再次问我店主在哪里。当我告诉他前一晚未回来时，他不相信我的话，走进了相邻的房间。他在里面没找到任何人后，出来说道：“店主昨天不在店里，今天也不在店里？我明天下午3点（12月24日）会再来店里，如果他还不在此，你最好小心点。”他还让我跟随他到外面，我照做了。走出店铺后，我看到同一辆

pages.en:
-3-
motor car being parked outside. Another Japanese Officer
descended from the car and directed the 1st officer to enter
the shop again. In his hand I noticed a folded envelope,
bearing several Chinese Characters " 司令部 ", which mean
"Military Headquarters". When the said officer intended to
show me the envelope, a third Japanese appeared and spoke some
Japanese language to the first two Japanese, after which he
took the envelope away. Three of them left the shop and boarded
the same car in an Eastern Direction along Weihaiwei Road.
When they opened the car door, I saw three more officers in
the same car.
The above is true statement.

〔签名〕                      Signed:- Tsang Pao Hwo.
pages.zh:
-3-
汽车停在外面。另一名日本军官从车上下来，指挥第一名军官再次进入店内。我注意到他手中拿着一个折叠的信封，上面有几个汉字“司令部”，意为“Military Headquarters”（军事总部）。当该军官打算向我展示信封时，第三名日本人出现，并对前两名日本人说了些日语，随后他拿走了信封。三人离开店铺，登上同一辆汽车，沿威海卫路向东驶去。当他们打开车门时，我看到车内还有三名军官。
以上陈述属实。

〔签名〕                      签名:- 张宝华（Tsang Pao Hwo）。

Letter from Cathay Middle School,

To
Police Department,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sirs,
(田 梨)
Mr. Tien Lee, our music instructor, was
carried away by three or four persons, their
nationality unknown, at 4 p.m. on December 16,
1937. We have no news concerning his where-
abouts until we read the Shanghai Evening Post
under the date of January 6 when we learned
that he was being detained by the Japanese
Military Authorities at Hung Dah No. 3 Mill
(According to the newspaper the person detained
was surnamed Tien; reason for this being un-
known). Our premises are situated on an Extra-
Settlement Road and the road is under the juris-
diction of the Shanghai Municipal Council. A
report was made to the Council after the incident
had taken place. As we have information concerning
his whereabouts now we would request you to be
good enough to make inquiries at the Japanese Mili-
tary Headquarters. Should Mr. Tien be found to have
involved in a serious crime, he should be handed
over to a competent Court for trial in accordance
with legal procedure. If there is nothing against
him we would also request you to take up the
matter with the Japanese Authorities with a view
to securing his early release.

Awaiting the pleasure of a reply.

(Chopped): Cathay Middle School.
