December 20, 1937. Morning Translation.

Ta Lei Wen Iao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-

CHINESE TEACHER ARRESTED BY JAPANESE

At 5 p.m. December 18, a Chinese called on Mr. Dien Li ( 田梨 ), a musical instructor of Hwa Hwa Middle School ( 華華中學 ), No. 1341 Yu Yuen Road. After some conversation, Mr. Dien accompanied the caller to the gate of the school where he was seized by four Japanese in plain clothes and taken away in a motor car.
About 45 minutes later, a number of Japanese soldiers arrived at the school in motor cars and searched Mr. Dien's dormitory, but nothing was found. The soldiers then left.
Upon receipt of a report, the Municipal Police sent detectives and policemen to the school at 7 p.m. the same day to make an investigation.
Mr. Dien Li, aged about 20, is a native of Fokien. He secured the position of musical instructor with the Hwa Hwa Middle School about a month ago by replying to an advertisement published by the school in the newspapers.

China Evening News of Dec.19 and other local newspapers :-

ARREST OF A BAMBOO HONG OWNER

On December 17, Cheng Lien-kwun ( 鄭連坤 ), native of Shanghai, owner of a bamboo hong to the west of San Koh Zang ( 三合場 ), Zau Ka Tu ( 曹家渡 ), Western District of Shanghai, was arrested on suspicion by a certain party. A joint request for his release made by the shops in the district has had no result.
Cheng Lien-kwun was formerly a member of the Merchant Volunteer Corps at Zau Ka Tu and is an ardent social worker.

Ta Mei Wen Iao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-

MR. TUNG KANG REQUESTS A CORRECTION

The following letter was recently received by this paper from Mr. Tung Kang ( 董康 ), a lawyer and an ex-Minister of Justice :-
"Recently I learned from newspapers that a provisional government had been established in Peiping and that I had been reported as being one of its promoters.
"I have to inform you that as I am old and am not in good health, I have taken no part in any outside movements. I have always remained indoors and devoted my time to the writing of books. I am a professor of Peiping University. As there is absolutely no truth in the reports concerning me published by the various newspapers, I therefore have to request you to publish this letter in your 'correspondence column'."
pages.zh:
1937年12月20日。晨间翻译。

《大美晚报》晨版及其他本地报纸：-

中国教师被日本人逮捕

12月18日下午5时，一名中国人拜访了位于愚园路1341号华华中学（Hwa Hwa Middle School）的音乐教员田梨（Dien Li）先生。交谈片刻后，田先生陪同来访者走到学校门口，随即被四名便衣日本人抓住，并用汽车带走。
大约45分钟后，多名日本士兵乘汽车抵达学校，搜查了田先生的宿舍，但未发现任何物品。随后士兵离开。
接到报告后，公共租界警察于当晚7时派遣侦探和警员前往学校进行调查。
田梨先生，年约20岁，福建人。他约一个月前通过回应学校在报纸上刊登的广告，获得了华华中学音乐教员的职位。

12月19日《字林西报》（China Evening News，注：此处原文可能指《字林西报》晚刊或类似英文报，但中文语境下常混用，依原文译名处理）及其他本地报纸：-

竹行老板被捕

12月17日，上海西区曹家渡（Zau Ka Tu）三合场（San Koh Zang）以西一家竹行的老板、上海籍人士郑连坤（Cheng Lien-kwun），因涉嫌被某方逮捕。该地区商铺联合请求释放他，但未果。
郑连坤曾是曹家渡商团志愿队成员，也是一位热衷的社会工作者。

《大美晚报》晨版及其他本地报纸：-

董康先生要求更正

本报最近收到律师、前司法总长董康（Tung Kang）先生的来信如下：
“近日我从报纸上获悉，北平已成立临时政府，并有报道说我被列为发起人之一。
“我必须告知各位，因我年事已高且身体欠佳，并未参与任何外部运动。我一直闭门不出，致力于著书立说。我是北京大学教授。鉴于各报纸刊登的关于我的报道毫无事实依据，因此恳请贵报在‘读者来信’栏目刊登此信。”

pages.en:
December 19, 1937. Morning Translation.

Social Morning Post (社會朝報) :-
TEACHER ARRESTED BY JAPANESE SOLDIERS
At 6 p.m., December 18, four or five fully armed Japanese soldiers, accompanied by three or four plainclothes policemen went to the Hwa Hwa Middle School (華華中學), Yu Yuen Road, to conduct a search of the school teachers' quarters, which lasted over 20 minutes, after which they arrested a musical instructor named Dian (田).
It is reported that this instructor came to Shanghai less than three months ago.

Ta Kei An Pao Morning Edition :-
THE REFUGEE ZONE IN NANTAO
Father Jacquinot issued the following public statement yesterday afternoon :-
"An agreement has been reached between the Japanese authorities and myself whereby the Refugee Zone in Nantao will continue to be controlled by the International Relief Committee. The Japanese authorities will co-operate with the Committee in policing the zone and will assist the Committee in administrative affairs."
One or two Japanese sentries remained on duty at road intersections along Boulevard des Deux Republiques and Fang Pang Road (方浜路) yesterday. Refugees in the zone are allowed to come out to buy rice or to get water.

Hwa Kei An Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-
JAPANESE TAKE OVER POLICE RIGHTS
The following information was obtained yesterday after the Japanese took over police rights in the Refugee Zone :-
(1) The refugees have been notified to remain calm and not to leave with any articles of property.
(2) The Refugee Zone Control Office established by the French authorities has been abolished and M. "Long-ba-lo" (龍伯祿), the Chief, has returned to the French Police Force.

Hwa Kei An Pao Morning Edition :-
THE DAITAO CITY GOVERNMENT
After the inauguration of the so-called Daitao City Government of Shanghai at Pootung, Chu Yu-tsang (朱玉堂) was appointed as Chief of the Police Bureau, Chen Fro-en (陳佛恩) as Chief of the Finance Bureau, Koh Ts-ki-ng (高志清) as Chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs and Chang Su-sung (張素松) as Chief of the Communications Bureau. Zing Chien (秦錢) has now been appointed Secretary and Manager of the Daitao City Government Bank.

《社会朝报》：-
教师被日本士兵逮捕
12月18日下午6时，四五名全副武装的日本士兵，在三四名便衣警察的陪同下，前往愚园路华华中学（Hwa Hwa Middle School），对学校教师宿舍进行了搜查，历时20多分钟，随后逮捕了一名姓田（Dian）的音乐教员。
据报道，该教员来上海不到三个月。

《华克安报》（Hwa Kei An Pao，音译）晨版：-
南市难民区
饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）昨日下午发表以下公开声明：
“日本当局与我已达成协议，南市难民区将继续由国际救济委员会管理。日本当局将在维持该区治安方面与委员会合作，并在行政事务上协助委员会。”
昨日，一两名日本哨兵仍在法大马路（Boulevard des Deux Republiques）和方浜路（Fang Pang Road）沿线的路口执勤。难民区的难民被允许外出购买大米或取水。

《华克安报》晨版及其他本地报纸：-
日本人接管警察权
以下是日本人在难民区接管警察权后于昨日获得的信息：
(1) 已通知难民保持冷静，不得携带任何财产离开。
(2) 法国当局建立的难民区管理处已被撤销，处长龙伯祿（M. "Long-ba-lo"，音译）已返回法国警察部队。

《华克安报》晨版：-
大道市政府
在上海所谓的“大道市政府”于浦东成立后，朱玉堂（Chu Yu-tsang）被任命为警察局局长，陈佛恩（Chen Fro-en）被任命为财政局局长，高志清（Koh Ts-ki-ng，音译）被任命为社会局局长，张素松（Chang Su-sung）被任命为交通局局长。秦钱（Zing Chien，音译）现被任命为大道市政府银行秘书兼经理。

ARREST OF MALE CHINESE BY JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.

On the morning of 22/12/37 Supt. Crouch, D.D.O."B" instructed that certain enquiries be made to ascertain if one named Tseng Lien Kwen (鄭連坤) owner of the Tseng Deung Woo Bamboo Hong, 1334, Jessfield Road, also Chief of the Zau Ka Doo Fire Brigade, had been arrested by the Japanese Military Police.

Enquiries by D.I.Teen, D.S.I. Wu Chen Mo and J.D.C. Sugimoto ascertained that Tseng Lien Kwen, age 33, native of Shanghai, resides at 1334, Jessfield Road, which is a bamboo hong, the house itself being situated in the yard about twenty yards from the roadway, inmates questioned stated that they pay S.M.C. taxes, but could not produce any tax receipt, **〔此处转录不清：左侧有一枚圆形印章及部分手写批注，正文此处有涂抹痕迹〕** the wife being away at the time, however, it is reasonable to believe that they do pay S.M.C. taxes as the parents of the arrested man reside at 1334, Jessfield Road (a short distance away) and they produced S.M.C. tax receipt for December quarter.

Enquiries at the Japanese Military Police Headquarters King Dah Mill, Jessfield Road, ascertained that Tseng Lien Kwen was detained by them, the officer i/c stating that this man had given them information from time to time and whilst making investigations they had learnt that he was connected with certain anti-Japanese movements, so when he attended their headquarters on Friday night/evg he was detained by them.

经探员Teen、副督察长吴振模（Wu Chen Mo）及日籍侦探吉本（J.D.C. Sugimoto）查询，查明郑连坤，33岁，上海人，居住在极司菲尔路1341号，这是一处竹行，房屋本身位于距马路约二十码的院内，被询问的住户称他们缴纳工部局捐税，但无法出示任何纳税收据，**〔此处转录不清：左侧有一枚圆形印章及部分手写批注，正文此处有涂抹痕迹〕** 当时其妻子不在家，然而，有理由相信他们确实缴纳了工部局捐税，因为被捕者的父母居住在极司菲尔路1334号（不远处），并出示了第四季度工部局捐税收据。

在极司菲尔路宏达纱厂（King Dah Mill）的日本宪兵司令部进行的查询查明，郑连坤被他们拘留，负责军官称此人不时向他们提供情报，而在调查过程中，他们得知他与某些反日运动有关联，因此当他于周五晚上/傍晚前往他们的司令部时，便被他们拘留。

Date December 21 1937.
Subject. Japanese Military Police functioning in the Western District.
Made by... D.S.I. Shih Sau-chien. Forwarded by C. Crawford **〔签名〕**

In the morning of December 16, members of the
Japanese Military Police effected the arrest of one MR.
Tseng Lien Kwen (郑连根), proprietor of the Tseng Zung Woo Bamboo
Hong at No.1334 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., outside the above
mentioned address. He was subsequently taken to the
Japanese Military Headquarters stationed at No.138,
Jessfield Road, and is at present detained there.

Enquiries tend to show that the cause of the
arrest was that Tseng Lien Kwen refused an invitation
from the Japanese Authorities to attend a meeting of
Chinese business men in the Western District, held on
December 11 in the Kung Dah No.3 Cotton Mill, 60
Singapore Road, O.O.L. The object of holding the meeting,
which was followed by the taking of a party photo, was
to prompt the Chinese business men in the Western District
to form a "Zau Ka Doo Merchant Circle's Union" with a
view to cooperating with the Japanese Authorities.

The refusal to attend the above mentioned meeting
apparently incurred the anger of the Japanese Authorities
and resulted in his arrest.

Mr. Tseng was formerly a captain attached to the
2nd Company of the Fah Wah Village Merchant Volunteer Corps
and captain of the Zau Ka Doo Fire Brigade and also an
executive member of the 3rd Branch of the 1st Special
District Citizens' Federation.

12月16日上午，日本宪兵成员
逮捕了曾增茂竹行（Tseng Zung Woo Bamboo Hong）老板
郑连根（Tseng Lien Kwen，注：此处中文名与上文郑连坤略有差异，依原文拼音及汉字译出）先生，
地址为极司菲尔路1334号，越界筑路区，在上述地址之外。
他随后被带至驻扎在
极司菲尔路138号的日本军方总部，
目前被拘禁在那里。

调查倾向于表明，
逮捕的原因是由于郑连坤拒绝了
日本当局邀请他参加12月11日
在新加坡路60号宏达第三棉纺厂（越界筑路区）举行的
西区中国商人会议。举行该会议的目的，
随后还拍摄了集体照，是为了促使
西区中国商人组建“曹家渡商界联合会”，
以便与日本当局合作。

拒绝参加上述会议
显然激怒了日本当局，
导致了他的被捕。

郑先生曾任法华镇商团志愿队
第二连连长，曹家渡消防队队长，
也是第一特区市民联合会第三分会的执行委员。

“MOTION PICTURE COMPANY PROPRIETOR NIEN TSUNG DANG
TRAFFICKS IN OPIUM”
8220/7
“His Employee, Woo Sih-Yung, Arrested and Sentenced 24 12 3
to Eight Months' Imprisonment”

The “News Digest” of December 21 published
the following article under the above headings:-

Woo Sih-yung (吳錫榮), age 37, native
of Nanziang, living at Rue Eugene Bard, French
Concession, was arrested by Chinese detective sergeant
Yih Nyoh-san (葉玉山) of Sinza Police Station at
11.45 p.m. December 19 at the corner of Avenue Road
and Yu Ya Ching Road and was found in possession of
two ounces of opium. When interrogated at Police
Station, Woo stated that the opium belonged to Wang
Yeu-kong (王又康) and Tsu Ah-kao (朱阿高), employees
of Nien Tsung-dang (嚴春堂), proprietor of a certain
motion picture company, and that he was undertaking
the delivery of the opium. Acting on this information,
Detective Sergeant Yih visited and searched Room 202
of the Oriental Hotel (東方旅館) which had been booked
by Nien Tsung-dang, but nothing was found.

The prisoner Woo Sih-yung was arraigned
before the Shanghai First Special District Court
yesterday when he was sentenced to eight months'
imprisonment.

Eastern Times :-

It was reported in yesterday's papers
that Woo Sih-yung had implicated Nien Tsung-dang after
he had been arrested by the Police for being in
possession of opium. According to a statement by Nien,
he has been devoting himself to the film industry during
the past few years and the Police had found nothing
when making their search at his room. The statement
made by Woo Sih-yung is false.

“电影公司老板严春堂
贩卖鸦片”
8220/7
“其雇员吴锡荣被捕并被判
八个月监禁”

12月21日的《新闻摘要》在上述标题下刊登了以下文章：

吴锡荣，37岁，南翔人，居住在法租界欧仁·巴尔路（Rue Eugene Bard），于12月19日晚11时45分在新闸捕房华籍侦探长叶玉山于爱文义路（Avenue Road）与虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）转角处将其逮捕，并查获其持有鸦片两盎司。在捕房受审时，吴锡荣称鸦片属于某电影公司老板严春堂的雇员王又康和朱阿高，而他负责运送该批鸦片。根据这一情报，侦探长叶前往并搜查了由严春堂预订的东方旅馆202室，但未发现任何物品。

犯人吴锡荣昨日在上海第一特区地方法院受审，被判处八个月监禁。

《字林西报》：

据昨日报纸报道，吴锡荣因持有鸦片被警方逮捕后，牵连出严春堂。据严氏声明，他在过去几年一直致力于电影业，警方在搜查其房间时未发现任何物品。吴锡荣所作的陈述是虚假的。

HOUSES ON OUTSIDE
ROADS SEARCHED

Japanese Arrest Family Of
Cinema Magnate

A growing sense of uneasiness
prevailed in the western extra-Settle-
ment districts yesterday, as armed
Japanese continued their search of
Chinese houses off such streets as
Yu Yuen Road and Great Western
Road, it was reported in the Chinese
circles.
So far as was known, four Chinese
had been apprehended and detained
by the Japanese. Whether there
were other similar cases could not be
ascertained yesterday.
The four Chinese, according to
these circles, were taken away by
armed Japanese detectives from No.
55 Yenchiachih, off Yu Yuen Road
from the family of Yen Chun-tang
who is engaged in the production of
Chinese motion pictures.
Both Mr. Yen and his wife together
with two other members of the family
still remained in Japanese hands yes-
terday. Two servants, carried away
by the Japanese at the same time,
were later released, it was reported.
The incident took place on Thurs-
day morning, when a group of armed
Japanese arrived in a motor car and
entered Mr. Yen's house. The reason
for the Japanese action was not
known, but it was held possible in
Chinese circles that Mr. Yen's busi-
ness might have incurred the dis-
pleasure of the Japanese.
During the past two days, armed
Japanese in uniform continued to
make house to house searches off Yu
Yuen Road and Great Western Road,
the area off the two extra-Settlement
roads being formerly under the Chi-
nese administration.
The pretext of the Japanese was
to discover arms and ammunition
which might have been left behind by
Chinese troops, although the area is
within the British defence sector,
Chinese circles reported yesterday.

（批：S.3 / OK 13/6）
pages.zh:
外围道路
房屋遭搜查

日本人逮捕
电影大亨家属

据华人圈子报道，昨天，随着武装日本人继续在愚园路和大西路等街道以外的中国民居进行搜查，越界筑路区西部地区的紧张不安感日益加剧。
据所知，已有四名中国人被日本人 apprehended（逮捕）并拘留。昨天无法查明是否还有其他类似案件。
据这些圈子称，这四名中国人是被武装日本侦探从愚园路外的严家宅55号带走的，该处住户为从事中国电影制作的严春堂家族。
据报道，严先生及其妻子以及另外两名家庭成员昨天仍掌握在日本人手中。同时被日本人带走的两名仆人后来获释。
事件发生在周四上午，当时一群武装日本人乘坐汽车抵达并进入严先生家中。日本人采取行动的原因不详，但华人圈子认为，严先生的生意可能引起了日本人的不满。
在过去两天里，身着制服的武装日本人继续在愚园路和大西路以外地区进行挨户搜查，这两条越界筑路以外的区域以前由中国当局管辖。
据华人圈子昨天报道，日本人的借口是搜寻中国军队可能遗留的武器弹药，尽管该区域位于英国防区内。

（批：S.3 / OK 13/6）

&
Subject Japanese Military/Consular Police functioning in the Western District.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford i. s

（左侧手写批注：file / DSR / 3/2）

At about 6 a.m. December 9, a party of some twenty Japanese, comprising of the Japanese Military and Consular Police, visited house No.55 Nyien Ka Zah off Tifeng Road, O.O.L., the home of one Nyien Tsung-dong (嚴春堂 ), General Manager of the Nyi Hwa Motion Picture Company, 1109 Connaught Road, and enquired the whereabouts of one Chen Pah Liang (陳伯良), a friend of his, and formerly a responsible member of the Shanghai Municipality Western District Foreign Cotton Mill Workers' Foh Li Society. (vide Special Branch Report dated 14.5.37). Because he was unable to tell the party as to the whereabouts of Chen Pah Liang, the Japanese took into custody the six persons then in the house (Nyien himself, his wife and servants) and detained them in the Temporary Headquarters of the Japanese Military Police stationed in the Kung Dah Cotton Mill Silk Spinning Department, 138 Jessfield Road, O.O.L. A thorough search was conducted on the premises but it was not known whether anything of an incriminating nature was found. The arrested persons were released in the afternoon of the same day with the exception of Nyien Tsung-dong, who is still now being detained.

（左侧印章：RECEIVED / 10 DEC 1937 / SPECIAL BR.）

It is reported that following the arrest of the above persons, the Japanese continued their search from house to house in that locality. Several complaints have been heard of money disappearing while these searches were going on.

As a result of the large scale search conducted by the Japanese Military Police, the residents in the above described locality are very uneasy, and a number have begun to remove into the Settlement and French Concession.

（左侧手写批注：Copy to / D.O.B. / Jdh. / 10/12）

（左侧手写批注：file / DSR / 3/2）

12月9日上午6时许，一支约二十人的队伍，由日本军方和领事警察组成，前往越界筑路区提封路外的严家宅55号，即康纳脱路1109号新华影片公司总经理严春堂（Nyien Tsung-dong）的住所，询问其朋友陈伯良的下落，陈伯良曾是上海市公用局西区外商棉纺工人福利会的负责人。（见1937年5月14日特科报告）。由于他无法告知该队伍陈伯良的下落，日本人将当时在屋内的六人（严本人、其妻子及仆人）扣押，并拘留在位于越界筑路区极司菲尔路138号公大棉纺厂缫丝部的日本宪兵临时总部。对该处所进行了彻底搜查，但是否发现了任何具有定罪性质的物品尚不清楚。除严春堂目前仍被拘留外，被捕人员于当日下午获释。

（左侧印章：RECEIVED / 10 DEC 1937 / SPECIAL BR.）

据报道，在逮捕上述人员后，日本人继续在该地区进行挨户搜查。在这些搜查过程中，听到多起钱财失踪的投诉。

由于日本宪兵的大规模搜查，上述地区的居民非常不安，许多人已开始搬入租界和法租界。

Director of the Hwa Ching Tobacco Co., Ningpo Road, and
residing at House 24, Lane 395, Yu Yuen Road, came to

who ascertained that members of the Japanese Military &

vicinity, stating that the person referred to had been
taken to their Headquarters at the Kung Dah Hill,
Jessfield Road.

The Japanese authorities had gone to 41, Nyien Ka Zah

December 11, 1937. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Iso Morning Edition :-

"JAPANESE SEARCH HOUSES IN WESTERN DISTRICT : S.M.C. HAS
NO INTENTION TO INTERFERE"

On the morning of December 9, Japanese soldiers
searched the home of Mr. Nyi Tsung-dsung ( 倪純 ) and
four other houses at Nyi Ka Zah ( 倪家宅 ), Jessfield Road
in the Western District. Five of the six persons arrested
were released the same night, but up to a late hour last
night no information could be secured as to whether or
not Nyi Tsung-dsung had been released.
There are many rumours about the cause of Nyi
Tsung-dsung's arrest. According to information secured
by this paper, a report had been made to the effect that
Nyi was giving shelter to a man named Chen ( 陳 ), formerly
a leader of snipers, and that ammunition was being
kept in his home. However, nothing was found by the
Japanese soldiers in Nyi's house. The report that Nyi's
arrest was due to the production of certain films by his
concern is untrue.
It is learned that Nyi Tsung-dsung is being
detained at the Japanese Military Headquarters at Wu Koh
Zang ( 五角場 ), Zau Ka Tu ( 曹家渡 ). The Japanese
authorities are still investigating the affair.
As the arrest took place in the extra-Settlement
roads area, many rumours are rife in that district. As
a result, many residents have removed.
The public are paying close attention to the
question of judicial rights of the S.M.C. on the extra-
Settlement roads. A reporter of the "China Press" the
other day called on a certain responsible official of the
S.M.C. and the latter made the following statement :-
"The S.M.C. is not exercising judicial rights on extra-
Settlement roads as these judicial rights have always been
in the hands of the Shanghai City Government. As the
Japanese army now occupies Shanghai, it may demand the
exercise of all rights in the extra-Settlement roads area.
There is no legal basis for the S.M.C. to interfere as
the district lies in Chinese territory".
Questioned by the same reporter as to why the
S.M.C. had formerly compelled residents of Yu Koh Tsung
( 俞家弄 ), Yu Yuen Road, in the outside roads area, to
pay the Municipal Rate, the responsible official said :-
"Yu Koh Tsung lies in the outside roads area, but the
residents enjoyed public facilities such as the sewerage etc.
provided by the Settlement. Furthermore, the road in
question was constructed by the Settlement. The S.M.C.
had spent a huge sum of money on all utilities and it had
to collect the Municipal Rate from the residents enjoying
these facilities. However, this question is in no way
connected with the question of judicial rights. At
present, the district is still being patrolled by policemen
of the S.M.C. Should Japanese soldiers pass through
these roads and take action in regard to the houses on
the roadside, the Council will not oppose their action;
but if the Japanese military send men to patrol the roads,
the Council will probably lodge a protest".
As to the searches now being made by Japanese
soldiers of houses along Great Western Road, Tifeng Road
and vicinity, it is learned that the Japanese authorities
had given advance notice of their intention to the British
military authorities.

1937年12月11日。晨译。

《大美晚报》晨刊：-

“日军在西区搜查住宅：工部局无意干涉”

12月9日上午，日本士兵在西区极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）倪家宅（Nyi Ka Zah）搜查了倪纯（Nyi Tsung-dsung）先生的住所及其他四所房屋。被捕的六人中有五人于当晚获释，但截至昨晚深夜，仍无法获悉倪纯是否已获释。

关于倪纯被捕的原因谣言纷起。据本报获得的消息，有人举报称倪纯庇护一名姓陈（Chen）的男子，此人曾是狙击手头目，且其家中藏有弹药。然而，日本士兵在倪纯家中并未搜出任何物品。有关倪纯被捕是因其公司制作某些电影的说法不实。

据悉，倪纯正被拘押在曹家渡（Zau Ka Tu）五角场（Wu Koh Zang）的日本军事总部。日本当局仍在调查此事。

由于逮捕发生在越界筑路区域，该地区谣言四起。结果，许多居民已搬离。

公众正密切关注工部局在越界筑路区域的司法权问题。日前，《字林西报》（China Press）的一名记者拜访了工部局某位负责官员，后者发表如下声明：-

“工部局未在越界筑路区域行使司法权，因为这些司法权一直掌握在上海市政府手中。鉴于日军目前占领上海，其可能要求在越界筑路区域行使所有权利。由于该区域位于中国领土，工部局进行干涉没有法律依据。”

当同一名记者问及为何工部局此前曾强迫越界筑路区域的愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）俞家弄（Yu Koh Tsung）居民缴纳市政捐时，该负责官员表示：-

“俞家弄位于越界筑路区域，但居民享受了由租界提供的下水道等公共设施。此外，相关道路由租界修建。工部局在所有公用设施上花费了巨额资金，因此必须向享受这些设施的居民征收市政捐。然而，此问题与司法权问题毫无关联。目前，该区域仍由工部局巡捕巡逻。如果日本士兵经过这些道路并对路边房屋采取行动，工部局将不反对其行动；但如果日本军方派人巡逻道路，工部局可能会提出抗议。”

至于日本士兵目前对大西路（Great Western Road）、迪丰路（Tifeng Road）及附近房屋进行的搜查，据悉日本当局已事先将其意图通知英国军事当局。

1.

被日本宪兵逮捕的中国人。

1937年12月5日下午2时，极司菲尔路1013号（华门牌）一家书店的老板韩近庸（Han Kyung Young）来到警局报告称，其一名名叫朱保旺（Tsu Pao Kwei）的助手，21岁，南京人，于1937年12月5日上午11时许在其店内被日本宪兵成员逮捕，并被带至极司菲尔路公大纱厂（Kung Dah Mill），即日本警察总部。

因店主不在，他们带走了上述店伙计，但由于他们无法确定此人就是喊出侮辱性言语的人，被捕者于1937年12月5日晚上11时30分获释。

pages.en:
December 7, 1937.
Morning Translation

Ta Mei ..an Pao Morning Edition :-

THE ARREST OF CHINESE BY JAPANESE AUTHORITIES

Four Chinese were arrested by the Japanese authorities at the Great Eastern Hotel, Nanking Road, yesterday morning but were released an hour later. Whether the Japanese made the arrest out of misunderstanding or with the object of testing the Shanghai Municipal Council or creating a precedent in the International Settlement is not known. After receiving a report from the Commissioner of Police, the S.M.C. is paying great attention to the affair and has submitted a protest to Mr. Sell, the Senior Consul.

According to another report, the S.M.C. held an informal meeting at 4.30 p.m. yesterday to discuss the affair. A responsible official of the Council stated that there was no doubt that the Council would lodge a protest with the Japanese authorities, but he held the view that a protest unaccompanied by action would have little effect.

The S.M.C. will hold a formal meeting today to discuss the measures to be taken. At the same time, Major Gerrard, the Commissioner of Police, will report on the Police investigations to the Consular Body.

Arrest Described

According to information secured by our reporter, two Japanese military trucks, carrying 12 Japanese, some of whom were fully armed gendarmes and the others armed plainclothes men, arrived at the Wing On Company on Nanking Road at about 6.30 a.m. yesterday. The Japanese entered the Great Eastern Hotel, which is attached to the Wing On Company, by the entrance on Kin Wo Ka (英華街) and proceeded to the 3rd floor with pistols in hand. Upon reaching the 3rd floor, the Japanese searched Rooms 310 and 309. Room 310 was at that time occupied by two Cantonese silk merchants named Yang Cheng-woo (楊震武), aged about 40, native of Kwangtung, residing in House 3, Lane 23, Avenue du Roi Albert, and another person (name unknown) of about fifty years of age, native of Kwangtung. The room was rented on December 4 in the name of Yang Kee (央記). The occupants of Room 309 were two Shanghai people, one of whom is named Wong Da-koo (王大可), aged between 20 and 30, the other being a modern woman of about the same age. The room was rented in the evening of December 5 in the name of Zung Koong-ching (陳公慶).

These four persons were roused from their sleep and were not allowed to put on their outdoor clothing. After being searched by the armed Japanese gendarmes, they were taken to the Japanese military headquarters in the Hongkew Park.

In view of the absence of police officers at the time the four persons were taken away, an employee of the Great Eastern Hotel informed Louza Police Station by telephone. A foreign detective inspector and many Chinese and foreign detectives were detailed to make enquiries. When they reached the hotel the Japanese had already left. The police then sent an enquiry to the Japanese authorities.
pages.zh:
1937年12月7日。
晨间译稿

《大美晚报》晨刊：-

日军当局逮捕华人

昨日晨，四名华人在南京路大东旅社被日军当局逮捕，但一小时后获释。日军此举是出于误会，还是意在试探上海公共租界工部局，或是在国际租界内制造先例，目前尚不清楚。警务处处长向工部局报告后，工部局对此事高度重视，并向首席领事塞尔先生（Mr. Sell）提出抗议。

据另一则报道，工部局于昨日下午4时30分举行非正式会议讨论此事。工部局一位负责官员表示，毫无疑问，工部局将向日军当局提出抗议，但他认为，若无实际行动配合，抗议效果甚微。

工部局将于今日举行正式会议，讨论拟采取的措施。同时，警务处处长杰拉德少校（Major Gerrard）将向领事团报告警方的调查情况。

逮捕经过描述

据本报记者获得的消息，昨日早晨约6时30分，两辆载有12名日本人的日军卡车抵达南京路永安公司。其中部分为全副武装的宪兵，其余为持枪便衣人员。日本人经由英华街（Kin Wo Ka）入口进入附属于永安公司的大东旅社，手持手枪直奔三楼。到达三楼后，日本人搜查了310号和309号房间。310号房间当时住着两名广东籍丝绸商人，一名叫杨震武（Yang Cheng-woo），约40岁，广东人，居住在阿尔贝王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）23弄3号；另一人（姓名不详），约50岁，亦为广东人。该房间于12月4日以“央记”（Yang Kee）名义租用。309号房间的住客为两名上海人，其中一人名为王大可（Wong Da-koo），年龄在20至30岁之间，另一人为年龄相仿的现代女性。该房间于12月5日晚以陈公庆（Zung Koong-ching）名义租用。

这四人在睡梦中被惊醒，未被允许穿上外衣。经武装日本宪兵搜身后，他们被带往虹口公园内的日军司令部。

鉴于四人被带走时现场无警察在场，大东旅社的一名职员通过电话通知了老闸捕房。一名外籍巡官及多名中外侦探奉命前往调查。当他们抵达旅社时，日本人已经离开。警方随后向日军当局发出查询。

pages.en:
December 7, 1937. Morning Translation.

The four persons were released about an hour later after having been questioned, searched and photographed. The Japanese state that the affair was due to a misunderstanding. A report was later made to the Louza Police Station by the four persons concerned. Investigations are being continued by the Police.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition :-

From enquiries made by our reporter last night, it was learned that the woman who was arrested by the Japanese at the Great Eastern Hotel yesterday morning is a girl guide in the employ of the Chu Loh Girl Guide Service (俱樂嚮導社) located in a certain room of the China Hotel, Kweichow Road.

When interviewed by our reporter, the girl gave the following account of her arrest:-
"At about seven yesterday morning I was still in bed with Yang Tseng-woo (楊增武). I could not leave him that night because he had taken too much wine and had become intoxicated. Moreover, he is my old client. We used to enjoy ourselves together in the Sun Sun Hotel and the Great Eastern Hotel in ordinary times. Yesterday morning, whilst I was sound asleep, I was awakened by sounds of heavy footsteps and noticed several Japanese holding pistols in front of our bed and ordering us to get up. I became frightened and at once roused my companion. We were then forced to get up from the bed and before we could put on our dresses properly we were forced downstairs and told to enter a motor car and we were then driven towards Nanking Road, thence over the Garden Bridge. Shortly afterwards, we passed another bridge. The car was being driven at full speed and we were closely watched by the Japanese with pistols. After about ten minutes, the car stopped. So far as I can recollect, the route we took was from Seward Road to Dixwell Road via Seward Road Bridge. Throughout the whole journey, not a single Chinese was seen on the streets. The car stopped in front of a large foreign style building, at the entrance of which stood two Japanese soldiers on guard. The building was surrounded by walls painted white. On entering, I noticed a tablet on which were printed two characters: 'Vung' (meaning 'soul') and 'Dien' (meaning 'field').

"Presently I realized that two other persons had been arrested by the Japanese. Both of them appeared to be about 40 years of age and one of them wore a moustache. I was taken into a room on the ground floor and was kept away from the others.

"During the interrogation, I was confronted with several Japanese soldiers who all pointed their pistols at my breast. I was first told by a Chinese, who acted as interpreter during the interrogation, that I should tell the truth. I nodded. I then told them that I am a girl guide. Upon learning of this, the Japanese officers appeared to be surprised. Later I was asked my age, nativity and address, after which I was taken out by the Japanese soldiers and led to another room."
pages.zh:
1937年12月7日。晨间译稿。

四人在接受讯问、搜身和拍照后，约一小时后被释放。日方称此事系误会所致。随后，这四名当事人向老闸捕房作了报告。警方正在继续调查。

《华美晚报》晨刊：-

经本报记者昨晚查询，获悉昨日晨在大东旅社被日军逮捕的女子，是受雇于贵州路中国饭店某房间的“俱乐嚮导社”（Chu Loh Girl Guide Service）的一名向导小姐。

在接受本报记者采访时，该女子讲述了其被捕经过：-
“昨天早上七点左右，我还和杨增武（Yang Tseng-woo）躺在床上。那晚因为他饮酒过量醉倒，我无法离开他。而且，他是我的老主顾。平时我们常在孙孙饭店和大东旅社一起玩乐。昨天早上，当我熟睡时，被沉重的脚步声惊醒，发现几名日本人手持手枪站在我们床前，命令我们起床。我吓得立刻叫醒同伴。我们被迫起床，还没来得及穿好衣服，就被强迫下楼，并被命令进入一辆汽车，随后车子朝南京路方向驶去，接着过了外白渡桥。不久，我们又过了另一座桥。汽车全速行驶，日本人手持手枪严密监视着我们。大约十分钟后，车停了下来。据我回忆，我们走的路线是从西华德路（Seward Road）经西华德路桥到狄思威路（Dixwell Road）。在整个行程中，街上未见一个中国人。车停在一栋大型西式建筑前，门口有两名日本士兵站岗。建筑四周环绕着白漆围墙。进入后，我看到一块牌子上印着两个字：‘Vung’（意为‘魂’）和‘Dien’（意为‘场’）。

“不久，我意识到另外两人也被日本人逮捕了。他们看起来都约40岁，其中一人留有胡须。我被带进一楼的一个房间，与其他人隔离开来。

“在审讯期间，几名日本士兵面对着我，全都用手枪指着我的胸口。首先，一名在审讯中担任翻译的中国人告诉我，要我讲实话。我点了点头。于是我告诉他们，我是一名向导小姐。得知此情况后，日本军官似乎很惊讶。后来他们询问了我的年龄、籍贯和住址，之后我被日本士兵带出，领到另一个房间。”

pages.en:
December 7, 1937.                                      Morning Translation

There I remained about two hours when a Japanese
appeared and took my finger prints. This having been
done, I was told to pose before the camera. Afterwards,
I was informed through an interpreter that I had been
arrested by mistake and that they were very sorry for
this mistake. Later, Yang Tseng-woo and I, together
with the other two men, were placed in a military car
and taken back to the Great Eastern Hotel under the
escort of the Japanese. Immediately after we had
alighted from the vehicle in front of the hotel, the
car drove off. We went at once to the Louza Police
Station and made a report of our arrest."
pages.zh:
1937年12月7日。                                      晨间译稿

我在那里待了大约两个小时，一名日本人出现并提取了我的指纹。做完这些后，我被要求对着相机摆姿势拍照。随后，通过翻译告知我，我是被误捕的，他们对这一错误深表歉意。后来，我和杨增武以及另外两名男子被送上一辆军用汽车，在日本人的护送下返回大东旅社。我们在旅社门前下车后，汽车立即驶离。我们随即前往老闸捕房，报告了我们被捕的情况。”

LOUZA
Misc.No.743/57
6th December, 37.

1

Chinese Arrested in Great Eastern Hotel
by Japanese Military Without Reference
to Police

At 7.30 a.m. 6-12-37, a telephone message
was received at Louza Station from the Manager of the
Great Eastern Hotel, a registered British Company,
situated at No.30 Kin We Ka off Nanking Road, to the
effect that three Japanese Soldiers in Uniform had
entered the Hotel and proceeded to Rooms Nos.309 and
310 where they arrested two male Chinese whom they
had taken away in a M/car.

On receipt of the above telephone message
a party of Police consisting of C.D.I. Sharman, C.I.
McFarlane, D.S. Brotherton, D.I. Loh Kang Sung, Inspt.
Liu Ya Xing and C.D.C.37 immediately proceeded to the
Great Eastern Hotel where the following was learned:

（印：B. -7 DEC. 1937）

At about 6.45 a.m. 6-12-37, three Japanese
Soldiers in Uniform and four Japanese wearing foreign
clothing with arm bands around their arms bearing
characters "Shien Ping" (憲兵) meaning Military Police
entered the Great Eastern Hotel by the main entrance
No.30 Kin We Ka off Nanking Road, two or three of whom
were carrying pistols in their hands and one **〔此处转录不清〕**
they entered Rooms Nos.309 and 310.

DC S.B. | S.I.
C.Y.
7/12

1937年12月6日。

1

日军在未通知警方的情况下
在大东旅社逮捕华人

1937年12月6日上午7时30分，老闸捕房接到位于南京路旁英华街30号的大东旅社（一家注册的英国公司）经理的电话留言，称三名身穿制服的日本士兵进入旅社，前往309号和310号房间，逮捕了两名男性华人，并用汽车将他们带走。

收到上述电话留言后，由刑事侦探督察夏曼（Sharman）、刑事侦探麦克法兰（McFarlane）、侦探警长布罗瑟顿（Brotherton）、侦探督察罗康松（Loh Kang Sung）、督察刘亚兴（Liu Ya Xing）及刑事侦探主任37号组成的一队警察立即前往大东旅社，获悉以下情况：

（印章：B. - 1937年12月7日）

1937年12月6日上午约6时45分，三名身穿制服的日本士兵和四名身穿西装、臂戴印有“憲兵”字样臂章的日本人，经由南京路旁英华街30号正门进入大东旅社，其中两三人手中持有手枪，一人 **〔此处转录不清〕** 他们进入了309号和310号房间。

特别分部侦探主任 | 特别分部督察

日本士兵进入时，309号房间的住客为

(1) 陈心庆（Zung Soong Ching），35岁，浙江人，居住于汉口路566号中央玻璃厂，

(2) 姜祝圣（Chiang Tsu Shun），46岁，嘉兴人，任职于江西路103号宗福银行，居住于叶茨路（Yates Road）大忠里104号，

(3) 邵家楣（Tsu Chan Mai），27岁，嘉兴人，任职并居住于新闸路中国银行，

310号房间的住客为

(1) 杨振武（Yang Tsung Voo），28岁，广州人，航运职员，居住于法租界阿尔贝王路230弄3号，

(2) 王星南（Wong Sing Nam），18岁，湖州人，男/女（原文如此），居住于派克路（Park Road）杨桃里19号。

上述日本一行人首先进入310号房间，命令住客起床并随他们离开。

随后，该队日本人前往309号房间并进入，命令躺在床上的三名男性住客起床并随他们离开。接到上述命令后，这三名男子从床上起来并接受搜身，随后对房间进行了搜查。两个房间的住客随后被带

M.I.C. No.743/37.

Sheet No.3.

1 cont'd.

downstairs, but whilst en route Zung Loong Ching,
one of the occupants of Room No.309, fell behind
the party apparently unobserved and returned to his
room.

On arriving outside the Hotel Zung Chei, Lai
together with the male and female occupants of Room
No.310 were ordered into a waiting M/car where they
were guarded by two soldiers whilst another soldier
drove the car.

Chiang Zau Shum was taken to another waiting
M/car and forced into the back seat, followed by two
Japanese in Foreign dress who handcuffed him and then
sat on either side of him.

The driver was dressed in foreign dress and
a Japanese soldier was seated beside the driver.

The M/cars were parked outside the Great
Eastern Hotel facing North and proceeded North to Nanking
Road, turning East to the Bund where they turned North
over the Garden Bridge into Hongkew District.

Not being familiar with roads north of the
Creek, the four above mentioned persons are unable
to state definitely as to what roads they traversed
after crossing the Garden Bridge or to where they
were definitely taken.
pages.zh:
情报编号 743/37。

第3页。

1 续。

下楼，但在途中，309号房间的住客之一陈龙庆（Zung Loong Ching，音译）落在队伍后面，似乎未被察觉，并返回了他的房间。

到达旅社外时，陈其来（Zung Chei, Lai，音译）以及310号房间的男女住客被命令进入一辆等候的汽车，由两名士兵看守，另一名士兵驾驶汽车。

姜祝申（Chiang Zau Shum，音译）被带到另一辆等候的汽车，被迫坐在后座，随后两名穿西装的日本人给他戴上手铐，分别坐在他两侧。

司机身穿西装，一名日本士兵坐在司机旁边。

汽车停在大东旅社外，车头朝北，向北行驶至南京路，向东转弯至外滩，然后向北经过外白渡桥进入虹口区。

由于不熟悉苏州河以北的道路，上述四人无法确切说明过外白渡桥后经过了哪些道路，也无法确定最终被带往何处。

Sheet No.4

1 cont'd.

It was learned from Zau Chah Mai that just
prior to entering a large compound the m/car he was
travelling in passed a Fire Station. On entering
the compound in question, the two m/cars were stopped
and the four occupants were ordered to alight and taken
inside a building to separate rooms.

The three males claim that they were stripped
naked and their clothing searched.

Zau Chah Mai states that in the room where
he was detained, there was a blackboard with the follow-
ing printed thereon Japanese Primary School, Range Road.

After being searched and questioned as to
their names, occupations, addresses and especially if
they had any connection with the office of the Woosung
Shanghai Garrison Headquarters they were instructed to
dress, following which the four persons were taken to
one room where they were informed that a mistake had
been made, and after signing that they had received
all their property they were photographed.

At about 9.45 a.m. 6-12-37, the four above
mentioned persons were placed in a lorry together with

据邵家楣（Zau Chah Mai，音译）称，在进入一个大院之前，他乘坐的汽车经过了一个消防站。进入该大院后，两辆汽车停下，四名住客被命令下车，并被带入一栋建筑内的不同房间。

三名男性声称他们被剥光衣服，衣物受到搜查。

The above incident was brought to notice
of the Station by reason of S.P.C. 1535 conversing
with two public ricksha coolies outside the Hotel at
about 7.10 a.m. who told him of seeing the Japanese
Military taking away four Chinese. The S.P.C. then
pursued his inquiries to the watchmen and the hotel
desk where he advised the accountant to inform the
manager and Louza Station.

Statements have been taken from the five
persons who were in the two rooms at the time the
arrests were made. Statements which corroborate
the arrests were also taken from the room boy Zung
Koo San (陳浦山), the desk clerk Kwan Chie Cha (關志楂)

上述事件引起巡捕房注意，原因是警员编号 1535（S.P.C. 1535）于上午 7 时 10 分左右在酒店外与两名公共人力车夫交谈，车夫告知他看见日本军方带走了四名中国人。该警员随即向守夜人及酒店前台进行查询，并建议会计通知经理及老闸捕房。

已对逮捕发生时身处两个房间内的五人取得供词。另从客房服务员陈浦山（Zung Koo San）、前台职员关志楂（Kwan Chie Cha）及私人守夜人陈家运（Zung Kya Yoong）处取得了佐证逮捕情况的供词。

C. D. I.

本人姓名袁秋初（Yuen Chiu Chu）（    ），年龄 36 岁，籍贯广东，受雇于南京路大东酒店（Great Eastern Hotel）担任艺人。
大东酒店 310 号房间由杨基（Yang Kee）（    ）于 1937 年 12 月 4 日预订，309 号房间于 1937 年 12 月 5 日预订。
1937 年 12 月 6 日上午 6 时，我看见三名日本士兵及三至四名身穿便服的日本人手持手枪进入酒店。他们逮捕了 309 和 310 号房间的四名住客并将他们带走。

pages.en:
FORM 40
G. 15M-11-36

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of YUNG Tsung Woo ( ) age 26,
native of Canton. WONG Ting Hun ( ) age 18,
taken by H. Colfe.
at Louza Station on the 6-12-37 and translated by Clerk: Ah Sun Tai.

(1) Residing No.3 Lane 239 Avenue Foch, Liberte.
(2) Residing No.9 Wing On Road, Nanking Road.

At 7am on 6-12-37 we both were in Room No.310 of the
Great Eastern Hotel, when suddenly Japanese snipers and
military police about 6 or 7 in number entered the room. We
were intimidated with pistol and subsequently forced into two
waiting Vans. We were escorted to a place in the vicinity
of Japanese Garden, Maxwell Road, Hongkew. Here we were ques-
tioned by Japanese re our name, activity, occupation and address.
Until 9.30 am the Japanese said "Hintake" and asked us to
write on a paper supplied, and finger printed. Then we were
brought back to the Great Eastern Hotel.

As it was holidays (Saturday and Sunday) we opened
a room together with 4 or 5 other friends, for the purpose of
amusing ourselves in playing with "Mah Jong".

Signed: YUNG TSUNG WOO & WONG TING HUN
pages.zh:
表格 40
G. 15M-11-36

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为荣宗武（YUNG Tsung Woo）（ ）年龄 26 岁，籍贯广东。黄定坤（WONG Ting Hun）（ ）年龄 18 岁，之供词，由 H. Colfe 于 1937 年 12 月 6 日在老闸捕房录取，由职员阿孙泰（Ah Sun Tai）翻译。

(1) 住址：福煦路（Avenue Foch）239 弄 3 号，Liberte。
(2) 住址：南京路永安路（Wing On Road）9 号。

1937 年 12 月 6 日上午 7 时，我们两人均在大东酒店 310 号房间内，突然约有六至七名日本狙击手及宪兵进入房间。我们被手枪威吓，随后被强行押入两辆等候的厢式货车。我们被护送至虹口麦克斯韦路（Maxwell Road，今溧阳路）日本花园附近的一处地方。在此，日本人就我们的姓名、活动、职业及地址对我们进行了讯问。直至上午 9 时 30 分，日本人说“Hintake”，并要求我们在提供的纸张上书写并按捺指纹。随后我们将被带回大东酒店。

适逢假期（星期六和星期日），我们与另外四五位朋友合开一个房间，目的是通过打“麻将”自娱。

签名：荣宗武 & 黄定坤

The following is the statement of **〔此处转录不清〕** Jung Toong Ching ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ), age 35,
native of Yue-Yao, Chekiang ........................................ taken by **〔此处转录不清〕** Rolf
at Louza Ctne ............ on the 6-12-37 .................... translated **〔此处转录不清〕**
and **〔此处转录不清〕** by Clerk: Sih Yun Pui.

I reside at the Central Glass Factory, 566 Hankow Road.
On 5-12-37, I opened room 303 at the Great Eastern Hotel for
the purpose of amusing myself with some other friends. We
played with "Mah-jongg" in the room, and as the time was too
late, I together with two friends remained therein. The next
morning at about 6-7 a.m. (6-12-37), Japanese soldiers and
sailors visited the room 3, knocking open the door, and took
my two friends away. I descended downstairs to the Accountant
Office and saw my two friends being escorted to a car which
was then driven away. Then I returned to my room but I did
not know what was the matter. The two friends of mine are
(1) Chiang Zau Chun and (2) Zou Yu Pei, both being my
relatives.

This is my true statement.

以下为 **〔此处转录不清〕** 郑东清（Jung Toong Ching）（ **〔此处转录不清〕** ）之供词，年龄 35 岁，籍贯浙江余姚（Yue-Yao, Chekiang） ____ ，由 **〔此处转录不清〕** Rolf 于 1937 年 12 月 6 日在老闸捕房（Louza Ctne） ____ 录取，由职员施云佩（Sih Yun Pui）翻译 **〔此处转录不清〕** 及 **〔此处转录不清〕** 。

本人居住于汉口路 566 号中央玻璃厂。
1937 年 12 月 5 日，我在大东酒店开了 303 号房间，目的是与几位朋友自娱。我们在房内打“麻将”，因时间太晚，我与两位朋友留宿房内。次日（1937 年 12 月 6 日）早晨约 6 至 7 时，日本士兵和水兵来到 3 号房间，撞开门，将我的两位朋友带走。我下楼至会计办公室，看见我的两位朋友被押送上一辆汽车，随后驶离。之后我返回房间，但不知发生了何事。我的两位朋友是 (1) 蒋祖春（Chiang Zau Chun）和 (2) 邹玉佩（Zou Yu Pei），两人均为我的亲属。

此为本人真实供词。

The following is the statement of J.P.C. 1536 Tse Yoon Sen (慈鳳山).
native of ____________________ taken by Mr. D.S.I. Chang Yuen Ching.
Louza Stn. 6-12-37 translated
at ________________ on the ________________ and interpreted by Clerk: Bang Su Tao.

I beg to report that I was on first day duty on 6-12-37
and was detailed to patrol 2 Section 1 Beat. At 7.10.a.m. same
date when I was walking on Kin Wo Ka near the entrance of the
Great Eastern Hotel, I encountered two public ricksha coolies who
had parked their rickshas outside the entrance of the hotel. These
two ricksha coolies at once told me that several Japanese soldiers
had arrested four Chinese from the hotel a short time previous.
I questioned them regarding the title of arrest, description of
persons arrested etc. when one of them related the following:-

At 6.50.a.m. 6-12-37 while he was standing on footpath
outside the hotel soliciting for hire, he saw several Japanese
soldiers in military uniforms and armed with pistols (actual
number of Japanese unknown) dragged three male Chinese and one
female Chinese out from the hotel into two motor cars which were
ranked on Kin Wo Ka a little North of the entrance of the hotel.
Having boarded the motor cars, the Japanese drove the cars along
Kin Wo Ka in a Southerly direction to Kiukiang Road.

In order to verify the above, I questioned a private
watchman on duty at the said entrance and he corroborated the
ricksha coolie's statement. Adding that the occurrence was also
known to the accountants of the hotel. I then went to the
Accountant's office of the hotel and after a length questioning,
one of the accountants admitted that there was such an occurrence
in the hotel and stated that he did not report the occurrence to
the Police because these Japanese were armed with pistols. I
persuaded them to report the occurrence to the Station by
telephone which they later did in my presence. I then left the

以下为警员编号 1536（J.P.C. 1536）慈凤山（Tse Yoon Sen）之供词，籍贯 ___ ，由副督察张元清（Chang Yuen Ching）先生于 1937 年 12 月 6 日在老闸捕房录取，并由职员邦苏道（Bang Su Tao）翻译及口译。

本人谨报告，本人于 1937 年 12 月 6 日值第一日班，并被指派巡逻第 1 巡区第 2 段。同日早上 7 时 10 分，当本人在大东酒店入口附近的九江路（Kin Wo Ka，即九江路）行走时，遇到两名将人力车停在酒店入口外的公共人力车夫。这两名车夫立即告诉本人，几名日本士兵在不久前从酒店逮捕了四名中国人。本人就逮捕名义、被捕者体貌特征等向他们询问，其中一人叙述如下：

1937 年 12 月 6 日上午 6 时 50 分，当他站在酒店外的人行道上招揽生意时，看见几名身穿军装、手持手枪的日本士兵（日本人确切人数不详）将三名中国男性和一名中国女性从酒店拖出，进入停在酒店入口北侧不远处九江路上的两辆汽车。日本人上车后，驾车沿九江路向南行驶至九江路（Kiukiang Road，注：此处原文 Kin Wo Ka 与 Kiukiang Road 可能指代同一区域或相邻路段，通常 Kin Wo Ka 指九江路，Kiukiang 亦指九江路，此处依原文译出）。

为核实上述情况，本人询问了在该入口执勤的一名私人守夜人，他证实了人力车夫的陈述。并补充说酒店会计也知晓此事。随后本人前往酒店会计办公室，经过长时间询问，其中一名会计承认酒店内确实发生了此类事件，并称因这些日本人持有手枪，故未向警方报告。本人劝告他们通过电话向捕房报告此事，他们随后在本人面前照办。本人随后离开

The following is the statement of Tsu Chai Kai (邵家楷), age 27,
native of Kaushing, taken by me Det. Black,
at Louza Station on the 6-12-37, and interpreted by Clerk Au Peng Yao.

My name is Tsu Chai Kai and reside in the premises of
the China State Bank, Sinsa Road, where I am employed as a
clerk. I have worked there for the past eight years and was
formerly employed in a native bank, Loong Chang (隆昌) now
closed, which was located on Honan Road.

At 12.00 noon on the 5-12-37, my friend Zung Koong Ching
(陈公之), engaged room No.309 in the Great Eastern hotel,
Nanking Road, I myself went to the room at 1.00 p.m. after
having been invited by Zung for recreation. On arrival at
the hotel I took a bath, after which I went to the head office
of the China State Bank in Peking Road. I returned to the
room about 3.00 p.m. at which time there were five other peo-
ple in the room all known to me as being connected with the
Central Glass Factory on Hankow Road near Chekiang Road. These
men were discussing business and I went to sleep on the bed.
I was wakened to partake of dinner and when four us, Zung,
Chiang, Tsu Sung (姜颂圣), Woo Ts Kong (吴之康) and myself
commenced to play Mah Jongg. We continued playing mah jongg
until 3.00 a.m. At this time three of us, Zung Chiang and
myself stayed in the room.

At about 6.15 a.m. 6-12-37, about eight Japanese in uni-
form all armed with pistols and some with swords entered the
room, about half of the Japanese had armlets indicating that
they were military police.

The intruders on entering the room pointed pistols at us
and spoke in Japanese which we did not understand, we rose
from the bed and then the Japanese searched us and also the

以下为邵家楷（Tsu Chai Kai），年龄 27 岁，籍贯嘉兴（Kaushing），之供词，由侦探 Black 于 1937 年 12 月 6 日在老闸捕房录取，并由职员欧鹏尧（Au Peng Yao）口译。

本人姓名邵家楷，居住于新闸路（Sinsa Road）中国银行旧址 premises，受雇为职员。本人在此工作已八年，此前受雇于河南路现已关闭的隆昌（Loong Chang）钱庄。

1937 年 12 月 5 日中午 12 时，我的朋友陈公之（Zung Koong Ching）在南京路大东酒店预订了 309 号房间，本人受陈邀请去娱乐，于下午 1 时前往该房间。到达酒店后，我洗了个澡，随后去了北京路中国银行总行。下午 3 时左右我返回房间，当时房间内还有另外五人，我都认识，他们与位于浙江路附近汉口路的中央玻璃厂有关联。这些人正在讨论业务，我便在床上睡觉。我被叫醒吃晚饭，随后我们四人，即陈、蒋、姜颂圣（Tsu Sung，注：拼音与中文名对应存疑，依音译及括号内中文）、吴之康（Woo Ts Kong）和我开始打麻将。我们一直打麻将到凌晨 3 时。此时，陈、蒋和我三人留在房内。

1937 年 12 月 6 日凌晨约 6 时 15 分，约八名身穿制服、均配备手枪、部分配有军刀的日本军人进入房间，约半数的日本人佩戴臂章，表明他们是宪兵。

闯入者进入房间后用枪指着我们，并用日语说话，我们听不懂，我们从床上起来，随后日本人搜查了我们以及

房间内的财物和抽屉。蒋在房间内被戴上手铐，我们三人被带下楼至靠近会计桌的门厅。蒋和我被日本人控制，但独自留在桌边的陈迅速溜走，日本人对其离去未加评论。被带出房间后，我看见一男一女，显然也被日本人逮捕，站在楼上的走廊里，他们随我们一起下楼至门厅。我不认识这些人，以前从未见过他们。

在门厅站立片刻后，
&
我们被带出门外/押入汽车，我与那对不知名的男女被安排进其中一辆汽车，车内另有四名日本士兵，其中一人驾驶汽车。

过外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）后，我不知道我们经过了哪些道路，因为我不熟悉苏州河以北的区域，但汽车驶入一个大院子，停在一栋大型石砌建筑的门口，就在进入院子之前，我看见一个消防站，在我被拘留的房间里，我看见一块黑板（日本小学，Range Head ?? 。到达建筑物后，我们被剥光衣服进行搜查，衣物随后归还给我们，然后我被带入另一个房间。一名讲中文的便衣日本人对我进行讯问。他听不懂我的回答，于是递给我纸和铅笔，我在上面回答了他的问题。他询问了我的姓名、地址和

occupation, particulars of the other occupants of room 309,
when the room had been occupied, and the reason for our being
there. He asked me if I was a member of the Shanghai & Woosung Garrison Headquarters and also stated that if I was I
would be killed. After this, I was taken into another room
where I saw the Chinese female being interrogated by a civilian
Japanese, the latter asked me to assist him in questioning the
female and from this I learned that she was a girl guide, he
did not question her as to her political beliefs.

After this interrogation, I was taken into another room
where there was an officer in uniform sitting at a desk, all
the other arrested persons were in this room. In this room
another Japanese in civilian told us that we were not the
persons wanted and could go. We had to sign a form to the
effect that we had received all our property back. Chiang
and myself were photographed together and the other male and
the female photographed together. Chiang and myself stood in
the compound for about 15 minutes then the male and female
came out and then we were taken back to the Great Eastern
Hotel in a motor car escorted by three Japanese in civilian
clothes.

We were in the custody of the Japanese for about 1½
hours.

The above is my true statement.

(Signed) Zen Chai Mei.

职业、309房间其他居住者的详情、
该房间何时被占用，以及我们在那里的原因。他问我是否是上海与吴淞警备司令部的成员，并称如果我是，就会被处决。此后，我被带到另一个房间，在那里我看到一名中国女性正接受一名日本平民的审讯，后者让我协助他审问该女性，由此我得知她是一名向导女（guide girl），他并未就其政治信仰对她进行盘问。

审讯结束后，我被带到另一个房间，那里有一名身穿制服的军官坐在办公桌前，所有其他被捕人员都在这个房间里。在这个房间里，另一名日本平民告诉我们，我们要找的人不是我们，我们可以走了。我们必须签署一份表格，大意是我们已收回所有财产。蒋（Chiang）和我合影，另外那名男性和那名女性也合影。蒋和我在院子里站了大约15分钟，然后那对男女出来，随后我们由三名身穿便服的日本人护送，乘汽车返回大东酒店（Great Eastern Hotel）。

我们被日本人拘留了大约1个半小时。

以上是我的真实陈述。

（签名）Zen Chai Mei（音译）。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Chiang Zau Sung (姜佐聖)
native of Zaushing taken by D.S.I. Tuck
at Louza Stn. on the 6-12-37 and interpreted by D.I. Loh Kung Sung.

I am a cashier employed at the Tsoong Foo Bank,
No.103 Jinkee Road, and reside at No.104 Dah Tsoong Li off
Yates Road, I have been in my employment for a period
exceeding ten years.
At about 5.p.m. 5-12-37, I proceeded to the Central
Glass Company, No.556 Hankow Road to locate my cousin named
Zung Loong Ching, who is employed as an accountant on the
premises.
Upon arrival I was informed that my cousin had engaged
Room No.309 of the Great Eastern Hotel, Kin Wo Ka, then to-
gether with a friend of my cousin named Wong Kyi Daung who
resides at the Chung Hwa Bank Building, Ave. Edw. VII, French
Concession, who was present on the premises, walked to the
Great Eastern Hotel and entered Room 309.
Inside the room was my cousin and three other males
two of whom are also employed together with my cousin at the
Central Glass Company, 556 Hankow Road, the other male named
Zau Chah Mai, cashier of the Branch of the Kau Wah Bank,
Boulevard de Montigny, F.C. a friend of my cousin and an
acquaintance of mine.
After the usual greetings had been exchanged I
proceeded into the bath-room which adjoins Room 309, and had
a bath then returned to the room where we had dinner (six
persons), same having been ordered during the time I was
taking a bath.
After dinner we decided to play "Mah Jongg" that is,
my cousin, Zau Chah Mai and one Woo Yoong Raung employed

以下为本人于1937年12月6日在老闸捕房对籍贯为嘉兴的姜佐聖（Chiang Zau Sung）所作的笔录，由督察罗公松（Loh Kung Sung）翻译。

我是金城银行（Tsoong Foo Bank）的出纳员，该行位于江西路103号，我居住在亚尔培路（Yates Road）大忠里104号，我在此任职已超过十年。
1937年12月5日下午5点左右，我前往汉口路556号的中央玻璃公司（Central Glass Company），寻找我的表亲宗龙庆（Zung Loong Ching，音译），他在该公司担任会计。
到达后，我得知我的表亲在金沃卡（Kin Wo Ka，即大东酒店）预订了309房间，于是我与当时也在该公司的表亲的朋友王奇当（Wong Kyi Daung，音译）一同前往大东酒店并进入309房间。王奇当居住在法租界爱德华七世大道（Ave. Edw. VII）的中华银行大楼。
房间里有我的表亲和另外三名男性，其中两人也与我的表亲同在汉口路556号的中央玻璃公司工作，另一名男性叫赵查梅（Zau Chah Mai，音译），是法租界蒙太尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）国华银行（Kau Wah Bank）分行的出纳员，他是我表亲的朋友，也是我的熟人。
寒暄过后，我进入与309房间相邻的浴室洗澡，然后回到房间，我们一起吃了晚饭（共六人），饭菜是在我洗澡期间点的。

1937年12月6日早上6点前的某个时候，向导女和伍一起离开了房间。

Subject Re Japanese activities in Lane 228 Burkill Road.

Made by D.S. Eymstone, Forwarded by O.A. Perkins Insp. "D"

Sir,

At 3.45 p.m. 4/12/37 a telephone message was received from
C.I.D. 2498 reporting that a party of Japanese had entered Lane
No. 228 Burkill Road ( the lane is known as Dong Tsung Fong).

C.D.S. 19 and the undersigned immediately responded but
on arriving at the above mentioned location it was discovered
that the Japanese had already departed.

Further enquiries ascertained the following details:-

At about 3.30 p.m. 4/12/37 a dark blue coloured motor car,
Shanghai Defence Force Plate No. 200 driven by a male Japanese
stopped on the North side of Burkill Road opposite the entrance
to Lane No. 228. Three male Japanese attired in mufti and one
male Japanese attired in a light brown military uniform, he being
armed with a pistol which he carried in a holster strapped to
his side, then alighted from the vehicle and walked into the
alleyway, proceeding to house No. 37 where one of the male Japanese
dressed in mufti knocked at the door, same eventually being
opened by a male Chinese named Tsau Yung Gih (赵永吉), age 45
years, native of Shanghai (refugee from Nantso.)

The Japanese in question then spoke in Mandarin and asked
Tsau Yung Gih whether any person employed by the Central Film
Censorship Committee resided therein and Tsau Yung Gih replied
in the negative then the entire party of Japanese departed from
the alleyway, boarded their motor car which was driven away in a
Easterly direction they having been in Lane 228 for about 10
minutes.

House No. 37 Lane 228 Burkill Road was formerly occupied by
the "Sweat and Blood Book Shop" (汗血书店) they having removed
to an unknown destination about 3 weeks prior to this date.

（左侧批注：S3. / See report of / DSR / 4/12 / Noted by / [签名] / 5 DEC 1937）
（左下角批注：DS 26 / DSC / 5/12）

事由 关于伯基路（Burkill Road）228弄内的日本人活动。

撰写人：警佐 Eymstone，转呈人：“D”区督察 Perkins

先生，

1937年12月4日下午3时45分，接到刑事侦缉处（C.I.D.）2498号电话报告，称一群日本人进入了伯基路（该弄堂名为东宗坊 Dong Tsung Fong）228弄。

刑事侦缉处特别组（C.D.S.）19号及本人立即响应，但抵达上述地点时发现日本人已经离开。

经进一步查询，查明以下细节：-

1937年12月4日下午3时30分左右，一辆深蓝色汽车，悬挂上海防卫军（Shanghai Defence Force）牌照第200号，由一名日本男子驾驶，停在伯基路北侧，正对228弄入口处。三名身穿便服的日本男子和一名身穿浅棕色军装的日本男子随后下车，后者腰间皮套内佩有手枪。他们走进弄堂，前往37号房屋。其中一名穿便服的日本男子敲门，门最终由一名中国男子赵永吉打开，现年45岁，上海本地人（南市难民）。

该日本男子随即用普通话询问赵永吉，此处是否居住着中央电影检查委员会的任何雇员，赵永吉予以否认。随后，整群日本人离开弄堂，登上汽车，向东驶离。他们在228弄停留了约10分钟。

伯基路228弄37号此前由“汗血书店”占用，该书店在本案发生前约3周搬往未知目的地。

（左侧批注：S3. / 见 DSR 报告 / 12月4日 / [签名] 注 / 1937年12月5日）
（左下角批注：DS 26 / DSC / 12月5日）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No.
Section 1, Special Branch    19/37
REPORT
Date December 2, 1937

Subject Sz Dai (時代職業中學) Vocational Middle School,
135 Jessfield Road, visited by Japanese military.

Made by D.S.I. Laurier    Forwarded by [签名]

On receipt of information from the French Police on
December 1, enquiries were made from which it has been
learned that at 10.55 a.m., December 1, five Japanese
officers armed with swords and two Japanese wearing foreign
styled plain clothes, visited the Sz Dai Vocational Middle
School, 135 Jessfield Road, arriving in two sedan motorcars,
special licence numbers 74 and 10212. Upon their arrival,
the principal of the school, Mr. Wong Ling King (黃林金) ran
away and about thirty students who were attending a class
in an upstairs room dispersed.

The ground floor of the school building is used as
a refugee camp and the upper floor is used as a class room.
The visitors demanded an interview with the principal of the
school, and upon being informed that he was absent, Miss
[签名/印章覆盖处] ing (楊), a member of the refugee camp staff, then
conducted the Japanese around the premises. The Japanese
officers gave as their reason for the visit a desire to
inspect the school. A discussion was held in the compound
for about 15 minutes after which the visitors departed at
11.10 a.m., proceeding in the direction of Robison Road.

撰写人 副督察长 Laurier    转呈人 [签名]

12月1日收到法国警察的情报后，经查询获悉：12月1日上午10时55分，五名佩刀的日本军官和两名身穿西式便服的日本人，乘坐两辆轿车（特别牌照号码分别为74和10212），访问了位于杰斯菲尔德路135号的时代职业中学。到达时，该校校长黃林金 (Wong Ling King) 先生逃走，约三十名正在楼上教室上课的学生四散离去。

校舍底层用作难民收容所，上层用作教室。来访者要求会见校长，在得知校长不在后，难民收容所工作人员楊 (Yang) 小姐[签名/印章覆盖处]随后带领日本人参观各处。日本军官称访问原因是希望视察学校。在院内交谈约15分钟后，来访者于上午11时10分离开，朝罗宾森路（Robison Road）方向走去。
